# Decompilation of Zax.exe – inventory and plan

Started 2026-10-21; the sections are dated individually, the latest state is 2026-11-01 (phase 6 done, sections 13 and 15). End goal (CLAUDE.md): the game should run from our own source code, portably, with modern technology and natively on each platform, based on the original assets. Single player and multiplayer are both in scope (since 2026-10-24; before, multiplayer was deferred). This includes a macOS port and support for higher resolutions and widescreen.

## 1. Inventory

The basis is the retail version without copy protection in `gamedata/Zax.exe` (SHA-256 `7d9efcae…`, 2,572,288 bytes). The values come from Ghidra 12.1.4 via REA and from the PE header (pefile) [confirmed 2026-10-21].

| Item | Finding |
|---|---|
| Format | PE32, x86, GUI, image base `0x400000`, linked on 2001-08-02. No symbols, no RTTI. |
| Compiler | Microsoft Visual C++ 6.0 (linker 6.00), according to the Rich header several service packs mixed (builds 8168 … 8966). |
| Translation units (Rich header) | about 443 C++ objects, 185 C objects, 39 assembler objects (MASM). That roughly matches the number of source files. The C objects are probably mostly libraries (zlib, Vorbis, C runtime). The assembler objects were taken for blit and blend routines; the blitter map of 2026-10-26 found no MASM code in the rendering ranges, they are most likely the C runtime's assembler routines [assumption: the objects cannot be mapped to addresses] (section 9, "The blitter range"). |
| Code | `.text` 2.0 MB. Ghidra alone finds 5,281 functions; with the vtable entries there were 7,918 on 2026-10-21 (without import thunks; `docs/functions.csv`; 11,765 at the milestone audit, section 10, "The milestone audit"). So Ghidra misses about 2,600 virtual methods that are only reachable through vtables. Game and engine code extends up to the import thunks at `0x5caa8e`. Before them lie vorbisfile and the GameSpy SDK (`0x5c3bf0`–`0x5ca9e0`), after them zlib 1.1.3, the MSVC 6 C runtime, libogg and libvorbis 1.0 beta 4 up to `0x5ea000`; exact ranges and versions in section 11 [confirmed 2026-10-25]. |
| Data | `.rdata` 124 KB (mainly vtables), `.data` 1.1 MB. `.cms_t`/`.cms_d` are the SecuROM loader, dead in this cracked exe (section 11). |
| Classes | 495 classes with 1,639 fields from the exe's class registration (`docs/classes.csv`, `docs/fields.csv`, generated by `tools/exe_classes.py`): parent class, size, vtable, factory, constructor and per field offset, size and, for switches, the bit mask. 442 classes have their own vtable, 53 are abstract. Large families: 111 actions (`CAction`), 93 AI classes (`CAIBase`, 45 of them directly below `CLayerPartAI`), 21 inventory items, 16 behaviour building blocks (`CEntityBehavior`). Unregistered helper classes (renderer, windows, containers) come on top. |
| Already named | 113 addresses in `docs/exe_symbols.csv` on 2026-10-21 (12,094 on 2026-11-01), plus the findings in `EXE_FINDINGS.md` and `FORMATS.md`. All file and level formats are known and readable with `zaxtools`. |

**Third-party libraries and system interfaces** (imports and strings of the exe):

| Area | In the exe | Replacement for the port |
|---|---|---|
| Graphics | DirectDraw (`DirectDrawCreate`), own 8/16-bit software rendering | SDL3 (window, texture upload), rendering stays software |
| Sound | DirectSound (ordinal 1), ACM (`msacm32`, converting ADPCM or similar), Ogg Vorbis (libvorbis 1.0 beta 4, section 11) linked statically | SDL3 audio, libvorbis/stb_vorbis, decode ADPCM ourselves |
| Movies | Bink (`binkw32.dll`, 16 functions) | FFmpeg (decodes Bink 1) or convert the movies once |
| Archives | `Data.dat` is an uncompressed zip read by the game's own code; zlib 1.1.3 static only for packed temp file blocks and `CZaxApp` data (`compress2`/`uncompress`, section 11; until 2026-10-25 this row said zlib for `Data.dat`) | current zlib or miniz |
| Input | window messages, joystick via WinMM (`joyGetPosEx`) | SDL3 (keyboard, mouse, gamepad) |
| Time | `QueryPerformanceCounter`, `timeGetTime`, `timeSetEvent` | SDL3 or `std::chrono` |
| Configuration | `Zax.CFG` via `GetPrivateProfile*`, registry (`RegQueryValueExA`) | own INI reading |
| Multiplayer | DirectPlay 8 (via `CoCreateInstance`), Winsock (the GameSpy SDK linked statically: LAN and master server queries, CD key check; section 11) | in scope since 2026-10-24 (game-side code with the phases, DirectPlay itself with the system layer; GameSpy LAN queries ourselves) |

## 2. Approach: step-by-step reimplementation inside the running exe

There are two common ways. The plan takes the second.

1. **Byte-exact decompilation**: the source is written so that VC++ 6.0 produces the same exe byte for byte. That is very laborious, needs the old compiler and hardly helps the port.
2. **Functionally equivalent reimplementation with hooking**, as in re3 (GTA III) and OpenRCT2: our own C++ code replaces the originals in the running Zax.exe function by function. The game stays playable the whole time. Every replaced piece is checked individually against the original. Once all functions are replaced, Zax.exe is no longer needed.

The technique for this already exists. `Zax-Launcher.dll` is loaded into the exe, redirects calls (`call` targets, import table) and is built with zig on the Mac (`zax-launcher/build.sh`).

**Rules for the reimplementation:**
- **Language C++ with the MSVC ABI** [decided and verified 2026-10-21]: the original is C++ with vtables (VC++ 6). As long as old and new code run side by side, object layout, vtables and calling conventions (`__thiscall`) must be the same. That is why clang compiles for the MSVC target (`i386-pc-windows-msvc`), and zig links. No Windows SDK is needed because `reimpl/src/win32.h` declares the few Windows functions itself. The probe confirms the MSVC peculiarities:
  - The destructor occupies a vtable slot (scalar/vector deleting dtor). The original has a vector deleting dtor in slot 1 (`test al, 2`, count at `[this-4]`).
  - Overloaded virtual methods are grouped.
  - The tail padding of a base class is not reused.
  - A call through an exe vtable (`CPickupAI`, slots 0 and 3) with our own class declaration runs in the VM.
  - Memory comes from the exe's heap (`operator new` → `0x5d033a`, `delete` → `0x5d0320`).
  - Important: `long double` is only 64 bit with the MSVC ABI. `-mlong-double-80` switches it to x87 precision internally; nothing changes at the interface to the exe.
- **Structures from the registration**: for the 495 registered classes the registration supplies size, parent class and field offsets. The header files are built from that, with `static_assert` on size and offsets (example: `reimpl/src/rotation_sequence.h`).
- **Floating point as in the original**: computations use x87 and `long double` where the original keeps intermediate values on the FPU stack. Rounding uses `fistp`, and comparisons follow the logic of `fcom` (helpers in `reimpl/src/reimpl.h`).
- **Names kept**: class and field names from the exe are kept. The evidence levels ([confirmed], [verified], [assumption]) apply as before.
- **Check per function**:
  - Pure functions (computation, reading files) run in the same process once in the original and once in the reimplementation, and the results are compared.
  - Everything else is checked in the VM with test levels and screenshots (`zax-testtools/tools/vmtest.py`).
  - Every reimplemented function can be switched off individually.
- **Measuring progress**: `docs/functions.csv` lists all 7,944 functions (as of 2026-10-22; 11,765 since the milestone audit, section 10) with subsystem and status (open, assigned, named, reimplemented, verified). Reimplemented functions are listed in `docs/reimpl.csv`.

## 3. Order

The order goes from the bottom up: first the foundation everything uses, then the game logic, the system layer last.

| Phase | Content | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Tools | Store the Ghidra database permanently (REA snapshot), import names and classes from `exe_symbols.csv` and the class registration. Create the function table with subsystems. Skeleton of the replacement DLL (table address → replacement, switchable individually, log). | Without stored names every session starts from zero. |
| 1. Core | `CObject`, `CClassInfo`, field descriptors, strings, containers, memory, file access and `Data.dat` (zlib), text and binary format of the objects | We already know the formats, and the game data is enough for comparisons. |
| 2. World | loading levels, layers, `Level Part`s, polygons, collision, way points (`.way`), camera | builds on 1; results are easy to check (level loads, `.way` identical) |
| 3. Game logic | object classes (`CEntity*`), AI (93 classes), actions (111), behaviour building blocks, weapons, inventory, quests, dialogue, save games | The largest part. The open questions from OPEN_ISSUES.md fall out of it along the way. |
| 4. Rendering and UI | software renderer (sorting, blending, light, shadows), fonts, menus, HUD, mini map | Most of the formulas are already confirmed (FORMATS.md 4–6). |
| 5a. System layer, faithful | reimplement every game function that calls Windows directly – DirectDraw (mode, surfaces, flip, lock), DirectSound/ACM, input and window messages, DirectPlay, the Bink wrapper, timers, the window, the message loop and `WinMain`, registry and INI configuration – with the same API calls as the original; checked like the rest: fake COM objects and APIs record every call with its arguments, original and reimplementation must give the same call sequence; the real interplay through game starts and the UI screenshot set (`--shot-set`). First a mapping batch counts and groups these functions (done 2026-10-28, section 10: 63 functions in four groups, two batches; the map also found 2,639 other game functions still open, most of them startup code and vtable slots missing from `docs/functions.csv`, batches C1–C5 there). | Every function of the game code then has its own source; together with 5b (the libraries) the decompilation is complete. Keeps a state checked function by function against the original up to the end. Decided with the project owner on 2026-10-27. |
| 5b. Libraries, matched | zlib 1.1.3 and libvorbis/libogg/vorbisfile 1.0 beta 4 built from their original sources into the DLL and checked with the same in-process checks against the copies in the exe; of the MSVC 6.0 C runtime and the GameSpy SDK the functions the game calls reimplemented and checked (behaviour, not Microsoft's or GameSpy's code); the dead SecuROM loader documented as not run | With 5a: **milestone "faithful and complete"** – every function of the exe is either reimplemented or shown identical, and the game runs on the reimplementation with the original's behaviour. The project owner wants this state before anything is modernised (2026-10-27). |
| 6. Detachment: a standalone exe | build the program without Zax.exe, still 32-bit x86 Windows with the original's API calls (DirectDraw, DirectSound/ACM, DirectPlay 8, Bink, WinMM, the window and the message loop exactly as in 5a): the globals, the constants and tables of `.data`/`.rdata` and the vtables that still come from the exe move into our own code and data; our own start (the PE entry, the C runtime start of 5b, `WinMain`); the functions too short to hook get their own source; SecuROM is left out. The hooking DLL stays a second build of the same sources, so the in-process checks against the original keep running; the standalone exe is checked by comparison runs against the original: the logged API calls (`TraceApi`), recorded input with the same game course and the same frames, the shot set, save games byte for byte | Mapped 2026-10-28, done 2026-11-01 (section 13: the inventory, the design, the batches 6-0 … 6-16; section 15: the rounds and the final check, passed on the x86 VMs 2026-11-01; the tag `milestone-standalone-faithful` waits for the project owner's consent). **Milestone "standalone and faithful"** (decided with the project owner on 2026-10-28): a Zax exe of our own that behaves like the original and needs only the game data. Before modernising, because then every later change (SDL3, other platforms, 64 bit) is compared against a program we build ourselves, and the hooking phase's layout assumptions (fixed addresses, the exe's memory image) are gone first. |
| 7. System layer SDL3 and port | put the API calls of 5a behind a narrow interface of our own and implement it with SDL3 (window, texture upload, audio, input, timers), step by step; current library versions only where 5b showed they behave the same; then macOS (arm64) and Linux; then 64 bit (pointers in structures; portable forms of the MMX code) | 5a documents exactly what SDL must reproduce (primary audio format, 565/555 pixel formats, buffer sizes, timing), so errors of the switch are told apart from errors of the reimplementation. The standalone exe of phase 6 is the reference for every step. Done in the fork zax-redone, not here (decided with the project owner on 2026-11-02): this repository stays the decompilation that follows the exe's structure; the interface is cut there first with the Win32 backend only and proven identical against this repository's references. |
| 8. Extensions | higher resolutions and widescreen: visible area, screen bounds of the AI, layout of UI and HUD (`Rules.txt`), mini map | requires our own renderer |
| with 1–5 | multiplayer: its game-side code (packets, sessions, messages) is reimplemented with the other subsystems; DirectPlay 8 itself reimplemented faithfully with the system layer (5a, done); own networking in place of DirectPlay only with phase 7 | in scope since 2026-10-24 |

## 4. Risks and open questions

- **Scope**: about 7,900 functions, about 7,100 of them in the game code (counted 2026-10-21; 11,765 and 10,911 since the milestone audit and batch 6-0, sections 10 and 13). re3 and OpenRCT2 took years for this. Progress is measured by the function table, not by deadlines.
- **Floating point**: VC6 computes with x87 (80 bit internally), new code mostly with SSE. Small deviations can change the course of the game (AI, physics). Hence the checks with comparisons in the same process.
- **Timing**: the game logic depends on the frame rate or on timers (measurement in EXE_FINDINGS.md, frame counter). That must be understood before higher resolutions.
- **Assembler parts**: 39 MASM objects, most likely the C runtime's assembler routines, not the blitters (section 9, "The blitter range"); the blitters are C++ with 97 MMX `__asm` functions, which must be reimplemented bit-exactly.
- **Bink**: the movies are encoded in a proprietary format. FFmpeg can read Bink 1. To be checked before phase 7 (5a and the standalone exe of phase 6 keep the original Bink calls).
- **Legal**: the reimplementation contains only our own code. Every player brings the original assets from their own copy, and `gamedata/` is never published.

| `reimpl/` | our own code, built with `reimpl/build.sh` into `out/reimpl/Zax-Reimpl.dll` (clang with the MSVC ABI, zig's linker; needs `brew install llvm zig`). The launcher loads the DLL if it sits next to Zax.exe. At start a self-test compares original and reimplementation, then the hooks are installed. With `/Original` or `Zax-Reimpl.ini` (`[Reimpl] Disable=0x…`) the originals stay active. Every hook creates a trampoline (the overwritten instructions and a jump back), so the original remains callable for comparisons (`original<T>(address)`). After `[Reimpl] CheckAfterMs=` milliseconds (default 20000, 0 = off) a separate thread runs checks inside the running game (`checks.cpp`, `checks_<module>.cpp`). `[Reimpl] Record=1` / `Replay=1` / `FrameLog=1` (also with `/Original`): input recording, replay and the per-frame hashes of `reimpl/src/replay.cpp` (section 13). `[Reimpl] ForceNoMMX=1` / `Force555=1` (also with `/Original`, and in the standalone exe): a simulated CPU without MMX (the exe's `Cpu_HasMmx` `0x5156b0` detects, then its flag `0x6cfdc4` is cleared) and a simulated 5-5-5 16-bit display (Zax.CFG's "Display is RGB 565" read as 0 and not written back), so the comparison sets reach the scalar and the 5-5-5 draw paths the VMs lack (`reimpl/src/sim_hw.cpp`, section 13, "Batch simulated-hw"). Log: `Zax-Reimpl.log`. |

**The static audit** (`tools/static_audit.py`, 2026-11-11; the owner asked for a check of functions, calls and constants against the original). The milestone audit (`tools/audit.py`) counts which functions are reimplemented and the DLL's checks compare behaviour at run time; this tool compares each reimplemented function's code with the exe's without running it. The exe side: the function's instructions from a recursive descent as `tools/audit.py`'s (stopping at every other table start), its direct and tail calls and code addresses used as values, imports by name, `call [reg + off]` as vtable slots, non-trivial immediates, field offsets, globals, x87 constants of `.rdata` by value and strings by text. The C++ side: the definition a hook entry names (also template instances, macro-generated functions, the libraries' C files, top-level assembler labels), its body read token by token with every helper that is no hook target expanded into it (parameters bound to literal arguments), every literal classified by its address range, named constants and `sizeof` of a type with a `static_assert` resolved. Differences are matched, explained by one of its mechanical rules (listed with their counts in `summary.md`: a callee one side inlines, a constant folded, a float written as its bits, a division by a constant as MSVC's multiplier, the x87 status bits of a comparison, …) or left open; an open difference may carry a hint, which never counts as an explanation. First run (main `543a2bc`): 11,380 of 11,572 functions compared (185 generated from the exe's bytes and not compared, 7 definitions not found), 8,660 without an open difference, 23,263 differences explained and 10,434 open: 1,480/537 calls, 355/28 vtable slots, 1,677/276 globals, 380/389 strings and 1,168/4,144 constants only in the exe/only in the C++ [verified 2026-11-11, `runs/static-audit/`]. The open differences are a review list, not a list of bugs: many are the tool's limits (receivers it cannot type, field offsets the exe reaches from another base, struct function pointers it takes for vtable slots), some are documented choices of the reimplementation (`StringField_Set` 0x4161d0 leaves out the no-op 0x40b280 by its comment) [verified 2026-11-11, sampled by hand]; `partitions.json` splits them by subsystem and file into six parts of about equal work. **The review** (2026-11-11, the six parts each read by hand against the exe's instructions, every pattern checked on at least one instance; results in `runs/static-audit/review/part1.md`–`part6.md` of the workspace, one verdict per difference) [verified]: of the 10,434 open differences 8,659 are the tool's limits, 1,770 the same behaviour written differently (constexpr tables compared entry by entry with the exe's pushes: the 45 key bindings, 71 item names, 19 cheats, 45 multiplayer field descriptors, 24 DirectPlay error texts; the MMX masks by their bytes; the libraries also against their unchanged releases) and 5 rows in three functions real deviations, none with an effect on the game's data: (1) `FrameFilter10::Apply` `0x4b2b50` kept its histogram on the heap (an exception then, `docs/ORIGINAL_BUGS.md` 2.27); (2) `CCaptureTheFlagGameType::DrawHUD` `0x4698f0` took "" for a third and fourth team's name and did not read on past the two names or crash at the fifth (the original's bug is `docs/ORIGINAL_BUGS.md` entry 3.10; Capture the Flag has two teams); (3) `CZaxApp_vtable::vf112` `0x59b400` left out two stores of base-class vtables (`0x5f7b94`, `0x602f90`) into two stack arrays just before they are freed and the function returns (no reader). The owner decided that the decompilation reproduces the original's behaviour here too: (2) and (3) are corrected since 2026-11-11 (section 16, "Batch ctf-faithful"; the review's "unset local" for the third team is the return address); (1) is corrected since 2026-11-12 (section 16, "Batch decomp-faithful2": the histogram on the stack through the exe's `_chkstk`). Also found: `docs/functions.csv`'s `0x5c9b70` "ArrayAppend" and `0x5c9bd0` "ArrayNth" are GameSpy hashtable.c's `TableEnter` and `TableLookup` [confirmed: `reimpl/src/gamespy_qr.cpp`]. What the audit cannot see: call order and count, argument values, control flow (the DLL's checks and the comparison sets cover these). The reviews' noise patterns, each written as a rule for the tool, are in the part files.

Names in Ghidra: names confirmed by hand come from `docs/exe_symbols.csv`. Per class `CName::vftable`, `classInfo`, `Create`, `CreateArray`, `RegisterFields` and the constructor are named. Every method of a vtable sits in the namespace of the lowest common parent class of all classes that contain it and is named after its slot `vf<n>`.

Subsystems (`docs/functions.csv`, on 2026-10-21): AI 13.8 %, rendering 13.1 %, inventory and weapons 8.1 %, actions 8.1 %, quests and dialogue 4.9 %, world 4.6 %, objects 3.6 %, core 2.5 %, game flow 1.8 %, user interface 1.2 %, sound 0.8 %, multiplayer 0.8 %. Libraries and copy protection together 10.5 %, not yet assigned 26.4 % (shares of the code in bytes). The assignment by class names and neighbours is an estimate.

**First reimplementation** [verified 2026-10-21, VM]: `ClampAngleToRange` (`0x5096a0`) and `CRotationSequence::AngleToRotation` (`0x55fdd0`).
- The self-test in the VM compares 200,000 inputs each, including NaN, infinity and edge cases. The results are bit-identical.
- The test level `Test/Nachbau1` contains 8 Korbos with facing angles from 0 to 7π/4. A run with the reimplementation and a run with `/Original` give pixel-identical images for all Korbos. The only difference is Zax, who stands in another frame of his idle animation.
- This proves the whole path: load the DLL, self-test, install hooks, the game runs.

Known gaps (2026-10-21; the fourth is closed by the milestone audit, section 10, and batch 6-0, section 13: every pointer target in `.text` is a table function or a listed row):
- For 10 classes the number of fields found differs from `zax-formats/zaxtools/exeschema.py` because the registration function is only read up to the first `ret`.
- For 76 fields the offset is unknown, mostly embedded objects (`emb`).
- The vtable length counts up to the next vtable start that code writes. That is an upper bound.
- Functions that are only reachable through other pointer tables are still missing.

### Reproducible builds (2026-11-01)

The same sources build the same `Zax-Reimpl.dll` and `Zax-Standalone.exe` byte for byte from any folder, given the same game data and tools (clang 22, zig 0.17.0) [verified 2026-11-01: main `bb4b64f` built in the worktree twice, in a copy without `.git` below the scratchpad, and in the main checkout: DLL SHA-1 `27537d62…` / exe `c0b3695c…` everywhere once both causes below were removed]. No build path reaches the binaries (no `/Users`, `/private`, `/var/folders` or `.pdb` string; `-fstrip`, no debug data besides the 28-byte build-id entry), and lld's COFF time stamp is derived from the build id, a hash of the content, not the clock. Two inputs made builds of the same tree differ:
- **The game data**: the DLL embeds the language pack's real `Local.txt` (`GERMAN.RED`, for the Local.txt checks) when `gamedata/` is there, and an empty table otherwise. A git worktree has no `gamedata/`, so worktree builds differed from main-checkout builds (+58 KB `.rdata`, other `.text`): `031231ad…` without vs `27537d62…` with the same sources; the earlier `e5a128a4…` (built in batch gaps-ui2's worktree) vs `eb4a3342…` (gaps-ui) of identical sources were this case. `build.sh` now takes the game data from `ZAX_GAME_DATA`, else `gamedata/` of the checkout, else that of the main checkout (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), for `GERMAN.RED` and the default `ZAX_EXE` of `--exe`, and warns when `GERMAN.RED` is missing. **Since the same evening the DLL takes nothing from the game data** (the project owner's decision): `zax-testtools/tools/vmtest.py` reads `Local.txt` from `GERMAN.RED` on the Mac and sends it with every `--reimpl` job as `Zax-Reimpl-Local.txt` next to Zax.exe (the VMs' game folders have no language pack, and `DATA.dat` has no `Local.txt`; the job's cleanup removes it), and `checks_local_table.cpp` reads it from there (without it the real file's cases are skipped with a note, as before without the pack). The DLL holds no game text any more (none of 200 sample lines of the pack's `Local.txt` in it) and builds the same from a copy without `gamedata/` (`8afbc7d0…` in both) [verified 2026-11-01: `OnlyChecks=local_table` on Cave1 `20261101-201126-c749` (x86-02) and on Nachbau1 `-201151-4943` (XP-01): the file copied and removed, "Load on test files and the real Local.txt: same (0 of 135 differ)"; full run `CheckScale=0.1` `-201126-e38c` (x86-03): all 1171 checks the same]. `build.sh` still uses the game data folder for `--exe` (Zax.exe's string table and version).
- **The locale**: the object order on the link line comes from the globs `src/*.cpp` and `src/libs/*.c`, whose order follows `LC_COLLATE`; with `en_US.UTF-8`/`de_DE.UTF-8` 29 of the 628 files move (`ai_chase_scan.cpp` before `ai_chase.cpp`), and the DLL became `6acc4fb4…` instead of `27537d62…` (other `.text`, `.data` size). The agents' shells run with the C locale, a Terminal with `LANG=de_DE.UTF-8` would not; `build.sh` now exports `LC_ALL=C` (also for `build_exe.sh`'s `ls`/`grep`). Since then a `de_DE.UTF-8` and an `en_US.UTF-8` build give `27537d62…` too. Check run of that DLL with `CheckScale=0.1` on `Test/Nachbau1`: all 1171 checks the same, `All checks done` (run `20261101-195455-0f61`, x86-01).
`zax-launcher/build.sh` has no glob; its only input of this kind is the icon from Zax.exe (it prints a note without one).

### Module layout and VM jobs (since 2026-10-22, for parallel batches)

- **Hooks per module**: every module lists its hooks at the end of its own `.cpp` as `ZAX_HOOKS(module) { const Hook list[] = {...}; return emit_hooks(out, list); }` (`reimpl.h`). `build.sh` collects all tables into `hook_tables.inc`; `main.cpp` stays unchanged for new modules. `MAX_HOOKS` is 16384 (raised from 1024 to 8192 on 2026-10-24 at about 1,000 hooks, to 16384 on 2026-10-28 at 8,208 hooks, `d1b7cbf`).
- **Checks per module**: new checks go into `reimpl/src/checks_<module>.cpp` as `ZAX_CHECKS(module) { ... }` (signature `(CClassInfo **cls, int n)`, run in the game thread after the older checks). The shared helpers (`Tally`, `compare_call`, `fnv`, `random`, string states, code and import patches, stand-ins for atexit/FreeLibrary) are in `check_util.h`. The older checks stay in `checks.cpp`.
- **Self-contained VM jobs**: `zax-testtools/tools/vmtest.py --reimpl out/reimpl/Zax-Reimpl.dll [--ini CheckAfterMs=0] [--ini Disable=0x...] [--arg /Original] --steps '...'` copies the DLL (and `Zax-Reimpl.ini` only from `--ini`), the test level `Test/Nachbau1` from `out/probe` of the main checkout (also from a worktree), runs the steps and puts the game folder back at the end of the same job (`cleanup`). Job ids are unique (`<time>-<4 hex>`). The helper runs jobs one at a time, so several sessions can submit at the same time. Steps for a check run: `[{"until_log":"Checks due"},{"key":"ESC"},{"wait":3},{"key":"ESC"},{"until_log":"All checks done"},{"wait":2}]` (after `CheckAfterMs` the DLL waits until the level has parts in its layer grid (a slow VM loads longer; run `20261024-193859-8674` started the checks during loading and two real-data checks found no level), then logs "Checks due"; ESC makes the game thread construct strings, which starts the checks there; the DLL writes "All checks done" after the last check and the helper step `until_log` waits for that line, by default up to 600 s, and fails if it does not come or the game ends – since 2026-10-24, before a fixed last wait of 30, 120 and 240 s that the growing checks kept outrunning; run `20261024-180502-4b1a`: checks 125 s, whole job 164 s instead of about 300 s. The game stands still while the checks run in its thread – check that the last module's check, currently `Zip CRC`, is in the log); screenshot run: `--ini CheckAfterMs=0 --compare-shots --steps '[{"wait":40},{"shot":"start"}]'` (shorter waits can catch the loading screen on a slow VM). Before "Checks due" the steps pressed ESC at a fixed 30 s, which broke with a later start (run `20261024-194601-ea80` with `CheckAfterMs=40000`: the checks never started, `until_log` timed out after 600 s).
- **Mouse steps and the helper's console (2026-11-01)**: a play whose game had ended went on clicking, the clicks landed in the helper's console window, and QuickEdit's selection there halted the helper until the project owner restarted it (x86-01, job `20261101-200925-69b0`). Both helpers now turn QuickEdit off for their own console at start (`SetConsoleMode`, only while they run; Windows' setting stays) and refuse a mouse step (`click`, `move`, `rclick`, `lhold`, `mmove`, `wheel`, `dclick`, `drag`, `press`) when neither the game nor `Zax-Launcher` runs: the job ends with "mouse step N not sent: neither the game nor Zax-Launcher is running" [verified 2026-11-01: the launcher window closed by Exit, then a click: `20261101-201552-8e4d` (x86-02), `-6728` (XP-01); QuickEdit off not observed directly]. `--launcher-window` starts `Zax-Launcher.exe` without arguments for steps in its start window.
- **Reference screenshot** (since 2026-10-24): `--compare-shots` compares the job's screenshots with a `/Original` run of the same map and steps, made once and kept in `out/probe/reference/` of the main checkout (`--new-reference` makes it again); differences only in two small areas count as the same (as between two `/Original` runs) and are reported as such: Zax at the start point (1290–1515 × 650–885; the frame of his idle animation depends on how much playing time 40 s of real time gave) and the last digit of the playing time clock in the bar (2040–2080 × 1700–1745; 00:00:33 or 00:00:34). Saves the `/Original` job of every screenshot comparison (run `20261024-200326-e946`: 44 s). - **Check run time: budget per module** (since 2026-10-25): a full run with all cases (no `CheckScale`) on `Assimilate Cave1` should take about 10 minutes of checks, and every module at most about 30 s there. Measure it with the full run on `Assimilate Cave1` from `Respawn2` and on `Test/Nachbau1`: the DLL logs `Module <name>: <ms>` after every module and, after every `Check …` report, a line `    <ms> ms` with the time since the previous report (or the module's start), so the slow check within a module stands out. A module above the budget first looks at its time per case: a few milliseconds per case is fixed overhead, not the case's own work. Trim repetition, not coverage: keep every case kind and edge case and the real-data kinds; real-data loops over a level's objects take at most a cap per kind, a deterministic spread (`spread_pick` in `check_util.h`: the first, the last and every k-th in level order); random case loops keep their count from `scaled()`.
  - Findings (2026-10-25): most of the time went into putting hooks out and in. Every case puts its module's hooks back to the original bytes for the original side and installs them again; each hook site had two `VirtualProtect` calls and a `FlushInstructionCache` each way, about 600 calls per case pair in the bigger modules, 5 to 22 ms per case on the VMs (Windows on ARM emulating x86). The exe's code section `.text` (`0x401000`–`0x5ea000`) now stays writable while the checks run (`write_code`, `CODE_START`/`CODE_END` in `check_util.h`, set in `checks.cpp`; also `patch_jump`); the flush per site stays. That alone took `Test/Nachbau1` from 1249 to 277 s and `Assimilate Cave1` from 1588 to 300 s, without a case less. The only module still above the budget was `entities` on `Assimilate Cave1` (38 of its 44 s in its real-data check: 1056 entities × 20 to 40 calls); it now tests at most 100 entities per kind (plain, destructable, animated; 178 of 1054, 5380 calls), 12 s. `polygon`'s building loop (2500 cases) now takes its count from `scaled()` too.
  - The hook site guard: every `checks_*.cpp` saves the sites it puts out in arrays of a fixed size (`MAX_SITES`). When a module had more hooks than that, `hooks_out()` returned silently, the module's checks compared the reimplementation with itself and reported "same". Now `hook_sites_fit` (`check_util.h`) logs `Check <module> hook sites: MISMATCH (<n> hooks, room for <m>; …)` once per module, a line that reads like a differing check (verified with `ai_slots` built with room for 4 of its 34 hooks, run `20261025-154155-79f9`). `ai_classes` (249 hooks) has room for 512 now.

  - Two check artefacts seen on `Assimilate Cave1` on 2026-10-25: `sort list: file slots on fake parts` compared the eax of CObject's slot 11 (`0x417500`), which after a skipped `{ … }` block is the stack line buffer's address with `'}'` in the low byte (`0x1ae07d` / `0x1ae17d`); the original's and the reimplementation's frames differ, so it differed whenever the two buffers fell into different 256-byte pages. The check now counts such a stack value by its low byte (`stack_low_byte`, `checks_sort_list.cpp`). `object classes: Create, CreateArray, …` differed once in 4 of 560 cases of `CWaterWaveFormData` (run `20261025-184102-22ec`): the case "Create on a freed block filled with a pattern" expects Create to get the freed block back, but the class has 0x218 bytes, more than the pool's largest size (500), so the block comes from the C heap, which the game's other threads use too. Leaving that case out for big classes sent them always into the CreateArray case, and that crashed both full runs (`20261025-184818-4898`, `-184822-f0d8`: eax raw heap addresses, empty event log, then no further output). [confirmed: disassembly `0x596a70`/`0x596ad0`, VM runs] Second cause, in the CreateArray case of all seven classes: with 0 elements the check called the array's deleting destructor through slot 1 of the first element, which does not exist (the 4-byte block holds only the count), so the vtable came from whatever lay behind the block; for the small classes that was mostly a stale object of the same class, for `CWaterWaveFormData` arbitrary heap bytes. Fixed in the check (`checks_object_classes.cpp`): the array destructor is called by its address (as `checks_world_data.cpp` already did), single objects still through slot 1; for heap-sized classes the pattern case allocates no pattern block, logs no "same block" event and compares only the bytes the constructor writes (`array_bytes`), and after a freeing destructor it no longer reads the freed heap block. Afterwards `OnlyChecks=object_classes` all 560 cases identical in six runs (`Test/Nachbau1`: `20261025-192824-6f4c`, `-192824-8984`, `-192946-8ff0`; `Assimilate Cave1`: `20261025-192824-661f`, `-192824-b553`, `-192946-5559`; both VMs), and the full runs with all cases `20261025-192948-2bdb` (`Test/Nachbau1`, VM-01) and `20261025-192948-e1a1` (`Assimilate Cave1`, VM-02): all 523 checks identical, all 4530 hooks installed, `Zip CRC` and `All checks done` in the log. Other modules: no other check expects a freed heap block back (the only other classes above 500 bytes, `CInventoryDisplayOptions` and `CPlasmaTileMap`, go through the inventory checks' arena or are not patterned); `checks_definitions.cpp` and `checks_path_classes.cpp` still destroy an empty CreateArray through slot 1 of a missing element (all their classes are pool-sized, so far without a difference) and should call the destructor by address too.

Three runs of the module alone were identical (`20261028-064424-b5bb`, `-064454-6250`, `-064523-8d22`; 291–342 real cases, the number follows the running level). Taken as a byte of a live object changing between the two sides; watch for it. The same full run first failed completely: 8208 hooks were more than the hook table's 8192, so the DLL installed none and no check started (`20261028-061409-0835`, `-061413-2fab`); the table holds 16384 since `d1b7cbf`.

For the text `""` slot 19 of the owned object kind (`0x4189b0`) deletes the object the prepared block holds (`CChaseInvestigateAI`'s "Investigate AI" at +0x10c is null in the level, slot 10 gives the fresh block a default object) and returns the deleting destructor's `eax`, the object's own address (`0x58c39c` `mov eax, esi`), a pool block. The sides get different blocks when the pool's free list order changes between them, which depends on what ran before (hence only in full runs on `Assimilate Cave1`). The check now counts a result equal to the deleted object's address as such (`DELETED_OBJECT`, `checks_field_objects.cpp`) and logs the addresses when the sides differ: run `20261028-125152-18d2` logged `Investigate AI text: deleted owned object at 29d99ec / 29d9820` (low bytes `0xec` / `0x20` as in the failing runs) and passed.
    - `weapons: RegisterFields against the registered fields (real data)` (run `20261028-114705-ef53`, `CDamageExpandingRadiusAI` field 3 "Damage", +0x20 `c9c2a10` / `1b09a814`): +0x20 of a field descriptor is the units `ZString` (section 6, "Field descriptors, base class"), here "Units/Sec" on both sides. `same_registered` (`checks_inventory_common.h`) took every pointer of side 1 into the arena for an element descriptor and compared it as one, which fails at once for a block that is no allocation of the case; a string buffer is only such a pointer when its pool block lies in the arena, i.e. the pool had blocks in check memory. The check now descends only into allocations of the case (`find_alloc`) and compares other pointers by value (string buffers by their text). Not reproduced (runs `20261028-122737-de3f`, `-130409-8f10`); the ways pool memory can land in check memory were closed: the arenas of `action_classes`, `entities`, `entity_classes` and `sound` took a growing pool's new chunk (only the `invcheck` arena filtered it), and the stubs of `checks_ui_common.cpp` (C1's `classreg_slots` with a fixed operator new, C2's `static_c2*`, `app_*`, `ui_controls`) answered it with a stub block; all now leave such a chunk to the C heap (`pool_grow_call`, `check_util.h`). A pool audit after every module (`check_pool_audit.cpp`) reports `Pool audit after <module>: MISMATCH` for chunks or free blocks in registered check memory (the arenas, the DLL image) and takes such free blocks out of the free list; free blocks outside their class's chunks in other memory (C heap blocks freed into the pool) are only logged when their count changes (`pool audit after …: n free blocks …`; up to 1229 after `plasma_tile_map` on `Assimilate Cave1`, from `action_helpers` on; not examined further).
    - Full runs with all cases afterwards, all 1064 checks identical, no pool audit `MISMATCH`, `All checks done`: `Assimilate Cave1` (Respawn2) `20261028-125152-18d2`, `Test/Nachbau1` `20261028-130409-8f10` (VM-02). ### Standard UI scenes: `vmtest.py --shot-set` (since 2026-10-26, for phase 4)

The end-to-end screenshot check of phase 4 (rendering, HUD, windows and menus): nine named scenes, each its own job with its own steps, `/Original` reference and known animated areas (`SCENES` in `zax-testtools/tools/vmtest.py`). The pixel checks inside the game (in-process) are built separately; this set checks what reaches the screen.

```
python zax-testtools/tools/vmtest.py --reimpl out/reimpl/Zax-Reimpl.dll --shot-set [--scenes automap,options]
python zax-testtools/tools/vmtest.py --reimpl out/reimpl/Zax-Reimpl.dll --shot-set --new-reference [--scenes …] [--runs 3]
python zax-testtools/tools/vmtest.py --reimpl out/reimpl/Zax-Reimpl.dll --shot-set --new-reference --more-variants --scenes inventory --runs 10
```

Other display modes (since batch 6-15): `--mode 800x600x8|640x480x16|640x480x8` adds `/ScreenWidth`, `/ScreenHeight`, `/ScreenBitDepth` to every scene's start and keeps the references per mode (the mode is part of the reference key; without `--mode` nothing changes); the animated areas of these modes are `MODE_AREAS` (section 13, "Batch 6-15"). `--jobs-at-once N` submits the jobs in groups of N when the VMs are shared.

Needs the editor's `.venv` Python (Pillow, numpy). The jobs go to the VMs of one platform at once (x86 by default, `--platform`; each to the least busy one, a queued job moves to the one that becomes idle first; `--share` for one VM); on the two ARM VMs (2026-10-26) the whole set took about 2 minutes, about 4 minutes on one. Per screenshot it prints `identical`, `differs only in animated areas (…)` or `DIFFERS (x0, y0, x1, y1), n pixels`, and for every difference it saves `<shot>-diff.png` next to the job's screenshots (darkened screenshot, red: differing pixels outside the animated areas, yellow: inside, cyan: the animated areas, green: areas checked again inside them). The exit code is 0 only when no scene differs outside its areas. `--compare-shots` (one screenshot after 40 s, `TIMING_AREAS`) is unchanged.

| Scene | Map | Steps after loading (keys) | Screenshots | Job run time | Animated areas (VM screen 2880 × 1806) |

How the scenes are made deterministic:
- **Timed from the end of loading**: every scene starts with the helper step `{"until_debug_log": "Preload things on Map"}`, which waits for that line in the launcher's `Zax-Debug.log` (`/DebugLog`, the exe's section log, written unbuffered; the helper checks every 0.5 s), so a slow start of the game does not move the screenshots. With it the playing time clock of `hud_nachbau1` is the same in every run (with the fixed 40 s of `--compare-shots` it was 33 or 34 s).
- **The mouse parked**: the game draws its own cursor where the VM's mouse is, which was wherever it had been left (in other places in other runs and on the two VMs), and the upper body and in scripted scenes the camera turn towards it. The new helper step `{"move": [x, y]}` sets the mouse without a click; every scene moves it to (2700, 1700), where the game clamps the cursor to its corner and it is not seen. The mouse has no linear mapping into the game (`SetCursorPos(100, 100)` drew the cursor at 537, 335, `(1440, 903)` at 1681, 1117, and different from run to run), so parking it in the middle did not work. Moving the Mac's mouse over a VM window during a run moves it again.
- **Keys**: the exe's default bindings (`0x59c550`, section 8 band D; names at `0x6249ec`–`0x624b14`): M "Toggle Auto-Map", I "Display Inventory", L "Display Log Entries", V "Display Voice Recorder"; Escape opens "Zax Menu"; its buttons and those of "Configure Menu" and the main menu react to their accelerators without Alt (`&Configure`, `&Load Game`, `&Save Game`, `E&nd Game`; `&Controls Configuration`, `&Video Configuration`, `&Sound Configuration`; `&Start Game`). "End Game" goes straight to the main menu; Escape closes a dialog and goes back to the menu that opened it.
- **Tolerance**: a pixel counts as different only when a colour channel differs by more than 2 (`SHOT_SET_TOLERANCE`). The menus outside a level (640 × 480) differ between VM-01 and VM-02 (now `ARM-01`/`-02`) by 1 or 2 in a few thousand pixels (main menu 1807 pixels, "Select Difficulty" 2181, identical between two runs on the same VM), the VM's scaling of the screen; a different 16-bit colour of the game differs by 4 or more.
- **Reference variants**: the bottom panel (inventory, log entries, voice log) slides in with the HUD bar on top of it and comes to rest at one of two heights one game pixel (3 screen pixels) apart, about once in ten openings the upper one, also with `/Original` (runs `20261026-183409-a7cb`, `-184225-e953`, `-184224-2fe7`). Only the panel's background moves, the translucent inventory windows in it stay, so it cannot be compared moved by a pixel. `--new-reference` groups the runs of a screenshot that are the same outside the animated areas into states and keeps the first state as the reference and every further one as a variant (`<shot>.v2.png`); a run counts against the closest variant. `--more-variants` keeps the references and adds the states new runs show (the inventory scene: 18 runs, two variants for each of its three screenshots). The scene's `reference_runs` (8 for `inventory`) raises `--runs`.
- **The dialogue**: the camera of the intro of `01 Main` stands one or two game pixels apart from run to run (moved 3 or 6 screen pixels; with the mouse in the middle or in the corner alike), and the dialogue's text scrolls in time with the voice, so only the window's opaque parts (portraits and frame) and the HUD are compared. A dialogue that starts while Zax stands still (a level not searched for yet) would allow more.

How the animated areas were found: `--new-reference` runs every scene three times with `/Original` on both VMs (`--runs`), keeps the first as the reference and prints the boxes the runs of a state differ in among themselves (`mask_boxes`: groups of differing pixels, a box around each, 2 pixels added) and whether the scene's areas cover them; the areas in `SCENES` are those boxes, named after what moves, with some room only where noted. The areas are in the ARM VMs' screen (2880 × 1806, the 4:3 picture in columns 236–2643); on x86 and XP the screenshot has the display mode's size, and `vmtest.py`'s `scaled_areas` maps the areas from that picture (since 2026-11-01). References in `out/probe/reference/shot-set/` (ARM) and, since 2026-10-31, `shot-set-x86`/`shot-set-xp` of the main checkout, `<scene>-<key>-<shot>` (the key changes with the scene's map, start point or steps, so changed steps need new references) and `<scene>-<key>.json` with the runs, the differences and the variants.
- Reference runs (`/Original`): `20261026-183408-8da9`, `-2316`, `-00db` (`hud_nachbau1`); `-183408-5e6b`, `-183409-84f2`, `-d328` (`hud_cave1`); `-183409-909f`, `-1983`, `-6c7c` (`automap`); `-183409-5111` … `-183411-ae6c` and `-184223-93d3` … `-184225-e953` (`inventory`, 18 runs); `-183411-3a84`, `-a037`, `-9d80` (`dialogue`); `-183411-0ff9`, `-144e`, `-9eec` (`pause_menu`); `-183411-c470`, `-183412-1528`, `-e710` (`options`); `-183412-c278`, `-23f9`, `-0bc8` (`save_load`); `-184738-4ca9`, `-3da6`, `-3a98`, `-36ec` (`main_menu`).
- Runs with the DLL of `main` `beae259`: `20261026-184524-c77b` … `-184525-ad03` (both VMs, 122 s), all of the set on VM-01 `20261026-184850-e53f` … `-ceb2` (224 s) and on VM-02 `20261026-184853-cb13` … `-bb14` (227 s): every screenshot identical or different only in its animated areas.

## 6. Phase 1: core (started 2026-10-21)

*Note (2026-11-01)*: the batch entries below are records of their day. Their "Not reimplemented", "Left out", "Leaving out", "not yet", "stays open", "left with the original" and "not hookable" lists give the state of that day: everything they name was reimplemented later or is listed with its reason in `docs/not_reimplemented.csv` (section 10, "The milestone audit"; the short "not hookable" functions are hooked through their padding, `reimpl/src/short_hooks.cpp`).

### CClassInfo [verified 2026-10-21, VM]

18 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/class_info.cpp`, list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): registration, base constructor, inheriting and appending fields, field search, name, version, derivation, creation, plus getter and fields of `CObject`.

Structure (evidence in `class_info.h`):
- The class info has two levels. The base has 0x40 bytes, vtable `0x5ec740` and the constructor `0x415110(name, version, parent, size)`. `CClassInfo` has 0x48 bytes, vtable `0x5ec83c`, and `ClassInfo_Register` is its constructor. The vtable with 29 slots belongs to a generic named-list interface: slot 1 returns the name of the i-th field, slot 2 searches, slot 3 searches with the error message "Fatal Not Found Error", slot 22 returns the count, slots 27/28 create.
- Fields: +0x04 field list, +0x0c name, +0x10 version, +0x18 parent, +0x1c list of children, +0x2c extra list, +0x30 field count, +0x34 inherited fields, +0x38 abstract, +0x3c size, +0x40 factory, +0x44 array factory.
- Parent 0 means "derived from `CObject`", -1 "no parent".
- Derived classes get copies of their parent's field descriptors (vtable slot 1 of the descriptor clones).
- **Version checksum**: after the fields are registered, `version = version + 7 · own fields + 3 · version of the parent class` (x87, intermediate sum unrounded).
- **Field search** `0x4154d0`: case-insensitive. First the field after the one found last is checked (global cache `0x62e664`), then all names in order, then all alternative names (+0x1c of the descriptor). With duplicate names the result therefore depends on the cache. That happens: `CEntityAnimated` has fields with empty names.
- Small objects come from per-size pools: `operator_new_ecx` `0x417710`, released via `0x54d130` with pointer and size. Field lists come from the C heap. The reimplementation uses both from the exe (`exe_base.h`).

Check in the VM, test level `Test/Nachbau1`:
- After 20 s the class table is written to the log, one line per class. Every line contains version and checksum (bit-exact), parent, size, abstract, factories, number of fields, children and extra entries, plus a checksum over all field descriptors. All 495 classes are registered. The table with the reimplementation matches the one from `/Original`.
- Compared against the original via trampolines:
  - name, version, field name and field count: 6,772 cases.
  - `IsDerivedFrom`: all 245,520 class pairs.
  - `FindField`: 72,270 cases with all names, alternative names, upper-cased and unknown names, each with three start values of the cache. Result, index and cache are compared.
  - Everything identical. A control run that calls the original twice is identical as well, so the game thread does not interfere.
- Screenshot after 25 s without the check thread: the reimplementation is pixel-identical with two `/Original` runs. A second reimplementation run differs at one Korbo, just like the run with the check thread. That animation frame depends on timing, not on the reimplementation.

Side finding: `docs/fields.csv` lists 16 own fields for `CEntityAnimated`, the exe reports 17. At least one field has an empty name.

### ZString [verified 2026-10-22, VM]

61 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/zstring.cpp`, list in `docs/reimpl.csv`):
- First batch (12): constructor, copy constructor, destructor, assignment from a `ZString`, a C string and the first n characters of a C string, length, empty/not empty, `c_str` and the shared empty buffer.
- Second batch (28): constructors from text (`CtorText`, `CtorTextN`, `CtorConcat`), assignment variants without a return value, `Empty`/`Clear`, path joining (`SetPath`, `SetPath3`), `Append`, `Format`/`AppendFormat` with the length estimate `FormatLength` (`0x585490`), `Mid`, buffer access (`GetBuffer`, `GetBufferDiscard`, `ReleaseBuffer`, `Reserve`), comparison with and without case, `GetAt` and the buffer helpers `Release`, `AllocBuffer`, `AllocCopy`.
- Third batch (19): appending (`AppendText`, `AppendTextN`, `AppendRepeat`, `AppendString`, `AppendChar`), `Insert`, `GrowTo`, path pieces (`AppendPathName`, `AppendPathN`), dash paths (`SetDashPath`, `SetDashPathSub`), splitting a path (`SplitPath`, `SplitPathText`), editing in place (`TrimLeft`, `TrimRight`, `KeepChars`, `MakeUpper`, `ReplaceChar`) and `SetHex`.
- Fourth batch (2): the time formats `SetTimeHMS` and `SetDuration`.

- A `ZString` is one pointer to a buffer `{reference count, capacity, text}`. The text starts at byte 8, and the buffer comes from the pool allocator with size capacity + 9. Assignment writes in place when the buffer is not shared and big enough, otherwise it releases the old buffer *before* copying and takes a new one of exactly the needed capacity.
- All empty strings share one static buffer `0x6c0ef0` (capacity 0). It is created on first use (guard bit `0x6c0f08`) with reference count 1 and counts every empty string, so it is never freed.
- `AssignTextN` (`0x4df160`) uses strncpy semantics (pads with zeros, capacity n even for shorter text) and returns nothing: `eax` is left over from the last call.
- `CtorText("")` allocates a buffer of its own with capacity 0; only null gives the shared empty buffer. `Mid` and `GetAt` do not check their position.
- `SetPath(dir, name)` (`0x4dfa50`, 22 callers) first makes room for `dir + name + 1`, then assigns `dir` and appends `/` unless the text is empty or already ends with `/`, then the name. `SetPath3` (`0x4e02c0`) also appends a suffix without a separator (e.g. an extension). Growing buffers get exactly the needed capacity: new buffer, copy, then release the old one.
- `Format` (`0x4e09b0`, cdecl, 122 callers) sizes the buffer with `FormatLength` and then calls the exe's `vsprintf` (`0x5d21ba`). `FormatLength` is an upper bound, not the exact length: literal characters 1, `%d`/`%i`/`%u` 32, floating point 64, `%p` 10, `%c` and `%%` 1, `%s` its length (cut to the precision), `#` adds 2, then at least the width. Conversions it does not know (`x`, `o`, `X`, `n`, length modifiers, even the terminator) count as flags, so the specification continues behind them; `%C` loops forever. If the estimate is 0, `Format` writes into the current buffer even when it is shared.
- `SetDashPath(dir, file, suffix)` (`0x4dffd0`) builds `dir/<directory of file>/-<name of file><suffix>`, e.g. `Save/Levels/-a.zax.bak`; the dash is the one-character string `0x60f634`. `SetDashPathSub` (`0x4dfc70`) puts `/sub` between name and suffix. Callers not yet examined.
- `SplitPath` (`0x4e0570`, from a `ZString`) and `SplitPathText` (`0x4e0770`, from a C string) use their own calling convention: path in `ecx`, directory output in `edx`, name output on the stack (`__fastcall` with three arguments). Both outputs are optional; `/` and `\` separate (`0x4a4570`). The directory comes without the final separator. A null C string gives the name `In Path Name Null!`.
- The editing functions first make the buffer their own (same capacity) and then call small text functions of the exe in place (`0x587b30` trim left, `0x587b80` trim right, both with the set tab/space/CR/LF at `0x622df4`; `0x587bc0` keep characters, `0x587c00` upper case a–z only, `0x587ce0` replace a character, `0x587fa0` hex digits). The reimplementation still calls these; they lie in the range that `docs/functions.csv` assigns to "AI", which is wrong (later reimplemented as the `Text_*` helpers, `misc_rest.cpp`; the range counts as Core since the assignment corrections of 2026-10-24).
- `GrowTo` (`0x4e0e60`) grows only if the capacity is too small and leaves a shared buffer shared, unlike `Reserve`. `AppendString` takes the source buffer before growing, so appending a string to itself reads the old buffer.
- Time formats (seconds as a float): `SetTimeHMS` (`0x4e0b30`) writes `%02d<sep>%02d<sep>%02d`. `SetDuration` (`0x4e0bc0`, 6 callers) writes over a day `days<d> hours<sep>minutes<min>`, over an hour `h<sep>mm<sep>ss<s>`, otherwise `m<sep>ss`, where the seconds are rounded up from more than 0.50 (59.6 s gives `0:60`). Separators and suffixes are localized global ZStrings (`0x6c0ee8`, `0x6c0efc`, `0x6c0f00`, `0x6c0f04`, `0x6c0f0c`), set by static initializers from the language pack. The arithmetic runs on the FPU stack with the float constants 1/86400, 1/3600 and 1/60 and truncates with `__ftol` (`0x5d0488`, 64-bit `fistp` with chop rounding, low 32 bits). The reimplementation does the same with `long double` and `x87_ftol` (`reimpl/src/reimpl.h`); the intermediate value before the seconds is rounded to float as in the original.
- Pool allocator: `0x506470` returns the global pool (created on first use), `0x5065b0`/`0x5065e0` allocate/free on it (thiscall). Sizes above the biggest pool size go to `operator new`/`delete`.

### Field descriptors, base class [verified 2026-10-22, VM]

4 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/field_desc.cpp`): constructor `0x418eb0`, copy constructor `0x418e10`, destructor `0x418f60` and the deleting destructor `0x418dc0`.

- Layout (0x28 bytes, vtable `0x5eccb0`, 24 slots, abstract; the subclasses' vtables have at least 34, see "Field kinds"):

  | Offset | Field |
  |---|---|
  | +0x04 | name without the group prefix |
  | +0x08 | help text (`0x419020`) |
  | +0x0c | group: the part of the name before the first `/` |
  | +0x10 | offset of the value in the object |
  | +0x14, +0x18 | unknown (constructor arguments 4 and 5) |
  | +0x1c | alternative (old) name (`0x419030`) |
  | +0x20 | units for the editor, e.g. "Seconds", "Degrees", "Units/Sec" (`0x419060`, constructor argument 2) |
  | +0x24 | flag set when the descriptor is passed on to subclasses through an extra list (`0x419040`); the constructor leaves it uninitialised |

- The extra lists of the class infos therefore hold field descriptors as well.
- Clones (vtable slot 1): 6 registered fields return no clone (`0x4011e0` returns 0). 3 clone through the parent's copy constructor and so get the parent's vtable (for example `0x53f240` for `CLandscapeAI`). Both are quirks of the original.

### Pointer arrays [verified 2026-10-22, VM]

88 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/ptr_array.cpp`, `ptr_array.h`): `RemoveAll` `0x402c90`, `AddPool` `0x5c1f00`, `AddHeap` `0x564f20`, `RemoveAt` `0x586fc0` and 84 deleting destructors (`reimpl/src/ptr_array_dtors.inc`).

- The pointer array is a template `{vtable, data, count, capacity}` (16 bytes). Every instantiation has its own vtable with three slots: 0 deleting destructor, 1 `RemoveAll` (`0x402c90`, `count = 0`, shared through identical code folding with every other slot that clears +8), 2 `Add` (element passed by reference).
- Two flavours, which differ only in where the data lives: 95 vtables take the data from the pool allocator with size capacity × 4 (`Add` `0x5c1f00`). 27 take it from `operator new` (`Add` `0x564f20`). A few heap instances hold other elements and have their own `Add` in slot 2 (e.g. `0x4a3840`, 16-byte elements), but they use the same destructor.
- `Add` returns the index of the new element (the old count, `return m_count++`), and callers use it. A first version without a return value passed every check on the array itself, but in the game the camera of `Test/Nachbau1` stood about 50 pixels off. That was found by switching hooks off one by one (`Disable=`), so the checks now compare the return value too.
- `Add` grows only when count + 1 exceeds the capacity, to max(count + 1, capacity · 1.2f). The capacity is loaded with `fild qword` (zero-extended), multiplied by the float at `0x5ea5f4` and truncated with `__ftol`; the comparison is unsigned. The pool flavour copies with `memmove` and returns the old block with its old size. The heap flavour copies element by element.
- `RemoveAt` is not virtual (18 callers). An index beyond the end does nothing; the rest moves down.
- The 84 deleting destructors (46 pool, 38 heap) are byte-identical copies except for the vtable they write and the relative call targets. They were found by a byte pattern over `.text`, and the call targets were checked (`pool_get`/`pool_free`/`operator delete`, resp. `operator delete` twice). Several destructors write the vtable of a neighbouring, identical vtable (e.g. `0x402ca0` sits in `0x5ea5dc` and `0x5ea5e8` and writes `0x5ea5e8`). The reimplementation therefore writes the constant from the code, not the vtable the destructor was called through.
- Hooks: 171, `MAX_HOOKS` raised to 256 (1024 since the module split).

Check in the VM (run `20261022-190148`, in the game thread):
- `Add`, `RemoveAll`, `RemoveAt` in both flavours on arrays with 18 capacities from 0 to 4097 and 4 fill levels (full, so `Add` grows; one free slot; half; empty), `RemoveAt` with indices inside and beyond the end. Plus 3,000 `Add`s in a row from an empty array (the capacity sequence of the growth rule). All 84 destructors with flags 0 on 4 capacities (vtable, data, count, capacity, return value) and with flags 1. Every case runs once through the original and once through the reimplementation. Compared are vtable, count, capacity, a hash of the contents and whether the data block moved. 1,022 cases, all identical. The other checks and the class table are unchanged and identical.
- Screenshot after 25 s without checks (run `20261022-190310`): pixel-identical with `/Original`.

Assigned along the way (`docs/exe_symbols.csv`; the range `0x4e1fb0`–`0x4e2240` behind `ZString`):

- **File spec** (0x2c bytes, on the callers' stack; constructor `0x4a09f0`, 22 callers; no destructor of its own, the callers destroy the 5 `ZString`s): +0x00 mode (subfolders: 0 all, 1 all but those starting with `-` (default), other values none), +0x04 1 = list folders instead of files, +0x08 names only (disk: nonzero, archives: exactly 1), +0x0c folder, +0x10 prefix the names start with, +0x14 number of extensions, +0x18 5 extensions without the dot. `Set(folder, ext)` (`0x4a0a60`) leaves +0 and +8 alone; `SetFolders(folder, dashed)` (`0x4a0aa0`) sets +4 = 1, prefix `-` or `""` and an empty extension; `AddExtension` (`0x4a0a30`, so far named `Files_FindByExtension`, which was wrong) appends up to 5 and returns the assigned `ZString` (the count when full). `0x4a09d0` sets the dwords of the constructor without the strings and returns 0.
- **Sinks** (slot 0 count, 1 `Add(name, {size, DOS date, DOS time})`, 2 `Contains(name)`): `AddIfNew` (`0x49d3a0`) adds only names the sink does not hold, so a file on disk hides the same file in an archive. The directory lists (`0x5f418c`), a counter (`0x5f40c8`; its `Contains` returns false, so `Files_Count` `0x4a12d0` counts a file on disk and in an archive twice) and a buffer of fixed-size names (`0x5f3cb0`, `Files_ListNames` `0x4a1150`: stride, at most max names, the sizes into a parallel buffer; a name longer than stride − 1 ends the game with "Illegal file name").
- **`Files_Search`** (`0x4a1190`, fastcall sink/spec, flags on the stack): unless flags bit 0x20, the folder becomes `./folder` and the 2 characters `./` are cut off the paths again. Then the disk search, then, if an archive is mounted (`0x6bdf64`), the archive search with the original spec. Returns the sink's count.
- **Disk search** (`0x4a4840`, recursive): the folder of the spec is cut after its last `/` or `\` (a folder without a final separator therefore gives paths relative to its parent). For each extension `FindFirstFileA(folder/prefix*.ext)` (empty extension: `*`); only files, or only folders with +4 = 1; names starting with `.` are skipped. With `folder_ext` (only from callers of our own so far; `Files_Search` passes 0) a folder counts only if a counter search finds a file with that extension in it. A name containing `~` ends the game (message box, `exit(-1)`). `strip_ext == 1` drops the extension. Paths are built in the static buffer `0x6be0a4`; with +8 = 0 the path below the search folder, otherwise the name. The date and time come from `FileTimeToDosDateTime`. Then, in modes 0 and 1, every subfolder from the pattern `*.` recursively (mode 1 skips `-` folders, a search for `*.ZIP` files skips `cache`). `FindClose` is also called with `INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE`. Returns the result of the last `FindClose`, or the mode when there is no recursion.
- **Archive folders**: the mounted archives are a pool pointer array of root nodes (`0x714570`, function-local static, getter `0x5c1650`, atexit `0x5c16a0`). A node: +0 parent, +4 name, +8 children (pool pointer array), +0x18 the archive directory. The search (`0x5c1da0`) goes from the last mounted root to the first: the deepest node along the folder path that has an archive (`0x5c1890`), else the node reached (`0x5c17b0`), lists its children recursively (`0x5c13c0`; folders by prefix with `strnicmp`, as name or as path) and then the files of its archive with `Zip_ListDir` (`0x5c2970`, not yet reimplemented). In the path lookup only components followed by `/` are searched; a final component without `/` is compared with the length of the one before (at first 0, so not searched). `0x5c1890` builds the full path of its result and drops it.
- In the VM one archive is mounted: a root with an empty name, an archive and no child nodes, so all folder matching happens in `Zip_ListDir`.
- Hooks: 273.

Check in the VM (run `20261022-203803-8ee7`, in the game thread):
- File spec, 152 cases: constructor and `Init` on prefilled objects, `Set` with 6 extensions (with dot, empty, long) on 3 folders followed by up to 7 `AddExtension`s, `Extension`, `Mode`, `SetFolders` with the dashed byte 0 and 2, `SetFolder`, `SetMode`. Compared are the dwords, the texts, capacities and reference counts of the extensions and the return values.
- Sinks, 44 cases: `AddIfNew` on a recording sink and on the counter, the name buffer with and without names and values, full, two strides, a name longer than the limit (message box and exit redirected).
- Disk search, 584 cases: a test tree in the temp folder (19 files in 8 folders incl. `-` folders, `cache`, `.` names, `*.zip`, names without extension) searched with flags 0x20 for 6 extension sets, modes 0–2, folders/names only, the dashed prefix, through `Files_Search`, `Files_Count`, `Files_ListNames` and directly with `strip_ext` 0/1/2, `folder_ext` and `skip`; 14 real game folders below `.` (also through the archive); the tilde error (message box and exit redirected). Compared are every name with its record in order, the counts, `Contains` calls, return values and the path buffer. 1,415 files in the searches into the recording sink.

### Field kinds [verified 2026-10-22, VM]

101 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/field_kinds.cpp`, `field_kinds.h`, list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the 37 constructors of the 28 field kinds (subclasses of `CFieldDesc`), 3 copy constructors, 25 clones (vtable slot 1), 8 destructors, and 28 value functions of the slots that only move memory (4 `CopyValue`, 6 `InitValue`, 8 `FreeValue`, 10 `SetDefault`).

- **Vtable slots** of every kind (the kinds' vtables have at least 34 slots, more than the 24 counted for the base): 0 deleting destructor, 1 clone (`operator new` + copy), 2 "plain value" (`0x401260` true, `0x401200` false), 4 `CopyValue(dst object, src object, src descriptor)`, 6 `InitValue(object)`, 8 `FreeValue(object)`, 10 `SetDefault(object)`, 13 visit the objects the field holds (slot 18 of the objects) and 20 "has a value to write" (both corrected in "Fields written as text, object visit"; earlier assumed to be binary streams), 16 value as text (`ZString *out`), 19 value from text, 23 write as text (`0x418fe0`), 33 element size (`0x418d70` for object fields; called by `0x419110`).
- **Constructor arguments**: name, [units,] offset, size (+0x14), a second offset that is not used, flags (+0x18), then the kind's own. `0x547fd0` and `0x58b840` take one resp. two unused arguments more.

- **Setters** are member functions of the object (thiscall) that the value functions call instead of writing; colours and points get a pointer to the value.
- **Converters** of the number kinds are function-local statics `{vtable}` with guard bit 0 (int `0x712204`/`0x712214`/`0x71220c`, enum int `0x712218`/`0x7121fc`, float `0x7160ac`/`0x7160b4`, double `0x7160a4`), built by the first constructor and set to another vtable at exit.
- **Name lists** (+0x40/+0x50): `{vtable, pool pointer array}` of entries `{name copy (0x587c20), value}`, built by `FieldDesc_AddEnum` `0x54da60`. The clones copy them deeply (int `0x54d8a0`, float `0x54e890`, double `0x54ea30` with 12-byte entries).
- **Quirks of the original**, kept: the clone of the object kind does not copy +0x28 (`0x418740`), the image clone copies only the base part (`0x4b5970`), the polygon clone clears +0x28 (`0x548010`), the elevation kind clones through the enum int copy constructor and so gets its vtable (`0x53f240`), `0x5fd8b0` has no clone (`_purecall`), `0x601c30` returns none (`0x4011e0`). Colour copies skip bytes 7 and 0xb. Equal limits mean "no limits" (enum int: 0/-1, with units 0/-2).
- **Return values** of the value functions are what the original leaves in `eax` (the offset, object + offset, the object, the setter's result, the copied length + 1). When an old C string is deleted without a new one, `eax` comes from `operator delete` (1 in the VM); the reimplementation returns that value too. A first run that returned 0 there was the only difference the checks found.
- Hooks: 351.

### Zip archives [verified 2026-10-22, VM]

22 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/zip_archive.cpp`, `zip_archive.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the directory of one archive, the folder tree of the mounted archives and mounting at start. Not in this batch: opening a file of an archive (`0x5c2e50`, called by `ZipList_Open`), `0x5c2080` (moves an entry to the end of the archive, only called from there) and `0x5c2dd0`. The chat window `0x5c1040`–`0x5c1120` in the same address range is a class of its own.

- **Directory** (`ZZipDir`, 0x2c bytes, operator new; constructor `0x5c2040`): +0 loaded, +2 keep the file open, +4 file buffer (0x1c bytes from the pool, constructor `0x4a1780`), +8 archive path and +0xc mount folder (operator new copies, `0x587c20`), +0x10 entries (operator new with the count in front), +0x14 entry indexes sorted by name, +0x18 count, +0x20 open flags, +0x24 end signature, +0x28 check_disk. +1 and +0x1c are only cleared.
  - An entry (0x30 bytes): +0 name = mount folder + name in the archive, +4 the central directory header without its signature (0x2a bytes: DOS time +0xc, date +0xe, size +0x18, local header offset +0x2a), +0x2f the result of the last `AddIfNew` in `Zip_ListDir`.
  - `Init` (`0x5c2710`): closes, copies the paths (a mount folder starting with `/` becomes empty), and with lazy = 0 sets keep_open and loads at once; otherwise the directory is read on first use and the file closed again.
  - `Load` (`0x5c2240`): opens with the flags | 0x404, reads the end record 0x16 bytes before the end (signature `PK\5\6` or `RE\5\6` of Data.dat), so an archive comment makes it fail. Without an end record (or with offset -1) it walks local headers from the current position; in practice that path only fails. The entries are read from the central directory offset + 4 (the first signature is not checked) until the end record or the count. A compressed entry ends the game ("Compressed Zip File Found"). With more than one entry it sorts the entries by offset (`0x5c2220`) and an index by name (`0x5c21e0`, stricmp, entries in `0x714584`); with one entry the index stays uninitialised.
  - `Find` (`0x5c2d50`): binary search over the index; the position out is the lower bound. `Exists` (`0x5c2830`): the folder of the path must start with the mount folder; the out byte is `File_Exists` of the archive itself with check_disk, else 0.
  - `Zip_ListDir` (`0x5c2970`): per extension the run of names below the search folder, starting at the lower bound of the folder. Files: the name must end with the extension (no dot check), mode 1 skips paths with a folder starting with `-` after the search folder, mode 2 has no effect on files (subfolders are listed as well); names_only 1 lists the name after the last separator. Folders (+4 = 1): every folder on the way to the file whose name starts with the prefix, as name or as path; mode 2 only the first level. Returns the number of extensions.
  - `Exists` and `Zip_ListDir` load a lazy directory first; if that fails, the error message is formatted with the archive path that `Close` has already cleared (null). The check run hung there with the original as well, so the checks leave that case out.
- **Tree** (`ZZipNode`, `ZZipList` in `file_search.h`): `Mount` (`0x5c1a30`; archive, new_root, check_disk, mount, lazy, flags) finds or appends a node per `/`-terminated folder of the mount path (empty components stay at the node; a last component without `/` reads through a null pointer) and gives the last node a new directory. On failure the directory goes away again, nodes appended on the way stay, a new root is deleted. `Open` (`0x5c1c70`) and `Exists` (`0x5c1d00`) go from the last root to the first to the deepest node with a directory along the folder of the path; `Exists` returns the answer of the first directory found. The children arrays have the vtable `0x6060b8` and get `0x6060c4` when destroyed. The destructors (`0x5c1260`, `0x5c1e20`, `0x5c1570` = unmount, `0x5c16a0` = atexit) delete from the last node; `0x5c11c0` reserves capacity in pool pointer arrays (also used by two other arrays).
- **Mounting at start** (`Zip_MountAll` `0x4a0c40`, fastcall name, mode, skip_zips; called with `"Data"`, 0, 0): mounting twice ends the game. Mode 0 mounts the exe itself (fails), else `Data.ZIP`, else `Data.DAT`, then every `./*.RED` (sorted with stricmp), each as a new root at `/`, read at once. Then the data folder `0x6135ec` becomes the name. Unless skip_zips, every `*.zip` below `.` (all subfolders, not `cache`) is mounted lazily with check_disk: the first as a new root, the rest into the last root, at its path without `.zip` plus `/`. `Zip_UnmountAll` (`0x4a1120`) deletes all roots. `0x4a1140` returns `"Cache"`.
- Hooks: 295.

Check in the VM (run `20261022-224522-fa4b`, in the game thread):
- Directory, 20,557 cases on 18 test archives in the temp folder (stored zips with mount folders, the `RE\5\6` signature, a comment, offset -1, fewer entries in the end record, a compressed entry, garbage, tiny and empty files, an empty and a single-entry archive, archives in subfolders): constructor, `Init` lazy and at once, `Load` with and without keep_open (incl. the compression exit), `Close` twice, both comparisons over all pairs, `Find` with 40 names, `Exists` with and without check_disk, `Zip_ListDir` with 13 folders × 5 extension sets × modes 0–2 × files/folders × names_only 0–2 × 4 prefixes on 6 loaded directories (17,094 names into a recording sink), and on lazy directories. Compared are the whole directory (entries, headers, index, file position), return values, sink records and the +0x2f bytes.
- Tree, 522 cases: 11 mounts step by step (new roots, nested and empty folders, missing and unreadable archives), `Open` with 0x5c2e50 redirected, `Exists`, `AddChild`, `DeleteNodes`, the destructor, `Clear`, `AtExit` on the swapped global list, `Reserve`/`Free` with 14 capacities.
- Mounting, 13 cases: `Zip_MountAll` with the global list, the flag and the data folder swapped out (modes 0–2, skip_zips, an unknown name, already mounted → exit) and the zip search redirected to the test archives; both unmounts twice each. The real Data.DAT is mounted in mode 0.
- Everything identical, the other checks unchanged and identical.
- Screenshot after 25 s without checks: the reimplementation run `20261023-001556-53e3` is pixel-identical with the `/Original` run `20261022-222129-d603`; against the `/Original` run `20261023-001558-e3d1` it differs only in the known Korbo region (1304–1498, 659–870).
- The VM ran very slowly during these runs (steps took minutes); the checks themselves take under a second.

### Field values as text [verified 2026-10-22, VM]

19 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/field_text.cpp`, `field_text.h`, list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): slot 16 `ToText(object, ZString *out)` and slot 19 `FromText(object, text, unused)` of the int, enum int, byte, bit, float, double, float point, integer point and colour kinds, and `FieldColor_SetRGBA` `0x53f080`, which the colour's `FromText` calls.

| Kind | `ToText` | `FromText` |
|---|---|---|
| int (`0x5fd440`, `0x5fd66c`; also slot 16 of the list and object array kinds: the count) | `0x417c40` `%d` | `0x54d690` `atoi`, clamped signed to [min, max] unless min == max; setter +0x38 |
| enum int (`0x5fd518`, elevation `0x5fcc34`) | `0x54db10` name of the value, else `%u` | `0x54db70` `atoi`; unless min == max: a value with a name stays, else a name gives its value, else clamped unsigned; setter +0x3c |
| byte (`0x5fd738`) | `0x54df00` `%u` | `0x54df30` `atoi != 0`; setter +0x28 |
| bit (`0x5fd7f4`) | `0x54e0f0` "1"/"0" by the mask | `0x54e130` `atoi != 0` sets or clears the mask; setter +0x30 |
| float (`0x5fdb68`) | `0x54ee60` name, else `%g` | `0x54ef30` `atof` (`0x5d03de`) rounded to float, then like the enum int with x87 compares; setter +0x38 |
| double (`0x5fdca4`) | `0x54f130` name, else `%g` | `0x54f220` like the float with doubles; setter +0x48 |
| float point (`0x5f46fc`) | `0x4a8110` `%f,%f` | `0x4a8140` `sscanf` (`0x5d1539`) `%f,%f`, no setter |
| integer point (`0x5fd1d0`) | `0x5455a0` `%d,%d` | `0x5455d0` `sscanf` `%d,%d`, no setter |
| colour (`0x5efe30`) | `0x46dee0` `%d,%d,%d` of the bytes +6, +5, +4 (red, green, blue) | `0x46df60` `sscanf` `%d,%d,%d`, then `FieldColor_SetRGBA(r, g, b, 0xff)`, no setter |

- **Colour layout** (from `0x53f080`): bytes blue, green, red, alpha at +0, blue, green, red again at +4, the 16-bit pixel of `0x433a10` (fastcall r, g, b; a table when `0x630578` is set, else 5-6-5) at +8, flag 2 in the dword at +0xc. The arguments are dwords; `0x433a10` indexes its tables with them unclipped.
- **Name lists**: slot 27 of the list finds the entry with a value (int `0x592320`, float `0x54f3c0`, double `0x54f550` with the value as two dwords; [confirmed: code `0x592320`, `0x54f3c0`, `0x54f550`, reimpl/src/field_text2.cpp; VM]), slot 1 gives its name, slot 2 `Find(name, -1)`. The original calls slot 27 and `Find` twice each when they succeed; the reimplementation too. Equal limits mean no limits: `FromText` then takes the number as it is and does not look at the names either. For the float kinds "equal" is the x87 `fcomp` result, so a NaN limit also counts as no limits.
- **Return values** (what the original leaves in `eax`): `FromText` returns the setter's result, or without a setter the value (int), 0 (enum int), the object (byte, float, points), object + offset (bit), the offset (double) or the colour's new flags. `ToText` returns nothing (`eax` from `ZString` `Format`/`SetText`).
- **Quirks of the original**, kept:
  - The byte's `FromText` writes the result into the low byte of the text argument's stack slot and passes the whole slot to the setter, so the setter's argument carries the upper three bytes of the text pointer.
  - The float and double setters are expected to return a float: `fstp st(0)` after the call pops it (with a setter that returns none, an FPU stack underflow, masked in the game).
  - The points' `FromText` let `sscanf` write into stack slots: a missing x keeps the bits of the text pointer, a missing y those of the descriptor pointer. Both ignore the setter the constructors store.
  - The colour's `FromText` reads red and green into uninitialised locals: a text without them leaves stack garbage in the colour. The reimplementation started them at 0 until 2026-11-12; since then it reads them from the exe's two slots in the exe's frame (section 16, "Batch decomp-faithful2"); a missing blue keeps the text pointer as in the original.
  - Floating-point values go through the FPU as in the original (`fld`/`fstp` quiets a signalling NaN, `fcomp` signals on quiet NaNs; `atof`'s `st(0)` is stored without another rounding); the reimplementation does these steps with inline assembly and keeps the values as raw bits in between.
- Hooks: 393 (19 new).
