### File buffer and archive streams [verified 2026-10-23, VM]

69 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/file_buffer.cpp`, `file_buffer.h`, `reimpl/src/zip_stream.cpp`, `zip_stream.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the file buffer `CFileBuf` and the file functions built on it, opening a file of a mounted archive, the archive stream, writing into an entry and the writer that appends a file to an archive. Not in this batch: `File_Open` `0x4a2440` and the disk stream behind it (`0x4a23a0`–`0x4a2bf0`, vtable `0x5f40dc`), the memory stream (`0x505e40`, vtable `0x5f9dfc`), the CRC of a stream `0x4a26c0`, the disk test `0x4a3d70` and the folder function `0x4a4000`; the reimplementation calls them in the exe.

- **`CFileBuf`** (the exe's own name, from the prefix `"~CFileBuf 0x"` `0x6136ec`; 0x1c bytes, vtable `0x5f40d4` with 2 slots: deleting destructor `0x4a17a0`, `Close` `0x4a2100`): +4 stream, +8 indent level, +0xc open flags, +0x10 number of reads below 2,000 bytes (statistics, never read), +0x14 sum of `Advance`, +0x18 a byte that is only set (`0x4a2140`) and cleared by `Open`. The exe counts the open buffers (`0x6bdf60`) and their maximum (`0x6bdf50`, signed). Every method calls the stream through its vtable and checks for a null stream (except `Advance` `0x4a2150`).
- **Streams** (base 0xc bytes: +4 the `FILE *` of the disk stream, +8 "owned", set by `File_Open`): slot 0 deleting destructor, 2 `Write(p, n)`, 3 `Read(p, n)`, 4 relative seek, 5 seek, 6 tell, 7 size, 8 set size, 9 close, 11 `Advance(n)` (memory streams: pointer to the position, then + n), 12 detach the memory, 13 read a line.
- **`FileBuf_Open`** (`0x4a1840`): a path `"~CFileBuf 0x"` + at least 8 hex digits takes over the stream at that address (bytes in memory order, `0x587ff0`); flag 0x200 reads the whole file into a memory stream (`0x505e40`, without the flag); otherwise paths starting with `\`, `/` or a drive letter get 0xa0 (0x20: no archives) and `File_Open` makes the stream. `Close` (slot 1, virtual) runs before the new stream is set; an empty path returns false without it.
- **Text output**: `WriteLine` (`0x4a1a40`) writes the text, `"\r\n"` and one tab per level and returns the level; `Indent` writes a tab at once, `Unindent` goes back one byte (relative seek −1). Counted texts: a length dword, then the bytes (`0x4a2220`, `0x4a2010` into an `operator new` block, `0x4a2300` into a buffer; a length beyond the rest sets `errno` to `ERANGE` and leaves the buffer alone).
- **`Move`** (`0x4a1b30`): n bytes from a higher to a lower offset in chunks of up to 64 KB (used by the archives); `CopyTo` (`0x4a1c40`, chunks of 512 KB, progress as stdcall `float` 0, the share before every chunk and 1; reads and writes are not checked); `Equals` (`0x4a1d60`).
- **File functions** (fastcall): `File_ReadExact` (`0x4a1300`, true only if the file has exactly n bytes and all were read), `File_WriteAll` (`0x4a13f0`, true if opened with flags 3; the write is not checked), `File_Delete` (`0x4a14e0`, below the data folder or with 0x20 as it is; al = deleted, the rest of `eax` from the runtime's −1), `File_BackupData` (`0x4a1540`, renames to `.BAK`, see below), `File_CanOpen` (`0x4a1570`, flags 0x84 plus 0x20), `File_Exists` (`0x4a1650`), `File_UniqueName` (`0x4a16e0`, `sprintf(pattern, i)` until `FindFirstFileA` finds nothing; the result relative to the data folder again; returns −1 with 0x20, else the length + 1), `File_Copy` (`0x4a1ea0`, src flags | 4, dst flags | 3).
- **`File_Exists` quirk**: if a mounted archive knows the path, the answer is the byte `ZZipList::Exists` returns, i.e. with check_disk whether the archive file exists, otherwise 0. A file that is only in Data.dat therefore does not "exist"; only the disk counts for it.
- **Opening a file of an archive** (`ZZipDir::OpenFile` `0x5c2e50`, mode = the open flags): the folder of the path must start with the mount folder; mode 0x8000 (`File_Open` for reads, first pass) only takes entries the last listing marked (+0x2f). A stream (`ZZipStream`, 0x24 bytes from the pool, vtable `0x6060d0`): +0xc own file buffer ((mode >> 4) & 1), +0x10 position in the archive, +0x14 entry, +0x18 file buffer, +0x1c directory, +0x20 mode. The data starts at offset + 0x1e + name length + the extra length of the central directory. Without an own buffer the archive's buffer (`ZZipDir` +4) is opened if needed, `ZZipDir` +0x1c counts the open streams and the entry's +0x2e marks it as open. Reads stop at the end of the entry; `Skip` must land inside the data (the end itself is not allowed), `Seek` takes 0 to the size (signed).
- **Writing into an entry** (mode 1, only with check_disk, i.e. the lazily mounted *.zip below `.`, and only without an open stream; `File_Open` with flags 3): the archive is opened with flags | 6, the entry is moved to the end (`0x5c2080`: everything behind it moves down with `CFileBuf::Move`, the offsets follow, the entry gets the offset behind the last one, both sorts again), its sizes, CRC, method and extra length are cleared, date and time are now (`0x4a3c80`) and the local header is written (`0x5c30d0`; the two sizes in swapped order, equal for stored files). `ZZipDir` +1 marks the central directory as changed. Writing past the size makes both sizes the position. `Close` (`0x5c3440`) with mode 2 computes the CRC of the stream (`0x4a26c0`) and writes the local header again; when the last stream closes, the central directory goes behind the last entry, then the end record with the archive's signature (`0x5c2dd0`, the file ends there), and the archive is closed. CRC-32: `0x5c31b0` (table `0x627814`), `0x5c31a0` = not.
- **Writer** (`ZZipWriter`, 0x148 bytes, vtable `0x606108`; `File_Open` with flags 3 and a path `archive;name`, `0x5c3660`): +0xc its `CFileBuf` (opened with 0x26), +0x28 the name, +0x128 the old central directory, +0x12c the end record, +0x140 the new local header, +0x144 the data. `Open` (`0x5c38d0`) needs the end record 0x16 bytes before the end (`PK\5\6` or `RE\5\6`), keeps the central directory in memory and writes a local header (version 10, the rest 0) where it started; the slots work relative to the data. `Close` (`0x5c3700`) writes the local header with the size again (no CRC, date or time), the old directory behind the data, a central header (version made 0x2a, needed 10) and the end record with one entry more and always `RE\5\6`.
- Quirks kept: the original's signature buffer of the writer is the slot of the name argument (if the read fails, the comparison sees the name's address).
- Hooks: 465.

Check in the VM (run `20261023-070528-8a57`, in the game thread, `reimpl/src/checks_file_buffer.cpp`, `checks_zip_stream.cpp`):
- `CFileBuf` on recording streams of our own, 594 cases: every method with data, short reads and writes and null streams (constructor, `Close` and the destructors also on a pool block, `Attach`, all writes and `WriteLine` with indent 0–3, reads of 0 to 6,000 bytes around 2,000, seeks/skips/tell/size/set size/read line at the boundaries, `Advance`, `Detach`, the counted texts with lengths beyond the rest, `Move` with chunks over 64 KB and failing reads, `CopyTo` up to 1.1 MB with and without progress, `Equals` with a different byte at 0, 65,535, 65,536 and the end, `FileBuf_Open` with `"~CFileBuf 0x"`). ### Disk and memory streams, File_Open, path helpers [verified 2026-10-23, VM]

51 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/disk_stream.cpp`, `disk_stream.h`, `reimpl/src/memory_stream.cpp`, `memory_stream.h`, `reimpl/src/path_util.cpp`, `path_util.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): `File_Open`, the disk stream, the line reader, the CRC of a stream, the `"~CFileBuf 0x"` paths, the memory stream with `File_OpenInMemory`, and the path and disk helpers `0x4a3c80`–`0x4a45f0`. The slots shared with other classes stay in the exe (`0x401200`, `0x401260`, `0x52dc80`, `0x46b760`, `0x483750`, `0x4ef8f0`).

- **`File_Open`** (`0x4a2440`, fastcall path, flags): flags 3 with a `;` in the path make a `ZZipWriter` (`"archive;name"`); otherwise flags 3 ask the mounted archives first (unless 0x20), then the disk (unless 0x40); flags 2 alone only the disk; flag 4 the archives with 0x8000 (entries of the last listing), the disk, then the archives with the flags as they are; neither 2 nor 4 gives null. Every stream it returns gets +8 = 1 ("owned", also on archive streams). A disk stream that cannot be opened is deleted again.
- **Disk stream** (0xc bytes from the pool, vtable `0x5f40dc`, base constructor `0x4a23a0` and destructor `0x4a2410` shared with the archive streams): `Open` (`0x4a2760`) with flags 3 opens `"wb"` below the data folder (0x20: the path as it is); if that fails, `File_Found` does not find the path and flag 0x100 is set, `ZString::SplitPathText` and `Folder_CreatePath` create the folder and `"wb"` is tried again. Without both bits 1 and 2 it is `"r+b"` (2) or `"rb"`, first below the data folder (unless 0x20), then the path as it is; for writing there is no second try, so an absolute path needs 0x20. The result is al = opened with the upper bytes of the `FILE *`. The slots use `fwrite`, `fread`, `fseek` (`Skip`/`Seek` 1 if it returned 0), `ftell` (−1 without a file), `Size` (ftell, seek to the end, ftell, seek back) and `SetSize` = `_chsize(_fileno(f), n)` (also slot 8 of the memory stream, which has no file: 0). `Close` and the destructor return `fclose`'s result, the handle itself if it is not owned, 0 without one.
- **Line reader** (`0x4a2ad0`, slot 13 of the disk stream, through the stream's own `Tell`/`Read`/`Seek`): reads n − 1 bytes, ends the line at the first CR or LF and seeks behind the line end. CRLF and LFCR count as one line end, CRCR and LFLF as two; a CR or LF followed by CRLF or LFLF is one line end of three bytes (so `"\r\n\n"` swallows an empty line). Without a line end in the bytes read it seeks back to the start and returns al = 0 (a line longer than n − 1 is never returned); the upper bytes are those of `Seek`'s result.
- **`Stream_Crc`** (`0x4a26c0`): CRC-32 from the start in reads of up to 64 KB whose results are not checked (start value from `0x592380` = −1). **`"~CFileBuf 0x"` paths**: `0x4a29d0` builds `"~CFileBuf 0x" + 8 hex digits of the stream pointer in memory order + "/" + name` (used by the temp files, `0x57b5a7`), `0x4a2a10` parses one, `0x4a2a70` deletes its stream (eax left over from the last call).
- **Memory stream** (0x20 bytes, vtable `0x5f9dfc`): +0xc position, +0x10 size, +0x14 capacity, +0x18 data (`operator new`), +0x1c owns. `File_OpenInMemory` (`0x505e40`) reads the whole file through a `CFileBuf` (flags as for `FileBuf_Open`); the constructors (`0x505f00` empty, `0x505fb0` takes over a block) call `Close` through the vtable's memory. `Reserve` (`0x506250`) grows to the larger of n, 1.5 times and 4 more than the capacity, but only if the buffer is owned or missing. `Write` grows the size to the end of the write, `Read` stops at the size, `Skip`/`Seek` return 1 with the argument's upper bytes, `Advance`, `Detach` (hands the data over, then `Close`), `Reset` (`0x5061e0`: `Close`, `Reserve(n)`), `Equals` (`0x5062d0`, same size and bytes).
- **Memory line reader** (`0x506140`): only CR ends a line (then one CR and one LF are skipped), so text with bare LF line ends comes back as one line if it fits; a line that does not fit into n − 1 bytes returns false without moving; the result is `this` with al = success.
- **Path and disk helpers** (fastcall): `Path_Join` (`0x4a4220`; returns the length of the name + 1, or 0 for an empty folder), `Path_JoinExt` (`0x4a42c0`), `Path_Join3` (`0x4a4380`), `Path_Append` (`0x4a4470`, `/`) and `Path_AppendBackslash` (`0x4a44f0`, `\`), `PathName` (`0x4a4570`), `Path_CutName` (`0x4a45b0`), `Path_Extension`/`Path_SetExtension` (`0x4a3f80`, `0x4a3fb0`; the last `.` anywhere, also in a folder name), `ConfigPath` (`0x4a45f0`, `".\Config.INI"`), `DosTime_Now` (`0x4a3c80`), `File_Found` (`0x4a3cb0`, FindFirstFileA), `File_FindUnusedName` (`0x4a3ce0`), `File_TempName` (`0x4a3d30`, GetTempFileNameA in the temp folder), `Folder_CreatePath` (`0x4a3ec0`: on failure it cuts at the last `\`, only without one at the last `/`, until a folder can be created, then starts again from the full path; with mixed separators it can therefore give up early).
- **The disk test** `File_DiskTest` (`0x4a3d70`, used by `File_Exists`): true for a file that is not read-only; if `GetFileAttributesA` fails, true when the folder of the path has any entry (`"*.*"` finds `.` in every existing folder), i.e. a missing file in an existing folder counts as existing. Read-only files count as missing.

28 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/field_slots.cpp`, `field_slots.h`, list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the remaining value slots 4 `CopyValue`, 6 `InitValue`, 8 `FreeValue` and 10 `SetDefault` of the `ZString`, flags, new[] array, pointer array, owned object, dynamic properties and polygon kinds, and the helpers they call. | Kind | Slots | Helpers |
|---|---|---|
| `ZString` (`0x5ec91c`) | 4 `0x415e70` (a copy of the source through `0x4161d0`), 6 `0x415fd0` `InitEmpty`, 8 `0x416000` `Empty`, 10 `0x416030` `Assign` of the default +0x2c; with +0x28 each also for the string at +4, resp. `0x5007c0` after storing | `0x4161d0` `StringField_Set(object, ZString)` (setter +0x30, else `Assign`; with +0x28 then `0x5007c0`), `0x5007c0` `StringField_Localize`, `0x500f50` `Local_Translate` |
| flags (`0x5ec684`) | 10 `0x414de0` | |
| new[] array (`0x5eca78`) | 4 `0x417a80`, 10 `0x417b70` | `0x4181f0` `ListField_Resize(object, count, at)` |
| pointer array (`0x5ecd6c`) | 4 `0x4192a0`, 8 `0x419320`, 10 `0x4193f0` | `0x419a10` `ObjectArrayField_Resize(object, count, at, exact)` |
| owned object (`0x5ecbf4`) | 4 `0x418840`, 10 `0x418890` | `0x416760` `Object_Clone(a, b)` |
| dynamic properties (`0x5f17ec`) | 4 `0x482f50`, 8 `0x4834c0`, 10 `0x482fd0` | the list (`0x5eca54`): `0x4828b0` destructor, `0x482c20` assign, `0x482e40` append, `0x482e10` init entry |
| polygon (`0x5fd2a0`) | 4 `0x548050`, 10 `0x548070` | `0x545e80` `Polygon_Assign` |

- **`0x5007c0` translates, it does not register** (correcting "Field values as text, second part"): it copies the string to the `ZString` behind it and passes that to `Local_Translate` `0x500f50` on the table of `Local.txt` (`0x6c2b90`, loaded by `0x500ac0`; +0x104 count, +0x108 capacity, +0x10c sorted entries `{ZString key, ZString translation}`). `Local_Translate(text, context)` does a binary search with `ZString::Compare`; a context appends `"[END]"` (`0x6190ac`) and `" (%s)"` (`0x6190b0`) to the key; a found key replaces the text. So the fields with +0x28 (the display option texts) keep the original text at the offset and the translated one at +4.
- **`ZString` setter**: `0x4161d0` calls the setter as `ZString f(ZString)` (hidden result pointer, 8 bytes popped; the result slot is an uninitialised local that holds the descriptor pointer); the object goes through `0x40b280` (`mov eax, ecx`). The only registered `ZString` setter, `0x58fc60` (field "Text" at 0x54), is `const ZString &f(const ZString &)` with `ret 4`: `CopyValue` on that field would assign from the descriptor pointer and corrupt the stack. The reimplementation calls the setter the same way; the checks use setters of the expected form.
- **Flags default** `0x414de0`: no default names: setter(0) or the low 16 bits cleared; `"$all"` (`_stricmp`, literal `0x60a6f4`): all bits up to the list's count (slot 22), setter or the low 16 bits replaced; other names go through slot 19 (`FromText`) while `g_LastFileOpened` (`0x713c14`) is set to the static text `0x62e658` (a copy of the `ZString` `0x62e660`, built on first use with guard bit 0 of `0x62e65c`, destructor `0x414f00` via `atexit`) and is restored afterwards.
- **new[] arrays** (`0x4181f0`): elements are objects (size +0x3c) of the class +0x38; a new array comes from slot 28 of the class (`capacity, 0, -1`), the old one is deleted with slot 1 (3) of its first element; elements move with slot 20 (copy from), new ones get slot 19. With a capacity field the capacity stays while the count fits, else it becomes twice the count; without one every change allocates. Quirks kept: shrinking in place copies the tail down and leaves the objects behind the count alive; growing in place calls slot 19 twice on every new element (once in the shift branch, once in the shared tail). `0x417a80` returns the count; `0x417b70` deletes the data, then resizes to the count (slot 22) of the default list +0x40 and otherwise returns the capacity offset.
- **Pointer arrays** (`0x419a10`): the elements go through the element descriptor +0x38: slots 6 and 10 for new ones, 8 for removed ones, 42 `move(dst, src)`, 33 element size, 38 `(capacity, 0, -1)` and 40 for the data unless +0x44 is set (then the pool with slot 33 × capacity). With a capacity field (+0x28) and `exact` (the low byte of the fourth argument) 0, the capacity stays unless the count exceeds it (twice the count) or drops below a sixteenth of a capacity above 20 (count + count / 16). `0x419320` frees the pool block with the size of the capacity field, i.e. 0 bytes for a pooled array without one (no registered field has that combination; the check leaves it out).
- **Owned objects**: `Object_Clone` `0x416760` = slot 27 `(a, b)` of the object's class info (slot 2), then slot 20 of the new object with the old one. `0x418890` creates the default with slot 27 `(0, -1)` and calls slot 19 without a null check.
- **Dynamic properties**: a pool block of 0x10 bytes `{vtable 0x5eca54, data, count, capacity}` of 8-byte entries `{descriptor, value}`; a value comes from slot 35 `(0, -1)` of its descriptor, is set up with slot 6 and released with slots 8 and 36. The destructor `0x4828b0` writes the base vtable `0x5eca60` and releases the data a second time if there still is any (the inlined base destructor). `0x482c20` (its first argument is not used) clears the list, then adds an entry per source entry unless one with that descriptor and a value exists, and copies the value with slot 4 of entry *i*: a source with a descriptor twice would read entries behind the count (not tested).
- **Polygons** (0x28 bytes): points (count × 8) and edges ((count − 1) × 12) from `operator new`, the other members copied; `0x548070` clears everything and assigns the default polygon +0x28 if there is one.
- **Return values** are what the original leaves in `eax`. Where that comes from a function without a result (the `ZString` functions, the pool), the reimplementation calls that function through its exe address and passes its `eax` on. The two resize functions return nothing. Without a list `0x482fd0` sets no `eax` (the reimplementation returns 0), and `0x482c20` with nothing to clear and an empty source returns the `eax` at entry (from `0x482f50`: the new list, which the reimplementation returns).
- Hooks: 529 on this branch (28 new).

Check in the VM (run `20261023-143005-47c7`, in the game thread, `reimpl/src/checks_field_slots.cpp`): every case runs twice, on side 0 through the original and on side 1 through the reimplementation, on objects of our own (0x4000 random bytes). Elements, element descriptors, objects, class infos and property descriptors are fakes whose slots record their calls (with arguments) in an event log and take memory from a per-side arena; pointers in logs, objects and return values are compared relative to the known blocks of their side (object, arena, pool blocks handed in, new pool blocks found afterwards), everything else byte for byte.

### Fields written as text, object visit [verified 2026-10-23, VM]

25 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/field_streams.cpp`, `field_streams.h`, list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): `Object_WriteText` (`0x4168f0`), slot 23 (write as text) of every kind except images and temp files, slot 20 of the dynamic properties, slot 13 of the five kinds that hold objects, the dynamic property list's visit and accessors, and the two visitors. The writer, the object table and the shared stubs stay in the exe.

- **Slots 13 and 20 are not binary streams** (correcting "Field kinds") [confirmed: disassembly]. Slot 20 `HasValue(object)` decides whether `Object_WriteText` writes a field: `0x46cd80` (`mov al, 1`) for every kind except the dynamic properties (`0x4831d0`: a list with entries). Slot 13 `VisitObjects(object, flag)` passes the objects a field holds to their slot 18, with a visitor on the stack if the flag byte is set, else null; kinds without objects have `0x4f0a80` (`ret 8`). What slot 18 does with the visitor is up to the object classes (428 of 442 classes with a vtable have the empty `0x401110`); the purpose of the visit is an [assumption: the developers' intent; the 14 non-empty slot 18 bodies not read for it] (checking or resolving object pointers). The binary write/read are slots 26 and 29 (found by the parallel batch "temp file and resource code").
- **Visitors**: `QueryVisitor` (vtable `0x5ec9e0`, `{vtable, &result}` with the result on the stack): slot 0 `0x417790` stores the object if its class derives from `CClassThatCanNotBeConstructedOrDerivedFrom` (class variable `0x62e698`, registered on first use by the inlined getter = slot 2 `0x417820`: 0x48 bytes from the pool, size 8, abstract), else null; slot 1 `0x417810` returns it. Used by `0x417bd0`, `0x54e750` and three object functions (`0x4164c0`, `0x416a00`, `0x416af0`). `ClassFilterVisitor` (vtable `0x5eca6c`, constructor `0x417720`, `{vtable, field, class}`): slot 0 `0x417740` stores the object into the field if its class derives from the visitor's class (a null class counts as a base of everything), else null; slot 1 `0x417780` the field; slot 2 `0x482de0` the class. `0x418920` builds one on the owned object's field with the class +0x2c of the descriptor.

Mode 0: `Object_WriteText` writes `"Referenced Object List Location=0x00420042"` once (`0x55c780`), registers every object it writes (`0x55cb30`) and writes `"Object ID=0x<address>"`; object references are collected (`0x55cad0`; its fast check against the last entry is dead code, `cmp edx, -1; jbe`) and the finish (`0x55cd90`, `0x55ce50`, also from the destructor) writes `"Referenced Objects"` and reports a referenced object that was not written as a `***Programming Error***`. Mode 1 writes neither; the game's change test `0x417100` writes two objects that way into memory streams and compares the bytes.
- **`Object_WriteText`**: the class name, `{`, indented: (mode 0) the object ID, then for every field with a non-empty name whose slot 20 is true `"Name="` (`sprintf` into a 1 KB buffer) followed by slot 23, then slot 9 of the object (its own lines, e.g. `"Tree List"`/`"Plasma Ground"` of a layer at `0x4e6a50`), `}`.
- **Slot 23 per kind**: plain kinds `0x418fe0` (slot 16 as one line); new[] array `0x417f10` (`Array`, `{`, `Array Count=%u`, per element `<name>=` + `Object_WriteText`, the name from slot 1 of the list +0x40 or `Array Item`, `}`); class pointer `0x4185f0` (the class name or an empty line); owned object `0x418c30`; pointer array `0x4196c0` (`Array`, `{`, `Item Count=%d` only without a name list, per element `<name>=` (the list or the element descriptor's name) + slot 23 of the element descriptor, `}`); dynamic properties `0x483200` (`0` without entries, else the count, `{`, `Name=` + slot 23 per entry, `}`); object reference `0x523f50` (`0x%08X (Class)` or an empty line, collected first); embedded object `0x54e7d0`; polygon `0x548210` (`%g, %g` per point, joined with `", "`, one line). Not here: image `0x4b5b20` (`CFrame(%d,%d,%d)` and pixel data) and temp file `0x58bd50` (reads the temp file into the text).
- **Return values** are the original's eax (mostly that of the last `CFileBuf` call or of the `ZString` destructor). ### Cached resources, resource and temp file slots, resource list registry, file name list [verified 2026-10-23, VM]

47 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/resource_cache.cpp`, `resource_cache.h`, `reimpl/src/resource_fields.cpp`, `resource_fields.h`, `reimpl/src/resource_lists.cpp`, `resource_lists.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the base methods of the cached resource `0x57b520`–`0x57bd30`, the value slots of the resource kinds (`0x54e2c0`–`0x54e490`) and of the temp file kind (`0x58b8b0`, `0x58b8f0`, `0x58be70`, `0x58bf20`, slot 16 `0x54e790`), and the rest of the file area `0x4a3480`–`0x4a3c00` (registry of the resource lists, file name list). Not in this batch: slot 23 of the temp file kind (`0x58bd50`, writes the text block; with the field text streams), the manager of the cache (done in the next batch, section 6, "Resource cache manager, …"), the callers of the registry, the compressor `0x5c3b40`/`0x5caa90`.

- **Cached resource** [confirmed; class name assumed, the exe has none for it] (0x40 bytes, every resource kind has its own vtable): +4 type, +8 cost, +0xc file name (operator new; a `"~CFileBuf 0x"` path when resident), +0x10 source resource, +0x14 flags (1 no priority bonus, 2, 8 keep, 0x10 was loaded, 0x20), +0x1c stamp of the last search, +0x20 replacement, +0x24 next in the manager's list, +0x28 passed to slot 9, +0x2c load cost, +0x30, +0x34 priority, +0x3c float. Slots the base methods call: 0 (before loading), 1 (other) takes its place, 2 (bool), 3 (0), 8 (int) scaled priority, 9, 10 (0), 11 unload, 12 and 13 (1) release and delete a replacement, 14 still valid, 15 (name, arg) load.
- **Manager** (`*0x713688`): vtable slot 3 creates a resource; +4 int (below −3000 nothing is inserted), +8 how many valid resources of one type may be loaded, +0xc byte (no caching), +0x14 stamp, +0x18/+0x1c most resources/cost loaded, +0x20 list head, +0x24 resources loaded, +0x28 float scale, +0x2c cost loaded, +0x34 priority bonus. The scaled priority is `__ftol((p + 3333) · scale − 3333.0f)` with p = priority (+0x34) plus the bonus unless flag 1.
- **Methods**: `Load` (`0x57b760`, name, keep, mode, arg): slots 11 and 0; mode 1 only copies the name; otherwise slot 15, then flag 0x10, keep bit, the manager's counters and cost (with maxima), the name freed, source and priority cleared, slots 8, 10 and 9. `Reload` (`0x57b520`, inlined in 7 others): loads the named file again and hands the source back (slot 1). `MakeResident` (`0x57b560`, 0): reads the file into a memory stream (`0x505e40`) and replaces the name with its `"~CFileBuf 0x"` path. `FindReplacement` (`0x57b630`): counts the valid resources of the type in the manager's list (invalid ones are unlinked and the count starts again), below the limit slot 3 (0) and itself; otherwise follows (and creates through the manager) the chain of replacements, each visited once per stamp. `Insert` (`0x57b950`, how): unlinks, checks the manager and the limit, reloads, with bit 0 takes the replacement path, with keep checks validity, then puts itself at the head of the list with the scaled priority. Setters for flags 2, 8, 0x20 (slot 11 when set, slot 2 (0) when cleared), type, load cost, priority (rescaled at once), +0x30; `Unlink` (`0x57bd00`), `Unload` (`0x57bd30`: slot 11, the manager's counters, deletes a resident stream, frees the name, releases the replacement).
- **Resource kinds** (vtables `0x5fd8b0`, `0x5fd970`, `0x5faf10`, `0x5ed320`, `0x5fb280`): the value is an index into the resource list that slot 47 of the descriptor returns for the object. Slots 10 `SetDefault` (`0x54e2c0`), 16 `ToText` (`0x54e370`, name of the index), 19 `FromText` (`0x54e3a0`, object, text, stream), 26 `WriteBinary` (`0x54e3c0`, counted text), 29 `ReadBinary` (`0x54e3f0`, counted text into 0x100 bytes; on `errno` false, else `FindOrFail`), 32 `Use` (`0x54e460`, slot 12 of the list). `SetByName` (`0x54e490`): `Find(name, −1)`; if missing and +0x2d is set, a number (`atoi`; nonzero or exactly `"0"`) below the list's count; otherwise `FindOrFail` (ends the game for a missing name). Then the setter +0x30 (object, index) or stored. `SetDefault` with a default name +0x28 sets `g_LastFileOpened` to the static text `"The Program EXE (C++ Source Code's default value)"` (`0x712200`, built on first use, guard bit 0 of `0x712211`, destructor `0x54e360` via `atexit`) during the lookup and restores it; without one the value is 0.

The data is stored packed: dword 0x3e9, packed size, size, the bytes of `0x5c3b40` (n · 101 / 100 + 12 bytes from operator new); data that already starts with 0x3e9 is taken as it is. Text form (slot 19 `0x58b8f0`, written by slot 23): `{`, `Length=<n> bytes`, `#### BEGIN TEMPORARY FILE ####`, n bytes, `#### END TEMPORARY FILE ####`, `}`; the reader skips to the first line with `=` (a `}` line ends it without data), reads the number by hand (the first character is not checked), and if n is not below the rest of the file it clears the value (slot 10) and searches the end line through a sliding window of its length. Binary form (26 `0x58be70`, 29 `0x58bf20`): the size dword (−1 = none) and the file's bytes. Slot 10 (`0x58b8b0`) deletes the file (`remove`) and frees the path; slot 16 (`0x54e790`, also the embedded object kinds `0x5fda30`, `0x5fbc9c`) gives the empty text.
- Quirks kept: the reader of both forms reads the 0x3e9 marker with a 4-byte `Read` whose result is not checked, so for fewer than 4 bytes the marker is uninitialised stack (not tested); `ReadBinary` with −1 sets the value to null without deleting the old file or freeing its buffer; `FromText` writes to null when no line has a `=` before the end.

28 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/object_table.cpp`, `object_table.h`, `reimpl/src/object_io.cpp`, `object_io.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the object table `0x55c6f0`–`0x55ce50`, the object stream's own methods `0x5240b0`–`0x524340`, `Object_ReadText` (`0x416b60`), `Object_WriteBinary`/`Object_ReadBinary` (`0x416f50`, `0x416fe0`), the read hook setter `0x4163a0`, the white space skipper `0x587ad0`, the object reference kind's slots 19, 26 and 29 (`0x523eb0`, `0x524000`, `0x524030`) and the temp file kind's slot 23 (`0x58bd50`).

- **The "writer" is a stream for both directions** [confirmed: disassembly, callers] (renamed `ObjectStream_*` in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): the same class (`CFileBuf` + table +0x1c + finished +0x20, vtable `0x5fb8fc` with slot 0 the deleting destructor `0x5240f0` and slot 1 `Finish` `0x524340`) is opened on a file (`0x5242b0`, `FileBuf_Open`) or a stream (`0x5242f0`, `Attach` with flags 0) and used by the readers too. Both open functions pass flags and mode to the table; reading is flag 4. `0x524320` finishes the table without closing. `Attach` and `FileBuf_Open` close an old stream through slot 1, i.e. through the stream's finish.
- **Table** (0x5c bytes) [confirmed]: +0 open, +4 location (-1 none), +8 the referenced list was read, +0xc format (0 text, 1 binary, 2 from the constructor; `Open` does not reset it), +0x10 flags, +0x14 stream, +0x18 mode, four lists `{vtable, data, count, capacity}` grown like the array templates: +0x1c read objects `{ID, object}` (`0x5fb904`), +0x2c unresolved references `{ID, 0, field, byte}` (`0x5fb910`), +0x3c referenced objects (writing) or IDs (reading), +0x4c written objects (both `0x5fb91c`).
- **Writing, mode 0**: the first object reserves the place of the list (text `"Referenced Object List Location=0x00420042"`, binary dword `0x2a`); every written object is collected and its address is its ID; references are collected once each. The finish (`0x55ce50`) appends `"Referenced Objects"`, `{`, the count, `0x%08X` per object, `}` (binary: `0x12345678`, the count, the addresses) and writes the list's position over the placeholder (same length). A referenced object that was not written is reported through `*0x6c02cc` slot 16 (`***Programming Error***`).
- **Reading, mode 0**: `Object ID` registers the object under its ID (`0x55cc90`); once the list was read (`0x55c800` text: seeks to the position, `stricmp` against `"Referenced Objects"`, skips `{`, `atoi` count, `strtoul` IDs up to `}`, seeks back; `0x55c9b0` binary, magic not checked) only IDs in it register. A reference (`0x55cb50`) gets its object at once if it is registered (the first entry with the ID decides, also when its object is null), otherwise the field holds the ID until the finish resolves it; an ID without an object becomes null. The class name of a reference (`0x%08X (Class)`) is passed on but not used. **Mode 1** (the change test `0x417100`, the file readers `0x4164c0` and `0x416a00` – levels are read this way) writes no IDs and turns every reference into null.
- **`Object_ReadText`** [confirmed]: optional class name line (must be registered and a base of the object's class), `{`, then per line (behind leading white space `0x587ad0`, characters of `*0x622dd8`): empty lines and lines without `=` are skipped; `}` ends; `{` ends the game (`"Found unexpected '{' while parsing class ..."`, `ShowErrorBox`, `exit(-1)`; checked with the box and exit redirected). `Object ID` only as the first field line or right behind location lines; the stop pair `*0x62e68c`/`*0x62e690` ends reading with true (the level loader `0x4d33f9` reads a layer up to `"Tree List"`); a field of the object's class (`ClassInfo_FindField`, also by alternative name) reads with slot 19; otherwise the part behind the first `"::"` is looked up and – found or not – then goes on as the name: `"Referenced Object List Location"` reads the list, anything else goes to the object's slot 11 (own lines). So a `Class::Field` line that is found reaches slot 11 as well. Result: the last line read is `}` (behind white space or as it is). The read hook `*0x62e688` (set by `0x4163a0`) runs before each object, also in the binary reader.
- **Binary objects** [confirmed]: version 27.0f, (mode 0) placeholder, address as ID, class version (float), slot 26 per field, the object's slot 13; the reader needs 27 and the same class version (x87: NaN counts as equal), takes 24 only in mode 1 (one dword skipped, then 25, so it fails), fails below 4, reads slot 29 per field (stops at the first false) and the object's slot 15. Object references: slot 26 collects and writes the pointer, slot 29 reads into the argument's stack slot (the reader's own address if nothing is left) and resolves.
- **Temp file slot 23** [confirmed]: `"TempFile"`, `{`, with a file indented `"Length=%u bytes"` + `"#### BEGIN TEMPORARY FILE ####"` (one `WriteText`), the file's bytes as they are (the packed form), `"#### END TEMPORARY FILE ####"`, `}`; without a file only `}`. A missing file gives length 0.

- **Items and definitions** [confirmed]: an item has its definition index at +8, an index into the item catalogue (records of 0x80 bytes at `*0x6c0c38`, count `*0x6c0c3c`); `0x4dd480` resolves it and loads the definition on first use (index beyond the count: record 0; a record being loaded: null). A definition (`CZaxInventoryItemDefinition`) has its category at +0x18 and a sort order at +0xfc. The order of two items (`0x42a3b0`/`0x42a3f0` → `0x5b8b00`/`0x5b8bd0`) is: sort order, then catalogue index, then inventory index. Item slots used: 1 delete, 2 class, 34, 41 count (-1 counts as one in `TotalCount`, as zero in the item counts `0x426860`/`0x4268d0`), 44/45 select/deselect with the inventory.
- **Neighbours** (`0x425350` previous, `0x425470` next, `0x425340` first): the nearest item of the category before/after `from` in that order, wrapping around to the last/first; they resolve the definition of every item without a null check (a null item ends the game, with the original as well).
- **Removing** (`0x426090`): the item goes to the disposed list (slot 2), the indices behind it move down, a focus on it becomes 0, a category without a selection selects its first remaining item. `Remove` (`0x426260`) of an item that is not in the list calls `RemoveAt(-1)`, which reads the entry before the list's data [confirmed: disassembly; checked with a sentinel there].
- **Repair** (`0x4262e0`, called while +8 is 0): selected flags against the categories' indices (select/deselect), invalid selected and "changing to" indices cleared, entries that `GetItem` returns as null deleted (slot 1) and removed (after a removal at index 0 the index check wraps, so no index moves), categories without a selection select their first item, the focus put into the list. If anything was wrong, the byte `0x60b5d4` is set and the inventory was inited before, the reporter `*0x6c02cc` gets slot 17 with the text above. +8 becomes 1.
- **`0x4267e0`** jumps to slot 36 of a layer part: the characters' inventory at +0x108 (`0x49a8c0`), other parts ask their owner +0xc (`0x4faf30`); reimplemented as the same two instructions.
- **Window helpers** [confirmed]: the `CRect` constructor; the edge test of a resizable window (bits 1 left, 2 top, 4 right, 8 bottom for a point relative to the window; the border is 2 × (font height / 5), within 6 × (font height / 5) of a corner the neighbouring edge counts too); the list box's scroll step (fastcall: at most `far` from the target, otherwise `near` closer to it than the start).

The 62 other functions of the UI range wait for the window classes.

### Object files, CObject base methods, the slots that create objects [verified 2026-10-23, VM]

60 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/object_files.cpp`, `object_files.h`, `object_base.cpp`, `object_base.h`, `field_objects.cpp`, `field_objects.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the object file functions `0x4164c0`, `0x4167e0`, `0x416a00`, `0x416af0`, the change test `0x417100` and the `ZString` stream operators `0x4162d0`/`0x416310`; the `CObject` base methods and the object functions around them (`0x416610`–`0x417660`), the dynamic property accessors of the descriptors (`0x418790`–`0x418810`, `0x418fa0`–`0x418fd0`, `0x4190e0`), the value block slots of the descriptor base (`0x419070`–`0x4190d0`), the `ZString` arrays (`0x416240`, `0x416290`) and three static pointer lists (`0x419ea0`, `0x419f00`, `0x419f60`); slots 16, 19, 26, 29 and 32 of the owned object kind (`0x418970`–`0x418d70`), slots 19, 26, 29 and 32 of the pointer array kind with its append and remove (`0x419470`–`0x4199f0`), slots 19, 26, 29 and 32 of the `new[]` array kind (`0x417c60`–`0x4181b0`) and the binary slots of the class pointer kind (`0x418620`, `0x418650`).

- **Reading objects from files** [confirmed: disassembly, callers; VM]: `Object_CreateFromFile` (`0x4164c0`, fastcall: path `ZString`, flags, write back, `&object`) opens an object stream on the file (flags | 0x204, mode 1), sets `g_LastFileOpened` to the path (restored at the end), reads the first line and creates the class it names (`ClassRegistry_Create` with 0, -1; a missing or abstract class ends the game), stores the object at once (the pointer dangles if reading fails), calls its slots 16 and 19 (19 = every field's default), reads it with `Object_ReadText` and visits its objects (slot 18) with a `QueryVisitor` because the mode is not 0. After the finish it writes the object back (`0x4167e0` with flags 0) if asked. The line read for the class name is not checked: an empty file leaves the buffer as it was. The game uses it for canned objects (`.can`), death behaviours, inventory item definitions and types, categories, damage types, `Rules.txt`, game types (`.ZGT`), difficulties and `.TXT` files (11 callers). `Object_ReadFile` (`0x416a00`) does the same into an existing object (flags | 4); without the file only slot 19 runs. The level loader `0x4d33f9` reads a level this way into the `CLayerSaveData` at +0x3c of a new `CLayer` (`0x4e9da0`), with the stop pair set to that object and `"Tree List"` (`0x615d18`).
- **Writing objects to files** [confirmed]: `Object_WriteFile` (`0x4167e0`, (path, flags)) writes only if `File_Exists(path, flags)`; the object as text (mode 1) into a memory stream, compared with the file (flags | 4, `FileBuf_Equals`), rewritten (flags | 3, `CopyTo`) when it differs or cannot be read; true if the file holds the text afterwards. `Object_HasChanged` (`0x417100`) writes both objects (mode 1) into memory streams and returns 1 unless length and bytes agree (a single caller, `0x53e71d`). `Object_ReadFromStream` (`0x416af0`): slots 16 and 19, `Object_ReadText`, the visit with a `QueryVisitor` if the table mode is not 0 (the `new[]` array slot 19 reads its elements with it).
- **CObject** [confirmed]: vtable `0x5ec9ec` (8 bytes: vtable, dynamic properties +4): 1 deleting destructor (`0x416650`, 8 bytes back to the pool), 2 class info, 7 precache (`0x4167b0`: slot 32 of every field; the overrides load sounds, e.g. `CPlayerWalkingControlAI` and `CZaxDialogAction`) [assumption on the name: ours], 11 own lines (`0x417500`), 19 every field's default (`0x417230`), 20 copy from another object (`0x417420`), 21 object size (`0x4174f0`). The constructor (`0x416610`) and destructor (`0x4166d0`) init/free CObject's own fields; `0x4173c0`/`0x4173f0` do the same for the class of the object (called by 1,726 constructors and 1,579 destructors). Slot 20 walks the source class up its parents until one class derives from the other, copies the common fields with slot 4 (dst, src, descriptor) and sets the rest to their defaults. Slot 11 looks the name up in the class's extra list (with alternative names); found, with a value other than `""` and `"0"`, it becomes a dynamic property read by its slot 19; otherwise the block behind the line is skipped (an optional class line beginning with `C` and without `=`, then `{` … `}` with nesting, else back to where the reader was).
- **Dynamic properties** [confirmed]: the list (+4) is created on first use (pool 0x10, vtable `0x5eca54`); add (`0x417260` → `0x482a70`, 0 if an entry with a value exists), remove, get, get or add, has; the descriptor side passes itself (`0x418fa0`–`0x418fc0`), reads/sets/takes the pointer at its offset in the value (`0x418790`, `0x4187c0`, `0x418810`; the setter +0x38 gets the value block as `this`). The descriptor base slots 35/36 give value blocks of +0x14 bytes from the pool and back, 38 an array from operator new, 43/46 return 0.
- **Owned object kind** (`0x5ecbf4`, +0x2c the class the object must derive from) [confirmed; VM]: slot 16 the class name or `""` (also slot 16 of the object reference kind); slot 19 deletes the object for `""`, reads into it if the class name is the same (`stricmp`), else deletes it and creates the named class — missing, not derived from +0x2c, or abstract: `"Invalid class type"` box with the field name and `g_LastFileOpened`, `exit(-1)` —, then slots 16/19 of the new object, `Object_ReadText` and slot 13 (visit) of the descriptor; slot 26 the class name as counted text and `Object_WriteBinary`; slot 29 deletes the object first, reads the class name into a 0x64-byte buffer and creates it without any check; slot 32 is slot 7 of the object (the old row named it slot 33 "ElementSize"; slot 33 is `0x591dd0`).
- **Pointer array kind** (`0x5ecd6c`) [confirmed; VM]: slot 19 without a reader takes the count from the text; with one (without a name list +0x40 it is emptied first) it skips the line after the field line and reads the block: `{`/`}` nest (the `}` at depth 0 ends), `Item Count=` or `Array Count=` resize, with a name list `<name>=` reads element slot 2(name) of the list (unknown names skipped), without one lines named like the element descriptor (or its alternative name) read the next element, the array growing by one when the count read so far is too small. Slots 26/29: the count, per element its name (with a name list) and slot 26/29 of the element descriptor (29 resizes exactly to the count or the name list's count, inits all elements and stops at the first false or unknown name). `0x4199b0` appends an element and returns it, `0x4199f0` removes the one at an index.
- **`new[]` array kind** (`0x5eca78`) [confirmed; VM]: slot 19 as above, but a count line recreates the data (deleted with slot 1 and 3, then slot 28 of the element class with n, 0, -1) when count or capacity differ; elements are read with `0x416af0`; without a name list each line before a count line appends an element (`0x4181f0`), after one they are read in order without growing; an unknown name reads into a scratch object of the class that is deleted. Slots 26/29: the count, names, `Object_WriteBinary`/`Object_ReadBinary` per element (29 recreates the data and gives every element slot 19 first). Slot 32 calls slot 7 of every element.
- **Class pointer kind** (`0x5ecb38`): slot 26 the class name as counted text, slot 29 reads it (0x64-byte buffer) and looks it up with `ClassRegistry_FindChecked` (`""` gives null).
- **Quirks found** [confirmed: disassembly; VM where noted]: `0x418cb0` and `0x418650` read class names into 0x64-byte stack buffers without a length check (`ReadCountedText` only checks the rest of the stream). `0x419810`, `0x418050` and `0x416310` read their count into an uninitialised slot (`0x416310`: the caller's ecx, the stream). A count line that does not match the elements leaves states the original cannot handle either: the pointer array creates default objects (element slot 10) and the game ends deleting them (runs `20261023-181036-a76c`, `-181358-e760`, `CChildList.Child List`), the `new[]` array reads past its data (run `20261023-183623-0b77`). Whole level files cannot be read on their own: with `0x4164c0` (run `20261023-194100-efba`) or into a `CLayerSaveData` of its own with the stop pair (run `20261023-194846-2266`) the original ends the game as well — it expects to sit inside a `CLayer` [assumption on the cause: not traced]. Copies of the game's single objects and drawn objects (`CRules`, `CLayer`, `CRotationSequence`, actions and AIs outside the world) created and deleted in the checks ended the game later; the checks avoid them.
- **Return values** are the original's eax; documented in the headers where not reproduced: the void resize functions (the array slot 19 results, `0x4199f0`), `0x4173c0` (the no-op slots 6 leave the eax they find), the block skipping loops (a stack address with the character in al), `0x417300` without a list (the caller's upper bytes).

### Broadcaster, listener references, update monitor list, child list [verified 2026-10-23, VM]

42 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/broadcast.cpp`, `broadcast.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): `CListenerReference` and `CBroadcaster` (`0x4674f0`–`0x467ee0`), `CUpdateMonitorInfo` and `CUpdateMonitorList` (`0x4e4830`–`0x4e5090`), `CChildList` (`0x4f97e0`–`0x4f9b70`), the class getter of `CLayerPart` (`0x4f9bf0`) and the broadcaster helpers of the layer parts (`0x4fc1b0`, `0x4fc200`, `0x4fc240`) and the AI objects (`0x4fd190`, `0x4fd1e0`).

- **The pattern of every class** [confirmed: disassembly]: the class getter in slot 2 registers the class on first use (pool block of 0x48 bytes, `ClassInfo_Register` with the exe addresses of Create, CreateArray and RegisterFields); Create = pool block + constructor (CObject constructor `0x416610`, members, vtable, slot 6 of the class's own fields through `0x4173c0`); CreateArray is fastcall with the count in ecx and one unused stack argument (heap block with the count in front, none constructed for a count below 1); slot 1 is the deleting destructor (bit 1: array form from the last element, returns the block, bit 0 frees: operator delete or the pool); RegisterFields makes the descriptors and adds each through `ClassInfo_AddField`, with its own inlined copy of the getter. The CObject pieces (`0x416610`, `0x4166d0`, `0x4173c0`, `0x4173f0`, slot 19 = `0x417230`, slot 10 of all fields) lie in `0x416000`–`0x419fff` (the object file batch) and are called through their addresses. CObject's slot 0 (`0x46cd50`, 3 bytes, not hookable) is the message handler `(sender, message)` and does nothing.
- **`CBroadcaster`** [confirmed] (0x28 bytes, version 2, **no parent class** although it starts with the CObject part; the same holds for `CChildList`): +8 "Objects Listening" (owned `CListenerReference`s, array vtable `0x5ef30c`), +0x18 "Listener" (listener objects as older files stored them, `0x5ef300`). `AddListener` (`0x467e60`, (listener, member offset, member name)): a new reference, its slot 19, the members, appended; returns the index. `RemoveListener` (`0x467ee0`): the *first* reference to the listener is deleted and removed; offset and name are not compared. `Broadcast` (`0x467d40`, (sender, message)): slot 0 of every listener from the last reference to the first; the index comes from the count at the start, the data pointer is read again for every reference, so listeners may remove themselves. Slot 18 (`0x467d80`) turns the "Listener" array into references (offset −1, empty name). The destructor deletes the references from the last one, then the fields are freed. All callers checked here pass offset −1 and the empty name (the update monitor list, `CLayerPart::vf71`, slot 18) [assumption for the other 17 callers of `0x4fc1b0`: not read].
- **`CListenerReference`** (0x14): +8 "Listener", +0xc "Member Offset", +0x10 "Member Name". "Member Offset" is **not initialized** by the constructor (the block keeps its old content; seen in the VM with both the original and the reimplementation), nor are "Half Width"/"Half Height" of `CUpdateMonitorInfo`.
- **Layer parts and AI objects** [confirmed]: a layer part has its broadcaster at +0x10, an AI object (`CAIBase`) at +0xc. The broadcaster is created with the first listener (`0x4fc1b0`, `0x4fd190`) and deleted with the last one (`0x4fc200`, `0x4fd1e0`); `0x4fc240` broadcasts with the part as sender. Messages seen: `"Delete"` (destructors of parts `0x4fa810` and AI objects `0x4fd080`), `"Died"` (`0x4fbf30`); the update monitor list also reacts to `"Leaving Scope"`. The callers (inventory items, actions, AI, sound, world: 45 callers of `0x4fc200`) are not Core and stay open.
- **`CUpdateMonitorList`** [confirmed] (0x18, version 2): +8 "Monitor List" of `CUpdateMonitorInfo` (0x14, version 1: +8 "Update Part" = reference to a `CLayerPart`, +0xc "Half Width", +0x10 "Half Height"). `Add` (`0x4e4f70`, (part, half width, half height) → al 0 if the part is already monitored) makes an entry and listens to the part; `Remove` (`0x4e5000`, → al); slot 0 (`0x4e5090`) removes the entry of a monitored part on `"Delete"`/`"Leaving Scope"` (case-insensitive) and passes everything else to `0x46cd50`. The destructor only stops listening; the entries are not deleted there [assumption: the field's free slot through `0x4173f0` deletes them; the owned array kind's free slot not read for it]. Its methods are called only by `CPointOfIntrestAI` (AI). `0x4e4b60` is a second copy of the getter (called by `CHudBarOptions::RegisterFields`).
- **`CChildList`** [confirmed] (0x18, version 1): +8 "Child List", owned objects of any class. `RemoveChild` (`0x4f9b70`): a null child does nothing; otherwise the child is taken out of the list if it is listed and deleted in any case (one caller, `0x4f5660`). RegisterFields keeps the element descriptor "Child" in the global `0x6c29c4`; the static registration of `CChildList`/`CLayerPart` (around `0x4f9600`–`0x4f97c4`, not in `docs/functions.csv`) then sets its class (+0x2c) to `CLayerPart` [confirmed: disassembly `0x4f97b6`, VM]. A layer part has its child list at +8.
- **Level objects** [confirmed: disassembly `0x579600`, `0x4f4500`, VM]: the parts of a level are kept in the `CSortList2D` "Tree List" at `CLayer` +0x50 (save data +0x3c, there +0x14): +0x10 columns, +0x14 rows, +0x18 cells of 16 bytes (pointer arrays), +0x1c the first cell of every row.
- **Not Core** (by subsystem): the two ranges are counted as Core in `docs/functions.csv` only for these classes; the layer part and AI helpers sit in World/AI ranges but only touch the broadcaster.

All of it is **multiplayer**: the GameSpy query answers (`0x51f180`–`0x51f420`: `"\%s\%s"`, `"gamemode"`, `"timelimit"`, `"fraglimit"`, `"team_t%d"`/`"score_t%d"`, `"openplaying"`, `"exiting"`, `"Net Game"`/`"Bind Host to IP Address"`, query port 0x68aa), the player and team list helpers (`0x51f440`–`0x51f5a0`), the GameSpy player answer `0x51f880` (`"name"`, `"ping"`), the net traffic graph (`"Max %d, Cur %d"`, `"Player %u"`, `"All Non-Local Traffic"`) and the packet. - **NetPacket** [confirmed] (0x34 bytes, two of them in the net session `0x4f7c50`, vtable `0x5f91c8`): +0 the registered block readers (heap pointer array, vtable `0x5fb580`), +0x10 data, +0x14 capacity, +0x18 "reliable" flag, +0x1c read position, +0x20 length, +0x24 bytes read before the last `Reset`, +0x28 a token map (vtable `0x5fb574`), +0x2c the reader of the last `ReadBlock`. Writes of 1, 2, 4 and 16 bytes, bools, byte runs and texts with their terminator grow the data to max(2 × capacity, capacity + n) and return the offset written at (texts: the new length); reads check position + n ≤ length and return al = 1/0 (`ReadBool` gives 1 when nothing is left; `ReadText` gives `""` when the text does not end inside, after scanning without a bound). `Skip`, `SkipToEnd`, `CanRead`, `Reset` and two unchecked patch functions complete it. Callers: the entities' slots 25/27 (state written into/read from the packet: `CEntityBase`, `CEntityAnimated`, `CEntityCharacter`, `CLightningLayerPart`, …), AI behaviours, `CZaxSaveGameStats` (game flow) and the world.

The reimplementation keeps the name path; the check runs it with stand-ins for the two map functions.

Not hookable (4 bytes): `0x5203b0` (length), `0x5203c0` (the flag), `0x51f450`.

### CSortList2D, the grid of a level's objects [verified 2026-10-23, VM]

34 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/sort_list.cpp`, `sort_list.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): all 32 functions of `0x579120`–`0x57aeb0` that `docs/functions.csv` lists, plus the cell arrays' deleting destructor `0x5794b0` (slot 0 of vtable `0x600a90`, missing from `docs/functions.csv`) and the cell writer `0x5790a0` (just before the range, called by slot 13).

- **Assignment** [confirmed]: the range is `CSortList2D` only (class registration through its getter `0x5792e0`; `0x57a030`–`0x57aeb0` were "open/neighbours" before). The class is the "Tree List" of the layer (`CLayer` +0x50) and so belongs to the world rather than to Core, but it only touches the layer parts through their slots and a few small world helpers, so it was taken here. `0x578fa0`/`0x579030` before the range are not part of it (a wait loop with `0x6c1050` and a helper around `0x578a70`) [assumption on their purpose; settled later: `ScreenImage::Wait` `0x578fa0` waits until the screen image has been shown for its time or a key is pressed, `ScreenImage_Blank` `0x579030` shows a frame at once on a screen image of its own; confirmed: code, reimpl/src/screen_image.cpp; VM].
- **Layout** [confirmed: constructor `0x579340`, `Resize` `0x5793e0`]: 0x28 bytes, version 1.01, no parent class and no fields (RegisterFields is the empty `0x58ea40`). +8/+0xc the last pixel (columns · 64 − 1, rows · 64 − 1), +0x10 columns, +0x14 rows (both rounded up from the size in pixels), +0x18 the cells (columns · rows pointer arrays of 16 bytes in one `new[]` block, pool flavour, Add `0x5c1f00`), +0x1c the first cell of every row (`0x4a8440`: max(rows, 2) entries), +0x20 the owner (the layer; not set by the constructor), +0x24 the id of the next part read as text (−1 after the constructor). Cells are 64 pixels square; coordinates are turned into cells in 16 bits (at most the last pixel, at least 0, `sar 6`).
- **Parts** [confirmed]: a part is listed in every cell its rectangle touches (slot 37 with kind 5; `Insert` does not look at its result) and keeps that cell rectangle at +0x30 (four words, −9999 when it is in no grid: a function-local static of `0x579ab0`, `0x713678` with guard `0x713681`). `Insert` (`0x579900`) also gives the part the layer (`0x4fc8f0`, recursively for its child list), stamp 0, and with the flags 0x20000, 0x200000 and 0x800000 together passes its kind-0 rectangle to the layer's +0x7c object (`0x540640`); then slot 74. `Remove` (`0x579a80`): slot 75, out of the cells, no layer. `Update` (`0x579c10`) re-lists a moved part only if its cells changed and its first kept cell lists it. `DeleteAll` (`0x579f50`) gives every part `0x4fbd00` first, then removes and deletes them. `Process` (`0x57a030`, called by the world update `0x4e7870`) runs slots 31, 32 and 35 of a list of parts (those not marked 0x10000) and then removes and deletes the marked ones; `MarkDied` (`0x57a6e0`) calls `LayerPart_Died` for every part whose +0x20 lacks a bit [assumption on both names: ours].
- **Queries** [confirmed]: a global stamp (`0x622200`, back to 1 after 0xefffffff) marks the parts visited by a walk (+0x2c), so a part in several cells comes once. The flag filter of all queries: every bit of `all` set, none of `none`, and with `use_any` at least one of `any`. `QueryRect` (`0x57a100`) appends the parts whose rectangle overlaps (kind 5, and the asked kind too if it is not 5) through `0x59a220`; without a rectangle it walks every cell with a stamp of its own (a part can come more than once) and takes `any` whenever it is not 0. `QueryName` (`0x57a7e0`, the name compared with `0x587d30`) and `QueryClass` (`0x57ab20`, exact class) use `0x59a140`. `FindRect`/`FindName`/`FindClass` (`0x57a770`, `0x57aa80`, `0x57aae0`) clear the list first and set `use_any` from `any`. `QueryRadius` (`0x57ac50`, 12 arguments) takes a temporary list (`0x59a470`), queries the bounding rectangle and calls the callback (thiscall on the part, context in edx, the squared distance as a float) for every part of the class (if given) other than `except` whose squared distance (`0x4fc020`, the y difference scaled) is at most radius², optionally only with a free line of sight (`0x4e8d40` on the layer's +0x3c; the part gets flag 0x2000000 meanwhile). `FindId` (`0x57a9a0`) looks for an id (+0x28) in the cell of a point; no caller found.
- **Files** [confirmed]: slot 9 writes every part once as `Level Part=` + `Object_WriteText`; slot 11 reads such a line (creates the class named by the value, reads it, gives it the next id and adds it through the layer's `0x4eb6f0`, which inserts it here); slot 13 writes per cell the count of not yet written parts and each as class name + `Object_WriteBinary`; slot 15 reads that back per cell (a part listed in several cells comes back in one cell, with the cell rectangle it saved). Slot 7 calls slot 7 of every part once, slot 19 deletes all parts.
- Return values are what the original leaves in eax; where it is not defined (`Process`; `Update` when the first kept cell does not list the part: only al) the comments say so.
- Hooks: 881 installed on this branch (34 new).

20 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/local_table.cpp`, `local_table.h`, `reimpl/src/small_helpers.cpp`, `small_helpers.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the rest of the `Local.txt` table (`0x4270f0`, `0x500740`–`0x500ac0`, `0x501030`), two small neighbours of it (`0x5003e0`, `0x500570`) and three self-contained DirectPlay helpers (`0x47f350`, `0x480c80`, `0x480cc0`). The two other ranges of the batch were looked at and left alone (see "Not Core" below).

- **The table** [confirmed: code of `0x500ac0`, `0x500900`, `0x500f50`] (`ZLocalTable`, 0x110 bytes, the one instance `0x6c2b90`, loaded once by `Game_Startup` from `"Local.txt"`): +0 the file name (copied without a limit), +0x100 0 when the file opened from the disk (flags 0x224: into memory, disk only, read), 1 when the second attempt with flags 4 (archives and the language pack) was needed or both failed, +0x104 count, +0x108 capacity, +0x10c the entries, a `new[]` block {count, `LocalEntry`[]} from operator new. `LocalEntry` is the string pair {key, text} (8 bytes): `0x500740` constructs it empty (56 callers, the pair is used elsewhere too), `0x500760` from two strings, `0x4270f0` destroys the text, then the key, `0x5008f0` is the qsort comparison (`ZString::Compare` of the keys). `0x500ab0` returns whether there are entries.
- **Loading** [confirmed] (`0x500ac0`, (file, unused second argument)): on success the old entries are destroyed from the end, 10 new ones made (capacity 10), then line by line: a line beginning with `"ENGLISH: "` (pointer `0x6190a4`, length `0x6c2cc0`) starts a pair; its key is the rest of the line, and while the line just read lacks `"[END]"` the next lines are appended with `"\n"` (the result of those reads is not looked at; at the end of the file the last line stays in the buffer). `"[END]"` is cut from the key only when its first occurrence is at the very end, so a key with a context keeps `"[END] (context)"`, the form `Local_Translate` builds. The next line is the text: its first 11 characters (the length of `"LOCALIZED: "`, `0x6c2ca4`) are skipped without a check, the same continuation applies, and the text is cut at its first `"[END]"`. Every pair goes through `Add` `0x500900`, which writes the entry at the count, grows by 10 when the count reaches the capacity (entries assigned into the new block, the old ones destroyed from the end) and sorts the whole table with qsort after **every** entry (687 sorts for the German `Local.txt`); after the file the table is sorted once more. Then, also when neither open worked, every registered string is translated through the table (with the old entries if the file was missing); a successful load sets `0x6c2cc8` (read nowhere else) and returns al = 1, the upper bytes of eax are the file buffer destructor's.
- Quirks kept: the three line buffers are 0x400 bytes and the parts are joined without a bound (a part longer than the buffer overruns the stack); a part without `"[END]"` up to the end of the file loops for ever; a second line shorter than 11 characters makes the text start behind its terminator (in stale buffer bytes); a text whose `"[END]"` sits within its first 11 characters dereferences null. The memory stream splits lines only at CR, so an LF-only file is one line: the key is the rest of that line (its first `"[END]"` is not at the end, so nothing is cut), the read of the text line fails at the end of the file and leaves the same line in the buffer, and the text is that line from its 12th character up to the first `"[END]"`. A line of 0x3ff characters or more ends the file there (the reader refuses it without moving on).
- **Registered strings** [confirmed] (`0x501030`, thiscall on a new `ZString`, (text, context); 363 call sites in the menus and windows, function-local statics): the string is built from the text and, unless it is empty, appended with its context to the list `0x6c2ca8` (8-byte entries {string, context}, vtable `0x5f99e0`, grown inline like the 8-byte arrays to max(count + 1, capacity · 1.2)); the list is built on first use (guard bit 0 of `0x6c2cbc`, destructor `0x500a70` via `atexit`) and `0x6c2cc4` points to it. `0x501030` itself translates nothing, so a string registered after the load stays untranslated unless something else translates it [assumption that nothing does; not traced].
- **Static initialisers** [confirmed]: `0x5007e0`, `0x500800`, `0x500820` store the lengths of `"ENGLISH: "`, `"LOCALIZED: "`, `"[END]"` (through the text pointers `0x6190a4`–`0x6190ac`), `0x500840` the length `" (%s)"` adds to a key (`0x6c2cb8`, 5 − 2 = 3; not read by the functions here); `0x500870` clears the table's entries and registers its destructor `0x500890` (entries destroyed from the end, count 0). Since the hooks are installed before the exe's start-up code, these run as the reimplementation.
- Not hookable: `0x5007a0` `FieldDesc_Name` (`add ecx, 4` + `jmp`) and `0x5007b0` (`lea eax, [ecx + 4]; ret`, 13 callers, the address of the second member).
- **Neighbours** [confirmed: callers]: `0x5003e0` is the 12-byte assignment of the layer part's slot 59 (`0x5001d0`, World); `0x500570` is `Reserve(n)` of `CLightningLayerPart`'s segment array (called by its slot 23 `0x4ff500`, Rendering): 0x58-byte elements whose constructor only writes the vtable `0x5f99c8`, max(n, capacity · 1.2) new elements, every member copied except the vtable and the bytes +0x0d–+0x0f, +0x27. `0x500080` (the lightning's geometry, `0x509100`/`0x508da0` trigonometry) and `0x5001d0` stay with Rendering/World.
- **DirectPlay helpers** [confirmed: strings, imports]: `0x47f000`–`0x480fff` was counted as Core through its neighbours only; it is the **DirectPlay 8 multiplayer** layer (`DPNERR_*` texts, `"Could not find any DirectPlay service Providers"`, `"Multi-player Netword Error"`, GameSpy start/stop, the critical sections `0x6bdbf0`/`0x6bdc08`/`0x6bdad0`, the message handler `0x47ff50` switching on the message id) plus, from `0x480e20`, a `CFrame`-derived image class (vtable `0x5f162c`, pixel access through slot 46, sizes through `0x4ab5a0`; Rendering). Reimplemented are only the self-contained pieces: `0x47f350` (fastcall, the result code in ecx) returns the exe's text for 24 codes (DPNERR_* and `DPNSUCCESS_PENDING` 0x15800e; partly through a byte-indexed jump table for `0x80158390`–`0x80158470`) and prints every other code with `"Unknown error %08x"` into the static buffer `0x6bdae8`; `0x480c80` clears the 100 12-byte player slots of the session object (+0x44c: bytes +0 and +1 and the dword +8 of each; "player slots" [confirmed: the message handler's 100 slots {added, removed, dpnid, session}, section 6 "Net game, net session, …", code `0x480c80`, reimpl/src/small_helpers.cpp; VM]) and the byte +0x8fc inside the critical section `0x6bdbf0`; `0x480cc0` deletes element i of a pointer array through its slot 0 and removes it (eax: data, the destructor's, i + 1 or memmove's). Open with the multiplayer: `0x47ef10`, `0x47fc20` (service providers), `0x47fdb0` (a deleting destructor around `0x51ead0`), `0x47fdf0` (creates the DirectPlay objects), `0x47ff50`, `0x4803c0`, `0x480800`, `0x480a70` and the unnamed code between them; with Rendering: `0x480e20`–`0x480fc0`.
- **Not Core: `0x57c000`–`0x57cfff`** [confirmed: imports and slots]: these are the **sound** manager and sound resources derived from the resource cache (COM calls through the objects at `0x713694` and `0x7136f4`: slots 15/16/17 with values as `IDirectSoundBuffer` volume, pan, frequency take them, slot 3 of `0x7136f4` with a buffer description as `IDirectSound::CreateSoundBuffer` [interface names: assumption, after the DirectSound headers; the code has only slot numbers]; the listener position `0x7136a0`–`0x7136a8` and the volumes `0x7136ac`, `0x713698`, `0x7136f0`; `CSoundResource` 0x9c bytes, vtable `0x600b8c`, reset `0x57c270` with defaults 10.0 and 100.0; `"ogg"` streams and a pool of 100,000-byte stream buffers `0x716080`/`0x716090` with `0x57cd40` (take a free one), `0x57cdb0` (give one back), `0x57ced0` (the flag array's constructor)). None of it is reimplemented in this batch: it belongs to the sound subsystem, which needs DirectSound stand-ins to be checked; the trivial setters and getters (`0x57c170`–`0x57c230`) come with it.
- Hooks: 948 on this branch (20 new).

Check in the VM (run `20261024-072121-d945`, in the game thread, `reimpl/src/checks_local_table.cpp`, `checks_small_helpers.cpp`; side 0 with all hooks of the module taken out, so `Load` → `Add` → the comparison run the original too, side 1 through the reimplementation):

### Small object classes, the canned object list, the water wave form [verified 2026-10-24, VM]

49 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/object_classes.cpp`, `object_classes.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): `CCannedObject` (`0x468230`–`0x4683f0`) with the canned object list (`0x468000`–`0x468150`, `0x468b30`–`0x468da0`) and its "Use" names (`0x468200`, `0x468220`), `CObjectHolder` and `CObjectCollection` (`0x5238c0`–`0x523c30`) with the resource list setter `0x523e20`, `CSphereOfZinOptions` (`0x582520`–`0x5826e0`), `CSphereOfZinData` (`0x5841c0`–`0x584430`) and `CWaterWaveFormData` (`0x5969f0`–`0x596b70`) with its three field setters (`0x596d20`–`0x596de0`).

- **Assignment** [confirmed: vtables, callers, game data]: all six are data classes read from text files; their own code (getters, Create, CreateArray, destructors, RegisterFields, the wave setters) touches nothing but the object system, so it is Core. What uses them is not: `CCannedObject` is the content of the `.can` files (`Resources/Canned Objects`, 7 files, used by `CUseCannedAction`, Actions); `CObjectHolder`/`CObjectCollection` hold layer parts (no game file uses them); `CSphereOfZinOptions` is "Sphere Of Zin Options" of `CZaxCustomRules` (`Rules.txt`), `CSphereOfZinData` the trigger list of `CSphereOfZinEnergyInventoryItem` (Inventory and weapons); `CWaterWaveFormData` is embedded four times in `CWaterWarpEffect` (+8, +0x220, +0x438, +0x650; "V1/V2/H1/H2 Wave", Rendering).
- **Layouts** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`, game data]: `CCannedObject` 0x10 (class `0x6bd10c`, version 1, parent CObject): +8 "Object" (owned CObject), +0xc "Use" (a typed resource field over the `ZEnumTable` `0x6bd0f0` {0 "Shared Global Instance", 1 "Local Copy"}; all 7 files say "Shared Global Instance"; corrected 2026-10-25: `Drop Cystals and Ore.can` reads as 0, and `CUseCannedAction` clones the object for 1 (section 8)). `CObjectHolder` 0xc (`0x6d013c`, version 1, **no parent**): +8 "Object" (owned `CLayerPart`). `CObjectCollection` 0x10 (`0x6d0140`, version 1, no parent): "Num Objects", a new[] array of `CObjectHolder` (+8 data, +0xc count). `CSphereOfZinOptions` 0x10 (`0x713800`, **version 0**, parent CObject): +8 "Evil Unit Lenght" (sic; float, units "Pixels^2", default 40000, 1 to 1e8, then the converter `0x6be350` and the units "Pixels"; `Rules.txt` gives 102400), +0xc "Apply Ceiling Prematurely" (byte, default 1, `Rules.txt` 1), both with help texts. `CSphereOfZinData` 0x18 (`0x713818`, version 0, parent CObject): an embedded array object at +8 {vtable `0x601374`, +0xc data, +0x10 count, +0x14 capacity}, "Trigger List" (new[] array of `CThresholdTrigger`). `CWaterWaveFormData` 0x218 (`0x713dc4`, version 1, no parent): +8 "Amplitude" (2, 0–30, step 0.1), +0xc "Pixels Per Second" (15, −100–100), +0x10 "Num Waves" (int, 4, 0–16), +0x14 a table of 128 ints, +0x214 a dword the class's code never writes; `Generic Water.txt`, for example, gives 4 and 6 waves, amplitudes 0.9–2.2 and speeds −12 to 15.
- **Wave table** [confirmed: code of `0x596d20`/`0x596d80`/`0x596de0`]: each setter stores its value and recomputes entry i = fistp(float(fcos(((i · n) << 1 as an unsigned 32-bit number) · π/128) · amplitude)) for i = 0–127 (`π/128` the float at `0x602928`), so the table holds n cosine periods scaled to whole pixels. The float setters return the value in st(0) (eax is 0x80 in the original, not reproduced); the count setter returns it in eax. The reimplementation runs the same x87 sequence (fild qword, fmul m32, fcos, fmul m32, fstp m32, fistp) in inline assembly, so the game's control word gives the same rounding.
- **Canned object list** [confirmed] (a definition list of `definitions.h`, 0x140 bytes, vtable `0x5ef330`, base vtable `0x5ef3d4`): the global `0x6bcfa8` is a function-local static of `0x468000` (guard bit 0 of `0x6bd108`, exit destructor `0x468090`; inlined again in four `CUseCannedAction` functions, two of which call the constructor `0x468ba0`); `0x5a3950` (outside the range, not reimplemented) fills it from the `.can` files. Own slots: 0 `0x468150`, 34 `0x468b50` (the element class, a copy of the getter), 35 `0x468c70`, 37 `0x468bf0` (`Object_CreateFromFile(<dir>/<name>.can, flags 0, written back)`), 39 `0x468d20` (`<folder>/<name>.can`); slot 40 `0x468da0` is shared by all definition lists (deletes the loaded objects through slot 1, frees the records, `RecordList_Set(0, …)`). `0x468b30` constructs an empty alias array (also called by `0x55b08a`); `0x523e20` stores the registry index (+0x2c, called by every list's `Init`).
- **Quirks kept**: `CSphereOfZinOptions::RegisterFields` writes the converter, units and help text through the first descriptor without checking its allocation; `CreateArray` takes heap memory and `InitFields` leaves the plain fields as the heap held them; `0x468220` leaves eax as the caller's (not reproduced, atexit ignores it). The getter copies `0x468230`, `0x582520`, `0x5841c0` are separate hooks with the same reimplementation.
- **Not reimplemented**: the startup registration stubs (`0x4683e0`, `0x523a20`, `0x523c20`, `0x5826d0`, `0x584420`, `0x596b60`: `push getter; mov ecx, …; call 0x417690`), like those of the earlier classes; `0x5a3950` (the list's `Init`, game flow); the `CUseCannedAction`, `CThresholdTrigger`, `CSphereOfZinEnergyInventory*`, `CWaterWarpEffect*` and `CNormalAttackAI` functions in the same ranges (Actions, Inventory and weapons, Rendering, AI); `0x584510` (the energy item's getter copy) and `0x5853f0` (slot 0 of the trigger array's vtable).
- Hooks: 1,048 installed on this branch (49 new). Not hookable: none.

Check in the VM (run `20261024-082520-44b0`, in the game thread, `reimpl/src/checks_object_classes.cpp`; side 0 with all hooks of the module taken out, side 1 through the reimplementation):

### Path classes and the A* search over the way point map [verified 2026-10-24, VM]

38 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/path_classes.cpp`, `path_classes.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the 29 functions of `0x535000`–`0x539fff` that `docs/functions.csv` counts as Core (open/named/assigned) and nine more that belong to them: the deleting destructor and slot-2 getter of `CPathCollideChecker` (`0x535ce0`, `0x535d60`, missing from `docs/functions.csv`), the exit destructor of the found path's array (`0x5357d0`), `0x536090`, `0x536f90` and `0x539af0` (the registration getters of the other three classes), `0x536450` (CPointList::AddPoint), `0x537370` (the cache's Acquire) and `0x5396c0` (empty point array).

- **Assignment** [confirmed: callers, vtables, strings]: these are not Core but the data and the search of the AI's path finding on the way point map (`CWayPointMap`, World): the CLayer keeps the level's map at +0x134 (read from the `.way` file, 936 way points and 3,514 segments in `Test/Nachbau1`), its way points (`CPathWayPoint`) are joined by `CPathLineSegment`s, a path is a `CPointList` of way point positions, `CPathPointListListCache` (alternative class name "CActivePathData") hands point lists to the paths, and a `CPathCollideChecker` answers per moving object whether a segment can be walked (slot 23) and its cost factor (slot 24). The map's path query `0x5386b0` (World) takes a list from the cache (`0x537370`) and runs the search on the function-local static `0x6d05b0` (built by `0x5354e0` on first use, exit `0x5389b0`). `docs/functions.csv` counted the classes as Core through their registration and their neighbours.
- **Layouts** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`]: `CPathCollideChecker` 8 bytes, no fields (RegisterFields the empty `0x58ea40`), vtable `0x5eebe8` (27 slots, a derived checker's vtable follows at `0x5eec54`); `CPointList` 0x1c: +8 "Is Available" (byte, default 1, not written by Create), +0xc "Point" (array of integer points, vtable `0x5f8dc4`, pool data, 8-byte elements); `CPathPointListListCache` 0x18, version 7: +8 "Point List" (pointer array of `CPointList`, vtable `0x5fc748`; FreeFields deletes the lists through their slot 1); `CPathLineSegment` 0x20: +8 "Flags" (bit 1 walkable, bit 2 checked; written by the search), +0xc "MaxPassWidth", +0x10 "Length", +0x14 "AngleAToB" (floats), +0x18 "AIndex", +0x1c "BIndex" (Create: flags 0, MaxPassWidth 0, indices −1; Length and AngleAToB keep the pool block's bytes). `CPathWayPoint` (0x24): +0xc position, +0x18/+0x1c the indices of its segments.
- **The search** [confirmed: code of `0x535610`, `0x535860`] (`ZPathSearch`, 0x54 bytes: sentinel nodes of the free, open and closed lists; nodes of 0x1c bytes {g, h, f, way point, index, parent, next}, 300 of them from operator new): `Search(mover, map, start, goal, point list, checker)` moves the open and closed nodes of the last search to the free list, opens the start (g 0, h the distance) and repeatedly expands and closes the first open node until it is the goal's (true) or nothing is open or the nodes run out (false). `Expand` visits every segment of the node's way point (count read once) whose other end (`0x53a0d0`) is not closed; an unchecked segment gets slot 23 of the checker (true = blocked) and its flags remember the answer; for a walkable one slot 24 gives the cost factor, a factor not above 0 (or NaN) skips it. g = Length · factor + the node's g, h = the table square root (`0x508c50`) of the squared integer distance to the goal. An open node of the same way point is updated (and moved) only when its f is strictly greater; a new node is inserted in front of the first node with a larger f (after equal ones); with no free node left after an insertion Expand stops with false. A found path is collected goal first in the static pointer array `0x6d0500` (built on first use, `atexit` `0x5357d0`) and appended start first to the point list.
- **Rounding** [confirmed in the VM]: every intermediate float (cost factor, g, h, f) is stored with `fstp dword` before it is compared. The first runs kept `f` in an x87 register with the extended precision: an open node whose rounded f equalled the new one was "improved" (another parent), and on a self-loop segment a node became its own parent, so building the path looped for ever (runs `20261024-081453-f0ca` to `-082452-7175`). The reimplementation now rounds through memory (`fstp_float`) wherever the original does.
- **Cache** [confirmed]: `Acquire(path)` (+0x30 the path's list) marks the old list available, takes the first available list of the cache (the count read once) or appends a new one (constructed like Create, its array through `0x5396c0`), gives it its field defaults (slot 19), removes its points, marks it in use and hands it to the path; eax the path's list after that (0 normally).
- **Helpers**: `0x536080` is the zero stub (thiscall, three arguments) in slot 10 of most classes; `0x539ac0` tests a point against an integer rectangle (right and bottom excluded; eax's upper bytes those of left or y); `0x535b60` and `0x5355d0` the squared and the table distance.
- **Not reimplemented**: the checker's slots 23–25 (`0x535dc0`, `0x535eb0`, `0x536030`; line of sight and swept collision through the layer, `0x4e8d40`/`0x4e8e00`, World), the derived checker around `0x430860`, the point list's drawing `0x536480` (Rendering), `CWayPointPath` and `CWayPointMap` (`0x536620`–`0x537e90`, World), the map's quadtree (`0x5392f0`, `0x539350`, `0x5396e0`, `0x539760`, `0x539910`), the four static registrations (`0x535db0`, `0x536300`, `0x5371f0`, `0x539cd0` through `0x417690`) and the vector helpers of `CSwirlParticleAI` (`0x535400`–`0x535440`, AI). Return values are the original's eax except where the header says undefined (`Dtor`, `FreeChain`, the exit destructor); `Search` is compared by al (its upper bytes are node or block addresses).
