The match state's own class getter `0x51bf50` (counted as Core) is left to the Core batch.

- **Classes** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, vtables, `docs/fields.csv`]: `CMultiPlayerGameType` (0xc8 bytes, class `0x6d0020`, version 0, abstract, parent `CGameType`) has its own vtable `0x5fb160`, written only by the constructor and the destructors (around `CGameType`'s `0x4ceaa0`/`0x4ceb20`); `CCaptureTheFlagGameType`, `CDeathMatchGameType` and `CSalvageKingGameType` share its slots 23, 26–29, 31, 32, 36–38, 43, 46–48 (Death Match overrides 24, all three 25). Fields: +0x18 "Max Number of Teams" (0 = "Unlimited"), +0x1c "Is Team Game", +0x1d "All Teams Share Spawn Points", +0x20/+0x24/+0x28 the actions "Have Taken/Lost/Tied For the Lead" (CAction), the mini score board +0x2c–+0x90 (six fonts, the two flag strings, x and justification of rank, flag, name, score, ping and two alternative scores, rules justification, line spacing, header spacing, top) and the end score board +0x94–+0xc4. Fonts are indices into the font list `0x6be1e0`, justifications into `0x6be1b8`. `CMultiPlayerGameData` (0x18 bytes, vtable `0x5fb104`, class `0x6d001c`): +8 "Match Is Over", +0xc "Players Ready To Start New Game", +0x10 the match time (a double, no field, not set by Create). The current one sits at +0x30 of what the application's slot 97 returns; every user fetches it again with an inlined class getter and IsKindOf.
- **The slots** [confirmed: code; names are ours, assumption: our names]: 23 starts a match (base `0x4cebb0`, a new match state – the old one is not deleted –, the team count for the net game, slot 46 for each world entity); 24 advances the time and ends the match at the time limit (rules +0x10, minutes) on the server; 26 adds to a team's score and ends the match at the frag limit (rules +0x14); 27 updates each player's lead state (+0xf8: 0 alone, 1 leads, 2 tied, 3 behind; the score is the short +0xf6) and fires the matching action when it changes; 28 assigns a joining player's team (smallest of max teams or 20 in team games, else a free player number); 29 passes its second argument to 46; 31/32 get and set the match time (not on the server); 36/37 the two bytes; 38 the rules' byte +0x19 in team games; 43 draws the mini score board (headings "Name", "Ping", "Score", one line per ranking entry, from the bottom the "Time Limit: %d Minutes" and "%s Limit: %d" lines placed by the rules justification); 46 removes a player entity; 47 switches a player between teams 0 and 1 (killed with "Unavoidable" damage of its own size, score kept, "%s changed teams"); 48 the kill message ("%s killed himself", "%s killed TEAMMATE %s", "%s killed %s"). `0x51c650` ends the match (once; the block reader `0x7144b8` sent to every connection), `0x51c800` counts players ready for the next match and at half of the connections starts it (reader `0x7144a8`, slot 23). The texts are ZStrings at `0x6cffe4`–`0x6d0018`, built by the static initialisers `0x51ca50`–`0x51cb90` and around `0x51d200` (not in `docs/functions.csv`).

### Pool allocator, CPU check and INI files, name tree and field name lists, the rest of the class info [verified 2026-10-24, VM]

81 functions are reimplemented in four modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the pool allocator (`reimpl/src/pool.cpp`, 14), the CPU check and the INI file wrappers (`platform.cpp`, 11), the name tree and the name lists of the number field kinds (`name_lists.cpp`, 21) and the remaining small functions of the object system (`core_misc.cpp`, 35). With them every function that `docs/functions.csv` counts as Core (open/named/assigned) outside the ranges the docs already identify as other subsystems is done or documented below.

- **Pool allocator** [confirmed: code, and in the VM the whole game runs on the reimplementation from the first allocation] (`0x506360`–`0x5065e0`, `0x54d130`, `0x417710`): the global pool `0x6c2d0c` is made on first use by `pool_get` (`0x506470`; guard byte `0x6196b4` is 1 in the data and cleared on first use, no `atexit`) with a largest size of 500 bytes, i.e. 126 size classes of 0x18 bytes {block size, chunk list, free list, blocks per chunk, made, used}; class i holds blocks of i · 4 bytes (class 0 blocks of 4) and grows by 4000 bytes' worth of blocks at a time (`0x506420`: a chunk of size · count + 4 bytes from operator new in front of the chunk list, its blocks linked first to last). A block of n bytes comes from class (n + 3) / 4, anything above the largest size from operator new/delete. Nothing is given back while the game runs; a class's destructor (`0x506380`) frees its chunks only when no block is out, and `0x5064b0` (referenced by no code and no table; missing from `docs/functions.csv`) would free the whole pool.
- **CPU check** [confirmed: code] (`0x5154e0`–`0x5156b0`): `Cpu_HasMmx` reads once (guard `0x6cfdc5`) the signature cpuid(1).eax & 0x3fff into `0x6cfdc0` and the MMX bit (edx bit 23, then `emms`) into `0x6cfdc4`; the renderer picks its MMX blend and copy routines with it (15 callers, Rendering). `0x515620` turns the signature into a class for the start log (Game_Startup `0x4cd949` and `0x4cdc70`–`0x4cdc90`): family 1–5 → 1, family 6 model 1/3/5/7 → 2/3/4/5, anything else 6. The original wraps cpuid and emms in SEH frames that answer 0 on a fault (CPUs before the Pentium); the reimplementation runs them directly.
- **INI files** [confirmed: code, imports] (`0x4a4610`–`0x4a47c0`): fastcall wrappers (file, section, key, …) of `GetPrivateProfileIntA`, `WritePrivateProfileStringA` and `GetPrivateProfileStringA` through the exe's import table; the section goes through `Text_SkipWhite` (`0x587aa0`) first, floats are written with `"%g"` and read back with `atof` (the default is written into the buffer that receives the value), `Ini_GetString` uses the buffer's text as the default. `0x4a4610` makes the file name `".\<name>.CFG"` (the game's `Zax.CFG`) or `"<name>CD.INI"` (Game_Startup `0x4cd90d`). Callers: the options and controls screens (User interface), actions, the renderer, multiplayer. Platform code, Core.
- **Name tree** [confirmed: code, vtable `0x5f154c`] (`0x47e560`–`0x47e9f0`; called `DefinitionList_Monitor_Ctor` before): the 0x34-byte object every definition list keeps at +0x13c and `DirList_Read` builds (17 callers) is a folder tree over the names of a named list: {vtable, list, its count, root node}; nodes (0x28 bytes, operator new) are {ZString name, heap pointer array of child nodes (vtable `0x5f156c`), heap array of entry indices (`0x5ee168`), parent}. The constructor files every name i under the folder node of its path up to the last `/` (`0x47e800` finds or makes the nodes part by part, comparing with `_strnicmp`, so folders differing only in case share a node). The vtable is a tree model whose items are entry indices (below the count) or node pointers: slot 0 the root (`0x47e910`, 4 bytes, not hookable), 1 the folder of an item (an entry's folder node, a node's parent), 2 its name (`PathName` of an entry, a node's name), 3 its number of children (entries first, then child nodes), 4 child k, 7 the deleting destructor (`0x47e670`, operator delete).
- **Name lists of the number field kinds** [confirmed: vtables, code] (`0x54f390`–`0x54fa70`, `0x5266e0`): the `FieldNameList`s of `FieldDesc_AddEnum` are named lists {vtable, pool pointer array} of entries {char *name (operator new), value} of 8 bytes (vtables `0x5fd5d8`, `0x5fdaec` and five more) or 12 bytes (`0x5fdc28`); slots 1 name, 2 find (hint, then every entry with `_stricmp`, then `NamedList_FindFileName`), 17 remove all, 18 add {copy of the name, 0}, 20 remove at (no check of the index before the entry is deleted), 21 swap, 0 the deleting destructors (pool 0x14). `0x5266e0` frees an entry's name.
- **CClassInfo** [confirmed]: the base destructor `0x4152a0` deletes the field descriptors through slot 0 (count read each time) and their array, the extra list through slot 0, frees the children's pool array and sets `ExtraList_Deleting` (`0x6bdc90`) first; the deleting destructors `0x415270`/`0x415820` (pool 0x40/0x48) only run at exit. `0x4153b0` (5 callers in actions) writes the class name without a leading `C` before an upper-case letter into a ZString and cuts a given suffix (case-insensitive) unless the name is exactly the suffix. `0x417690` is the static registration stub every class's static initializer calls (getter, then `ClassRegistry_Add(class, 0)`). The descriptor setters `0x419020`/`0x419030`/`0x419060` assign help, alternative name and units, `0x419040` sets the inherited flag.
- **Field values in dynamic properties** [confirmed: code; checked in the VM]: `0x415f50`/`0x54d630`/`0x54ede0` return the value of a string/int/float field from the object's dynamic properties (`0x417320`) or the descriptor's default (+0x2c, +0x34); `0x415f80`, `0x54d660`, `0x54ee10` set it (`0x417340` adds the value; the string kind hands a ZString by value to `0x4161d0`, the number kinds call the setter at +0x38 with the dynamic block or store the value, the float one through fld/fstp, so a signalling NaN is stored quiet). The dynamic value is a block of the value's size (+0x14) addressed with the descriptor's offset, so these helpers only make sense for descriptors whose offset is 0 (the dynamic properties of the extra lists) [confirmed: code of `0x482970`, `0x419070`]. `0x415ef0` is the string kind's copy constructor (callers in actions and the world), `0x54d440` a zeroed array of n dwords (slot of the vtables `0x5fd40c`, `0x601cc8`).
- **Class getters with an inlined parent getter** [confirmed]: `CItemTypeData` `0x4242b0` (with its deleting destructor `0x424230`, single and array), `CMultiPlayerGameData` `0x51bf50`, and the eight quest statistics classes `0x5557f0`–`0x55aa30` (`CQuestCounterData`, `CQuestFloatAccumulatorData`, `CQuestTimeData`, `CQuestPercentageData` and their `…ParScore` twins), which register their abstract parent `CQuestStatData` (`0x712324`) or `CQuestStatParScoreData` (`0x712320`, both 8 bytes, Create `0x46b760`, CreateArray `0x52dc80`, no fields) on the way: the class's block is taken first, the parent's after it. `0x585380` casts an object to `CSphereOfZinData` (getter inlined), `0x5853f0` is the trigger array's deleting destructor (slot 0 of `0x601374`; the data is deleted through slot 1 of its first element with flags 3), `0x4d4cc0` `CHueRemapHolder`'s constructor. These belong to their classes' subsystems (Inventory, Multiplayer, Quests) but are plain object system code.
- **Definition list bases** [confirmed: vtables `0x5ed564`, `0x5ed4b4`/`0x5ed5f4`, `0x5ed530`/`0x5ed670`]: `0x41e830` is the resource list's deleting destructor (aliases, pool 0x30), `0x41e940` the definition list base's (like `0x46a890`, but the loaded objects are deleted through slot 0, base vtable `0x5ed5f4`), `0x41ec30` unloads one entry (slot 0 of its object, then object, keep, in use and loading cleared). `0x47e540` destroys three ZStrings (+0xc, +8, +0; caller `0x47bfe0`).
- **Not reimplemented, with reasons**: not hookable (shorter than 5 bytes or a relative jump in the first 5): `0x415680` (`mov eax, [ecx+0x2c]`), `0x4186e0` (`ret 4`), `0x47e910`, `0x4dec80` (`ZString_EmptyBufferAtExit`, `ret`), `0x4011e0`, `0x46cd50`, `0x5007a0`, `0x5007b0`, `0x579c00`, `0x419050` (`add ecx, 0x1c` + `jmp`), `0x5c2070` (a `jmp` thunk); `0x4ceb60` forwards to slot 14 of `g_App` with the caller's arguments (application, its signature unknown). Not Core, although `docs/functions.csv` counts them through their neighbours: `0x4d4a50`–`0x4d4ce0` (a cache of colour tables keyed by six floats, `0x43bfe0`/`0x43c0b0`, Rendering; only the `CHueRemapHolder` constructor `0x4d4cc0` among them is done), `0x4de5e0`–`0x4de790` (destructor and two methods of a window class with vtable `0x5f86d0`, base destructor `0x402f00`, items made by `0x40f9b0`; User interface), `0x4e74a0`–`0x4e79b0` (the layer's update of its object grid through `CSortList2D_QueryRect`/`Process` and a dispatch over `g_World`'s players by object flags, World), `0x525a60`–`0x525ba0` (a stream reader on a `FileBuf` with the decoder functions `0x5c3ce0`–`0x5c4e40`, Sound [confirmed later: the Ogg Vorbis reader's slots `OggStream_*`, code `0x525a60`, reimpl/src/sound_ogg_c5.cpp; VM]), `0x57be20` (the sound manager's deleting destructor, Sound), `0x47ee70`/`0x47ef10` (GameSpy answers, Multiplayer), `0x506320`/`0x506350` (callers in the window toolkit and the AI, not part of the pool).
- Hooks: 1,167 installed on this branch (81 new).

Check in the VM (run `20261024-143716-a50c`, in the game thread, `checks_pool.cpp`, `checks_platform.cpp`, `checks_name_lists.cpp`, `checks_core_misc.cpp`; side 0 the original (the pool through its trampolines, the other modules with all their hooks taken out), side 1 the reimplementation):
- Pool, 1,032: 300 sequences on size classes of our own (SetSize 0–600, SetChunkBytes, Grow, Alloc, Free, the destructor with blocks out or none; eax with block pointers as chunk and offset, the whole free list after every step), 130 sequences on pools of our own with largest sizes 0–1000 (every class after every Alloc/Free, `0x5064b0` with the test pool in the global for the duration of the call), `pool_get`, and `operator_new_ecx`/`pool_delete` of both sides crossed for every size 0–600 on the real pool (a freed block comes back from the other side, the used counts stay balanced).
- CPU and INI files, 1,722: signature and MMX test (whole eax), the CPU class for 768 signatures in the global and 200 random ones, `Cpu_HasMmx` detected and not; 400 random sequences of the six INI wrappers on one temp file per side (ints from the whole range, floats with zeros, NaNs, infinities, denormals and huge values, string buffers of 1–40 bytes; returns, Ini_GetFloat's double bits, buffers and the files' bytes), `Ini_FileName` with 12 names and both flags; **real data**: all 108 keys of the game's `Zax.CFG` read through both sides as int, float and string. Writing to an empty section name (`""`) ended the game inside kernel32 in the first runs (`20261024-142945-ac63`, `20261024-143344-6960`, through the original wrapper as well); the game never uses one, so the check leaves it out.

### Net game, net session, block readers, DirectPlay game side [verified 2026-10-24, VM; DirectPlay and GameSpy with fakes only]

65 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/net_game.cpp`, `net_session.cpp`, `dplay.cpp` with their headers; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the GameSpy query answers, player and team helpers and the traffic graph's drawing and update (`0x51f180`–`0x520150`, 20), the net session, the local net layer and the block readers' accessors, write functions and sound tables (`0x4f78a0`–`0x4f9530`, 36) and the game side of the DirectPlay 8 net game (`0x47ee70`–`0x480a70`, 9). Not hookable and therefore left with the original: `0x51f450` (player count), `0x5203b0` (packet length), `0x5203c0` (the packet's flag), all 4 bytes, and `0x4f7ee0` (`xor cl, cl; jmp 0x4e9d90`, a relative jump in 7 bytes). That closes the 69 open multiplayer functions of the three ranges.

- **Net game** [confirmed: code of the functions and of their callers `0x47ee70`, `0x47eed0`, `0x47f0b0`, `0x480bd0`; names ours, assumption: our names]: the DirectPlay net game (vtable `0x5f15a8`) has +4 the game type (slots 15–18 add the GameSpy keys of the type, 2 receives a message, 9/10 a player joined/left, 20 makes a player, 21 a team), +8 the settings (+0x0c max players, +0x10 time limit, +0x14 frag limit, +0x18 dedicated), +0x10 the players (heap pointer array, vtable `0x5fb558`) and +0x20 the teams (vtable `0x5fb54c`) and +0x30 the GameSpy state text. **The players are net sessions** (`NetSession`, `0x4f7c50`): +0x0c id, +0x14 team, +0x1c the player settings whose first member is the name. Teams are named values (name, score). `NetGame_FreePlayerSlot` (`0x51f560`) actually returns the first team index below 20 no player has.
- **GameSpy** [confirmed]: the answers append `"\key\value"` with `ZString::AppendFormat` (eax undefined except the team answer, which returns the team count). `GameSpy_Start` builds the secret key `"J3An3s"` byte by byte on the stack and calls the qr SDK linked into the exe (`0x5c82a0` with the query port 0x68aa, the game name `"zax"`, the bind address read through the config object `0x6bd330` (`0x46ec70`, `"Net Game"`/`"Bind Host to IP Address"`) only when longer than one character, the four answer callbacks `0x51ef40`–`0x51f0f0`). The SDK itself (`0x5c5000`–`0x5c9fff`) stays as it is (in this batch; reimplemented in phase 5b, section 11, "GameSpy SDK (2001), reimplemented").
- **Traffic graph** [confirmed]: `Draw` places graph `index` at x = (6 − index mod 6)·90, y = (index/6 − graphs/6)·75 + 390, shifts the samples (the original copies 4·samples − 1 bytes and so reads 3 bytes behind each array, which the new sample overwrites), keeps the highest sample of all graphs in `0x61caf0` as the scale (unsigned 32-bit `imul`/`div`), draws through slot 51 of the surface and `0x4b33f0`, the labels in the font `"Small Blue"` (the resource list's inlined `Get`, `resource_list_get`). `Update` (fastcall: surface, net layer; &"all traffic" graph) only clears the counters while the graphs are off (`0x6d00ec`), keeps the "all traffic" graph only while more than two players exist (created inline like `0x51f8e0`), and which packet counts as sent depends on slot 12 of the error reporter's slot 1 object.
- **Block readers** [confirmed: the registration names, the reads in the vtables]: twelve static readers (`0x6c2910`–`0x6c2990`, list in `net_session.h`), each with an initialiser, an accessor (`mov eax, reader; ret`), a vtable of three slots (the read is slot 2; the reads are not in `docs/functions.csv` and stay with the original in this batch; reimplemented later, section 8, "The game's own behaviours and CCameraTrakerAI with the client block readers, …" and "Phase 3 remains, band B") and a write function (thiscall on the reader, not virtual). `0x4f7bf0` registers the client's five, `0x4f93e0` seven registrations of other subsystems and then the server's seven; slot 106 of the world (`0x5a2c80`) runs them on a new session's packets. The config control write turns two floats in [−1, 1] into words ((v + 1)·65535·0.5 on the FPU, NaN and below 0 → 0, above 65535 → 65535, `__ftol`).
- **Sound tables** of `CClientPlaySoundBlockReader` (`0x6c2960`, 0x28 bytes) [confirmed]: two heap pointer arrays (vtable `0x5f9288`) of 20-byte entries {id, array (vtable `0x5f9294`) of {byte channel, sound}}: +8 the free channels, +0x18 the playing sounds. `FreeChannel` restarts its scan at the second element after every hit (as in the original, so a channel equal to element 0 after a restart is not seen); `Add` sets the id only after appending the new entry and takes the sound of the id from the sound manager `0x713708` (`0x57e650`, then the replacement `0x57b630`) only when asked; the deleting destructor frees the arrays but not their entries.
- **Net session** (0xec bytes, vtable `0x5f91c8`) [confirmed]: base, +0x38/+0x39, two packets (+0x3c, +0x70: slots 13 and 12 of the net layer), the traffic graph +0xa4, +0xd8 1.0f, +0xdc the level index of the local player (`0x4f1050`), a ZString +0xe4, +0xe8 the key binding object of 0x1c8 bytes from slot 41 of the world (`0x59c550`; destructor `0x46f2f0`, freed to the pool). **NetLocal** (vtable `0x5f91d4`, base `0x5fb484`): the net layer the world creates once through slot 44 (`0x5a33e0`, derived vtable `0x602fa8`, global `0x713f18`) – it also exists in single player.
- **DirectPlay** [confirmed: imports, slot numbers, message ids; interface and message names after the DirectPlay 8 headers: assumption, the code has only slot numbers and ids]: the server, client and address objects are the globals `0x6bdc2c`/`0x6bdc30`/`0x6bdc34`; all COM calls go through the same slots as in the original (Release 2, Initialize 3 with the trampoline `0x47ead0`, EnumServiceProviders 4, GetClientInfo 9, ReturnBuffer server 25 / client 15). The message handler keeps 100 player slots of 12 bytes at +0x44c {added, removed, dpnid, session} (lock `0x6bdbf0`) and a queue of received messages at +0x43c (20 bytes {context, sender, data, size, handle}, lock `0x6bdc08`, DPNSUCCESS_PENDING keeps the buffer). Quirks kept: a new player gets the highest free slot from **100** down to 2 – slot 100 is the "slots changed" byte +0x8fc and the dword +0x900, one past the array; a player context of 0 at create player is ignored; a null session or provider name makes the original use its stack buffer as it is (stale bytes); a session in two slots would be searched as index −1 (`data[-1]`).

### Checks in the game thread

The ZString and descriptor tests allocate from the pool, which is not thread-safe. So the check thread only raises a flag after `CheckAfterMs`, and the reimplemented `ZString` constructor runs the checks in the exe's main thread (found with Toolhelp in `DllMain`; the launcher loads the DLL from a separate thread while the main thread is still suspended). In a running level the main thread can go for long stretches without constructing a string; opening the menu (ESC) triggers it reliably.

Check in the VM, test level `Test/Nachbau1`, ESC after 30 s (first batch: run `20261022-172404`):
- `CClassInfo` checks as before (all identical), class table identical with `/Original`.
- ZString: 1,581 cases (5 start states × 8 operations × 8 texts, several n) against the original via trampolines. Compared are text, capacity, reference count, use of the empty buffer, whether the buffer stayed the same, and the reference counts of the partner and source strings and of the empty buffer. All identical.
- Field descriptors: 256 cases (8 names × 4 units) for the constructor, copy constructor, destructor and deleting destructor. All identical. Clone and delete of all 7,592 registered fields: base part identical, reference counts balanced.
- Screenshot after 25 s without the check thread: the reimplementation differs from `/Original` only at the one Korbo whose animation frame depends on timing. That is the same region (1301–1498, 659–873) in which earlier runs differ among themselves. The new `/Original` run is pixel-identical to an earlier one.

Correction: in these runs (`20261022-172028` to `-172404`) the game ended shortly after the checks; it went unnoticed because the log was complete. The cause was in the checks, not in the reimplementation: a diagnostic text was written with `wsprintfA` (no size limit) into a 120-byte stack buffer, and the long test name overflowed it. Found by switching the test groups off one by one; all diagnostic buffers are bounded now.

### Way point map, path, way points, way point polygons [verified 2026-10-24, VM]

79 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/waypoint_map.cpp`, `waypoint_map.h`, hook table `waypoint_map_hooks.inc` generated from the exe's bytes; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the way point classes `CWayPointPath` (`0x5365d0`–`0x536f70`), `CWayPointMap` with its quadtree, building, path query and `.way` slots (`0x537440`–`0x539910`), the methods of `CPathLineSegment` (`0x53a010`–`0x53a0f0`) and `CPathWayPoint` (`0x53a200`–`0x53a8c0`), `CWayPointsPolygon` (`0x598d90`–`0x5992e0`) and the zero stub `0x53bbc0` (slot 25 of the polygon, counted as AI). Eight of them are missing from `docs/functions.csv`: the static registrations `0x5365d0` and `0x53a200` and the six exit destructors of the function-local statics `0x5389b0`, `0x5389c0`, `0x538a50`, `0x538da0`, `0x5392a0`, `0x539670`.

- **Layouts** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`]: `CWayPointPath` 0x34 bytes (vtable `0x5fc690`, class `0x6d065c`, version 3, alternative class name "CFindPathParams"): +8 "Start Point", +0x10 "End Point" (integer points), +0x18 "Length", +0x1c "Max Dist To Travel", +0x20 "Num Failed Paths", +0x24 "Max Failed Paths", +0x28 "Pos To Move Index", +0x2c "Dist So Far", +0x30 "Path" (reference to the `CPointList` from the cache). `CWayPointMap` 0x34 (vtable `0x5fc760`, class `0x6d0664`, version 8, alternative name "CPathData"): +8 the way points and +0x18 the segments (owned pointer arrays, vtables `0x5fc7c8`/`0x5fc7bc`, destroyed as `0x5fc7d4`/`0x5fc7e0`), +0x28 "MinDistBetweenWayPoints" (default 30), +0x2c "MaxDistToConnect" (default 59), +0x30 the quadtree root (no field: slot 13/15 write and read the arrays). `CPathWayPoint` 0x24 (vtable `0x5fc86c`): +8 "Flags", +0xc "Position X", +0x10 "Position Y", +0x14 the segment indices (int array, vtable `0x5fc8c8`). `CWayPointsPolygon` 0x78 (vtable `0x602b2c`, version 2, parent `CFreeRangePoly`): +0x74 "Insertion Priority" (typed resource field over the list `0x713dd8`, default "Secondary"); RegisterFields hides 15 inherited fields ("Name", "Child List", "Visible", "Is Collidable", "Active", "Half Height", "Full Height", "Stationary", "Is Temporarily Excluded", "Is Marked For Deletion", "Activity", "Category", "Has Hit Points", "Broadcaster", "Current Target") by emptying their name and clearing +0x18.
- **Quadtree** [confirmed: code]: nodes of 0x20 bytes {x, y, way point index, parent, four children}; the children split by the node's position: +0x10 x ≥ and y ≥, +0x14 x < and y ≥, +0x18 x < and y <, +0x1c x ≥ and y <. New nodes go in as leaves (`0x538df0`, `0x537ae0`). The range query `0x539760` (the root level inlined three times) appends the indices inside a rectangle (right and bottom excluded) and visits the children with the rectangle cut at the node. `0x5392f0` finds a position exactly (0x7fffffff when none), `0x539350` the nearest way point within a distance (unsigned squared distances, starting from d² + 2 so the final test against d² can still fail; with a mover only way points whose line is free).
- **Building** (`0x5383f0`, called by `0x4eca80` with the world's slots 66, 62, 63, 65, 64; in `Test/Nachbau1` offset 20, MinDist 20, MaxDistToConnect 39.8, max offset 79.6 (2 × 39.8 as floats; "79.8" before 2026-10-29 was a slip), step 5) [confirmed: code; values logged by the check]: the map is cleared, MinDist/MaxDistToConnect truncated from the arguments, the free test uses 0.74 × MinDist. The layer's way point polygons (grid query by class, flags 0x200000 without 0x9d0000) are walked in two passes by Insertion Priority (0, then 1): every outline unshifted, then for offset, offset + step, … below half the max offset shifted out and in by that much (`0x538230`). An outline vertex (`0x537e90`) is the intersection (`0x5093d0`) of the two neighbouring edges moved along their normals, clamped to the distance from the end of the first edge (a miter limit). Points are placed along every edge at steps of at most 0.9 × MaxDistToConnect (`0x5380d0`); a point becomes a way point when no collidable part holds the circle (`0x537d40`: grid query kind 3, flags 0x840000 without 0x190000, doors skipped, `0x5469c0`) and no way point is within MinDist. A new way point is joined (`0x538ae0` → `0x53a780`) to all within MaxDistToConnect; the skipped entry is the list position equal to the index (the self loops of the `.way` files, FORMATS.md 4). A segment between two way points is reused when the other end lists it (and then appended to both lists again).
- **Path query** (`0x5386b0`, from the AI at `0x4305d3`) [confirmed: code]: the path's point list from the cache (`0x537370`), false above the length `0x5fc7f4`; with a free line of sight (`0x537960`: the line moved by the mover's offset, swept through the layer's collision `0x4e8e00` while the mover's flag 0x2000000 is set) the two end points are the path. Otherwise the way point for each end: an existing one within 4, a temporary one (static nodes `0x6d0560`/`0x6d0630`) when one is within MaxDistToConnect, else an existing one within 4 × MaxDistToConnect; the A* search between them (`0x535610`); the temporary way points and the segments added since are removed again (`0x5385b0` → `0x538f80`). `0x536e70` then smooths the path while walking (points whose neighbours see each other are dropped).
- **`.way` slots** [confirmed]: the map's slot 13 writes the way point count and each way point (Object_WriteBinary), then the segments; slot 15 reads them, the way points straight into the quadtree without joining. The way point's slots write and read the segment indices.
- **Rounding and NaNs** [confirmed in the VM]: the geometry keeps the original's mix of extended and rounded intermediates (products with x components stay in the FPU, the y ones are stored as floats first; `fild qword` of MaxDistToConnect; `__ftol` on extended values; `fistp` with the current rounding mode); the reimplementation rounds through memory (`fstp dword`) exactly where the original does. With two NaN operands of equal significand the x87 keeps the destination operand's, so `0x537e90` takes the original's operand roles and instruction forms through small inline-asm helpers (`add_r`, `add_m`, `mul_m`, …): clang had swapped them and a negative default NaN came out positive (run `20261024-164955-0552`). Under the VM's x86 emulation (Windows on ARM) a NaN memory operand of `fadd m32` also lost its payload (`0xfff94fe3` became the ARM default NaN `0x7fc00000`, run `20261024-164512-212a`), so the fake shapes of the check use default NaNs only.
- **Return values**: the original's eax, except where the header says only al or undefined (`FindPath`, `FindNearest` without a tree, `Draw` without a list, the exit destructors).
- **Not reimplemented**: `CFreeRangePoly` (`0x4b5c60`–, layer part batch), the grid queries, the temporary part lists `0x59a0f0`–`0x59a510`, the collision helpers `0x4e8e00`, `0x5469c0`, `0x545a20`, `0x5093d0`, `0x509100` (atan2), the derived collide checker `0x430860`/`0x430890`, `0x4eca80`/`0x4ec520` (loading and saving the `.way`), the drawing `0x536480`, the static registration stubs through `0x417690`. The rest of `0x598000`–`0x59bfff` (`0x599300`–: `CWeaponDischargedMessage`, `CWindowedBrowsableImage`, the part lists, `World_StartNewGame`) is not way point code.
- Hooks: 1338 installed on this branch (79 new).

Check in the VM (run `20261024-165554-9159`, in the game thread, `reimpl/src/checks_waypoint_map.cpp`; side 0 with all hooks of the module taken out, side 1 through the reimplementation):

### Polygons, the collision sweep, the CLayerPart helpers and the layer parts' multiplayer blocks [verified 2026-10-24, VM]

93 functions are reimplemented in two modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names and details in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`):
- `reimpl/src/polygon.cpp`, `polygon.h` (43): all polygon functions of `0x545620`–`0x547d60` except the drawing, the segment intersection `0x5093d0` and the layer's sweep `0x4e8e00`/`0x4e8d40`. Shared x87 building blocks in `reimpl/src/x87.h`.
- `reimpl/src/layer_part_helpers.cpp`, `layer_part_helpers.h` (50): the non-virtual `CLayerPart` helpers `0x4fa960`, `0x4faf50`–`0x4fc8c0` that were still open, the multiplayer blocks `0x4faa10`/`0x4faa40` (CLayerPart) and `0x5716f0`/`0x571780` (CSimpleLayerPart).

- **POLY2D** (0x28 bytes, the value of the polygon field kind) [confirmed: code]: +0 points (count × {x, y}, a closed outline repeats its first point), +4 edges (count − 1 × {unit normal (dy, −dx)/length, (0, 1) for a zero edge; length}), +8 count, +0xc left/top/right/bottom (floor of the minimum and ceiling of the maximum through `0x509340`/`0x5093a0`, rounded with `fistp`, right/bottom one more when equal to left/top), +0x1c flags (bit 0: the outline turns both ways; bit 1: the turns between consecutive edge angles add up to within 2 of +2π), +0x20 the mean of the points without the last one (x snapped to 0 within ±0.05). Every setter recomputes rectangle/mean (`0x5460b0`) and edges/flags (`0x546240`); moving (`0x546070`) only the first. The setters `0x545d50`/`0x546580` copy through the 25-point buffer `0x711120`; inserting (`0x5466c0`) stops at 25 points. The binary form (`0x545fa0`) is the 12-byte header "POLY2D\0", a byte 7 and the count, then the points; the points are freed before the header is checked (a wrong header keeps the count with no points).
- **Tests** [confirmed: code]: inside (`0x546830`) is the rectangle, then the winding of the outline around the point counted in quadrant steps (a two-quadrant step decided by where the edge crosses the point's row), ±4 inside; the circle test `0x5469c0` widens the rectangle by r, then inside or an edge within r (`0x546c70`, which runs the segment/circle test `0x545620` per edge and writes the distance into its own argument slot of r). `0x545620` projects the centre on the segment (no contact beyond −r … length + r), inside the segment the perpendicular distance decides (its normal from the foot point; when the centre lies on the line, perpendicular² ≤ 0.0001, the direction's perpendicular, read through the pointers, so a normal output aliasing the direction gives (d.y, −d.y)), outside the distances to the end points. The two segment intersections differ: `0x5093d0` (fastcall, the point, range tests switchable, parallel below |0.01|), `0x5476b0` (thiscall on the share, range tests always, the first sign test on the unrounded denominator, parallel below |0.0001|). `0x547920` is the smaller root of the circle contact (double root within 0.00001).
- **Sweep** [confirmed: code]: the movement object (0x38 bytes, vtable `0x5f8ba8` whose slots `0x4e96b0`–`0x4e9c80` are CLayer code; +4 kind, +8 movement, +0x10 direction, +0x18 length, +0x1c "notify") and the 9-dword result (+0 share, starts at 1; +4 movement until the contact; +0xc normal; +0x14 position). `0x547230` sweeps a point against the edges facing the movement: touching within 1.01 now (share dist − 1, the normal in its own local, not in the edge direction), the crossing with the edge shifted out by its normal, or the first contact with a radius-1 circle around an end point; `0x547a30` sweeps the points of one polygon (for an open outline the last point's second edge is read one past the edge array, as in the original); `0x547bb0` both ways, the reverse result turned around; `0x547d60` overlap (points inside, points within 0.5, a shared start point, crossing edges). `0x4e8e00` (a method of the layer's +0x3c object, its +0x14 the grid) queries the swept rectangle (kind 3, all 0x840000 or +0x8000000 for sweep kind 2, none | 0x2000000, any or +0xc000000 for kind 1), filters with the mover, a fastcall filter, both parts' slot 65 and the sweep's slot 0, sweeps against the part's polygon (slot 48) at its offset (slot 50); slot 66 lets the mover pass (slot 67 tells the part when the sweep notifies), otherwise the nearest contact is kept and the part hit is told at the end with the normal reversed. `0x4e8d40` does the same for a point with the one-point polygon `0x6c1b38`.
- **CLayerPart helpers** [confirmed: code]: the "centre" used by most of them is the polygon's mean + the offset (slots 48/50) or the position (slot 43), inlined everywhere in the original (`0x4fb0a0` is its out-of-line copy). Distances (`0x4fbf60`, `0x4fc020`, `0x4fc090`) multiply dy by a y scale (callers pass 1 or the oval ratio 0.712766); angles (`0x4fb0f0` and its part/turn variants) use the exe's table functions `0x509100` and `0x508fe0`, which stay in the exe; the turn subtracts the facing (`CEntityAnimated` +0xc4, otherwise slot 46). The nearest-part query `0x4fc390` searches the grid square around the rounded centre from the last entry, below r² and within an angle in (0, π). The activity helpers append through the array's slot 2, mark AIs done at +8 and delete through slot 1; the "last element" shortcut of the remove functions compares the count with −1 unsigned and is dead code. `0x4fbba0` adopts AIs hung on the part as the dynamic pointer property `[0x6c299c]` (chained through `[0x6c29dc]`). The child list is created on first use (`0x4fc710`); `0x4fc7e0` takes a list without setting parents.
- **Multiplayer blocks** [confirmed: code]: CLayerPart writes one bool "stationary" (this part and its top parent) and reads it back as flags 0x8a20000/0x8820000; CSimpleLayerPart adds x and y as words (truncated, plus slots 52/53 of parents of the class `0x487620`) and reads them back as signed words. The readers read into argument slots that still hold the packet pointer and the saved this pointer when nothing is left, as the original does.
- **Rounding** [confirmed in the VM]: the code keeps the original's mix of extended and float intermediates, `fstp dword` exactly where the original stores, `fistp` with the current rounding mode, `__ftol` where the original truncates, wrapping integer sums (huge coordinates give the `fistp` value 0x80000000; signed overflow in C++ would let the compiler reorder the comparisons, the first runs differed there).
- **Return values**: the original's eax where the callers can see it; al where the original leaves status words or other upper bytes; not reproduced: `0x547920`'s root count (its only caller ignores it), `0x4faa10`, the early exits of `0x5466c0`.
- **Not reimplemented**: the drawing `0x546d40` (outline and point numbers through the canvas and the error reporter's font), the static initializer `0x5470f0` of the ten polygon pairs (not in `docs/functions.csv`; their atexit destructor `0x547130` is done), the table functions `0x509100`, `0x508fe0`, `0x509340`, `0x5093a0` and the small vector helpers `0x548430`, `0x548470`, `0x4ee8c0`, `0x493ef0` (the module has its own inlined copies). Hooked without a trampoline (shorter than 5 bytes or a jump): `0x4fa960`, `0x4fbf20`.

- **CModel** [confirmed: constructor, destructor, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`, `zax-formats/docs/FORMATS.md` 6]: 0xc4 bytes, vtable `0x5facdc`, class `0x6cfdd4`, version 193, no parent. The layout is in `models.h`: the 27 fields, +0x48/+0x4c/+0x68 the sequences (count, `CRotationSequence` objects of 0x6c bytes from the pool, their names as a `new[]` ZString array), +0x6c the path "Models/…/-<name>" (the counted text after the fields), +0x78 the embedded bounds polygon, +0xb4 a resource handle pointing at the model, +0xc0 the stream buffer kept after loading (the frames point into it; Clear gives them back through `0x56bb40` first). The constructor sets Sorting Y to the bottom of the empty polygon's box (0). A `.mdl` file is an object file: the fields, then slot 15 (count; none: false; the path; per sequence a byte "present", the name – in a stream holding the whole file a counted text read in place –, the sequence object); slot 13 writes the same. Load builds "Cache/<folder>/<name>" + ".mdl"/".mdl16" (8/16 bit) or the dash path with ".mdl24"/".mdl32", by the colour depth of a surface or of the display (`0x55d030`); it returns true also when the file does not open. Sequence references (+0x50) are followed while flag bit 9 (+0x1c) is set (`0x517410`, `0x517460`). The turn speed in radians (`0x517510`) is left unrounded in st(0).
- **Model list** [confirmed]: a definition list (0x140 bytes, vtable `0x5fad44`, base vtable `0x5fadec`) in the global `0x6cfdd8` (1,119 records in the game), built by a static initializer, not a function-local static; slot 37 loads a new CModel, slot 41 returns the factory `0x518230` of the editor's model preview.
- **Entity_CreateFromModel** [confirmed: code; checked with real models]: (model index, fallback class, creator, a, b): an index beyond the end means record 0, a record not yet loaded is loaded (`0x55e090`); a clone of the model's Default Entity (Object_Clone with a, b), else a new object of the class (its slot 27, then slot 19). Then slot 58 with 0x200000 (Stationary), slot 46, for a CEntityAnimated the model index (slot 93) and its angle (slot 104), for every object the default sequence (`0x48b120`, 0 when that gives -1) and slot 69 with the creator (Created By). A non-animated object still gets slot 93 and the sequence calls (as in the original). `CSpawnableModel`'s slot 23 (two arguments, the second unused) makes a CEntity of its "Model" (none for index 0).
- **Map caching** [confirmed: code, strings; checked with a fake world]: `CSwappedLayerFilenameMappingTable` maps a level's partial name to temp files ("Current Temp File" written during the mission, "Mission Temp File" from the last mission start; GetTempFileName with the exe's base name). Without a mapping a layer comes from "Levels/<name>.zax"; an expired mapping loads the level "Expired Error" with a warning; saving into an expired mapping or loading/saving one without files ends the game. Expire marks the mapping (made with the name plus ".zax") and puts the loaded layer on the unload list; Flush (not for the current layer: a warning) moves it from the LRU list (the layers' save data, a CLayer's +0x3c) to the flush list. The per-frame Update (`0x589db0`) flushes the oldest of more than 3 cached layers, unloads (`0x4f3490`) and saves (`0x4f4380`) the listed layers, and on a pending mission start turns the current files into mission files and makes a new marker file (the application's slot 109); RestartMission (`0x589cc0`) drops what happened since (slot 110). The inlined pointer searches never take their shortcut for the last element (a `jbe` against -1): plain searches. FlushAll loops for ever on a name without a loaded layer, as in the original.
- **COtherMapList** [confirmed]: 0x18 bytes, vtable `0x5ed780`, class `0x62e938`, parent CObject: "ActionList" of `COtherMapAction` (+8 the action, +0xc the map). `0x41f6c0` (instigator, map) fires the actions for a map (slot 23 through `0x41a740`) and removes them; `0x41f780` counts, `0x41f7d0` removes.
- **Not reimplemented**: CModel's static field "Model AI" (`0x516d10`, `0x516d60`, `0x516d70`; the startup registration adds it to CAIBase), the editor's model preview (vtable `0x5fae90`: `0x5179b0`, `0x517a40`, `0x517a80`, drawing `0x517c60`, `0x517f20`, `0x518080`, `0x518230`–`0x5182c0`; user interface and rendering) and the jump thunk `0x517810` (slot 34).

### World update and object placement: part queries, Entity_PlaceNear, bounce, shake and views, multiplayer sounds [verified 2026-10-24, VM]

21 functions of `0x4e8000`–`0x4ebfff` are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/world_update.cpp`, `world_update.h`, hook table `world_update_hooks.inc` generated from the exe's bytes with capstone; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`): the dirty marks `World_MarkDynamicDirty` `0x4e8810`, the part queries `0x4eb050`, `0x4eb1c0`, `0x4eb200`, `0x4ebbc0`, `0x4e9e60`, `Entity_PlaceNear` `0x4eb7b0`, the bounce `0x4e91e0`/`0x4e96c0`, the entity type fix `0x4e97c0`, the shake and view update `0x4e9f70`, `0x4ea220`, `0x4ea350`, `0x4ea6e0` and the multiplayer sound and position packets `0x4ea880`–`0x4eaf80`. Names other than `World_MarkDynamicDirty` and `Entity_PlaceNear` are [assumption: ours] from what the code does.

- **Part queries** [confirmed: code; checked with real parts]: `0x4eb050` (thiscall on the layer: part, point, preferred class, all, none) takes the parts of kind 3 in the bounding rectangle (`0x546ad0`) of the part's shape moved to the point minus the part's offset (slot 43 − position `0x4fb0a0`), keeps those that collide both ways (slot 66 false and slot 65 true, each way) and whose shape overlaps (`0x4fc620`), and returns the first of the preferred class, otherwise the last one found; `0x4eb1c0` is it at the part's own position. `0x4eb200` (part, from, angle, half width, distance, all, none) builds a corridor of the direction (`0x508fe0` sin/cos) with half width + `0x5f8de4` and length distance · `0x5eee2c`; its four corners stay in the function-local static `0x6c1cb0`–`0x6c1ccc` (guard `0x6c1c88`, empty destructor `0x4eb660`), the rectangle around them (min/max with the original's fcom tests, `fistp`) is queried with kind 2; the nearest part ahead (positive dot product), whose shape radius (`0x546a90`) + half width exceeds its distance to the centre line and that collides both ways, wins. `0x4ebbc0` (fastcall: part in ecx, layer in edx or null for the part's own) sweeps the move a → b (both minus the part's offset: x with the extended difference, y with the rounded one) through the layer's collision `0x4e8e00` with the part's flag 0x2000000 set (slots 58/59; the old bit put back). `0x4e9e60` (x, y) returns the definition's +0x5c of an entity at the point (`0x4ed350`, 0x2000000 excluded) or the +0x48 of the tile map's `CGroundTextureFrame` there (`0x541fd0`).
- **Entity_PlaceNear** [confirmed: code; checked]: the part is put at the reference's position (`0x4fb680`, slot 39). A random angle in [−π/7, π/6] (`0x55c550` on the game's generator `0x7124c0`) plus an animated reference's facing (+0xc4 when it is a `CEntityAnimated`) gives the direction. While a blocker (`0x4eb050` with all 0x840000, none 0x2000000) is at the part or the way from the reference is blocked for the larger of the two shapes (`0x4ebbc0`), the part tries six directions (0, ±1, ±2, 3 steps of `0x5eecc8` · `0x5eeea0` around the angle, wrapped by 2π; for an animated reference scaled by (atan2(√(d²/s² − 1), 1) + `0x5ee000`) · `0x5f8de8` with the table square root `0x508c50` and `0x509100`) on a ring of distance d, starting at the sum s of both radii and growing by the part's radius per ring; at the maximum distance it goes back to the reference. Then the part leaves its old layer (its monitor entry is removed inline as in `0x4e73c0`, then the grid) and is inserted into this layer's grid (eax: `CSortList2D_Insert`'s).
- **Bounce** [confirmed: code; checked with fakes]: `0x4e96c0` (on the save data: mover, result, arg) gets the motion from the mover's slot 94 into a fresh `0x545a00` object (0x38 bytes, vtable `0x5f8ba8`: +8 move, +0x20 velocity, +0x28 friction, +0x2c bounce, +0x30 damping, +0x34 minimum speed [names: assumption, ours]), does nothing for a zero move and runs `0x4e91e0` from the position +0x4c; after a hit slot 95 with the result, slot 41 to the new position and slot 67 (part hit, hit point, normal, 0), otherwise slot 41 back to +0x100; al 0. `0x4e91e0` sweeps a copy of the motion up to five times through `0x4e8e00` (the hit record 0x24 bytes, `0x545c90` sets t = 1): after a hit the position moves by the free part, the rest of the move and the velocity are each reflected at the normal (normal part removed, the rest times 1 − damping, cleared below the minimum speed, the normal part times friction taken away again when it exceeds the bounce; "Warning: \"Bounce >= 1.1f\"…" to the error reporter's slot 17), the rest becomes the next move (`0x545b30`, false when nothing is left); without a hit the whole move is done; five hits put the part back to the start.
- **Entity type fix** `0x4e97c0` [confirmed: code; checked with stand-ins]: after a save game is read (`0x4ebeb0`) every entity (`0x487620`) whose definition (`0x48b290`) names an object (+0x74) of another class is replaced by `Object_CreateSame` of that object (slot 20 with the old entity) in the grid, with the status lines "Fixing entity types", "Fixed a %s to use %s." (entity name slot 61, class short name) and "Done fixing entity types" (`0x536080`, a stub) and the message pump `0x5998f0` after each fix.
- **Shake and views** [confirmed: code; checked with a fake layer]: `0x4e9f70` (float position) removes the last shake offset (+0x12c), makes a new one of the envelope's amplitude (+0x114, or +0x110 while +0x11c is 0) in a random direction, fades it over the second half of the shake time (+0x100 of +0x104) and subtracts half the last one; al 0 without shake. `0x4ea220` (dt) runs `0x4ea350` with the layer's own int view position in a temporary 8-byte array from the pool. `0x4ea350` (views, dt) counts the shake time down (the envelope's slot 23 with dt), puts a view rectangle (as `0x4ea110`) per view into the static 16-byte array `0x6c1bd8` (guard `0x6c1be8`, atexit `0x4ea610`; grown by `0x4eeab0` to max(count + 1, capacity · `0x5ea5f4`)), runs the world update of the save data `0x4e74a0` (not reimplemented: Core in `docs/functions.csv`) and places the ambient sounds of the layer that plays sounds (`0x6c1c70`) at the listener (`0x57c1c0`, `0x4ee100`); byte +0x1ce = 1. `0x4ea6e0` (packet) takes the view rectangle from four packet words (a client's view: the player's view +0xc0/+0xc4 is set while the world's slot 1 object's slot 12 is false; the layer's view +0x80 moves there, is clamped by `0x4ed7f0`, rounded into +0x88 and given to the frame `0x524fe0` when it changed and a tile map exists) or from slot 36, draws (World_DrawView `0x4e7c00` while the draw byte `0x6c1d08` is set, otherwise the draw pass `0x4e8900` and +0x1cc/+0x1cd = 1) and sends a "frame received" block.
- **Multiplayer sounds and positions** [confirmed: code; checked with fakes]: the senders `0x4ea8c0`/`0x4eaab0` (and `0x4ea880`/`0x4eaa60` at the position of the part's topmost parent `0x4fc6f0`) send a "play simple sound" (`0x4f8b90`) or "play sound" (`0x4f8e30`) block to every player of the world's slot 44 (count slot 11, player slot 23, packet slot 13) whose view centre (+0xc0/+0xc4 plus the view size times the player's zoom `0x4f6960` and `0x5eee2c`) is within min(width, height) · `0x5f8dd0` · `0x5ec838` – with a channel to all players; nothing while `0x6c1d0c` is set or for sound −1. Mode 0 without a channel takes the sound's first free channel (`0x4f8ec0`); al is the channel. The receiving side `0x4eaca0` plays a sound without a position through the sound manager `0x713708` (`0x57e890`); in the layer that plays sounds and within hearing range (never in mode 2) the channel's sound resource (`0x4f8f30`, without a channel `0x57e650` + `0x57b630`) is kept (`0x57bbc0`), made resident, given the two radii (slot 5) and placed at (x, 0, −y) (slot 4, or `0x57b290` when it is not valid); out of range (or with a channel, or mode 1/2) the channel's sound is stopped (slot 11) and removed (`0x4f8f90`). `0x4eae90`/`0x4eaf80` write and read a position as two words: (x + `0x5f8ddc`) · `0x5f8dd8` / (width + 1600) and (y + `0x5f8dd4`) · `0x5f8dd8` / (height + 1200), clamped to 0 and 0xfffe, 0xffff for none (read: ok = 0).
- **Floating point**: every value the original stores as a float goes through `fstp dword` (inline asm `fstp_float`): a plain float cast stayed in the x87 register with the extended precision in clang's code (first check run `20261024-195306-97f2`: `Entity_PlaceNear`'s ring distance kept its extended sum, a position differed by one ulp). Extended intermediates are kept where the original keeps them (`0x4eb200`'s x products, `0x4ebbc0`'s x offset, `0x4e91e0`'s x damping factor, `0x4e9f70`'s half of the last x offset); `__ftol` (`x87_ftol`) and `fistp` as in the original. Angles must be finite: `0x508fe0` indexes its tables with the rounded angle (the check uses no NaN or infinite angles).
- **Return values**: the original's eax where callers see it; al for `0x4e91e0`, `0x4e96c0`, `0x4e9f70`, `0x4eaa60`, `0x4eaab0`, `0x4ebbc0`; the void functions are named in `world_update.h`. `0x4eaab0` pushes the channel to the writer as a dword whose upper bytes are left from the stack in the original; `0x4e96c0` passes an uninitialised stack slot as the "part hit" that the sweep writes on every hit. - **Identified ranges** [confirmed: code]: `0x540000`–`0x542140` (17 functions, unnamed before) is the rest of `CPlasmaTileMap`: `+0x7c` of the layer, the object of `0x540640` that the layer parts tell about flag changes, is the tile map, and `0x540640` releases the tile cache handles of a rectangle. In `0x598000`–`0x59bfff` only `0x59a0f0`–`0x59a520` are part lists; `0x599300`–`0x5998f0` are small classes of the user interface and the message loop (`0x599330` `CWindowedBrowsableImage`, `0x599580` the key mapping, `0x5998f0` the message pump), `0x59a670`–`0x59b3a0` the application object `CZaxApp` (`g_App` `0x713f14`, vtable `0x602dc8`; its constructor registers the cheat names), i.e. game flow, not World. `0x4ec600`, `0x4ece20`, `0x4ed150` build and load the mini map image and `0x4ed350` fills the draw queues (Rendering); `0x4ed960` is the ambient sound layer (Sound).
- **Part lists** [confirmed: code]: a pool pointer array with a stamp at `+0x10`; AddNew appends a part only when its `+0x2c` is older (unsigned) and gives it the list's stamp. The temporary lists are nodes of 0x20 bytes in a circular chain whose sentinel is the static node `0x713e20`; GetTemp takes the first free node or appends a new one behind the last, Release only sets the free byte (the list keeps its parts and capacity). **The sort's comparator `0x59a2f0` has an error**: it means to order by slot 56 + slot 53 (bottom) and then by slot 52 (x), but reads the first part for both sides of the first comparison, so that is always equal and the parts end up ordered by x alone; it never returns 0. Its only caller is the draw queue fill `0x4ed350`, which sorts the queues again (`DrawQueue_Sort`). The reimplementation keeps the error and the call order of the slots.
- **Mini map and view** [confirmed: code; verified in the VM, zax-formats/docs/FORMATS.md "Mini maps"]: the image rectangle divides the level without its clipping by the world's slot 100 (the zoom factor, stored as a float), truncates, shrinks by `min(1, height / h, width / w)` – the width test multiplies the width with the factor that the height test left, as floats – truncates again and centres (margins halved towards 0). The mapping recomputes the scales when either is 0 or NaN: unsigned divisions through `fild qword`, the x offset with the unrounded x scale, the y offset with the stored float. The view clamp keeps x in 0 … `((tile map width − 1) & ~0x7f) − visible width` and y at least 0 and at most `((tile map height − 1) & ~0x7f) − visible height` (that limit may be negative and is used as it is); scrolling towards a target moves the view so the target lies in half the given box around the view position plus half the offset (the x correction through a float, the y correction unrounded); SetView rounds the integer view position with `fistp` and sets the frame offset (`0x524fe0`).
- **CPlasmaTileMap** [confirmed: code]: layout in `plasma_tile_map.h`. The elevation and seed grids are 8-bit `CFrame`s (`+0x2c6c`, `+0x2cac`); `+0x2d24` holds columns × rows × 3 tile cache handles (ground and two transition layers) for the shared tile cache `0x7110e0` (made by the first tile map, freed by the last; the count is `0x7110dc`). Every constructor refills the 256 plasma tables at `0x6d1030` (`0x55c390` with the seeds `0xe6cef · i`, `zax-formats/zaxtools/plasma.py`). Slot 9 writes "Num Textures", "Texture <i>", "Elevations Row <r>" and "Seeds Row <r>" (hex); slot 11 reads them: row 0 sizes the frame (and for the elevations rebuilds the handles), a row past the grid is ignored, a "Texture" line looks the name up in the texture definitions `0x6c1d50` (an unknown name takes entry 0). Slots 13/15 write and read the same binary (count, counted names, both frames). Setting an elevation point to a new value releases layers 0–2 of the four cells that touch it (the cell, the one to the left, the one above, the one above left); the band at a pixel (`0x542000`) is bilinear between the four grid points, in the original's x87 order, `__ftol`.
- **Texture lists** [confirmed: code]: `0x4b40f0` is the constructor of the list type `0x5f4994` (0x15c bytes; the plasma list is that plus 4 bytes, vtable `0x5fccf4`). The constructor leaves the folder (`+0x38`) and the source pointer `+0x15c` as they are; `+0x15c` is only set by CopyEntry, which loads the source entry through the source's slot 37 when it has neither an object nor a load in progress (an index past the source's end loads entry 0 but copies the entry at the given index). SetCount allocates one entry more than it counts.
- **Return values**: the original's eax where callers can see it; not reproduced: slot 9 `0x53f7c0`, `0x540460`, `0x5405e0`, `0x540640`, `0x4b4670`, `0x4ed6e0`, `0x4ed7f0`; al only: slot 15.
- **Not reimplemented**: the drawing of the tile map (`0x53ff90`, `0x540000`, `0x540790`–`0x541250`, the band table `0x541710`, the texture list's slot 37 `0x4b4240`), the slot 34 jump `0x4b46e0`, the mini map image `0x4ec600`, `0x4ece20`, `0x4ed150`, the draw queues `0x4ed350`, the sound layer `0x4ed960`, `0x4eda60` (a 3-byte `add` and a jump into the save data's level start `0x4e7870`: not hookable with a trampoline and not callable in a check), the static initializer of the chain `0x59a370` and its exit function `0x59a3c0` (not in `docs/functions.csv`), and the game flow and user interface code of `0x598000`–`0x59bfff` (see above).

172 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/action_classes.cpp`, `action_classes.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): `CAction`'s class getter `0x41a650` and constructor `0x41a6b0` (281 callers), and for the 56 classes of the action file `0x4b8000`–`0x4c7fff` (`CMultipleActionsAction` … `CShakeScreenAction`, with `SyfaceTypeSoundItem` and `CSendWeaponDischargedMessage`) 56 Create, 56 CreateArray, 53 RegisterFields, the three stand-alone class getters `0x4b8460`, `0x4c0cf0` (`CSwitchMapActionBase`), `0x4c4aa0` (`CDischargeWeaponThisFrameBaseAction`), `CSwitchMapActionBase`'s constructor `0x4c0fa0` and `CPainAction`'s constructor with values `0x4c3c20`. The behaviour (the virtual slots: execute, destructors, …) is the next step (done since, section 8, "Behaviour of the action classes 0x4b62d0–0x4bffff …" and "… 0x4c0000–0x4cafff …").

- **Choice of the range**: the action classes outside the World ranges of the parallel batches; `0x41c000`–`0x41ffff`, `0x4b4000`–`0x4b7fff`, `0x514000`–`0x517fff`, `0x588000`–`0x58bfff` hold 48 more of their registration functions (`CActionQueue`, `COtherMapAction`, `CDelayAction`, `CWhileAction`, the map actions …) and stay for later (done since in later batches of section 8), like the classes `0x51d920`–`0x5b5600` (`CZaxDialogAction`, `CRelocateAction`, the inventory actions; about 130 functions).
- **Layout** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`]: every action starts with the CObject part {vtable, dynamic properties}; `CAction` (8 bytes, abstract, class `0x62e770`, vtable `0x5ece50`) adds nothing and registers no fields (its RegisterFields `0x58ea40` is a single `ret`, as for every class without fields of its own). The constructor of a class is inlined into its Create and CreateArray, one level per class: CAction's constructor (CObject's, vtable, `Object_InitFields`), then for each class down to the created one its members (ZStrings; `CMultipleActionsAction`'s embedded pointer array at +8 with vtable `0x5f5290`; `CShakeScreenAction`'s embedded `CLengthEnvelope` at +0xc with `CEnvelope`'s level inlined), its vtable and `Object_InitFields` again; `CSetCategoryAction` clears +0xc after its level, `CSwitchMapActionBase`'s out-of-line constructor +8/+0xc. The abstract classes (`CCreateLayerPartAction`, `CXDoorAction`, `CSwitchMapActionBase`, `CPositionedAction`) register the shared null factories `0x46b760`/`0x52dc80`. The class getters are inlined into RegisterFields (and the slots); the registration's parameters are the same in every copy [verified: the zero path of every copy emulated].
- **Fields** [confirmed: code; VM]: name fields that accept `$Trigger`/`$Instigator` (`"Target Name"`, `"Door Name"`, `"Position"` …) are string descriptors whose vtable is replaced by `0x5ed924` after the constructor (39 of 48 string fields); `"Radians"` floats get the unit converter `0x6be328` and the units `"Degrees"` after `ClassInfo_AddField`, without a null check; `CSeriesAction`'s `"Debug/Next Action Index"` gets the converter `0x6be330` and empty units. `CSpawnEffectAction`'s RegisterFields sets the class's alternative name to `"CCreateExplosionAction"` (the old class name: files with it load as `CSpawnEffectAction`); `CCloneAction`'s calls slot 48 of its inherited `"New Location"` with `""` (`CCreateLayerPartAction`'s default is `"$Trigger"`) [assumption: slot 48 sets the default; the descriptor's slot 48 not read for it]. `SyfaceTypeSoundItem` (sic; 0x10 bytes, parent CObject) is the element of `CPlaySoundBySurfaceTypeAction`'s `"Sound/Specializations"` list (surface type and sound). The CObject part's `"Dynamic Properties"` is inherited by every class.

Left out: `CPatrolPathAI`'s RegisterFields and `CFollowPathAI`, `CPickupAI`, `COverridePickupAI` (`0x53c000`–`0x53ffff`), `CPlayerControlAI`/`CPlayerWalkingControlAI` (`0x540000`–`0x543fff`) (done since, section 8, "The patrol, pickup and player control AIs …").
- The 16 out-of-line constructors these call: `CAIBase` `0x4fd060` (154 callers), `CEntityBehavior` `0x494470` (64), `CTouchingTriggerAI` `0x4223f0`, `CEntityBehaviorMoveToPos` `0x4302c0` (26), `CEntityBehaviorTurnToAngle` `0x495310`, `CEntityBehaviorIdle` `0x498d90`, `CEntityBehaviorPlaySequenceLooped` `0x499cc0`, `CFidgetData` `0x4a04e0`, `CParticleSystemAI` `0x52dd20`, `CEnvelope` `0x52de80`, `CRenderEffectBehavior` `0x55e400`, `CSkeletonBaseAI` `0x577db0`, `CShootEntityBehavior` `0x5780b0`, `CPointWeaponAtTargetEntityBehavior` `0x578780`, `CEntityBehaviorStateSetClosestTarget` `0x586770`, `CEntityBehaviorQueue` `0x586e10`.
- The 12 class getters and the 9 RegisterFields of the trigger AIs: `CTriggerAI`, `CTouchingTriggerAI`, `CollideTriggerAI`, `CPassThroughTriggerAI`, `CRelayAI`, `CRepeatTimerTriggerAI`, `CSpawnPointAI`, `CTouchingOvalTriggerAI`, `CTouchingPolygonTriggerAI` (`0x41c900`–`0x4227e0`).

- **Constructors** [confirmed: code, capstone]: Create takes a pool block of the class size (`0x417710`), CreateArray a heap block with the count in front (`0x5d033a`, fastcall with one unused stack argument); both inline the whole constructor chain: per class level the members' constructors, the level's vtable, `Object_InitFields` (`0x4173c0`, slot 6 of the level's own fields) and the level's defaults. For all 106 classes Create and CreateArray give the same calls and stores (compared with a capstone script; the compiler only reorders stores between two calls), and the sizes and Create/CreateArray addresses equal `docs/classes.csv`. The code was written from that extraction and names the class of every vtable (through its getter) and the field of every offset. Most AIs start with `CAIBase` + `CLayerPartAI` (vtable `0x5ed1d0`), the behaviours with `CEntityBehavior`; embedded members are behaviours (`CEntityBehaviorMoveToPos` at +0x10/+0x14/+0x1c/+0x34 of the chase, patrol, go-to and companion AIs, turn and idle behaviours), pointer arrays and ZStrings.
- **Quirks kept**: `COldBadPatrolAI`'s constructor reseeds the random generator `0x6d06c0` with 2342342 (`0x55c390`: an LCG `0x41c64e6d`/`0x3039` fills 250 dwords, then a mask pass; the other generator is `0x7124c0`), so every such object created changes the game's random sequence. `CTurretAI`/`CSentinonAI`/`CAutoGunAI` copy the category mask `0x6c29a0` into "Valid Targets". `CEntityBehaviorMoveToPos` creates its `CPathCollideChecker` (pool 8, vtable `0x5eebe8`) only when +0xb4 is 0 after InitFields. `CFidgetData`'s constructor calls `0x4a0860` with 0 (its model update; not reimplemented). CreateArray elements are uninitialised heap where no constructor or InitFields writes.
- **Getters and RegisterFields** [confirmed: code, startup registration]: every RegisterFields allocates each descriptor on the heap and adds it through an inlined copy of the class getter; the trigger AIs' descriptors are bytes, floats (with units, ranges, steps and the oval's "YX Ratio" setter `0x421410`), owned actions (`CAction`, class `0x41a650`), a typed resource ("Retrigger Disallow Time For", list `0x62e7a8`, default "All Objects"), an object reference ("Debug/Touching LayerPart", `CLayerPart`) and a string kind of its own (`0x5ed924`, "Triggered By/Triggered By Name"); alternative field names "Repeat Seconds", "IsClose", "Seconds To Disallow Retrigger", "Seconds Between Actions", "Plus or Minus Seconds", "Radius". Two RegisterFields set the class's alternative name (+8, searched by the class registry): "CProximitySwitchAI" (`CTouchingOvalTriggerAI`) and "CTouchingPolyongTriggerAI" (sic, `CTouchingPolygonTriggerAI`, which registers no field of its own). Return values are the last call's eax (AddField's count, SetAltName's, or the class info).
- **Level files** [verified: all 112 levels of `gamedata/Data/Levels` (then unpacked; since 2026-10-29 the game data is `gamedata/Zax - German/DATA.dat`)]: 4,585 objects of the trigger classes (`CRepeatTimerTriggerAI` 1,084, `CollideTriggerAI` 754, `CSpawnPointAI` 646, `CTouchingPolygonTriggerAI` 644, `CRelayAI` 615, `CTouchingOvalTriggerAI` 599, `CPassThroughTriggerAI` 243; no `CTriggerAI`/`CTouchingTriggerAI`, both abstract) use only the registered field names, except "AI Instigator" and "AI Trigger" (200 objects, right after `CAIBase`'s "Broadcaster"): the exe has neither string, so they are fields of an older `CAIBase` (version 3 now registers two fields) that the loader skips. None of the alternative names occurs.
- **Not reimplemented**: the AIs' virtual slots (behaviour), destructors and the RegisterFields of the other 89 AI classes; `CPickupAI`'s constructor `0x53d8f0` and `CAction`'s `0x41a6b0` (called through their exe addresses); `0x535440` (a pointer array constructor, not in `docs/functions.csv`).

An objective that is complete afterwards runs its completed action (`0x41a720` with the current layer) and deletes it; one that stops being complete warns "A mission objective can't become un-completed..." (slot 16); one that becomes complete in the quest game (`0x59ff80` the game type, IsKindOf `CQuestGameType`) counts one more for statistic 6, "Mission Objectives Completed" (`0x552940` the game type's statistic, a `CQuestCounterStat` (`0x554ae0`), `0x555930` with its entry in the quest data `0x5525b0`; section 8, "The quest game type and the quest statistics"; until then read as a HUD panel). - **Actions** (slot 23, `(layer, a2, a3, a4)`, al the result) [confirmed: code; checked with fakes and the level's actions]: `CDefineMission` (al 0 without a mission) finishes the current mission in the quest game (the application's `0x5a0c00` with `0x6cfd60`, 1.0, 0 and the game type's `0x5528c0` with the mission), adds a copy of its mission unless its tag is taken ("Tried to add a mission with an IdTag that was already used"; the copy is not deleted, a leak of the original) and makes it the current one with the change time, then starts the mission time (`0x5a3600` 0), sets +0x361 of the application and flushes (`0x5a0860`) every cached layer of the application's list (+0x2bc/+0x2c0) except the current one whose file name is not expired in the map table (+0x33c, `0x5899b0`) and not in its list of maps not to flush (the original first tests the count above 0xffffffff, never true). `CSelectMission` selects the mission with the tag ("Could not find specified mission IdTag"), `CSelectNoMission` warns ("This is likely to cause trouble with mission statistics... -- Loren 07-09-2001") and sets the index to -1 (its slot 18 only warns). `CAddMissionObjective` adds a copy of its objective to the current mission and sets the mission time 0. `CUpdateMissionObjective` sets the objective's status (remembered) and `CIncrementMissionObjective` calls its slot 23; both then run the mission's completed action once all objectives are complete and set the mission time 1 (objective complete) or 2. `CDeleteMissionObjective` deletes the objective and moves the rest down (`memmove`). `CIsMissionObjectiveComplete` gives the objective's slot 24 (the whole eax), `CIsMissionObjectiveDefined` whether the current mission has it (no report), `CIsMissionComplete` whether every objective is complete. All but the last report "There is currently no mission defined" without a current mission (the defined test silently) and "Could not find specified objective IdTag in current mission" with the tag. `CDisplayMissionFailedScreenAction` calls the game type's slot 29 (mission, a2, the message's text; no null check of the game type), `CDisplayMissionCompletedScreenAction` creates the mission over window (pool 0x1b4, constructor `0x50cab0`, user interface: not reimplemented) with the reporter's `0x4cdf30` and shows it through the reporter's slot 23.
- **Return values**: the original's eax for Create, CreateArray, the getters, RegisterFields (the last call's; the failed screen's the class), the destructors, slots 24/25 (0/1), `0x512170` (al), `0x512280`, `0x512330`, `0x512350`, `0x5127e0`, `0x512800`, the actions' al (`CIsMissionObjectiveComplete` all of eax), the base slot 23 and slot 18 (the reporter's). Void in use [assumption: no caller reads eax]: `0x510e20`, `0x5114d0`, slot 23 of the count and series objectives and `0x5122f0`.
- **How it was made**: Create, CreateArray and the getters by hand from the disassembly (the inlined constructors and destructors one level per class, as in section 8, "Class registration of the action classes"); RegisterFields from the action batch's emulation tool (`emit_register_fields`, adapted to the range; `CMission`'s and the failed screen's by hand); the hook table from the address comments (it must stand in the `.cpp`: `build.sh` collects `ZAX_HOOKS` only from `src/*.cpp`; the first runs of this batch had it in an included `.inc`, so none of its 111 hooks was installed and the checks compared the original with itself).

### The entity base classes CEntityBase, CEntityDestructable, CEntityAnimated [verified 2026-10-25, VM]

121 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/entities.cpp`, `entities.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): of `0x487240`–`0x48bdf0` (CEntityBase) 50, of `0x48bdf0`–`0x48dbb0` (CEntityDestructable) 21 and of `0x48dcc0`–`0x48ffc0` (CEntityAnimated) 50, each with its class getters (and slot 2 copy), Create, CreateArray, out-of-line constructor, destructor, deleting destructor and RegisterFields, the virtual slots of the three vtables (`0x5f1c4c` 97 slots, `0x5f1e4c`, `0x5f2010` 105 slots) that lie in the range, the multiplayer blocks (slots 25/27, the position block `0x4890c0`/`0x489230`, the reader registrations `0x487f60`/`0x48e8b0`) and the non-virtual helpers (the model `0x48b290`, the sequence functions, the rendering height setters, the damage and frame functions, `PlaySequence` `0x48f700`, the definition list's `0x48d8f0`).

- **Layout** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`; the comment of `entities.h` has every member]: CEntityBase (0x7c, class `0x6bdd44`, version 11, alternative class name "CEntity") adds to `CLayerPart` the position (+0x4c/+0x50 floats, +0x54/+0x58 rounded with fistp: two hidden int fields without a name), a cached rectangle +0x5c..+0x68 (cleared in the entity and every entity parent by `0x488cf0` whenever position, height or model change), the rendering heights +0x6c (int, -500..500) and +0x70 (float), the model index +0x74 and the sequence index +0x78. CEntityDestructable (0x90, `0x6bdd4c`, version 13) adds "Cur Damage" +0x7c, the three owned actions +0x80/+0x84/+0x88 and "Default Death Type" +0x8c. CEntityAnimated (0xe4, `0x6bdd98`, version 20, alternative class name "CEntityCrate") adds the embedded CEntityBehaviorStack +0x90, nine flags +0xb0 (8 after the constructor), the fade +0xb4 (1.0), "Play Ratio" +0xb8, the frame +0xbc (float) and its index +0xc0, the aiming/movement/start facing angles +0xc4/+0xc8/+0xcc (radians, field units "Degrees" through the converter `0x6be328`), "Created By" +0xd0 (a part the entity listens to) and a pool pointer array +0xd4 (vtable `0x5f21b4`) of attached objects that the multiplayer block writes and the destructor deletes.
- **The model** [confirmed: code]: the model is record +0x74 of the model list (`0x6cfdd8`; records `0x6cfe08`, count `0x6cfe0c`; index 0 beyond the end), loaded on first use through the list's `0x55e090`; most slots inline that lookup. Slots 24, 25, 29, 31, 33, 34 and 41 of the model's activity (CModel +0x08, `CFlyweightLayerPartAI`, shared by all entities of the model) run before the layer part's own AIs in slots 33, 35, 63, 29, 65, 66, 67. Sorting Y (slots 56/57) and the bounds polygon (slots 48/49) are the model's, so setting them changes every entity of the model.
- **Damage** [confirmed: code]: hit points are the model's "Damage/Hit Points"; slot 99 (`0x48d380`) scales the amount by the world's difficulty factors (world slot 58, +0x10/+0x14, for the category masks `0x6c29a8`/`0x6c29a0`), runs "Hit Action", lets slot 100 and every AI's slot 30 change the amount, runs "Damaged Action", messages the first `CEntityCharacter` in the creator chain of the damaging part (slot 68), adds the damage (at most the hit points), plays the model's pain sound and then either dies (world slot 91, "Destroyed Action", slot 97, "Has Hit Points" cleared) or sends a damage message (`0x476450`) to slot 63. Type "!None" is an error ("ERROR: Someone tried to subtract Hit Points of Damage Type !None.", world slot 17). Slot 67 (collision) makes a living entity take the other destructable's "Damage/Collide Damage" (type "Unavoidable" without a model); `0x48d7f0` takes the damage of the `CGroundTextureFrame` under the entity. Slot 97 of CEntityDestructable marks the entity for deletion for the default death type (`0x5fe8f8`), otherwise calls the death type's `0x478260`; CEntityAnimated's first explodes (slot 101: "Damage/Explosion Radial Damage" in a radius of twice the value, `0x477640`), broadcasts the model's "Explosion" and plays the death sound.
- **Angles and frames** [confirmed: code]: an animated entity faces backwards when "Facing Backwards" is set or movement and aiming angle differ by more than 95 degrees (85 when it faced backwards the frame before; `0x48f260`), then slot 46 turns the movement angle by pi and `PlaySequence` negates the play ratio. Slot 35 turns the aiming angle towards the movement angle by the model's turn speed times the seconds (at once for the categories `0x6c29a0`); slots 103/104 wrap the angles into 0..2 pi and pass them to the animated children. The frame setter `0x48feb0` wraps the frame into the sequence's frame count by repeated adding/subtracting (it does not end for NaN, infinity or huge values, in the original as here) and keeps a locked frame; "Play Ratio" outside -10..10 makes the error reporter complain ("Play Ratios should stay between -10.0 and 10.0... -- Loren 07-08-2001") and is kept anyway.
- **Multiplayer blocks** [confirmed: code; VM with recorders]: the position block is one dword: the model index (11 bits), y and x relative to player 0's view (10 and 11 bits; +0x110 / +0x2c0), summed over the entity parents, optionally the height as a word; reading adds them to the current layer's +0x88/+0x8c and sets model (slot 93) and position (slot 41) through the vtable. Stationary entities without parent, height, hue remap and with sequence 0 write the short block of `CEntityBaseBlockReaderObjectSimpleStationary`, others the complete one with the sequence (times 2, bit 0 for a hue remap, then the remap's six bytes: hues / 360 and errors / 100 times 255); animated ones add the facing angle byte (2 pi / 255), the frame byte, the fade and the attached objects. The readers' create functions (slot 2 of the reader vtables `0x5f1dd0`…: `0x487080`, `0x4872d0`, `0x48dac0`, `0x48db30`, `0x48dbb0`) select the variant through `0x6bdd40`/`0x6bdd94` and stay with the multiplayer.
- **Quirks kept** [confirmed: code]: several functions end the game on a missing model or sequence, in the original as here (`0x48b120` reads slot 25 of a null sequence, `PlaySequence` and slot 93 call `_stricmp` with a null name for a sequence index beyond the model's or a model without sequences, slot 92 reads `0xb4` when the top parent is not animated). Slot 29 calls the AIs of the model through `0x4fd0b0` (following a `CUserDefinedClassRef`); slot 97 of CEntityAnimated asks for the creator (slot 68) and does not use it. Slot 65/66 combine whole bytes (AND/OR), not booleans.
- **Return values**: the original's eax where callers can see it (Create/CreateArray the object, RegisterFields the class info or SetAltName's eax, the setters of the flag bits the new flags, slot 63/65/66 the layer part's eax with the combined al, slot 25 the block count), st(0) unrounded where the original leaves it so (`0x48d030`, `0x48d260`, slot 46, `0x48f600`).
- **Left out** (in `0x484000`–`0x48ffff`): the drawing (slot 23 `0x488f80`, `Entity_Draw` `0x488d70`, `DrawRotationSequenceLayers` `0x4886a0`, the drawable pool `0x488bb0`/`0x488bd0`/`0x487fa0`; Rendering), slot 37 `0x48a100` (the rectangle from the frames of the rotation sequences, 1.5 KB with a jump table), slot 38 `0x489cd0` (the pixel hit test through slot 23 with two function-local static lists `0x6bdd30`/`0x6bdce8`) and slot 82 `0x489a40` (dirty rectangles of the frames, `0x480fc0`), which all need the frame and drawing code; the block readers' create functions and their static initializers (`0x4872a0`, `0x4872b0`, `0x487460`–`0x487613`, `0x48da50`–`0x48dc4d`, multiplayer); the static registrations (`0x487a90`, `0x48c370`, `0x48de70`) and the dynamic field's initializer `0x48dc10`/`0x48dc50`; the setter thunk `0x48da40` (slot 93); CEntityAnimated's slots 81, 86–91 at `0x490130`–`0x490360` (beyond the range, with CEntityMovable); the HUD and inventory classes of `0x484000`–`0x487080` (Inventory and weapons).
- **How it was made**: from the disassembly of the range (capstone with the names of `docs/functions.csv`; Ghidra's decompiler through REA knows only 5,281 functions and none of the vtable-only slots), written function by function; the hook table was generated with capstone (first instructions of at least 5 bytes, a relative call marked).

- **Quirks kept**: `CInventoryItemDefinition`'s RegisterFields sets the class's alternative name "CInventoryItemDefiniton" (sic) after its last field. `CInventoryDisplayOptions`' resource fields default to the fonts "Character Dialog", "Small Green" and "Small Red" (the font list `0x6be1e0`), which a descriptor loads on construction and releases when it is deleted. The deleting destructors of `CInventoryBase` and `CInventoryItemDefinition` have no array path. `0x4d6300`/`0x4d6410` read their float from address 0 + offset when the definition has no loaded projectile (the game ends there, as in the original). The item slot 33 (`0x42a550`, an item taken by a part) passes the inventory as the third argument of the definition's slot 26 only when ammunition came with the weapon, otherwise the item itself. `Part_UseItems` (`0x426930`) marks a non-count item for deletion and searches again from the start, finding the same item until n are used up. `CInventory::Update` (slot 24) bounds its category loop by `*0x6c0814` (+0x14 of the category list), the constructor sizes the category data by `*0x6c0834` (+0x34).
