### The entity behaviours and the behaviour stack 0x494410–0x49a802 [verified 2026-10-25, VM]

124 functions are reimplemented (`reimpl/src/ai_behaviors.cpp`, `ai_behaviors.h`; list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): every function of the range that `docs/functions.csv` counts as AI (107) and 17 second copies of the class getters that `docs/functions.csv` lacks (each class's static registration pushes its own copy, e.g. `0x494510` next to slot 2 `0x494560`). For the 19 classes `CEntityBehavior`, `…TurnToAngleBase`, `…TurnMovingAngle`, `…TurnAimingAngle`, `…TurnToAngle`, `…TurnToTarget`, `…SetRotationSequence`, `…PlaySequenceOnce`, `…SetPlayRatio`, `…MarkForDeletion`, `…ClearFlags`, `…Wait`, `…Transition`, `…Fade`, `…Idle`, `…SetCurFrame`, `…ExecuteAction`, `…PlaySequenceLooped` and `CEntityBehaviorStack`: class getters, deleting destructors (slot 1) and the out-of-line destructors, RegisterFields (13), the behaviour slots, the helpers that make a behaviour ready to push, and the stack's functions. Their Create, CreateArray and constructors were done before (section 8, "AI classes: …").

- **Behaviours** [confirmed: code, vtables `0x5f2930`–`0x5f31cc`; checked with fakes]: `CEntityBehavior` (0xc bytes) has +8 flags (bit 0 set by Begin and when pushed, bit 1 by the helpers). Slots (names ours): 0 message (sender, text), 1 deleting destructor, 2 class getter, 18/19 (Idle: empty its fidget sequence; 19 resets the fields), 23 Begin (entity; al: keep it on the stack), 25 Update (seconds, entity; al: still running), 26 the same default (al 0), 28 debug drawing (entity, view), 29 End (entity; deletes the behaviour); the turn behaviours also 30 (the entity's angle) and 31 (set it).
  - Turning: Begin keeps the entity's flag 0x200000 ("Stationary", entity slot 59 clears flags, 58 sets them) and clears it; Update turns at most the model's turn speed (`CModel::TurnSpeedRadians` `0x517510`) times the seconds towards "Angle To Turn To" (TurnToAngle, the moving angle +0xc8, entity slot 104) or towards a target part (TurnToTarget, the aiming angle +0xc4, slot 103; the angle from `CLayerPart_AngleFromPart` `0x4fb2d0`, only within "Max Dist To Target": the squared distance `0x4fbf60` with the factor 0.7128); done within the tolerance +0x10 (0.1 rad), "Stationary" back. The angles are computed on the FPU as the exe does: differences wrapped once each way into [-π, π], angles into [0, 2π), the step clamped to ± the turn speed, where the negative bound stays the unrounded product (only the positive one is stored as a float first).
  - Sequences: SetRotationSequence sets "Sequence" and takes itself off the stack; PlaySequenceOnce moves the frame itself (play ratio 0, the old one back in End) by the player's frames per second × "Speed To Play" × seconds, backwards for a negative speed, with "Move With Sequence" moves a `CEntityMovable` by the sequence's motion (`0x55fc70` writes x, y into the 8 bytes the exe had used for the frame count as a qword), and at the end sets "Done Sequence" at "Done Frame" (-1 = the last frame minus 0.01); it counts its Update calls in `0x6bddfc`. PlaySequenceLooped plays forwards, backwards, ping-pong or synchronised (`0x55e4b0`), "Start Animation"/"Stop Animation" messages (`0x499f30`); "Debug/Stoping" stops at the next end.
  - Idle: the idle sequence ("IdleCrouch" for a `CEntityWalking` with "Movement Speed" 2 whose model has it, otherwise "Idle"), fidgets from the model's `CFidgetSettings` (+0xbc) or "Override Fidget Options": the time until the next fidget is the settings' delay × 0.25–1.75 from the game's random generator `0x7124c0` (`0x55c550`), a random start frame and a frames-per-second ratio 0.9–1.1 per start; at the fidget's last frame back to idle. Update restarts the idle sequence every frame the model has it (`0x4990e0`, as in the exe).
  - The others: Wait counts seconds; Fade sets the entity's fade +0xb4 (1 minus it for "Transition In Or Out" 1); SetPlayRatio, ClearFlags ("Visible" 0x20000, "Collideable" 0x40000, "Tries To Collide" 0x80000, "Stationary" 0x200000, "Active" 0x800000), MarkForDeletion (`LayerPart_Died`) act in Begin and take themselves off the stack; SetCurFrame ends at once (al 0); ExecuteAction runs "Action" (`0x41a720`, layer = entity +0x48, instigator the entity) and stays.
- **The stack** [confirmed: code; checked with probes and the level's entities]: `CEntityBehaviorStack` (0x20, embedded at +0x90 of every `CEntityAnimated`): +8 "Debug/InProcess", +0xc "Misc./Blocking Priority" (enum `0x6bde48`), +0x10 a pointer array (top = last). `0x49a560` Push (entity, behaviour, priority) ends and removes everything and pushes when the priority is at least the current one and the current one below 3, otherwise refuses (and returns the behaviour without deleting it); `0x49a480` Update begins the top (`0x49a760`, which ends and removes every behaviour whose Begin returns al 0) or updates it and, when done, ends it and begins the next; ending (slot 29) deletes. All of them read the count again after every call into a behaviour, so behaviours may change the stack under them (checked).
- **Return values**: the original's eax for the getters, destructors, RegisterFields (AddField's), End (the destructor's), slot 31 (the entity's), the debug drawing's, the helpers (the new object or 0), the stack's Push/Append/BeginNext/Update/RemoveTop/Clear; al for Begin/Update and the bool helpers (their upper bytes are left from calls, compared only as al).
- **Leaving out**: the debug drawing slot 28 only forwards to `0x4fceb0` (Rendering, not reimplemented). No sound.
- **Findings**: SetRotationSequence and SetPlayRatio take the top off the stack without looking (an empty stack would read before the array; never in the game). The helpers `0x4974e0`, `0x497720`, `0x497f30`, `0x4994d0`, `0x498f10` use the new object without a null test. `TurnToAngle_Make` (`0x4953b0`) does not set "Angle To Turn To" (callers set it with `0x4953a0`). `0x49b810` is `CEntityWalking`'s getter (not `CEntityCharacter`'s; "Movement Speed" +0x12c).

The charger's count-down (slot 30) charges the inventory's battery by its definition's "Energy" per second, at most the battery's own "Energy". An energy item's charge (+0x18) is at most its definition's "Energy" (+0x4c, `0x5afe50`); slot 50 uses an amount if there is that much. An energy storage item is taken into the inventory's item of the same class (slot 2) unless that one is full ("Pickup If Full": always). A battery charge adds its charge times the world's energy factor (the world's slot 58, +0x1c) to the battery; for the local player (`0x59e6f0` with `0x5babc0`) the "Primary"/"Secondary" weapons without ammunition that slot 38 rejected before and accepts after the charge go to the automatic weapon choice `0x425a70`. `0x5aeec0` counts a part's rounds of a definition's ammunition (slot 41 of its `CAmmunitionInventoryItem`), `0x5aef60` a mineral, `0x5b0da0`/`0x5b0e50` find the battery and its charge.

- **AI slots** (`CLayerPartAI`'s vtable `0x5ed1d0`; names ours [assumption: our names]): 23 (entity), 24 Begin (entity), 25 Update (entity, seconds), 31 (part, other, -) whether the other may touch it (al; ANDed by the part's slot 65), 34 collision (part or entity, other, three more), 41 debug drawing (entity, view); the patrol AIs add 43 (the area's drawing) and 44 (pick a new point), the player AI 7 (precache), 36 (demo record/check), 43 (a new life), 44, 45 (the key vector). `CLayerPartAI`'s slot 25 is `0x46cd50` (`ret 8`): the AIs that end with it return whatever eax held.
- **COldBadPatrolAI** [confirmed: code; checked] (alternative class name "CPatrolAI"; its constructor reseeds the generator `0x6d06c0`): Update makes a `CEntityMovable` with behaviours below priority 2 collide, try to collide and leave "Stationary", starts "Walk" once and asks for a new leg (`0x53acf0`); with "Return Home Dist" above 0 it sets "too far from home" (+0x2c) when the entity is further than that from slot 40's point (dy scaled by 1/0.7128). A leg: the stack cleared, up to three directions swept through the layer's collision (`0x4e8e00` with the entity's polygon, after `0x4916f0`): the first away from home when too far, the others a random twelfth of a circle, each squeezed by atan2(cos · 0.7128, sin) (the table functions `0x508da0`/`0x508ec0`/`0x509100`), as long as a random distance in [min, max) (+0x14/+0x18, 120/200). Three blocked tries: play ratio 0, a `CEntityFlying` told through slot 110, an idle of 2 s (priority 2), the distances shrink by 10 (or the minimum by 5). A free leg resets them and, for a `CEntityCharacter`, pushes a move to the end of the leg (`0x4308c0`) and a turn to the angle; with a "Primary" weapon that accepts the entity (slot 38) and the first character within 640 also play ratio 0, a `0x5ab300` behaviour (-1) and a turn to that character. Slot 34 starts a new leg for a mover below priority 3. A second sweep in the free path is set up and never used (as in the exe).
- **CPatrolAreaAI** [confirmed; checked]: Begin clears "Retry New Point", sets a walker's "Movement Speed" 0, picks a point (slot 44) and begins the move behaviour (+0x14). A point (`0x53b960`): up to four random points in the oval of "Radius" around slot 40's point (`0x55c550` on the generator `0x712cc0`, the sine/cosine table `0x508fe0`, y × 0.7128) until the move behaviour finds a way (`0x4303f0`), then one around the entity in about the direction of the centre (± 1.309 rad); without a way "Retry New Point" = 1 s; the behaviour is aimed at the last point once more. Update counts the retry down or updates the move behaviour and picks a new point when it is done. Slot 34 reads the reporter's time and drops it (unless the fifth argument is set).
- **CPatrolPathAI / CFollowPathAI** [confirmed; checked]: the path is the part "Path Poly" names (`0x41ad40`) with at least two points; Begin takes the nearest point (`0x546bc0`, the last point and with "Ignore last point" the one before left out). Update aims the move behaviour at "Target Point"; when it ends further than 10 from the point (the polygon's point + the part's offset), the point becomes "Revise Point" for 0.5 s ("Revising Data"), otherwise the next point: "Order" 0 back and forth, 1 forth and back, 2 loop, 3 random (another point, up to five tries until the way is free, `0x491250`), 4 go to end (-1 at the end); a turn, a new loop or the end runs "End of path action" (`0x41a720`). The drawing looks the path up without keeping it. `CFollowPathAI` only changes the inherited descriptors: "Order" defaults to "Go To End", "End of path action" takes `CSendAIDoneMessage`.
- **CPickupAI** [confirmed; checked]: the item (`0x53e4c0`) is a `COverridePickupAI`'s "Item", else the default item (`0x5b7aa0`) of the "Normal Item" catalogue record (loaded on first use, `0x48d8f0`'s code inlined), else "Special Item". Slot 31 lets an entity touch it when the item or, when it refuses (slot 32), the alternate item accepts it; the alternate item is the definition's template item (+0x1c) or a local `CInventoryItem` given the definition (`0x54fdb0`); characters of a category in "Who Can Pick Up" get the item prepared first (definition slot 25). The pickup (`0x53e110`, slot 34 with a set fifth argument) gives the item or the alternate (slot 33; with neither accepting, the alternate is not tested for null, and the pickup still disappears), runs "Picked Up Action", adds the model's +0xa4 to the layer, shows it in the HUD (`0x5a3480`), hides itself for a respawn or marks itself for deletion, and sends the "Pickup Effect" explosion. The respawn (Update, the `COverridePickupAI`'s "Respawn Mode"): 1 counts "TimeUntilNextRespawn" down while gone, 2 times it to the next multiple of "Respawn Delay" after "Min Respawn Delay" + "Time Offset", 3 accumulates: for every multiple passed a present pickup gets a copy near it (`Object_Clone`, a random distance below 1.5 × its polygon's size, the copy's override not respawning) and a gone one comes back; "Last Simulation Time" is a double. Slot 11 reads the old lines "Inventory Item"/"Custom Item" into "Normal Item" (message boxes for a definition without or with another default item).
- **CPlayerControlAI / CPlayerWalkingControlAI** [confirmed; checked]: the input comes from the player object (world slot 89): an action pressed (`0x46ed70`), the mouse vector (+0x5c/+0x60), the aiming angle (`0x470b50`), the item bound to a weapon key (`0x46f4a0`); the raw input reading stays outside. The mouse direction (`0x542360`): the mouse vector (or the key vector, slot 45) scaled by min + range, its length by the table square root, the unit vector times (length - min) / range up to 1; against the last direction it gives 0. Update: with the game object's slot 84 the character idles; with mouse control it walks or runs 100 pixels ahead (ratio between "Min Walk/Run Ratio" and 1 over "Start Walk/Run Mouse Dist" of the rules' `CPlayerWalkingControlSettings`, `fsin`/`fcos` on the FPU), then the keys: inventory pages, next/previous weapon, the weapon keys (`0x544b10`, "Multiplayer Full Auto Pistol" and "Alien Electrical Weapon 02" as fallbacks), the autogun and the companion drones (the undeployed item with the best projectile), secondary fire (`0x5ab900`'s behaviour, or the dry fire and a switch), the zoom keys (0.25–2 in steps of 0.01); and the fire (`0x543830`): a firing direction (keys 0x18–0x1b or the mouse) fires the "Primary" weapon by the fire message `0x5fcfd4` after turning the aim (slot 103); without ammunition the dry fire sound plays once and the weapon may switch. Slot 31 lets no projectile of the player's own or (without friendly fire, game type slot 38) of the same team hit him. Slot 36 records or checks a demo (`0x6bd2e0`–`0x6bd2e8`). The constructor loads the "Direction Pointer" model's sequence once (`0x711110`; a fatal error box and exit without the model).
- **CPlayerWalkingWeaponAI / CPlayerWalkingItemAI** [confirmed; checked]: "Force Invisable" unless the character's current "Primary" item (the item AI: of "Type Index" with "Definition Index") exists; then `CSameAsParentAI`'s Update.
- **FieldColor** [confirmed; checked]: bytes b, g, r, a and again b, g, r, the 16-bit pixel (`0x433a10`), the palette index +0xa, flags +0xc (2 from RGB, 1 index valid); `0x53f100` sets it from palette entry i (its bytes 1, 0, 2 as b, g, r), `0x53f160` finds the nearest index (`0x526e40`) in `0x633388` or the palette `0x433a80`/the reporter's.
- **Findings**: `CPlayerWalkingControlAI`'s slot 43 takes the entity as its second argument (the first version took the first: the game hung when Zax was placed; found by disabling the hooks in halves). `CPickupAI`'s pickup reads the alternate item without a test when the item refuses (a crash in the exe when there is none) and removes the pickup even when nobody took the item. The key vector returns the vector's pointer in eax. The direction pointer's sequence is shared by all player AIs. `CPatrolPathAI`'s "Order" 0/1 rewrites the field itself at each turn (back and forth and forth and back alternate). With "Random" and only one point to choose from (the polygon's count - 1, less one with "Ignore last point", equal to 1) while at point 0, the loop that wants another point never ends (in the exe too; no level of the checks has one). `CPatrolAreaAI` registers "TimeOfLastChangeDirectionDueToCollide" (+0xd0), which no reimplemented function reads or writes [confirmed for this range]. `CPlayerWalkingControlAI`'s constructor makes the path checker (+0xd4) only when +0xb4 is 0.
- **Leaving out**: the tile map's drawing `0x53ff90`–`0x541710` and the polygon outline `0x546d40` (Rendering); the debug drawing slots are reimplemented but forward to the exe's drawing (`0x4fccc0`, `0x546d40`, `0x4b33f0`). The sounds are only named to the sound manager (`0x57e7b0`, `0x57e820`) or the layer (`0x4fc8c0`).

Check in the VM (`reimpl/src/checks_ai_patrol.cpp`, `checks_ai_pickup.cpp`, `checks_ai_player.cpp`, the fake world `checks_ai_world.h`/`.cpp`; in the game thread; side 0 with the hooks of the three modules taken out, side 1 through the reimplementation):
- **The fake world**: the 105 exe functions of its table that the slots reach outside the modules jump to recorder thunks (`mov eax, id; jmp`), whose stand-in records the call (ecx/edx and the stack arguments by kind: pointers comparable, floats by bits, strings by text, the points behind pointers by value), pops the arguments as the callee would and answers from a value sequence that depends only on the case and the call's number (ints, bools with random upper bytes, floats in st(0), fake objects or 0, outputs written). 64 fake objects of 0x200 bytes lie in one static block (the same addresses on both sides); entities, behaviours, inventories, items, definitions, the world, the game object, the reporter, the game type, the view, the AIs and the catalogue and model list each have a vtable of recorder thunks. While a side runs, the globals the slots read (world `0x6c2080`, game object `0x713f14`, reporter `0x6c02cc`, the catalogue's and model list's vtables and records, the direction pointer, the demo buffer, the static colours and their guards) point into the fakes. Compared per case: eax (masked where the exe leaves it undefined), the call log, the whole fake block and the globals afterwards, the FPU stack. A per-case policy keeps answers non-null where the exe reads them without a test.
- **The classes**: getters (both copies, class variable set and 0), Create/CreateArray and the deleting destructors (the C heap from the arena of `checks_inventory_common.h`; arrays and the walking AI's path checker side by side), RegisterFields and the registered descriptors (`CFollowPathAI` by its own comparison: it makes no descriptor).

Assimilate Cave1 gives 4 `CPatrolAreaAI`, 1 `CFollowPathAI` and the player's `CPlayerWalkingControlAI` (all its patrol AIs sit inside `CSkeletonAI`s; the first scan of the parts' own AIs found none); no level of the two check maps has a `CPickupAI` or `COldBadPatrolAI`, so these run in the fake world only.

Slot 33 sends types 1 and 2 to one or all players in a multiplayer game (`0x5bd5d0`/`0x5bd640`), else adds the line to the voice log and shows it in the HUD (type 1, unless the voice log took it and there is no Local.txt) or as the status text for 1.5 s (type 2); type 0 opens the dialogue window with speaker and text split at ": " within the first 0x13 characters (`0x5a4bd0`). Slot 7 precaches the voice "<line>.wav" when "Play Voiceovers" is on and the speaker's quip category (its record's +0x7d at the index as given, the first time +0x7e and its object's slot 7). `CSwitchMapAction` refuses during a sequence, warns for an invalid "Return to map" and switches through `0x59b3a0` after "Leaving Scope"; `CRelocateAction` keeps the part's offset from the trigger with "Relative Position" (slot 29) before the base's relocation; `CTeleportAction` pushes a clone of "Warp Behavior" onto an animated instigator's behaviours and plays "Teleporter.wav" in every case. `CDiscoverInventoryItemAction` (un)discovers in the first character's inventory and reports only a definition without "Must Be Discovered First"; al 1 otherwise, also without a character. `CIsEnemyNearbyAction` queries the first character's layer within 320 pixels of its rounded position (no null test). `CDropAllOreAndCrystalsAction` moves a character's "Ore Deposits" and "Crystals" into a pile near it with a `CollideTriggerAI` whose `CMultipleActionsAction` gives them back (a `CGiveCustomInventoryItemAction` each, a clone of "Extra Pickup Action", a `CDeleteAction` on "$trigger", the exe's function-static string `0x713f90` with its guard bit `0x713f68`); al 0 always. `CDropCurrentItemOfTypeAction` runs its embedded drop action with the inventory's current index set to the category's, then restores the focused item (one less when needed). The confiscate actions move the first character's inventory into and out of its extra field "Confiscated Inventory" (`0x713f6c`) and report a second confiscation or a return without one.

- **The AIs** [confirmed: code; checked]: `CWaitAI` sets "Time Left" from "Time To Wait", runs "Behavior to run" (with the part only when it is a `CEntityAnimated`) and at 0 (the unrounded difference; NaN too) runs "Done Action" (`0x41a720` with the part, the AI, the part). `CLimitedTimeAI` runs "What To Do" while "Time Left" is above 0 (Begin calls it without a null test), then "Done Action". `CIdleAI` runs its embedded `CEntityBehaviorIdle` for animated parts and then `CLayerPartAI`'s slot 25. `CForceUpdatingAI` puts its part into the layer's update monitor list (`0x4e72a0`, half sizes "Updated Radius") and takes it out on "deactivate AI" (`0x6c29e8`), passing every slot to "AI To Force". `CHandleMessageAI` runs "Action" when the message has the name "Message To Handle" (`0x506620`); its slot 41 calls the action's slot 25.
- **`CGeneratorAI`** [confirmed; checked]: a pending generation comes first; then "Time Till Next Generate" counts down and, when it reaches 0 and while "Delay Between Spawns" is above 0, rises by the delay with one generation each time unless "Max Simultaneous" is reached (`0x4d08e0`: the pending ones plus the parts named "New Name" that are not destructable or have hit points left; without a name the reporter says "A CGeneratorAI tried to generate something without giving it a name" and it counts as full). A generation waits (pending + 1) while a blocker stands at the generator (`0x4eb1c0`: a `CEntityMovable` preferred, flags 0x840000 without 0x2000000) that does not let the first character through (its slot 66 with (character, 0): the `push 0` before `World::FirstCharacter` is that slot's second argument), otherwise picks an item by weight (`0x55c470` on the generator `0x712cc0`, r in [1, sum]) and spawns it (`0x4d05a0`): an animated entity turns to "New Facing Angle" ± "Angle Variation" (the game's generator `0x7124c0`, wrapped into [0, 2π) once; slots 103/104), gets "New Name", loses its AIs ("Remove Default AIs", `0x4fbd00`), is centred on the generator, gets slot 39, is added to the layer and gets copies of "AIs to Add"; an active entity gets slot 33, an inactive one of a `CSpawnableCloneByName` becomes active; "After Action" runs with the new entity as a4; with "Warp In" an animated entity gets the warp effect through a `CAddEffectAction` on the stack (target "$Instigator", the exe's function-local static `0x6c0438`; the effect a 0x30-byte behaviour (`0x571b70`) with the sequence "Warp Effect 1" made into a warp behaviour by `0x5aabe0`; the pool block is used without a null test). The count-down never ends for NaN seconds or a NaN time (in the exe too).
- **`CGoToAI`** [confirmed; checked]: Begin resets the flags, starts the move (slot 45: "Destination" through `0x41ad40` plus "Offset" becomes the part's target (slot 71); a collideable destination is made "no collision" meanwhile; a move speed above 0 becomes "Play Ratio"; when no way is found the path failed and the move behaviour is aimed with speed 0) and begins the move behaviour unless it found no way. Update: the first frame only runs "Starting Action"; then slot 44 (no target: start again), the move behaviour's frame (done: with "Set Facing Angle" the turn (slot 47: "Turn Sequence Name" from frame 0), else finished), "Time To Try To Move" (1 s, a stopped move starts again); while turning the turn behaviour and the entity's frame moved on by the sequence's speed with the sequence's motion (`0x560300`), wrapped by the frame count. Finishing (slot 46) clears the target it set, "Make New Home" (slot 39), and slot 42 runs "Done action" or, for a failed path, sends the message `0x6c29d8` to the part. Touching the target finishes; "deactivate AI" clears the target. Slot 11 reads the old lines "X Offset"/"Y Offset" (atof).
- **The temporary task** [confirmed; checked]: `CAssignTemporaryTaskAction` gives its target a new `CTemporaryTaskAI` (pool 0x1c) with a copy of "Temporary Task AI": the part's first AI becomes "Original AI" (`0x4fba80`) and gets the message `0x6c29d4`, the temporary task AI takes its place (`0x4fbaa0`) and, on an active part, its AI begins. The temporary AI gets every slot (no null test); "AI done" (`0x6c29d8`) to it as the first AI puts "Original AI" back and begins it unless "Supress Begin After Done".
- **The turrets** [confirmed; checked]: every "Retry Time" (0.3 s) a character turret looks for the nearest part within "Start Attack" (+ "Stop Attack Extra" while it sees its target; flags 0x840000, "Valid Targets") and keeps a character only when the line to it is free (`0x4912b0`, kind 2, the target's 0x2000000 set meanwhile). Unless its behaviour stack is busy (priority ≥ 2): a target within the radius (dy × 1.4029851; 9999999 when not in sight, unreachable) gets a burst: a wait of "Burst Delay" (pushed, priority 2), per shot a wait of 0.2 s, frame 0, a fire behaviour (`0x5ab300` with −1) and a turn to the target within 1.5 × the radius, then a wait and a turn within the radius; unless it plays "Shoot1" it turns to "Deploy Angle" (degrees × 0.017453292) and plays "Deploy" into "Shoot1"; without a target a turret not in "Idle" plays "Deploy" backwards into "Idle" and turns to "Deploy Angle". The sequence names are function-local static ZStrings of the exe (guard `0x713a1e`, `0x713a10`–`0x713a24`). `CTurretAI`'s slot 31 says "Please change all CTurretAIs to Sentinon AIs" every time and lets nothing touch a character in "Idle"; `CSentinonAI`'s only keeps projectiles off. `CAutoGunAI` counts "PickupDelay" down and lets parts of the category mask `0x6c29a0` pick it up through its embedded `CPickupAI` only after the delay. "Retry Time" is registered with the units "Degrees" (a slip, kept).
- **The map actions** [confirmed; checked with fakes only]: the name is copied, backslashes are reported ("Map Name *MAY NOT* contain backslashes …") and turned into slashes; a missing map is reported; `CFlushMapAction` flushes (`0x5a0860`), `CExpireMapAction` and `CExpireMapsInFolderAction` (every `Levels/<dir>/*.zax`, trailing slashes cut; the exe reads the character before an empty name) expire (`0x5a0880`) after removing pending other map actions (`COtherMapList`), never the visible layer ("Can't Flush/Expire Visable Layer"). The checks run them on stand-ins only, so no map of the running game is flushed or expired.
- **The lists** [confirmed; checked]: the game type list (`.ZGT`, element `CGameType`) and the surface type list (`.STY`, the global `0x713868`) have the category list's slot shapes with their own extension; slot 37 of the derived surface type list keeps only objects that are `CSurfaceType`s. The item category list `0x713a58` is a function-local static (guard `0x713a50`). `0x5886c0`/`0x5886e0`/`0x588700`/`0x588720` are the shared slots 29 (in use), 33 (keep), 8 (loaded, no test of the records), 9 (being loaded).
- **The application base and the platform** [confirmed; checked]: see the header of `app_base.cpp`. The fixed steps run slot 3 with at most the longest step until less than one step is left, then slot 4; the time carried over is cut to +0x5c. The handle heap is a best-fit allocator over a size tree with compaction and discardable blocks (callers: the tile map, Rendering).

Not hookable: `0x4cde80`, `0x4cdea0`, `0x4cdf30`, `0x4ceb50` (3–4 bytes), `0x58ea40` (1 byte), the handle functions `0x4d2670`, `0x4d2760`, `0x4d27a0` (a short branch in the first five bytes). The static initialisers and atexit functions run before the hooks.
- **Findings** [confirmed: code; checked]: `CLimitedTimeAI`'s Begin, every slot of `CTemporaryTaskAI` (its temporary AI), `CTenaciousInvestigateAI`'s Update (the target of the part taken as an animated entity, 0 otherwise), the generator's warp behaviour block and the definition lists' slots 8 and 9 have no null test (the exe ends there as the reimplementation does); the generator's count-down loops for ever with NaN seconds or a NaN time. The blocker's slot 66 gets (the first character, 0): the `push 0` the exe places before the `World::FirstCharacter` call (which takes none) belongs to it. **Toolchain**: clang 22 compiled `(v & ~0xffu) | load8(v + …)` into one `movzbl` (the upper bytes of eax lost; `DefinitionList::InUse`'s check found it); `def_list_slots.h` uses `with_low_byte` (an inline `movb`); `World::LoadingFlag` in `world_class.cpp` had the same wrong code (fixed 2026-11-01 with the audit of every byte merge, section 13, "Batch section-12 leftovers", 1).

### The skeleton AI, the shields, the segmented items and the simple AIs 0x569560–0x577fc0 [verified 2026-10-25, VM]

184 functions are reimplemented (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): 163 of `docs/functions.csv` (96 AI, 36 Inventory and weapons, 31 Actions; every function it counts there in `0x568000`–`0x577fff` that was not done, apart from the drawing, among them 24 unnamed helpers) and 21 it lacks (20 class getter copies of the static registrations and the setter `0x574f90`).
- `reimpl/src/ai_simple.cpp` (54): `CSelectiveCollideAI`, `CSeriesAI`, `CActionAI`, `CSendAIDoneMessage` (with its Create/CreateArray), the shot AIs `CShotAI`, `CShootOverAI`, `CTurnToBounceDirAI`, `CPassThroughShooterAI`, `CExplodeOnImpact`, and `CSimpleCollideTriggerAI`: getters (both copies), deleting destructors, RegisterFields, the slots.
- `reimpl/src/ai_shield.cpp` (59): `CSegmentedInventoryItem` and the non-drawing part of `CSegmentedInventoryDetailRenderer`, `CShieldAI`, `CPercentInvulnerableAI`, `CShieldInventoryItem`, `CShieldChargeInventoryItem`, `CRechargeShieldAction` and the heap pointer array constructor `0x56f8a0`.
- `reimpl/src/ai_skeleton.cpp` (71): `CSkeletonAI`, `CSkeletonBaseAI`, `CSkeletonTransition` and its list (append `0x577b60`, deleting destructor `0x577cb0`), `CShootEntityBehavior`'s getters and destructor, and the actions `CSetPatrolAIAction`, `CSetPursueAIAction`, `CSetAttackAIAction`, `CCallForReinforcementsAction`, `CSetTargetTypeAction`, `CSetTargetAction`.
- Shared helpers: `reimpl/src/ai_helpers.h` (on `ai_common.h`). How it was made: the RegisterFields bodies from the action batch's emulation tool (section 8, "Class registration of the action classes …", adapted to this range), everything else by hand from the disassembly (capstone with the names of `docs/functions.csv`); the hook tables generated with capstone from a list of addresses (first instructions of at least 5 bytes, a relative call marked).

- **The skeleton AI** [confirmed: code; checked] (`CSkeletonAI`, 0xac, the state machine of most enemies; layout in `ai_skeleton.cpp`): "Debug/State" (enum `0x7135d0`) is 0 Patrol, 1 Pursue, 2 Attack, 3 Retreat, 4 Investigate, 5 Any; each state has an AI (+0x28 patrol, default `CPatrolAreaAI`; +0x60 pursue; +0x80 attack, default `CNormalAttackAI`; +0x70 investigate, default `CChaseInvestigateAI`) with a start and an end action. A state change (`0x5776d0`) tells the old AI "deactivate" (`0x6c29e8`), runs its end action, sets the state, runs the start action and begins the new AI (attack first forgets the failed targets; retreat only runs "Retreat Start Action"), then runs the transitions (`0x577a90`). The update (slot 25) loops at most 99 times while the state changes: patrol lets the embedded `CEntityBehaviorStateSetClosestTarget` (+0x38, "Target/Target Type": +0x48 the sight radius, +0x50 the categories) search and notices the target through slot 43 (within the sight radius, not too far from home (`0x576f80`: "Pursue/Max dist from home" from slot 40's point, the target within that plus "Attack/Max Dist"), visible (`EntityMovable_CanSee`)), otherwise updates the patrol AI; pursue gives up when too far (patrol, "Target Lost"), investigates a target it cannot see, attacks within "Attack/Max Dist", otherwise updates the pursue AI; investigate pursues a target it sees within the view angle (`0x586760`, the turn `CLayerPart_TurnTo`), searches again and updates the investigate AI; attack without a target patrols ("Never Unacquire": investigates), updates the attack AI within "Attack/Max Dist" and otherwise pursues a target within the sight radius. Ground distances scale y by 1.403 (`0x5ee9bc`); some are kept on the FPU, others stored as floats in between, as in the exe. Messages (slot 29): while patrolling a part in sight (`0x713df8`), damage (`0x6bd708`, "Target shooter if hit" makes the shooter the target) and a call for reinforcements (`0x7130c0`, "Respond to calls for reinforcements") give a target; a "CFailedTargetMessage" puts the part on the failed list (+0x10, each forgotten after 1.5 s, +0x20) and patrols; damage at or below "Retreat when" % health starts the retreat action once. Slot 0: "Delete" of a part on the failed list removes it, "Leaving Scope"/"Died" of the target patrols.
- **Transitions** [confirmed; checked]: a `CSkeletonTransition` (0x1c) runs its "Action" when the state changes from "From State" (or "Any") to "To State" (or "Any"; 6 "Target Acquired" and 7 "Target Lost" are pseudo states the AI passes for those events); "Trigger" 0 "First Time" and 2 "Once Per New Target" mark it done ("Once Per New Target" is armed again by every new target), 1 "Every Time" never. The action gets the transition's index as the field argument of `0x41a720`. The list (+0x98, vtable `0x6008d0`) is a heap array with the count in front that grows to max(count + 1, capacity × 1.2).
- **The actions** [confirmed; checked]: `CSetPatrolAIAction`/`CSetPursueAIAction`/`CSetAttackAIAction` give the target's `CSkeletonAI` (slot 64 with the class and 1) a copy of their AI template (`0x5775e0`/`0x577620`/`0x577660`: the old AI deleted; in that state the state becomes "Any", so the next update begins the new AI); `CSetTargetTypeAction` sets the categories (`0x5776b0`); `CSetTargetAction` resolves "Target to attack" in the attacker's layer and makes it the target (`0x576e50`) when it is "Collideable"; `CCallForReinforcementsAction` lets the target call (`0x55d070`: message `0x7130c0` to the parts within "Max Distance" of its categories), "Requester Name" only selects the target.
- **Shields** [confirmed; checked]: a `CShieldInventoryItem` (parent `CEnergyItem`, "Current Charge" +0x18) given to a character (slot 33) adds a copy of its "AI" (a `CShieldAI` of the damage type) unless one of that type is there, replaces a weaker shield of the type (the definitions' "Energy") and keeps the charge at most the most charge. The `CShieldAI` makes the shield entity from "Shield Gfx" on the first hit (a child of the character, turned to the hit point), plays it while visible; damage of its type (slot 30) is absorbed while the item has charge (a player's damage scaled by the world settings' +0x20): below the charge the item uses that much, otherwise the shield shuts down ("Shutdown") and the item uses its whole charge; in both cases the whole damage is absorbed. `CShieldChargeInventoryItem` adds "Charge to Add" (a player's scaled by +0x24), `CRechargeShieldAction` "Recharge Uints" (sic) or "Recharge Percent" of the most charge. `CPercentInvulnerableAI` scales damage of its types by "Damage To Take".
- **Segmented items** [confirmed; checked]: a `CSegmentedInventoryItem` holds "Segments" (indices of the item catalogue's "Segment" records); the definition's `CSegmentedInventoryDetailRenderer` (slot 34 of a `CZaxInventoryItemDefinition`) lists the segments needed. Taking one adds the segments the renderer needs to the item the part has; with all of them the "Completed Item" (the template item of a catalogue record) is given, the renderer's "Compleated Action" runs ("Action to execute when the gun is fully assembled") and the segmented item is removed. The detail text: the item's display name and "%u of %u Pieces".
- **The simple AIs** [confirmed; checked]: `CSeriesAI` runs its "AIs" one after the other (each ends with "AI done" `0x6c29d8`; "When Done" 0 "Repeat Series", 1 "Do Nothing" (default) tells the entity); `CActionAI` runs "Action" once, then reports "AI done"; `CSendAIDoneMessage` sends "AI done" to its target; `CSelectiveCollideAI` refuses collisions with its categories; the shot AIs: `CShootOverAI` lets shots pass, `CTurnToBounceDirAI` and `CPassThroughShooterAI` ignore their shooter (the latter also its other shots), `CTurnToBounceDirAI` turns a bouncing shot to its direction of motion ("Laser Bounce.wav"), `CExplodeOnImpact` destroys the part it hits ("Unavoidable" damage of all its hit points, or the world removes it); `CSimpleCollideTriggerAI` runs "Action" when touched by anything, players (default), enemies or shots.
- **Quirks kept**: `CShieldAI`'s damage slot absorbs the whole damage even when it exceeds the charge. `CShieldAI_FindItem` and the item slots read the character's inventory without a test (a shield AI on a non-character would end the game). `0x56a6b0` reads address 0x1c when the catalogue has no records, `0x56da70` address 8 when the damage type has no loaded record. `CSkeletonAI`'s slot 29 also checks for a "CFailedTargetMessage" after a message the patrol branch handled. The skeleton update's loop counter has a dead comparison with 49. `CSetPatrolAIAction`'s RegisterFields returns the shown class (`CPatrolBaseAI`, `CPursueAI`, `0x42e870`'s), not AddField's count.
- **Findings**: the damage message `0x6bd708` carries the shooter at +0x18; the skeleton AI sends the 12-byte message of `0x5788a0` (vtable `0x600a84`, id `0x713670`) to the reporter's slot 12 on every update of an enemy entity [assumption: a statistics or debug hook; the reporter's slot 12 not traced]. `docs/functions.csv` names `0x5867a0` `EntityBehaviorStateSetClosestTarget_Ctor`, it is the destructor. `CShotAI`, `CShootOverAI`, `CTurnToBounceDirAI`, `CPassThroughShooterAI`, `CExplodeOnImpact` and `CSkeletonBaseAI` register the empty RegisterFields `0x58ea40`.

- **The game types** [confirmed: constructors, destructors, RegisterFields, `Resources/Game Types/MultiPlayer/*.zgt`; slot names ours, assumption: our names]: `CCaptureTheFlagGameType` (0xfc bytes, vtable `0x5ef544`, class `0x6bd12c`) and `CSalvageKingGameType` (0xdc, `0x5fed48`, `0x71316c`) derive from `CMultiPlayerGameType` (section 6) through its constructor `0x51bfa0` and destructor `0x51bff0`. Capture the Flag: +0xc8/+0xcc/+0xd0 the points for a good frag (1), a bad frag (a team mate, 0) and killing oneself (−1), the display of the capture count (+0xd4 font "Small Green", +0xd8 the point 270, 14), +0xe0 the team colour overlay's point, +0xe8/+0xec the blue and red overlays (list `0x6c0540`), +0xf0 "Display/Force Team Colors On Players", +0xf4/+0xf8 the blue and red hues (215, 0; 0–360). Slot 25 (a frag: victim, killer) first calls slot 48 (the kill message), then needs the victim's net player (`0x5bac80`); the killer's player, when it is another one, gets the bad frag points (same team, +0x14) or the good frag points added to its score, otherwise the victim gets the points for killing itself; then slot 27 (the lead states). Slot 39 writes the team hue of a player of team 0 or 1 when the colours are forced. Slot 45 gives the address `0x6bd120`, Salvage King's `0x713164` (globals of the game types; not read). Salvage King: +0xc8 "Ore Points Value" (1.0), +0xcc "Crystal Points Value" (3.0), +0xd0 the frags font "Number Grn", +0xd4 its point (348, 31). Slot 40 copies an entity's ore and crystals (`0x426860` with the catalogue indices of "Ore Deposits" and "Crystals", found once: guard bits `0x713168`, cached in `0x713160`/`0x71315c`) into its player's +0xee and +0xf2 and zeroes +0xf0/+0xf4 (the setters `0x5ba360`–`0x5ba3f0`; without a player the original calls them on null too). `CSalvageKingScoreMineralsAction` (8, `0x5fee0c`, `0x713170`, no fields) slot 23: in a Salvage King game (the application's game type `0x59ff80`, asked three times as in the original) and for a `CEntityCharacter` instigator with a player and an inventory, every `CMineralInventoryItem` of the two kinds scores count × value + score (`__ftol` of the x87 sum: `fld`, `fimul`, `fiadd`) and is taken (slot 52 with 0 and the count); then slot 27, and the match ends (`0x51c650`) when the net game's frag limit (settings +0x14) is above 0 and the score reached it; al 1, else 0.

In the code: CUseCannedAction's +0xc is used as a clone exactly when the canned object's +0xc is 1 (`CCannedObject`'s "Use" value 1), and only then deleted. Section 6 had the "Use" names the wrong way round: `Drop Cystals and Ore.can` ("Shared Global Instance") reads as 0 in the VM, so 0 is "Shared Global Instance" (the canned action itself is executed) and 1 "Local Copy" (a clone); corrected there [verified].

The item definitions give "Primary"/"Secondary" items a `CSelectCurrentInventoryItemAction` and "Health" items a `CHealTriggerFromCurrentInventoryItemAction` as their use action (section 8, "The game's own inventory items …", slot 18). Select changes to the item in its category (`ChangeTo` mode 0) and updates the inventory (slot 24 with the part if it is a character, 0.01). HealTrigger heals a destructable part whose hit points are below its maximum (NaN: no): a `CHealthItem` gives its +0x24 (slot 53 with the part), an old item 40 after the report "Using old-style health item... Please Fix... (--Loren)" and is removed; the part's slot 98 heals. The old action does either by the item's category ("Health", else "Primary"/"Secondary", else al 0). Drop needs a `CZaxInventoryItemDefinition`: its power-up model (`0x5b76d0`) becomes an entity (`Entity_CreateFromModel`, `CEntityBase`); it gets a `CPickupAI` (a new one when the model's default entity has none) and a `COverridePickupAI` (0x38 bytes, made inline: `CAIBase`'s constructor, vtables `0x5ed1d0`/`0x5f83b4`, ResetFields) holding a clone of the item, or of the definition's default item when that has fewer rounds (slot 41); a clone that is selected is deselected (slot 45) on the path with a new pickup AI. Three reports catch an override that holds an item already or exists without a pickup AI. Then the item leaves the inventory (`CInventory_Remove`) when the default item has at least its rounds, otherwise it gives up the pickup's rounds (slot 52 with (0, n)); the entity is placed 500 pixels near the part (`Entity_PlaceNear`) and the inventory updates.

Slot 35 of the catalogue (object, a2): for a `CInventoryItemDefinition` (its getter inline) that is one of the records, slot 39 (the entry's path, `0x46ae50`) with (index, a2); al 1, else 0.

Slot 24 puts the part into its layer's update monitor. Slot 25 (part, dt): with a rate above 0 the whole units of rate · dt + leftover (the rest kept) change each ground cell (`CPlasmaTileMap` +0x7c of the part's layer, 64-pixel cells) in the width × height rectangle around the part's position towards the target, skipping cells above the upper or below the lower bound; with shape 0 only the ellipse: (row distance · width / height)² + column distance² ≤ (width / 2 + 32)². A cell at the target stops a "Stop When" 0 AI (rate 0); when nothing changed the rate becomes 0 unless "Stop When" is 2. Slot 41 `0x4e4280` draws the shape (editor drawing, not reimplemented).

- **Key table** [confirmed: code]: a dword per key code 1–0x1ff (bit 0 down, bit 1 pressed since last taken), at +0x800 a queue of 10 typed characters (+0x80c count, +0x810 write, +0x814 read; a full queue drops its oldest), +0x818 an optional filter (fastcall (+0x81c, character), al 1 swallows it). While the byte `0x6c1870` is set no key counts as pressed. Functions: read a character, clear the queue / presses / downs / all (pumping the messages `0x5998f0` first unless their argument is set), take a press (pressed or down), is down (key 0 always), take the first pressed-or-down key, the first newly pressed key, the first newly pressed key other than a given one (the presses before it taken too), take a key pressed with up to three modifiers down, key down, key up, add a character.
- **Key names, keyboard repeat** [confirmed]: `GetKeyNameTextA(scan << 16)` into `0x6c1974` (0 when it fails; `0x4e2a90` then gives the string `0x6c1048`); the delay `v · 1/3 · 0.75 + 0.25` s from `SPI_GETKEYBOARDDELAY`, the repeat interval `(31 − v) · 1/31 · 0.3667 + 0.0333` s from `SPI_GETKEYBOARDSPEED`.

The poll: x and y to −1..1, outside the dead zone (NaN counts as below) shifted and scaled; after 30 s without a movement above 0.35 both read 0; the bits: buttons 0–23, the four hat directions from the POV (up below 75° or above 285°, right 15°–165°, down 105°–255°, left 195°–345°; 0xffff none) and the four stick directions; a bit counts once until it was released (+0x4c). The bit names: the eight directions by name, buttons "Button n" or the registry's name (`…\Buttons\<bit>`); the text of several bits writes "Joy " or "+" and then the bit's name over the whole string, so only the last bit's name remains (as in the original).
- **Not reimplemented** (documented): drawing and user interface: `CInventoryDisplayPageOptions` `0x4d8410`–`0x4d85d0`, the inventory pages and item list window `0x4da240`–`0x4db960` (`CInventoryDisplayPage`, `CItemListWindow`, "Info Use Deploy Button"), the window `0x4de290`–`0x4de790` (vtable `0x5f86d0`), `0x4e2240`, `0x4e2b80`/`0x4e2bb0`/`0x4e2df0`/`0x4e38e0` (a window class, base `0x599510`), the font factory `0x4e3680`/`0x4e38b0` (vtable `0x5f88fc`), `0x4e2f10`, `World_DrawView` `0x4e7c00`, `CLandscapeAI`'s slot 41 `0x4e4280`; sound: `0x4e1fb0`–`0x4e2220`, the sound object factory `0x4e2610`/`0x4e2670`/`0x4e26a0` (vtable `0x5f88c0`); static registration stubs (`0x4dc290`, `0x4dc580`, `0x4dcb40`, `0x4dcf20`, `0x4dd210`, `0x4dd370`, `0x4dd770`, `0x4dd850`, `0x4e3b60`, `0x4e4630`), static initializers and exit functions (the joystick `0x4dd890`/`0x4dd910`, the block reader `0x4e4360`/`0x4e4400`, the Local strings `0x4d8380`–`0x4d83d0`); not hookable: `0x4dde40` (the joystick's name: an add and a jump), `ZString_EmptyBufferAtExit` `0x4dec80` (1 byte).

### The continuous fire weapons, the energy ammunition, the expanding damage radius, the damage in a radius, the deployable items with their actions, the death behaviour definitions and the death match game type 0x472440–0x47ba80 [verified 2026-10-25, VM; the fire, deploy and frag slots with fakes only]

The list's Init `0x4784e0` is the template `ZDefinitionList::Init` of `definitions.cpp` (an explicit instantiation added there); its file lookups use `def_list_slots.h`.

The Create and CreateArray of the four AIs and of the death behaviour definition and `CPickupDeployedItemAI` are `ai_classes.cpp`'s (section 8, "AI classes"). `docs/functions.csv` lacks 20 of these functions (the getters `0x472ed0`, `0x4747e0`, `0x4751a0`, `0x475b00`, `0x4764a0`, `0x477ce0`, `0x478840`, `0x478ce0`, `0x47b270`, `0x47b5b0`, `0x47b8c0`, the copies `0x479c90`, the callbacks `0x476b20`, `0x477510`, the list slots `0x4780c0`, `0x4783b0`, `0x478420`, `0x4787d0`, `0x478b30`, `0x478bb0`) and calls `0x472880` (CContinuousFireWeaponItem's getter) and `0x4734e0` (the AIs' destructor level) FUN_.

- **The continuous fire weapon** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`, the definition getters `0x5b7670`–`0x5b78f0` (`zax_item_defs.cpp`); slot names ours, assumption: our names]: an item definition's +0xcc holds a `CContinuousFireWeaponData` (0x20, vtable `0x5f03e4`, class `0x6bd6f0`): the start and finish actions (+8/+0xc), the impact explosion (+0x10, the projectile list), the spread angle (+0x14, 15 degrees), the extra close range damage (+0x18, 15) and the looping discharge sound (+0x1c). The item `CContinuousFireWeaponItem` (0x20, `0x5f0440`, `0x6bd6f4`) holds the muzzle flash entity (+0x18) and its owner (+0x1c) while firing: slot 49 starts (the frame locked, the "weapon discharged" message `0x599300` to the parts within 500 pixels, the definition's muzzle flash spawned as a child of the root character, the start action), slot 50 stops (finish action, muzzle flash dies, frame unlocked, `SetWaitingForDischarge` 0), slot 45 (deselect) and the message 0x6bde98 about the owner (slot 34) stop it; slot 38 needs a character that may use it and, with the flag 0x10000000, an energy source with charge above 0.
- **The fire AIs** [confirmed]: `CFireContinuousFireWeaponBaseAI` (0x34, `0x5f050c`, `0x6bd6f8`): begin (slot 24) finds the character's continuous fire weapon of "Weapon Definition Index", listens to its muzzle flash, starts the looping sound and spawns the impact explosion; the update (slot 25, 2,888 bytes) makes the beam polygon (`0x474510`: the origin and five points at the range, turned by −2…2 quarters of the spread), finds the parts in its rectangle (`CLayer::FindRect`, kind 3, flags 0x940000) that a projectile would hit (their slot 65 with the function-local static `CEntityProjectile` `0x6bd5d8`), whose polygon touches the beam and that the character can see, takes the nearest within the range as the target, puts the impact explosion at the sweep's hit point on it, damages a destructable target (the definition's slot 23 at the distance times the seconds, shortened to what the energy source holds, the definition's damage type +0x38, slot 99), sends it "Damaged Message Name" and counts the quest accuracy statistic 0xe (hit and shot; a miss counts a shot), lets the energy source pay (the definition's +0x4c times the seconds times −1, times the world setting +0x18 for a player; emptied when that fails) and calls slot 42 to draw the beam. After seven updates without the muzzle flash's "I Moved" message the AI is done and the weapon stops. `CFireElectricalWeaponAI` (0x40, `0x5f05bc`) draws a clone of "Lightning To Use" from the muzzle to the hit or, without a target, at a random length (0.5 to 1 of the range) and direction within the spread, cut by the layer's point sweeps; a part clipping the bolt gets "Clipped Message Name". `CFireParticleWeaponAI` (0x40, `0x5f0668`) runs a clone of "Particle System" on the muzzle flash and sets its life from the reach and its speed. Their messages (slot 0 "I Moved", "Died", "Delete"; slot 29 "deactivate AI") end the listening, the sound and the beam objects.
- **The energy ammunition** [confirmed] `CEnergyAmmoItem` (0x1c, `0x5f0714`, parent `CEnergyItem`): taken by a part that has one of the same definition its charge goes into that one (times the world setting +0x1c for a player); may be taken while that one is not full; setting the amount keeps it at most at the maximum and marks it for deletion at 0.
- **The expanding damage radius** [confirmed] `CDamageExpandingRadiusAI` (0x34, `0x5f08c8`, version 5): the radius grows from "Start Radius" to "End Radius" over "Start To End Time" (or half the current frame's width with "Use Animation For Radius", "YX Ratio" its height over width); every destructable part within it (`CSortList2D_QueryRadius`) takes "Damage" per second of "Damage Type" from the part's creator. The damage in a radius `0x477640` (fastcall layer, centre; the part left out, radius, damage, type, instigator, two flags) queues a `CPainAction` for every destructable part within the radius, falling off linearly to 0 at the radius, delayed by the distance at the speed of sound (1 / (344 · 3.2808 · 10) per pixel times 5, made once into `0x6bd75c`), with the target "$trigger".
- **The deployable items** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, the static messages]: `CDeployableInventoryItem` (abstract, 0x18, `0x5f0ee0`) pairs two definitions through their "Ammunition" (+0x2c): the undeployed item (`CUndeployedInventoryItem`, 0x1c, `0x5f0e18`, +0x18 "Current Damage") and the deployed one (`CDeployedInventoryItem`, 0x20, `0x5f0fa8`, +0x18 the entity, +0x1c the owner). Deploy (`0x47a0f0`) checks the pairing, the inventory and the projectile's entity class (each failure a static message to the reporter and al 0), makes the entity from the item's projectile model next to the part (500 pixels), applies "Current Damage" as "Unavoidable" damage, gives the part a clone of the deployed item that listens to the entity and the owner and marks the undeployed item for deletion. Recall (`0x47a990`, also on "Leaving Scope" from the owner) checks the same the other way, gives a clone of the undeployed item the entity's lost share of hit points, kills the entity. The actions' slot 28 deploys or recalls the item and updates the inventory and the layer for 0.01 s; `CPickupDeployedItemAI` sets the given item's "Current Damage" from the part it sits on. Not hookable: `CUndeployedInventoryItem`'s slot 49 `0x479e00` (`fld [ecx+0x18]; ret`).
- **The death behaviours** [confirmed]: `CDeathBehaviorListDefinition` (0x18, `0x5f0ba4`, `0x6bd9f4`) holds "Behaviors" (a heap pointer array of `CEntityBehavior`); `0x478260` gives a part a new 0x34-byte AI (`0x42f5e0`) with clones of them. The list `0x6bd8b0` ("Death Behaviors", .txt; 42 entries in the running game) has the slots of the other definition lists (sections 6 and 8) plus its own use (12: in use, loaded, precached once with the object's slot 7; on a record being loaded the original reads address 0), clear (28) and unload (31). Its slot 37 reads a definition from its file or writes the defaults there (`0x4782d0`, like `0x46a630` without the second try).
- **The death match** [confirmed] `CDeathMatchGameType` (0x100, `0x5f0d54`, parent `CMultiPlayerGameType`): a kill (slot 25) first sends the kill message (slot 48), gives the killer's net player a frag (its +0xf6) and ends the match at the world's frag limit, or takes one from a suicide or a kill without a killing player; then the leads (slot 27). Slot 45 gives the `Local.txt` string "Frag" (`0x6bda08`).
- **Return values**: the original's eax for Create, CreateArray, the getters, RegisterFields (the last call's), the destructors, the item's start and stop (the action's, the muzzle flash, `SetWaitingForDischarge`'s), the take slots, the message constructor, the queries, the death match's kill (slot 27's), the list slots; al for the may-fire, may-take, deploy, recall, the actions' execute, the file lookups and the deployed item's message slot (its recall path gives the recall's al); st(0) for the damage share. Void in use [assumption: no caller reads eax]: the AIs' begin, update, beam drawing, the radius update, the pickup collision.
- **How it was made**: identified from the disassembly (`tools/disasm.py`) and the vtables (Ghidra through REA knows none of the vtable-only slots); RegisterFields with the action batch's emulation tool (`emit_register_fields`; the death behaviour definition's by hand), with the getters fetched after operator new where the original does; the hook tables from lists with the generator's `hook_entry`.

The quip list's slots 0, 35, 39 and its base slot 37 use the shared definition list slots (`def_list_slots.h`).

- **Non-interactive sequences** [confirmed: code, RegisterFields; checked]: `CBeginNonInteractiveSequenceAction` (0x28, version 3, alias "CBeginNonInteraciveSequenceAction") holds "Scene List" (+0xc, a list object with vtable `0x5fb658`: +0x10 a new[] array of `CNonInteractiveSequenceScene`, +0x14 count, +0x18 capacity), "Debug/State" (+8, enum `0x6d0108`: 0 "Not Playing", 1 moving to a scene's target, 2 in the scene, 3 returning to the player, 4 returned; names of 1–4 ours [assumption from the code: our names]), "Debug/Current Scene Index" (+0x1c), "Camera Returned Action" (+0x20, alt name "After NIS Action") and "Camera Speed" (+0x24, 30 pixels per second, 0 "Immediately"). A scene (0x14) has "New Camera Target" (+8, the name of a part), "Camera Arrived Action" (+0xc) and "Camera Speed" (+0x10, 150). Slot 23 hands the action to the application (`0x5a2b10`, which plays a clone and calls Start `0x521e90`). Every scene finds its target (`0x41ad40` with the sequence as the caller); the player as the target gets the speed on its `CCameraTrakerAI` (slot 64; +0x14 "following" off while a sequence plays, +0x10/+0x1c/+0x18 mode, arrived, speed), another part gets a new camera tracker (0x20 bytes, `0x5aa4d0`) that the layer's monitor list watches; a speed of 0 (or a missing tracker, name or target, each with the reporter's warning) makes the scene arrive at once (`0x522060`: the scene's action runs with the player as a4). `CEndCurrentNonInteractiveSequenceSceneAction` (8, alias "CEndNonInteraciveSequenceAction") ends the current scene through the application (`0x5a2b60` → `0x522110`): the tracker put on a target leaves (`0x4fbd80`), the next scene begins; after the last the camera goes back to the player and, once the tracker reports arrival (`0x5222a0`, its second argument the layer), the "Camera Returned Action" runs and the application ends the sequence (`0x5a2b90`). Ending a scene while returning only warns (reporter slot 16).
- **Old properties** [confirmed: code, the static descriptors `0x521c40`–`0x521e00`; checked]: files of the old format carry "New Camera Target", "Change Camera Position" and "First NIS Action" as dynamic properties (the extra descriptors `0x6d00f4`, `0x6d00f0`, `0x6d00fc` registered for the class); slot 18 (after loading, with the parent) turns a set "Change Camera Position" into a new scene (the list grown by 1.2 as the list's slot 2 does, the vector constructor `0x402090` with `0x5226e0`, the scenes copied by assignment) with the sequence's speed, the "First NIS Action" as its action (a property of another type is deleted with a warning) and the old target as its name; a sequence without scenes but with a "First NIS Action" under a `CMultipleActionsAction` parent becomes a new `CMultipleActionsAction` of the sequence and the action, handed to the parent's slot 0. While a scene arrives an old "First NIS Action" still runs (`0x522060`).
- **The sequence player** [confirmed: code; checked; names ours]: `CRotationSequence` +0x44 holds one int pair per frame of all rotations (the motion from the frame before; the first frame of a rotation none, the step from the last frame back to the first adds the first's), +0x48 the frames per rotation (`0x55f790` sets it when the count divides the frames), +0x5c/+0x60 the triggers (a new[] array of `CAnimationTrigger`, one per frame of a rotation: +8 "Action", +0xc bits "Trigger Forward" 1 and "Trigger Reverse" 2, both default 1). The motion at a fractional frame interpolates the deltas of the whole frames around it (`0x55fb60`); between two frames (`0x55fc70`, `0x55fd30`) it is the difference, plus or minus the first frame's delta when the play wrapped. The frame index (`0x55fee0`) is the rotation of the angle (as `AngleToRotation` `0x55fdd0`) times the frames per rotation plus the frame; a synchronised sequence (flags +0x1c bit 7) takes the frame from the game time instead (tick count × slot 26's frames per second × 0.001 plus the entity's offset unless bit 8, the offset chosen by `Layer_DrawDirect`); `0x55e4b0`/`0x55e500` are the same for the entity behaviours. Playing from one frame to another fires the triggers of the frames passed (`0x560300` forward "Trigger Forward" after the start up to the end, `0x560480` backward "Trigger Reverse" from the end up to before the start, the frame number wrapping at the frames per rotation; `0x560600` chooses by the play ratio), each through `0x41a720` (layer, entity, 0, entity, sequence, frame) with an animated entity's frame set to the trigger's while it fires and put back after; a locked frame index (`0x48ec20`) stops, and when it is locked from the start only one trigger fires (the start's forward, the end's backward, both by the "Trigger Forward" bit). Nothing happens while the game does not run (the world's slot 1, its slot 12). `0x560270` cuts a frame's rectangle to a strip between the cuts (+0x54/+0x58, unless `0x6bdd48`).
- **CNormalAttackAI** [confirmed: code, RegisterFields; checked] (0x4c, version 6, alias "CStandGroundAttackAI", parent `CAttackAI` `0x42e870`): "Shoot/Shoot Behavior" (+0x10, embedded `CShootEntityBehavior`), "Turn/Turn Behavior" (+0x24, embedded `CPointWeaponAtTargetEntityBehavior`), "Move/MoveBehavior" (+0x30, a `CEntityBehaviorMoveToPos` or none), "Move/Minimum Attack Distance" (+0x34, 100; 0 "Do not move while attacking"), "Move/Move Buffer Zone" (+0x38, 50), "Move/Waiting For Threshold" (+0x3c); not registered: +0x40 the phase timer, +0x44–+0x47 the phase flags, +0x48 the time until the next move. Update: nothing for an entity in a warp effect or playing "Death"; an entity in a synchronised sequence (slot 102) only turns and moves; otherwise shooting (1 s) and waiting (3 s) alternate, shooting only with the current item in reach (its slot 39 against the timer), a weapon item (`0x472880`'s class) marking the character through the dynamic byte property `0x62ea2c` (cleared again by "deactivate AI" and `0x6c29d4` messages, which also take the weapon items out of use, their slot 50). The move behaviour aims every 0.5 s at the place on the line to the target the minimum distance away from it (`0x4303f0`); without a way, or when it stops while bits 5 or 6 of its flags are set, at a random place within the buffer zone around the target (`0x5231d0`). The debug drawing shows both distances as ovals.
- **CEntityOm** [confirmed: code, RegisterFields; checked] (0x16c, parent `CEntityWalking`, the boss of the last levels): its collision polygon turns with the facing angle (slot 48: CEntityBase's polygon turned around its centre in the view's oval, through the point buffer `0x711120`; slot 49 turns a set polygon back); a hit (slot 67) counts as "in the eye" while the angle from the centre to the hit point, less "Angle Of Allowed Collisions" (+0x15c), lies within "Angle Plus Or Minus" (+0x160, 7.5 degrees) of the facing angle, and only then slot 100 passes the damage on; a turn (slot 104) that makes the polygon overlap another part (not a character, neither ignoring the other) is taken back and runs "Collided While Rotating Action" (+0x168).
- **CSayQuip and the quip list** [confirmed: code; checked] (`CSayQuip` 0x10: "Quip Category" +8, "Probablity Of Saying Quip" +0xc): slot 23 runs the category's "Condition" action (CQuipCategory +0x10), then decides with a draw below 101 of the generator `0x712cc0` against the probability and hands the decision to the quip packet writer (`0x5bd300`/`0x5bd560`) for the player of a2/a4, so every machine says the quip. The quip categories (`.Quips` files in `Quips`) are a definition list (the function-local static `0x712370`, made by any of three copies of its guard code); its slot 15 plays a random sound of a category, `0x55bd50` counts the categories' timers (+0x14 the delay, +0x18 the time until the next quip; at 0 a sound plays when no voice is playing), slot 37 reads a category with its sounds (`CQuipCategory::ReadSounds`).
- **The random generator** [confirmed: code; checked]: the R250 generator of Kirkpatrick and Stoll (250 dwords, a successor table `0x620004`, seeded by an LCG 0x41c64e6d/0x3039 and a diagonal of 32 bits; layout in `random_misc.cpp`); integers below n (`0x55c470`, the upper half of n × the draw), between two bounds (`0x55c4e0`), floats in a range (`0x55c550`), towards the middle (`0x55c5b0`, x·|x|) and towards the ends (`0x55c650`, 1 − x²). The static initializers of `0x7124c0` and `0x712cc0` seed from `timeGetTime`; every constructor also fills the bit count table `0x7128c0`.
- **The rest** [confirmed: code; checked]: `CSetMusicAction` (0x20, an embedded `CMusicMixerData` at +8: the fade time 5 and three songs) copies its data into the world's music mixer (+0x334) and marks it changed; `CSwitchMusicTrackAction` (+8 "Track") switches the mixer's track (`0x51e520`, Sound); `CThresholdTrigger` (0x18: "Threshold Value", "Re-Trigger Amount" 5, "Threshold Action", "Trigger Direction" enum `0x7137e0`, "Increasing") is only data here (its users are elsewhere); the multiplayer helpers: node lists of names (vtables `0x5fb47c`/`0x5fb480`, a heap copy of the name and the next node, `0x51eb10` the first whose name contains a text, case-insensitive), the handler pointer `0x6d00a8`, a holder (vtable `0x5fb4dc`) of two pointer arrays and a name with a back pointer from its owner [assumption: part of the GameSpy or session layer; their callers not traced].
- **Quirks kept**: the scene list's append and the conversion copy the scenes shallowly (an owned action of an old scene would be deleted with the old array while the new one points to it; the game's scenes never have one there [assumption: about the data, not counted]); CSayQuip's slot 23 reads the category without a test (with the list empty or the entry loading the game would end), the decision's dword carries three bytes of the stack; the backward trigger play tests the forward bit when the frame index is locked; `CSetMusicAction`'s and `CSwitchMusicTrackAction`'s al results carry the upper bytes of the mixer's address or of the switch's eax; `0x55e090` loads a record without a range test or a test for an object already there; `0x55c650` reads the status word after a multiplication (the sign of the compare survives on the x87; kept in asm).
- **Findings**: `docs/functions.csv` gives `CSayQuip` the slots 28, 42–44, 62–67: they are the quip list's (its vtable `0x5fe74c` follows `CSayQuip`'s 28 slots); `0x5bd300` ("SayQuipReader") takes no arguments, the three pushed values are the writer's (`0x5bd560`); `0x587c70` is a case-insensitive substring search.
- **Leaving out**: Rendering: `COffsetClippedProxyFrame` (`0x524450`–`0x5251d0`), the palette and colour functions `0x5266d0`–`0x527fa0`, `CRenderablePolygon` (`0x55d210`–`0x55dd90`), `CVerticalCut`, `CRotationSequence`'s class functions (Create, CreateArray, destructor `0x55f830`, constructor `0x55f7d0`, RegisterFields, slots 9, 11, 13, 15, 19, 21, 23, 27); Sound: `CMusicMixer` (`0x51df00`–`0x51e520`: its class functions create the music stream `0x587060`), the Ogg callbacks and streams (`0x525380`–`0x525ba0`), `0x525410`–`0x525760`; the voice output of the quips (`0x595b50`, `0x595be0`); not hookable: `NetGame_PlayerCount` `0x51f450`, `NetPacket_Length` `0x5203b0`, `NetPacket_IsReliable` `0x5203c0`, `NetTokenMap_Translate`/`IsKnown` `0x55d1f0`/`0x55d200`; the static registration stubs and the enum tables' static initializers (`0x5214e0`, `0x51dc50`, `0x583c20`, the old descriptors `0x521c40`–`0x521e00`).

### The particle AIs, the particle system, the particle infos and the start point types 0x528550–0x535440 [verified 2026-10-26, VM]

112 functions are reimplemented (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): every AI function of `0x528000`–`0x537fff` that was not done apart from the drawing, and the particle descriptions there that `docs/functions.csv` counts as Rendering although they draw nothing.
- `reimpl/src/particles.cpp` (56): `CParticleAI`, `CGravityParticleAI`, `CFloatParticleAI`, `CSwirlParticleAI` (both copies of every class getter, deleting destructors, RegisterFields, the behaviour slots), `CParticleSystemAI` and `CGenericParticleSystemAI` (getters, the destructor `0x52ded0` and the deleting destructors, RegisterFields `0x52f220`, reset, begin, message, the old text lines, the emission `0x52e2d0` and its helpers `0x52e080`, `0x52eb40`, `0x52ebd0`, the six field getters), the vector helpers `0x52a200`, `0x535400`, `0x535420` and the pointer array constructor `0x535440`.
- `reimpl/src/particle_start.cpp` (56): `CParticleInfo` and the start point types `CParticleStartPositionType`, `CPointParticleStartPositionType`, `CDiskParticleStartPositionType`, `CLineParticleStartPositionType`, `CCylinderParticleStartPositionType`, `CSphereParticleStartPositionType` (getters, Create/CreateArray, deleting destructors, RegisterFields, the start point slot 25, the envelopes' values, advance and reset, the old text lines) and `0x52cc70` (CEnvelope's and CObject's level of an envelope's destructor, which the cylinder's destructor calls).

- **Layouts** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, `docs/fields.csv`]: `CParticleAI` (0x24, abstract) +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 the centre, +0x1c follow the parent (no field), +0x1d "Animated", +0x1e "Obey Sequence FPS", +0x20 "Y To X Ratio"; `CGravityParticleAI` (0x34) +0x24 "Gravity" (9.8), +0x28 "Bounce Sound", +0x2c "Use Velocity to Advance Frames", +0x2d "Bounced Last Frame", +0x30 "Gravity Constant"; `CSwirlParticleAI` (0x34) +0x24/+0x28 "Angular Velocity" (π/3, in degrees per second as the units' second name "Degrees/Seg" with the converter `0x6be328`) and its variance, +0x2c "Rotate Velocity", +0x30 the current angular velocity; `CFloatParticleAI` (0x24) nothing of its own. `CParticleSystemAI` (0x134, abstract): six embedded envelopes (+0x10/+0x34 outer/inner cone angle, +0x58 face angle, +0x7c cone trajectory, +0xa8 speed, +0xd0 age; an envelope's value is its start value +8 while its speed +0x14 is 0, else its current value +0xc), burst frequency and variance +0xa0/+0xa4, speed and age variances +0xcc/+0xf4, max/min travel distance +0xf8/+0xfc, "NumBursts" +0x100 (the share of a burst due), "CurFrequency" +0x104, the switches +0x108–+0x10b, the bursts so far +0x10c, "Start Point Type" +0x110, "Particles" +0x114 and "Sounds" +0x124 (pointer arrays); `CGenericParticleSystemAI` (0x148) adds the x/y offset and height +0x134–+0x13c, "Num Bursts To Stop After" +0x140 ("Don't Stop" = 0) and three switches +0x144–+0x146. `CParticleInfo` (0x24): "Model" +8, "AI" +0x10 (a `CParticleAI` the system clones onto every particle), "Animated"/"Obey Sequence FPS" +0x14/+0x15, "Num Particles" ± "Num Particles Variance" +0x18/+0x1c, "Tries To Collide" +0x20 (alternative name "Particle Collides"), "Collidable" +0x21. The start point types: disk (0x58) inside and outside radius (+8, +0x2c, `CLengthEnvelope`), +0x50 "Use Cone Angle For Start Pos", +0x54 "YX Ratio"; sphere (0x58) the disk's fields; cylinder (0x7c) + "Height of Cylinder" +0x58; line (0x2c) "Center Length" +8; point (8) nothing.
- **The emission** [confirmed: code (Ghidra's decompilation of `0x52e2d0` cross-checked with the disassembly); checked]: slot 26 (part, seconds) does nothing while disabled, while all particle systems are stopped (the byte `0x6d04f8`) or in multi-player with "Disable in multi-player" when the game type's slot 33 says so (the game type getter `0x59ff80` is asked twice). It advances the six envelopes (slot 23) and the start point type (slot 27), draws a frequency when "CurFrequency" is 0 (variance ± from the generator `0x712cc0`; "NumBursts" then 1 - frequency × seconds) and adds frequency × seconds to "NumBursts". From 1 on: the emitter's origin (`0x52e080`: the part's position with its parents', or only the offset to its slot 43 position for "Make Child of Generator"; plus the integer offsets, an entity's height (slot 54); with "Orient To Parent's Rotation" turned by the part's facing (slot 46) + the face angle), the whole bursts taken (fistp), at most up to "Num Bursts To Stop After" (which disables the system). Every burst emits per particle info "Num Particles" ± variance (the game generator `0x7124c0`, negative counts 0) projectiles of the info's model (the model list's `0x5176f0`, with "Use Particle As Shot" as children of the part's root): a direction in the cone (`0x52eb40`: a random turn in [-π, π]), the speed (envelope ± variance), the age (envelope ± variance, kept between the min and max travel distance divided by the speed, at least 0.01), the start point (slot 25 of the start point type, else the origin) and the velocity turned by face angle and trajectory (`0x52ebd0`), placed at the origin with y scaled by 0.712766, flags 0x820000 set and 0x200000 cleared, collidable (0x40000) and tries to collide (0x80000) from the info, added to the part (child) or the layer, the target and rendering height set, the velocity set (slot 107); with "Limit Duration To First Collision" a point sweep through the layer (`0x4e8d40`) and the age 0.1. The info's AI is cloned (`Object_Clone`), gets the origin as its centre (slot 42), the info's two switches (slot 43) and the start point type's YX ratio (slot 44, else 1.0) and is added to the particle. After the bursts a new frequency is drawn and, with sounds, one plays at the origin (`0x4ea8c0`): by the share of particles emitted of all possible ("Choose Sound Based On Burst") or at random.
- **The particle AIs** [confirmed: code; checked]: `CParticleAI`'s slot 45 (entity, seconds) sets a projectile's frame from its age: with "Obey Sequence FPS" the age × the sequence's fps modulo its frame count (`_CIfmod`), else the age's share of the projectile's duration × the frame count; with +0x1c the centre follows the parent (slot 68: its position and height). Slot 26 of `CParticleAI`/`CFloatParticleAI` runs slot 45 for a movable entity (asking `IsKindOf` twice); slot 31 lets particles of the same parent pass each other. `CGravityParticleAI`: Begin (slot 23) sets "Gravity Constant" = "Gravity" × the double at `0x5fbed0` and the acceleration (0, 0, -constant) (slot 118), Update (slot 26) the acceleration again; slot 45 with "Use Velocity to Advance Frames" advances the frame by the speed in x and y × seconds over the sequence's fps; slot 25 bounces an active entity below the ground (slot 46): falling, the velocity loses its normal part and is scaled by 1 - the model's +0x38, stops below the model's +0x3c (squared length), loses the normal part × the model's +0x34 once more when that is longer than the model's +0x40; the height becomes -depth and the rise is limited to the velocity × seconds; the next frame above ground plays "Bounce Sound". `CSwirlParticleAI`: Begin draws the current angular velocity (± the variance's absolute value), Update turns the entity around the centre in the plane with y stretched by 1/(ratio · 0.712766) and, with "Rotate Velocity", sets its velocity again (unchanged).
- **The start points** [confirmed: code; checked]: point: the origin itself; line: along z, the centre length × a random factor in [-1, 1] (the game generator); disk: a random unit vector in the y-z plane (generator `0x712cc0`), or with "Use Cone Angle For Start Pos" the direction's y and z normalised (a random one when both are 0), times a random radius between the inside radius and inside + outside, y × "YX Ratio"; cylinder: the disk's point with x random in [0, height]; sphere: a random vector in the cube [-1, 1]³ normalised, or the direction itself, then the disk's radius. Slot 27 advances and slot 28 resets the type's envelopes; slots 29/30/31 give the first, second and third envelope's value.
- **Table trigonometry** [confirmed: the swirl's rotation `x' = dx·cos - dy·sin`, `y' = dx·sin + dy·cos` only works out with this reading; section 8, "The entity classes above CEntityAnimated"]: `0x508da0` is the cosine and `0x508ec0` the sine (`ai_common.h` names them the other way round; the reimplementation calls them by address). They reduce the angle to [0, 2π) with fistp and read their table at an index from it [confirmed: code `0x508da0`]; for huge angles the float reduction leaves the range [assumption: why the original ended the game with random angles in the checks; not traced]: the checks keep the angles finite.
- **Findings**: the system's slot 26 asks the game type getter twice and `CParticleAI`'s slot 26 asks `IsKindOf` twice for the same class; the exe relies on the same answer (with a different one it would use a null game type or entity). A failed `Entity_CreateFromModel` or `Object_Clone` (or a particle AI template that is no `CParticleAI`) leaves a null pointer that the exe uses without a test. `CGravityParticleAI`'s bounce height is 2 · a4 - depth with a4 always 0. `_CIfmod` with 0, NaN or infinity returns NaN without an error (checked in the VM).
- **Not hookable**: `CDiskParticleStartPositionType`'s slot 26 `0x52b5d0` (4 bytes: `fld [ecx+0x54]; ret`; the reimplementation's `DiskStart_Ratio` documents it).
- **Leaving out** (Rendering): the system's debug drawing (slot 41 `0x530830` with `0x52ecd0`, the static colours `0x6d0200`/`0x6d0460`/`0x6d03d0`/`0x6d0398`), the start point types' debug drawing (slot 24 `0x52bd50`, `0x52c530`, `0x52d470`, `0x52dc00` with `0x52b010`, `0x52cfb0`, `0x52af80`), the sprite blitters `0x530d70`–`0x535310` with `0x5317b0` (not blitters but the converting wrappers between the start point types, corrected in section 9, "The last effects: …", "The 'particle sprite drawers' are converting wrappers"; 60-entry function table `0x5fc048` filled by the static initialisers `0x52a220`–`0x52a8a0`; `docs/functions.csv` counts them as `CSwirlParticleAI`'s slots 47–105 because the table follows its vtable) and the palette mapping `0x5280e0`. The registration names "Particle System On"/"Off" (`0x52dd00`, `0x52dd10`, static initialisers) stay with the message registry.

Two functions start with a branch (`Text_ToUpper` `0x587c00`, `Text_ReplaceChar` `0x587ce0`) and have no trampoline (the checks put the original's bytes back).

- **CShootEntityBehavior and CPointWeaponAtTargetEntityBehavior** [confirmed: code, RegisterFields; checked]: the shoot behaviour (+0xc the owned "Play Sequence", +0x10 the last angle off the target, 2π for none) waits while the angle to the target (`CLayerPart_TurnToPart` with the entity's slot 47 of 1.0) is above the primary weapon's shoot angle (`0x4d6520`) and still shrinking; otherwise, when the entity may shoot (slot 102), a walking entity gets the "shoot" message (`0x713c3c`, vtable `0x5fcfd4`) and a flying or stationary one fires: the weapon's sequence name (its slot 35) through the behaviour's own slot 30, which plays the sequence once (back to the function-local static "Idle" `0x713660`) when the model has it and otherwise fires once through a `CDischargeWeaponThisFrameBaseAction` built on the stack (Set 0, 0, 0, 1.0; `CAction_ExecuteFrom`); the weapon is told (slot 23). A weapon that is not ready (slot 39 above 0) or no primary item does nothing. The debug drawing is the cone of the shoot angle around the aiming angle, 999 pixels long. The point-at behaviour turns the aiming angle (slot 103) towards the target by at most the model's turn speed (`0x517510`) × seconds while the angle is above `0x600a80`; its RegisterFields only sets the class info's old name "CTurnToTargetEntityBehavior" (+8).

Its debug drawing is an oval of the distance for a cone not below `0x6016cc`, else the cone's arc. The queue runs its behaviours (+0xc, pool array) one after the other: the current one (+0x1c) begins when "Changed Behavior" (+0x20) is set, the next follows when it ends or is null; Begin restarts a queue past its end; Append marks the first behaviour of an empty queue to begin.
