### Batch R4: the MMX spans T18–T23 [verified 2026-10-27, VM]

102 functions in two modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): `reimpl/src/spans_mmx.cpp` (34: T18 Alpha_Copy_MMX, T19 Alpha_Fill_MMX) and `spans_mmx_opacity.cpp` (68: T20 Opacity_Copy_MMX, T21 Opacity_Fill_MMX, T22 AlphaOpacity_Copy_MMX, T23 AlphaOpacity_Fill_MMX), each table's entries 1–16 and its generic loop. The MMX blocks, the portable form and the templates are in `reimpl/src/spans_mmx.h` (on top of R3's `spans16.h`). These are the spans the game really draws with: the blend modes register their MMX blitters when `Cpu_HasMmx` says yes, which every x86 CPU since the Pentium MMX does (the VMs too: the checks log "the CPU has MMX: 1").

**Structure** [confirmed: code of all 102 functions, an instruction listing per function compared]: one C++ template per table with an `__asm` block. A span of n pixels (the entry's own n or the generic loop's count) blends n >> 2 groups of four pixels in MMX (a do-while over the groups, entered only for n ≥ 4), then the n & 3 last pixels in C with the scalar blend and the scalar weight of the twin table T12–T17 (`blend565`, R3). Entries 1–3 and the generic loops with n ≤ 3 run no MMX instruction; their code is the twin's. The generic loops test the count (n = 0 does nothing), unlike the do-while generic loops of T12, T14 and T16. Calls and stubs as T12–T17 (entry 0 `Stub_Ret8` for T18, T19, T22, T23, `0x401110` for T20, T21; fastcall `(dst, src or value; [alpha,] n)`). There are only four distinct MMX blocks, the same instructions in every entry of a table: T18 (`0x4516e0`), T20 (`0x455470`), T22 (`0x459350`) and one fill block shared by T19, T21 and T23 (`0x453510`); each has its own copy of seven qword masks (`0x60cc78`, `0x60ccb0`, `0x60cce8`, `0x60cd58`, rows in `exe_symbols.csv`).

**The MMX blend** [confirmed: code; the checks compare the portable form with the original]: per 16-bit lane, with the weight w (0..255), a6 = w >> 2, a5 = a6 >> 1, i6 = 63 − a6, i5 = 31 − a5 (`psubsb` from 0x3f and 0x1f): green G = 16 · gs · a6 + 16 · gd · i6 + 0x200, g = ((G + (G >> 6)) >> 5) & 0x7e0; blue B = bs · a5 + bd · i5 + 0x10, b = (B + (B >> 5)) >> 5; red R likewise with the top five bits, shifted back by 11; the pixel b | g | r. No lane overflows for w ≤ 255 (G ≤ 64016), so the `pmullw`/`paddw` arithmetic equals plain integer arithmetic and the portable form is exact. It is a weighted mean with the divisor 31 (63 for green) and rounding; weight 255 gives the full source (the scalar blend never does), 0 the destination.

**The weights** [confirmed: code]: T18 the alpha bytes, T19 the alpha's low byte, T21 and T23 the scalar twins' bytes (`g_OpacityTable` + 0x3fc, + 4 · alpha). Two differ from their own scalar tails: T20's groups take the **low byte** of the dword at `g_OpacityTable` + 0x3fc, its tail the whole dword (as T14); T22's groups take (alpha · o) >> 8 with o that low byte (`pmullw`, `psrlw 8`), its tail the opacity table's dword `g_OpacityTable[alpha]` (as T16). With the real fade tables (dwords ≤ 0xff) the T20 difference vanishes, the T22 one does not. T22's block also loads the group's four alpha bytes into edx and never uses them.

**MMX state** [confirmed: code; the checks compare it]: the fill block ends with `emms`, the three literal blocks do not, so a literal span of four or more pixels leaves the MMX state set (all x87 tags valid, top 0) for the blitter's own `emms` (and `BlitAmplifyLight_16RleTo16_MMX` `0x4355f0` has none: R5). The reimplementation runs the four blocks instruction for instruction (generated from the original blocks; the object code's blocks were compared with the exe's after building, the same instructions and operands but the masks' addresses), so it leaves the same mm0–mm7 values and tags; only the GPRs around them are the compiler's.

**Do MMX and scalar spans give the same pixels? No** (the open question of the blitter map) [confirmed: formula over all channel values, VM checks]: the MMX groups round to the nearest of a weighted mean, the scalar spans add 31/32 (63/64) of the difference rounded down. Exhaustively per channel over all weights: blue (and red) differ in 117,600 of 262,144 (s, d, w) combinations, green in 495,668 of 1,048,576, by at most 2 steps; equal only for w = 0 and, blue/red, w < 8. Over random pixels and weights 83 % of the pixels differ. In the game's own data (the checks below, random and real pixels, real edge alpha bytes, the real fade tables): 69.7 % of the MMX group pixels of T18/T19 and 73.8 % of T20–T23 differ from the scalar twin, at most 2 steps per channel, while every pixel the MMX spans blend in C (entries 1–3, the tails) is the twin's. Since the game uses the MMX spans on every machine it meets, **the port takes the MMX results**: `blend565_mmx` for the groups of four and `blend565` for the tail, i.e. the result depends on the pixel's position in its RLE run (index ≥ 4 · (n >> 2) of the span). R7 found the same for the polygon fills.

**Checks** (`checks_spans_mmx.cpp`, `checks_spans_mmx_opacity.cpp`, shared in `checks_spans_mmx.h` on the frame harness and R3's span cases):
- The live tables: T18–T23 entry 0 the stub, entries 1–16 the module's hooks, 17–63 one hooked generic loop.

### Batch R7: the line and polygon rasterizers and the frame load filters [verified 2026-10-27, VM]

106 functions in five modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): `reimpl/src/raster_line.cpp` (6: CFrame slot 52's line rasterizer `0x42b160`–`0x42c9e0` and its tables), `raster_poly.cpp` (31: the polygon point lists, the clipping, the edges, `PolyRaster_Draw` and the 8/16-bit fills with the MMX twins), `frame_load_convert.cpp` (15: the depth conversion, filter kind 11), `frame_load_filters.cpp` (30: the filter list and the filters 2–7, 10), `frame_load_rle.cpp` (24: the RLE encoder, kind 8), with `frame_load.h` for the filter layout. Checks: `checks_raster_line.cpp`, `checks_raster_poly.cpp`, `checks_frame_load.cpp` (one module for the three load-filter modules: their hooks are taken out together).

**The line rasterizer** [confirmed: code; compared in the VM]: slot 52 draws an antialiased line of one pixel (Wu's algorithm, not a thick line as the blitter map assumed): the float end points become 16.16 relative to the origin, are clipped with the frame's rectangle (slot 36, which includes the origin) shifted by 16 (`Line_ClipToRect`), and one of three rasterizers steps the major axis by pixels and the minor one by a 16.16 slope (`Platform_MulDivShift`, one smaller in magnitude when it would overshoot), blending two pixels per step with weights 255 − f and f (f = the minor coordinate's bits 8–15). 8 bits: the channel tables per palette index `0x62eb18`/`0x675fb8`/`0x674fb0` blended with truncation towards zero, then the 5-5-5 inverse colour table `0x633388`; 16 bits: green with w >> 2 and a logical shift by 1, red and blue with w >> 3 on unsigned differences, each masked into its field; 24 bits per byte; 32 bits nothing. The 8-bit rasterizer gets the end points without fractions. Quirks kept: the rasterizers draw unclipped when both end points (+2) lie inside the frame (the x-major paths clamp a negative row to 0, the steep ones do not), else they test every pixel against slot 36's rectangle (origin included while the coordinates are not); the 16-bit red keeps the colour argument's upper word. `SpanTables_Init` `0x42b320` builds two tables nobody in the range reads: a coverage table (Gupta-Sproull terms with `_CIasin`, 79 entries at `0x62ea40`) and 65536/√(1 + x²) in 1024 steps (`0x62ea3c`).

**The polygon rasterizer** [confirmed: code; compared in the VM]:
- The polygon (vtable `0x5fd35c`) is a point list with an embedded array of 12.4 fixed-point points at +4 (pool allocated), +0x14 the render type, +0x18 its parameter (the texture frame of type 5); `PolyPoints_FromFloat` `0x549530` makes it from the float polygon (× 16, truncated). The constructor `0x5484a0` also stores `Cpu_HasMmx` in `0x7121f4` and, while `0x7121f3` is 0 (nothing sets it), builds the 8-bit tint tables from the game palette: half brightness `0x7120f4`, blue + 72 `0x711ff4`, red + 72 `0x711db8`, green + 72 `0x711ef4` (the nearest index, 1–254).
- `PolyRaster_Draw` `0x549050` clips the polygon to slot 36's rectangle (`PolyRaster_Clip` `0x548920`: outcodes left 1, right 2, top 4, bottom 8 against the rectangle × 16; a polygon inside is drawn as it is; else Sutherland–Hodgman plane by plane (left, top, right, bottom) between the two static clip lists `0x711d88`/`0x711ec8` (vtable `0x5fd368`, an outcode array at +0x1c; function-local statics with the guard `0x711db4`), the crossing by `MulDiv`), and draws nothing below 3 points. Quirks: a plane ORs the full outcode of the first point of every pair that lies outside it into its result, and the closing edge returns the first point's code in that case (both only decide which planes follow and which static list comes back); after the right plane the clip tests the codes of the plane before, so it never returns early there.
- The fills draw the triangle fan (0, i, i + 1): the corners sorted by y with signed compares, the three edges set up for the rows from ceil(y/16) with an exact fraction (`PolyEdge_Setup` `0x54d040`: floor division with the remainder, the denominator dy × 16) and stepped per row (`PolyEdge_Step` `0x54d0f0`); the long edge left when the cross product is ≥ 0. A span covers [left x, right x) minus the origin. 16 bits: 0 black (`Mem_FillBytes`), 1 half brightness (`& 0x7bef`), 2 blue + `[0x61eacc]` (10), 3 green + `[0x61ead4]` (0x140), 4 red + `[0x61ead0]` (0x5000), each saturated in its field; 3 and 5 walk the whole polygon themselves. 8 bits: 0 the index of the colour `0x6be368` (a static dword `0x7160bc`, guard bit 1 of `0x7160b8`), 1–4 through the tint tables (2 blue, 3 green, 4 red).
- MMX [confirmed: code; compared in the VM with `0x7121f4` on and off]: types 2–4 of 16 bits have MMX twins (`0x54bb70`, `0x5495a0`, `0x54c180`): groups of four pixels as `((q & field) << s) +us (k << s) >> s | (q & rest)` with `paddusw` (s = 11 blue, 5 green, 0 red), `emms` after each span's groups, the remaining pixels scalar. The reimplementation uses the same MMX instructions. The twins differ from the scalar fills when a field saturates: green gives 0x7ff (the blue bits set) instead of 0x7e0, red 0xffff instead of 0xf800 with the other fields; blue saturates alike. Every CPU the game runs on today takes the MMX path.

**The frame load filters** [confirmed: code; compared in the VM]:
- A filter (`frame_load.h`) is {vtable (0 deleting destructor, 1 Clone, 2 Apply (frame, rect) → al), next, kind, depth (−1), lock byte, parameter}; the list is a filter itself (the base vtable `0x5f4934`, Apply `0x4e96b0` = true), the others sorted by kind, each kind once (`FrameFilterList_Insert` `0x4b2060` replaces it, deleting the old one with the chain flag `0x613d78` cleared). `FrameFilterList_Run` `0x4b21a0` applies the list and every filter with the rectangle (0, 0, width, height) and ANDs the results (the blitter map's "Copy"); `0x4b1d50` clones a list into another (not "Apply"); `0x4b22d0` and `0x4b2680` construct filters 2 and 6 (not "Unlock"/"Lock").
- Kinds: 2 origin moved by half the rectangle (unsigned halves), 3 alpha below the parameter (5; 3 with CSequence flag 8) cleared in 32-bit frames (its Clone reloads the parameter through a qword × 1/255 × 255), 4 for "Blend Black Bias": at target depth 8 palette indices/pixels whose largest channel is below 0x28 become 0 (asking slot 46 per pixel), else a 24-bit frame is blitted into a 32-bit one and every alpha becomes the largest channel (any other depth is treated as 32 bits), 5 for "Blend Amplify Light": 32-bit pixels whose largest channel is below the parameter (15) cleared, 6 cropped to the bounding box with the origin moved (an empty frame freed), 7 un-premultiplied alpha (alpha 1–254: A = a/255 raised to c/255 for a channel with c/A > 255, then min(255, c/A + 0.5); black becomes blue 1), 8 the RLE encoder, 10 the palette of an 8-bit frame from a colour histogram (its Apply stays the exe's: it crashed in the checks on a frame without a palette), 11 the depth conversion (12 in `FrameFilterList_Add` is 11 with dither). `Add` computes the target depth for kind 3 and never uses it; kind 4 adds kind 7 unless the target is 8 bits.
- The depth conversion (kind 11, +0x14 the depth, +0x18 dither): plain frames converted in their own buffer (to 8 bits the nearest index in `0x633388`'s palette, 1–254, or the error-diffusion ditherer `0x4811b0`; to 16 bits `Pixel16_FromRGB` or the ditherer quantising to 5 bits per channel until it is satisfied; to 24 bits from 32 bits only, and only when the first pixel's alpha is at least 250 — it tests that one pixel width × height times); compressed frames re-encoded row by row in place: control bytes copied (dropped for the alpha block), each literal pixel and each run's pixel converted, the row table and the block's size rewritten. An "8-bit RLE" frame of 32 bits converts all five blocks. A literal of length 0 loops 2^32 times (the encoder never writes one).
- The RLE encoder (kind 8, +0x14 0 for 8-bit, 1 for 16-bit frames; Apply only while `0x613d74` is set): a 32-bit frame is split into alpha bands (`RleEncode_AlphaBand` `0x4aecd0`: lo < alpha ≤ hi kept). 8 bits: above 229 the pixel block, 178–229 the edge block, 127–178 the alpha block, 76–127 the third block (+0x24), 25–76 the extra block (+0x1c) — so the 8-bit frames' translucency is five fixed levels; 16 bits: above 250 the pixel block, 5–250 both the edge and the alpha block (two encodings of one band). The row encoders emit up to 0x7f clear pixels as a skip, runs of more than 8 equal pixels (at most 0x3f) and literals (up to 63, ended before 8 equal pixels); the values stay whole 32-bit pixels for the conversion filter after it. "Equal": the nearest palette index (8 bits), the 5-6-5 pixel (16 bits), for the 16-bit edge band (`RleEncode_Blocks24`) also an alpha differing only in its low three bits, for the 8-bit edge band (`RleEncode_Blocks16`) never (`0x4b1b60` returns 0: only literals). 8- and 16-bit sources are encoded as they are (`RleEncode_Bytes` `0x4b16d0`, `RleEncode_Words` `0x4b18b0`), 24-bit ones blitted into a 32-bit frame first (black pixels with alpha 0). The rows go through the scratch frame `0x6be7e8` (width in `0x6be7e0`); `0x6be828` counts the bytes saved. Corrected names: see `docs/exe_symbols.csv` ("was … in the blitter map").

**Not reimplemented here** (open; since done: the fills, their helpers and filter 10 in batch R6, `raster_rest.cpp`, the static initializer `0x4aeca0` in `static_rest4a.cpp`): the 24-bit polygon fills and their span helpers (`0x549d50`–`0x54a860`, `0x54caf0`–`0x54cdf0`, 11 functions: no 24-bit frames in the game), the textured fills `0x549aa0`/`0x54c9b0` (16 bits) and `0x54b230` (8 bits), the green fill's span helpers `0x549820`, `0x54c790`, `0x54c8e0` (only the original green fills call them), filter 10's Apply `0x4b2b50`, the static initializer `0x4aeca0` (runs before the DLL). Draw calls them through their addresses.

**Checks** (in the game thread; side 0 with the module's hooks out):
- Lines: `CFrame_DrawLineSpans` 4,000 cases on fake frames of 8/16/24/32 bits (sizes 1–90 × 1–70, pitch padding, origins ±6, CDIBFrame), float end points inside, on and across the edges, far outside, degenerate (point, horizontal, vertical, 45°, sub-pixel), colours with and without the index, every fourth case on a real frame's pixels; the three rasterizers directly 3,000 (16.16 end points, both paths); the tables with no, a big enough and a too small cover table, and the free (10).
- Polygons: `PolyRaster_Draw` 3,000 on fake frames of 8/16/24 bits with 0–12-point polygons (inside, across edges and corners, far outside, collinear, sub-pixel, flat edges), every type, MMX on and off, the black static made anew or kept, a power-of-two texture; the clip with its outcodes and the edges 3,000; the point lists, their destructors and `FromFloat` 600 sequences on heap objects (only written elements compared: `SetCount` leaves pool contents), the constructor with the tables rebuilt, the static lists' destructors on stand-ins.
- Load filters: the conversion of plain frames 1,500 (16/24/32 bits, random and real pixels, all depths, dither) and of RLE frames 1,500 (both RLE kinds, 3- and 4-byte pixels, any of the five blocks, rows adding up exactly); the row encoders and length helpers 3,000 (rows with runs, literals, clear stretches, the row width cut anywhere); the list 600 random sequences of Add (kinds 0–13), Remove, Find, the depths, CloneInto and locks; the small filters 1,800 on fake frames (directly and through `Run`) and 400 on heap frames (6, 4 at depth 16, the clones); the encoder's Apply 500 on heap frames of 8/16/24/32 bits for both encoders with and without a (dithering) conversion filter, every fifth on a real frame's pixels: every block and table, the flags, the origin, the bytes saved and the scratch frame.
- Development finds (all in the reimplementation's first draft or the checks, none in the original): `RleEncode_RunLength16` compares the alphas with xor, not or; the planes' and the closing edge's codes of pairs outside (the returned static list differed in 15 of 2,988 clips, the drawn pixels never); the pool's calling convention (`pool_get` `0x506470` takes no argument; `pool_alloc` (pool; size), `pool_free` (pool; block, size)); a check's rectangle drawn per side; filter 10 crashing on frames without a palette.

Runs: development jobs `20261027-064846-1635` … `20261027-073638-7742` (each difference found there is listed above). Final build: all modules with all cases on `Test/Nachbau1` `20261027-075818-b273` (all 814 checks the same; `frame_load` 6,625 ms, `raster_line` 875, `raster_poly` 3,094) and on `ACT 2/M9/09 Assimilate Cave1` (start point `Respawn2`, `--no-level`) `20261027-073722-9737` (all 814 the same; 6,875, 953, 3,219 ms), 6575 hooks installed (106 new; the two not installed are `DebugLog_SectionBegin`/`End` as before), `Zip CRC` and `All checks done` in the log. The Nachbau1 run before (`20261027-073722-1d66`) had `SpanTables_Init` differ in 2 of 10 cases, in the hash of a reused cover table that the check gave each side as a fresh heap block [assumption: entries the builder leaves unwritten kept the blocks' different contents; not traced]; the check now fills that block alike and clears the MMX state first. `--shot-set` `20261027-075818-658e` … `20261027-075819-c8c4` (the line, polygon and load-filter hooks in): all 9 scenes identical or different only in animated areas; the load filters were also in for `20261027-071511-495a` … `-121a` (four scenes, the same).

### Batch R5: the blitters with 8- and 16-bit destinations, their rows and RLE drawers, the screen and Filter modes [verified 2026-10-27, VM]

102 functions in five modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`), shared shapes in `reimpl/src/blitters.h`: `rle16.cpp` (39: the 16-bit RLE blitters of Copy, Amplify Light, Overlap and the hue remap with their full drawers, clipped rows and edge rows, and the remap helpers), `rle8.cpp` (20: the 8-bit RLE blitters of Copy (to 8 and 16 bits), Black Bias / Test Light and Amplify Light with their drawers and rows), `blitters_raw.cpp` (20: plain sources: Copy, Black Bias, Overlap, Tile, TileWrap, Normal Scale with their rows), `blitters_screen.cpp` (17: ScreenCopy and the Up/Down levels for 5-5-5 and 5-6-5 displays, MMX and plain), `blitters_filter.cpp` (6: the Filter mode's two blitters and its resampler). Checks in `checks_blitters.cpp` (one check module per module).

**Hooks, not registry patches** [confirmed: code]: the blitter map proposed patching the registry entries because the blitters are reached through `FindBlitter`; every one of the 102 entries has five bytes without a relative jump, so they are hooked like every other function. A hook at the original address catches the registry's calls, the direct callers (the hue remap and Normal Scale blitters call drawers by address, `CScreenFrame::vf23` the screen modes through the registry) and the checks alike, and `Disable=` and the checks' hook switching work unchanged. The rows, edge rows and drawers call each other through their exe addresses, the spans (R2–R4) through their tables (`call [n * 4 + table]`), so whichever version a table holds runs.

**The shapes** [confirmed: code; compared in the running game]:
- The opacity test of every blitter: `CBlendMode_GetOpacity` compared with 1.0f (`0x5ec3f4`) by `fcomp`/`test ah, 0x40`: equal or unordered (NaN) takes the opaque path; otherwise `g_OpacityTable` = `g_FadeTables` + opacity255 · 0x400 first.
- RLE rows (FORMATS.md 5): x starts at dstRect.left − srcRect.left; full rows draw whole segments while x < dstRect.right, clipped rows cut each segment to [dstRect.left, dstRect.right); a run's value is the dword at its data (low byte or word counts). Edge rows take one alpha byte per literal pixel and one per run, in order.
- 16-bit RLE blitters: srcRect.left = 0 and srcRect.right = the source's width (slot 45, asked only when left is 0) take the full drawer (`fastcall (src, srcRect; dst, dstRect)`, `ret 8`: the pixel block's rows, then the edge block, both from the same first destination row; slots dst 40, src 31, dst 31, dst 46, src 46, then src 35, 34, 50, 49), otherwise the clipped rows row by row. Copy, Transparent Mask and Black Bias share `0x438c40`/`0x4388f0`; the MMX blitters differ only in their rows' span tables and end with `emms` on every path, except Amplify Light's `0x4355f0` (the map's finding). Overlap draws the full frame whatever the opacity (setting `g_OpacityTable` only when it is not 1) and uses the same rows on both clipped paths.
- 8-bit RLE drawers (`ret 0x10`, a level and an unread table pointer): the level (the mode's +0x24, 5 − (6 · opacity255 >> 8)) shifts the source's five blocks along four span table pairs and a row function, the pairs kept in the globals `0x630330`–`0x630357`: at level 0 the pixel block is drawn opaque (T0/T1), the edge block with the 20/80 tables (T2/T3), the alpha block with 40/60 (T4/T5), the third (+0x24) with 40/60 SD (T6/T7) and the extra block (+0x1c) through the row with T8/T9; at level k the pixel block with pair k; level 5 and above draws nothing. What the five blocks of an 8-bit RLE frame hold is open (neither test map has one; the game runs in 16 bits) (answered by the RLE encoder, batch R7 above: alpha bands above 229, 178–229, 127–178, 76–127 and 25–76; the opacity steps confirmed in the game at 8 bit by the editor on 2026-10-30, CLAUDE.md step 38).
- Plain blits: width and height of dstRect, the row starts src + (rows[srcRect.top] + srcRect.left) · bytes (slots src 31, 46, dst 46, 31, src 40, dst 40), the height tested first; the opaque paths ask the source for a palette (slots 59, 58) and pass its data to rows that ignore it. Copy 16 → 16 with an opacity blends with the dword at `g_OpacityTable` + 0x3fc (R3's `blend565`), Copy 8 → 8 with an opacity takes the 20/80 table whatever the opacity; 8 → 16, 16 → 8 and the screen modes draw the same on both paths. Black Bias 8 → 8: `dst = table[src · 256 + dst]` with the mode's table (vtable slot 3, also put into `g_Blend8Table` and cleared afterwards), the source's palette when the mode has none. Black Bias 16 → 16 MMX (its only registration): groups of four in MMX with the weight's low byte, the rest scalar with the whole dword. Overlap remaps the destination through the Overlap map and never reads the source. Tile masks the source position with the power-of-two masks (slots 41/42), TileWrap (dead code) wraps by compare. Normal Scale scales the whole source to dstRect in 16.16 steps ((size << 16) / n, lowered by 2 while it overshoots), returning when dstRect is empty, starts below 0 or ends beyond the frame; srcRect.left is added to every source row, srcRect.top ignored.
- The screen modes (`CScreenFrame::vf23` only): ScreenCopy converts 5-6-5 to 5-5-5 (`((M1 >> 1) & (p >> 1)) | (M0 & p)`, the masks read from .data), 8 → 16 through the 5-5-5 palette. Up/Down: the plain pixel looks up three dword tables at channel + level (5-5-5: after converting); the MMX groups add the shifted levels with saturation (Up, `paddusw`) or **subtract** them (Down, `psubusw`). **Correction to the blitter map**: Up and Down have the same arithmetic only in their plain variants (the tables min(31, i) and min(63, i) from R1, read at channel + level: both brighten); the MMX Down darkens. `CScreenFrame::vf23` gives Down the negated level (a positive one, SetLevel clamps to 0..255), so the MMX Down darkens as intended and the plain Down brightens instead [confirmed: code; the plain variant is only registered on a CPU without MMX]. This answers the map's open question: the game never needs a negative level, the two Down variants simply disagree.
- The MMX rows and inline paths of the screen modes go to an 8-byte aligned destination pixel by pixel (stopping at count 0), then groups of four with `emms` after them, then the rest with the plain pixel, **reading the rest from where the groups started** (the destination is advanced, the source is not) [quirk kept]; the plain ScreenCopy row converts an unaligned first pixel without testing the count.
- The hue remap (CBlendHueRemap, +0x44 its 16-bit table): the blitters put the source's blocks through a render effect on the stack (vtable `0x5eeed4`: `0x571b70` constructor, slot 28 `0x572020` saves the blocks and gives the frame a buffer, slot 30 `0x572680` puts them back, `0x571bb0` destructor), remap them with `HueRemap8_Literal` (an 8-bit RLE block through a 256-byte table: all five blocks of an 8-bit frame, with the mode's palette data) or `HueRemap8_Run` (a 16-bit RLE block through the word table `0x6bb4d8`: the pixel and edge blocks), then draw like Copy; the opacity clipped path goes through a drawer of its own (`0x43d980`/`0x43d720`, renamed `Rle16_DrawClipped_HueRemap(MMX)`: they clip, the map's "Unclipped" was wrong). The remap helpers loop while the pixels left in a row are not exactly 0 and their literals are do-while loops (a zero-length literal runs 2^32 times). The 16-bit blitters on an 8-bit RLE source would pass an uninitialized stack dword as the remap table (unreachable: registered for 16R → 16 only).
- The Filter: the blitters copy srcRect into a 16-bit stack frame (CFrame::Blit with Copy, the screen object's +0xd0 setting switched off by `0x569520` around it), resample it into a frame of dstRect's size and blit that with Copy (`Frame_BlitAt`); 8 → 8 converts the result to 8 bits first (a depth filter, dither 1). The resampler (FilterState, a static at `0x716120`, built on first use: guard bit 1 of `0x716100`, atexit `0x43bf20`) is a separable Mitchell–Netravali cubic (B = C = 1/3) in x87: weight lists per output column and row (taps from ceil(c − r) to floor(c + r) around c = i / scale, r = 2 / scale when shrinking (x and weight scaled by `scale`), else 2; indices mirrored at the edges), the pixels unpacked to blue << 3, green << 2 and red, the weighted sums through three tables (round(i · 31/255) and round(i · 63/255), clamped, for −128..383) at sum + 128.5. The column pass keeps the minimum and maximum of red + 0.5 in `0x6b9c98`/`0x6bacd4` (read nowhere) and steps through its frames by width · 2 (they are made by SetSize). The weights are rebuilt only when the scale (out / in, 80 bits, against the stored float) and the sizes are unchanged.
- **Small frames read outside their buffers** [confirmed: VM]: the mirrored tap indices stay inside a row only for at least 3 pixels on both ends (e.g. 1 → n upscaling takes taps −2..2, mirrored to index −1 for a 1-pixel row); below that the original reads heap bytes around its row buffer (different on the two sides of a check: the first runs differed in about 10 % of the cases). The checks use 3 × 3 and more; the port should clamp the indices.
- Quirks kept: the do-while width loops of the blending, converting and Overlap loops (width 0 runs 2^32 times); Amplify Light's edge rows call address 0 (its edge tables are 0; R3); dynamic span tables with a zero-length code run 2^32 times (R2).

### Batch R6: the 24- and 32-bit destinations — the span tables T24–T35, the blitters to and from 24/32 bits, Transparent Mask's own blitters, and the rest of R7 [verified 2026-10-27, VM]

275 functions in six modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`), shared shapes in `reimpl/src/blit24.h` (on top of R5's `blitters.h`): `blit24_spans32.cpp` (68: T24–T27 with their generic loops), `blit24_spans.cpp` (70: T28–T31, their generic loops and the two no-op entries 0 of the 24-bit Fill tables), `blit24_spans_op.cpp` (68: T32–T35), `blit24.cpp` (34: Copy's blitters to and from 24/32 bits with their rows, the 32 → 24 pixel blend, the 24R → 24 and 16R → 32 blitters with their drawers and rows, Normal Scale 24 → 24/32 with its rows, Tile and TileWrap 24 → 24, the screen mode's 24 → 16), `blit24_tm.cpp` (15: Transparent Mask's own blitters `0x464fe0`–`0x465d10` with the 24R → 32 drawers and rows `0x466080`–`0x466910`) and `raster_rest.cpp` (20: the rest of R7: the 24-bit polygon fills and their half-triangle helpers, the textured fills of 8 and 16 bits, the green fills' helpers, filter 10's Apply with its colour histogram). Checks: `checks_blit24.cpp` (one check module per blit24 module) and `checks_raster_rest.cpp`.

**Mapped here** (the blitter map left them out) [confirmed: code, the tables in `.data`, the registrations of `CBlendTransparentMask_Ctor` `0x4479c0`]: T31's entries 7–16 `0x4600c0`–`0x4609c0` (`Span24_Alpha_Fill_7`…`_16`), T32 `0x460ac0`–`0x461a70` (`Span24_Opacity_Copy_1`…`_16`), T33 `0x461b80`–`0x462c20` (`Span24_Opacity_Fill_*`), T34 `0x462d40`–`0x463d00` (`Span24_AlphaOpacity_Copy_*`), T35 `0x463e20`–`0x464ec0` (`Span24_AlphaOpacity_Fill_*`), the no-op `0x463e10` (entry 0 of T31 and T35, `ret 8`); Transparent Mask's raw blitters 8 → 8 `0x464fe0`, 8 → 16 `0x4651d0`, 8 → 24 `0x4653d0`, 8 → 32 `0x465660`, 16 → 16 `0x4658d0`, 16 → 24 `0x465ae0` and 24R → 32 `0x465d10` with its full drawers `0x466080`/`0x466260`, clipped rows `0x466440`/`0x466660`, clipped edge rows `0x466540`/`0x466760` and edge rows `0x466880`/`0x466910`. Its other keys (24/32 → 24/32, the RLE keys 8R/16R/24R) are Copy's.

**The spans** [confirmed: code of every entry; compared in the running game]: fastcall `(dst, src or value; [alpha,] n)` like R2–R4, entries 1–16 one template instance per count, 17–63 the generic loop.
- T24–T27 (16 → 32): blue `p << 3`, green `(p >> 5) << 2`, red `(p >> 8) & 0xf8` (each its low byte), the fourth byte 0xff (T24/T25), the alpha byte `alpha[i]` (T26) or the alpha's low byte (T27).
- T28/T29 (24-bit copy and fill): three bytes per pixel; the fill stores the first pixel and copies it forward with `rep movsb` over the rest.
- T30–T35 (24-bit blends): per channel `c = d + trunc((s − d) · w / 256)` in 32-bit signed arithmetic (`imul` wraps; `cdq`, `and edx, 0xff`, `sar 8`), the three channels put back together as `((d2 + q2) << 8 + d1 + q1) << 8 + d0 + q0` and its low three bytes stored, so a weight above 0xff carries one channel into the next. The weights as for 16 bits (R3): T30 `alpha[i]`, T31 the alpha's low byte, T32 the **dword** at `g_OpacityTable` + 0x3fc, T33 the byte there, T34 the dword `g_OpacityTable[alpha[i]]`, T35 the byte at `g_OpacityTable` + 4 · alpha. Unlike the 16-bit blend, weight 255 gives 255/256 of the difference rounded towards zero.
- Entry 0: `0x401110` (T24, T25, T28, T32), `Stub_Ret8` (T26, T27, T30, T34), `0x45e730` (T29, T33) and `0x463e10` (T31, T35), the last two the Fill template for n = 0 (`push ecx; mov [esp], edx; pop ecx; ret`). The generic loops of T30, T32 and T34 are do-whiles (n = 0 runs 2^32 times), all others test n.

**The blitters** [confirmed: code; compared in the running game]:
- Plain blits: R5's start (slots src 31, 46, dst 46, 31, src 40, dst 40, the height tested first); the opaque paths ask the source for a palette (slots 59, 58). Copy 24 → 24 and 32 → 32 pass its data to their rows (`0x4378f0`, `0x437950`: a byte copy of width · 3 or · 4 bytes) and copy the same bytes inline on the opacity path: **no blend** with an opacity. 8 → 24/32 through the mode's palette data (vtable slot 3, also in `g_Blend8Table`, cleared at the end), on the opaque path the source's when the mode has none (from address 0 when the source has none either: R1's crash); 16 → 24/32 as T24; 24 → 8 through the 5-5-5 inverse colour table `*0x633388` at `blue[b] + green15[g] + red15[r]`; 24 → 16 Pixel16's tables, the screen mode's 24 → 16 (`0x443d70`, registered by all five screen modes) the 5-5-5 ones; to 32 bits the alpha byte 0xff. The width loops are do-whiles.
- 32 → 24 blends by the source's alpha byte a through the pixel function `0x435230` (fastcall `(weight, dst; out, dst pixel, src pixel)`, `ret 0xc`, returns out; the blitter map's "row"): `c = d + trunc((s − d) · w / 255)`, put back together like T30. Opaque: a ≥ 0xfd copies, a = 0 skips; with an opacity: a ≤ 5 skips, `w = g_OpacityTable[a]` (a dword), w > 0xfa copies.
- RLE: 24R → 24 (Transparent Mask, Black Bias / Test Light, Amplify Light: one function `0x435cb0`), 16R → 32 (Copy, Transparent Mask: `0x440390`) and Transparent Mask's 24R → 32 have R5's shape (the full drawer when srcRect covers the whole width, else the clipped rows; drawers and rows calling each other by exe address, the spans through their tables), 3 bytes per 24-bit RLE pixel. 16R → 32 has no opacity functions: its opacity paths set `g_OpacityTable` and draw with the copy rows.
- Normal Scale, Tile and TileWrap: R5's shapes with 3-byte pixels; Normal Scale's 24 → 32 row writes the three colour bytes and leaves the destination's alpha byte.
- Transparent Mask's raw blitters skip a source pixel 0 (index or word); 8 → 8 and 16 → 16 test the width (loops over source pointers), the others are do-whiles; 8 → 24/32 take the palette like Copy's.

**Quirks kept** [confirmed: code; the checks cover them]:
- Transparent Mask's 24R → 32 draws with the **24-bit** spans T28–T35 on a 32-bit destination: a literal or run of n pixels writes 3n packed bytes from x · 4, so every pixel after a segment's first lands between the destination's pixels.
- The 24-bit polygon fill of type 1 (half brightness, `0x549fe0` and its helper `0x54caf0`) halves the bytes at q + 6, q + 3 and q while stepping q by 3 to the span's end: every byte from the fourth on is halved three times and the five bytes after the span too. Types 2–4 add the tint constant's low byte shifted by 3 (blue), 2 (green), 3 (red) with an 8-bit wrap (the "saturation" compares the wrapped sum with 0xff), so with the constants 10, 0x140 and 0x5000 blue gets + 80 and green and red + 0.
- Filter 10's Apply (`0x4b2b50`) keeps a 1 MB colour histogram (2^18 dwords, 6 bits per channel) on the stack (`_chkstk` 0x100000), as much as the exe's whole stack reserve (`SizeOfStackReserve` 0x100000): it overflows the main thread's stack whenever it runs [confirmed: VM, run `20261027-190931-c6ca` crashed the game in this check; R7's "crash on a frame without a palette" was this]. The reimplementation kept the histogram on the heap (the DLL has no stack probes) until 2026-11-12; since then it is on the stack through the exe's `_chkstk` (section 16, "Batch decomp-faithful2"); the check runs both sides on a thread with a 4 MB stack, and since then also on one of 1 MB, where both overflow. Its helpers: `Histogram_Clear` `0x46dc30` and `Histogram_Add24` `0x46dc50` (width · height 3-byte pixels from the pixels' start, the pitch ignored), then `DrawPalette_Build` `0x527fa0` (kind 1, 0xfe colours) into the frame's palette (slot 58).

**The rest of R7** [confirmed: code; compared in the running game]: the whole-polygon fills (fastcall `(polygon, frame; parameter, 0)`, `ret 8`: the six 24-bit fills by type and the 16-bit texture fill `0x549aa0`) walk the fan (0, i, i + 1) like R7's fills, the first half inline, the second through a helper (fastcall `(frame, parameter; left edge, right edge, rows, 0)`, `ret 0x10`: `0x54caf0`, `0x54cbb0`, `0x54cd30`, `0x54cc70`, `0x54cdf0`, `0x54c9b0`; type 0 draws both halves inline with `Mem_FillBytes`); the 8-bit texture fill `0x54b230` is a triangle fill with both halves inline. A textured half asks frame 43, 44, texture 41, 42, frame 46, 31, texture 46, 31 and tiles the texture in absolute frame coordinates (row `y & ymask`, column `x & xmask` from the span's left x). The green helpers `0x549820` (the scalar tail of the MMX fill's first half), `0x54c8e0` and `0x54c790` (the second halves; R7's reimplemented green fills draw their halves themselves) are the R7 green spans. **Corrected names**: `0x435230` `Blend32To24_Pixel` (was `BlitCopy_32To24_Row`), `0x4658d0` `BlitTransparentMask_16To16`, `0x549820` `PolyFill16_GreenTail` (was `PolyFill_SpanSetup`), the 24-bit fills by what they draw (`PolyFill24_Black`, `_HalfBrightness`, `_Blue`, `_Green` `0x54a640`, `_Red` `0x54a420`, `_Texture`; the map's type numbers swapped 3 and 4), the helpers `…Half`, the textured fills `PolyFill16_Texture`, `PolyFill8_Texture`.

**Does the game use 24/32-bit frames?** [confirmed: callers, VM counters]
- Callers: the 24/32-bit blitters are referenced only as immediates in the blend modes' constructors (their registrations) and the screen modes' (24 → 16); the span tables T24–T35 only by the R6 rows and drawers and by the generic-entry fill of `0x4479c0`; the 24-bit polygon fills only by `PolyRaster_Draw`'s depth-24 branch. So they run only for a frame of 24 or 32 bits (a blit key or a polygon target).
- Frames: every frame the harness finds in the level (the models' sequences, the fonts, the image lists, the ground textures, the world's frames) is 16 bits: `Test/Nachbau1` 7,339 sprites, 3,951 glyphs, 10 textures, 3 world frames; `Assimilate Cave1` 11,420 sprites, 3,951 glyphs, 17 textures, 3 world frames; no frame of 8, 24 or 32 bits.
- Counters: every blitter of the batch counts its calls (`count_call` in `blit24.h`, logged by the first check module of the batch as "R6 evidence"). From the start of the game to the checks (loading and about 20 s in the level, through the reimplementation): no call on `Test/Nachbau1` (run `20261027-185944-036b`) or `Assimilate Cave1` (`20261027-191355-fb4f`, with the auto-map and the inventory opened); with the auto-map opened on `Test/Nachbau1` 277 calls of Transparent Mask's 16 → 16 `0x4658d0` (run `20261027-190931-c6ca`): the auto-map's fog of war and frame. So the game draws with one function of the batch, the 16 → 16 Transparent Mask blit; everything with a 24- or 32-bit frame is unused in the levels tested [assumption for the rest of the game: the data has no 24/32-bit frames (FORMATS.md 5), the screen is 16 bits; 24-bit images that get loaded are converted by the load filters (R7)].

### The HUD: item renderers and their render data, the inventory screen's detail renderers, the item icons, the auto-map [verified 2026-10-26, VM; the drawing through the exe's frame, blitter and font code]

Four modules, 230 hooks (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): `reimpl/src/hud_classes.cpp` (150: the classes), `hud_data.cpp` (25: the render data's network slots), `hud_render.cpp` (24: the HUD renderers, the placement, the item icon, the energy meter, the auto-map), `hud_details.cpp` (31: the detail renderers and the definitions' icons), each with `checks_<module>.cpp`; `checks_hud_common.h` is shared by the drawing checks. 211 of the 219 functions `docs/functions.csv` lists for these classes and helpers, plus 17 static getter copies and `CShieldHUDRenderData::SetShieldCount` `0x56ec50` that it lacks or names `FUN_`. The frame, blend, blitter and font functions they call stay the exe's (R1–R7); `tools/function_table.py` now counts these classes as Rendering (they matched "Inventory" or "HUD" before).

**Classes** [confirmed: constructors, destructors, RegisterFields, docs/classes.csv; VM]: `CInventoryHUDRenderer` (abstract, vtable `0x5edf7c`) with `CCompassRenderer`, `CFlagInventoryHUDRenderer`, `CWeaponInventoryHUDRenderer` ("Show Ammo Icon"), `CShieldInventoryHUDRenderer`, `CEnergyInventoryHUDRenderer` with `CCharacterInventoryHUDRenderer` ("Font") and `CSphereOfZinEnergyInventoryHUDRenderer` (pulse percentages and rates, "Flip HUD Sequence Order", "Overlay HUD Sequence"); `CInventoryHUDRenderData` (0x14: +8 opacity, +0xc catalogue index, +0x10 changed bits) with `CCompassRenderData`, `CWeaponHUDRenderData`, `CEnergyHUDRenderData` and `CShieldHUDRenderData` (an embedded pointer array of energy data); `CInventoryDetailRenderer` (abstract, vtable `0x5f10d8`) with 14 detail renderers; `CHudBarOptions` (the auto-map's layout, sounds, zoom, colours; its three default colours are function-local statics of RegisterFields, guard `0x6c2d7c`, built through the exe's guard and atexit functions). `CAnimationOverlayInventoryDetailRenderer` and `CSphereOfZinEnergyInventoryDetailRenderer` register an alternative class name ("CAnimationOverlayDetailRenderer", "CEnergyInventoryDetailRenderer"); `CEnergyTextInventoryDetailRenderer` keeps its two format descriptors in `0x6bdcbc`/`0x6bdcc0` and has version 0. Generated with the action classes' generator (symbolic emulation of Create/RegisterFields, side-session notes `phase3-action-classes-gen`), four RegisterFields by hand.

**How the HUD draws an item** [confirmed: `CZaxWorld::DrawHud` `0x59e730`, the slots; VM]:
- The net player's records (+0x100, 12 bytes {catalogue index, render data, flags}) are kept by slot 25 of the item definition's "Display/HUD Renderer" (slot 32 of the definition, else +0x24 of its type definition): (part, item reference, opacity, render data slot) makes the render data of the renderer's class when the slot holds another one (the old one deleted) and fills it; al says it was made. Slot 26 (packet, slot) does the same and reads the data (its slot 25). The data's slot 23 sends the changed values, 24 all of them, 25 reads them, 26 says whether anything changed; the opacity goes as a byte (×255, back ×1/255), the index as a word token of the catalogue, floats raw, a NaN never counts as changed (fcom, test ah, 0x40).
- Slot 28 (render data, frame, x offset; -0x50 after a shield renderer) places the item with `InventoryHUD_Place` `0x4298d0`: the type definition's +8/+0xc, +0x10/+0x14 the anchors (1 centre, 2 from the right or bottom edge of the frame), +0x18 bit 1 above the HUD bar (minus +0x108 of the application's HUD object +0x340).
- Compass: the "HUD Overlay" frame the compass points to: atan2 of the player's position minus the target (`0x62e9d8`, set by slot 23 from the layer's `CZaxLayerSaveData` "Compass Target" or by `CAttractCompassAI`; `0x62e9d1` "known"), minus `0x5ee000`, wrapped to [0, 2π), times (frames − 1) · `0x5edff8`, rounded, +1; it pulses with the Transparent Mask's opacity · (64 + a triangle of `timeGetTime() >> 2`, at most 128) / 128 (`0x5ee004`). Flag: the "HUD Sequence" at "Animation Speed" through the clock (`Sequence_SyncFrame`), backwards when negative. Weapon: the meter rectangle from the inventory display options (+0x238..+0x244), ammunition as "%d" (+0x1e0/+0x1e4 for "Primary", else +0x1e8/+0x1ec, font +0x1f0), a continuous fire weapon "+%d" whole rounds and the fraction in the item's energy meter (a whole fraction of 0 counts as 1 of the previous round), the ammunition's icon after the text with "Show Ammo Icon", without ammunition the battery; then the item icon. Shield: one row per shield item, meter and "%d/%d %s" in "Small Gold". Energy: the definition's meter (+0x16c/+0x170 its size, centred). Character: the meter and the special ability's name. Sphere of Zin: a frame swinging with a sine whose phase (static `0x713810`) advances with the time since the last draw (`GetTickCount`, static `0x7137f8`) at a rate between "Min/Max Energy-Pulse Rate" by the charge ratio.
- `EnergyMeter_Draw` `0x486d10` (CEnergyMeter: frame, rectangle, value, maximum): taller than wide black with a frame in +0x18 and the filled part from the bottom in +0x38; wider (only for a maximum above `0x5f1c3c`) black, lines in +8 top and bottom, the ends as bars between +8 and +0x18 split at a third, the filled part as two bars between +0x28 and +0x38.

**The inventory screen's detail renderers** [confirmed: the slots; VM]: slot 24 (item, frame, x, y, inventory) draws the item's detail, slot 25 (item, inventory) describes it as a line of the item list: a new 0x1c-byte line object (vtable `0x5f1140`, +0xc name, +0x14 text, +8 the column layout, +0x10/+0x18 colours; the weapon's +0x18 0/1/2 for no, few, more than "Warn Getting Low Threshold" shots), 0, or the static `0x714140` "listed elsewhere" (ammunition a weapon of the inventory uses, "Ore Deposits" and "Crystals", a second health item of the same index). Texts from the renderers' "Format" (Local.txt entries) and the registered strings `0x714088`–`0x71432x` at (x + 0x2d, y + 0x14) in the renderer's font, meters at (5, 0x11)–(0x55, 0x1c); the weapon detail adds a projectile line with "+0x24"/"+0x30" of the projectile (or the continuous fire data's +0x18) through two function-local static ZStrings (`0x7140ac`, `0x71409c`); the overlays draw the "Detail Image" list `0x6c0948` at the display options' detail position (+0x44/+0x48) and then the next renderer; the random overlay picks a frame with the game's random generator every 1 / fps · `0x5eb2cc` ticks. `CEnergyTextInventoryDetailRenderer`'s slot 18 turns an old "Format" (dynamic field of `0x6bdca0`) into both new formats ("%…f" → "%s"). The definitions' icons: `CZaxInventoryItemDefinition::DrawIcon` `0x5b8ca0` (slot 27: detail image, an animation overlay's image at the definition's animation frame +0xe0, the HUD image at +0xe4/+0xe8, then `InventoryItem_DrawIcon` `0x4d69d0` with the two "Inventory Icons" at +0x58/+0x5c).

**The auto-map** [confirmed: code; VM]: `HudMiniMap_UpdateFog` `0x508000` counts the open/close timer (mode 1 → 2, 3 → 0) and clears the current layer's fog of war over the view's mini map rectangle when the view moved more than "Fog Of War Update Distance" (squared; `0x5f9e38` "Always Update") or the layer changed. `HudMiniMap_Draw` `0x508180` builds the static frame `0x6c2d38` ("MiniMap Size", the game type's own map through its slot 43, else the layer's image, the fog (Transparent Mask), the player's dot and the monitored parts' dots) and blits it with the Copy mode at "Mini-Map Opacity".

**Quirks kept and findings**:
- The drawing code reads definitions, type definitions, HUD and detail sequences without null tests and divides by a sequence's frame count: an item the HUD never shows (no type definition, no HUD icon, a detail image without frames, a deployable template without its part) crashes the original as it does the reimplementation. The checks pick their data accordingly.
- For R1 (CFrame slot 51, the line, `0x4abae0`) [confirmed: code, crashes in the check runs]: it subtracts the frame's origin before it clips to the rectangle that includes the origin, so a frame with an origin ≠ 0 gets lines outside its buffer; a horizontal line exactly on the frame's height is drawn one row past the buffer; the meter's bars take their width from value / maximum unclipped (a value above the maximum writes past the frame). The game's HUD frames have origin 0 and its meters lie inside the screen.
- The blend modes' one-entry `FindBlitter` cache (+0x2c/+0x30) is state between draws: a second run of the same blits finds it in another state and asks the frames for their flags once more (one more frame call, the same pixels). The drawing checks put it back before each side (`checks_hud_common.h`).
- Not hookable: `CInventoryHUDRenderer::vf23` `0x4ceb50` (3 bytes, `ret 0xc`).
- The checks load nothing the level has not loaded beyond the item definitions (as `checks_inv_actions.cpp` does): the weapon detail's projectile values load the projectile's model (`ProjectileFloat24/30` `0x4d6300`/`0x4d6410` through the model list `0x6cfdd8`), and with those models loaded the models module's real-data entity cases ended the game on `Test/Nachbau1` (runs `20261026-221752-6117`, `20261026-222858-7d8a`; `models` alone and after `hud_render` passed, after `hud_details` it failed: `20261026-224213-908c`). So the detail checks take only weapons whose projectile model, and images and icons that are loaded already; how many depends on the level (counts in the log). Why the models module's entity cases failed on models loaded that way: such a model has no sequences, and the original ends the game making a `CEntityAnimated` of it; the models check takes only models with sequences since 2026-11-01 (section 13, "Batch section-12 leftovers", 5b).

**Checks** (in the game thread): classes 540 Create/CreateArray/destructor cases, 51 getters, 36 RegisterFields, 45 registered descriptors (real data); render data 7,100 cases on fake packets; HUD renderers: placement, display options, meter and icon 2,265, slot 28 of the renderers on the catalogue's real definitions (flag, weapon, shield, Sphere of Zin; compass and energy as objects of their classes on a weapon and a shield definition, the catalogue has none) into fake 5-6-5 frames 1,230, Update and Read on fake worlds 4,500, the auto-map 500 (the level's fog and the static frame saved and put back), slot 23 on the real layers; detail renderers: slots 24 and 25 with 440 cases each on `Test/Nachbau1` and 680 on `Assimilate Cave1` on the real definitions with copies of their template items (a deployable's condition, slot 49, from a copy of its vtable: a template has no deployed part) and the first character's inventory (read only) or a copy of it without items (always for the weapon detail: some real items' count reads an owner), the energy text, shield, charger and random overlay detail renderers (none in the catalogue) as objects made by their own Create on the battery's definition and an animation overlay's image (the random overlay only where one is loaded: Cave1); the icons 216 / 294 cases, slot 23 and slot 18. Stand-ins: the clocks (`timeGetTime`, `GetTickCount`, `Platform_Ticks24`), the error reporter; the statics (Sphere of Zin phases, the health message counter, the random overlay's state, the game's random generator) set alike before each side and put back. Not covered: the character renderer's slot 28 and the character detail renderer (they need a `CCharacterInventoryItemDefinition`, which the catalogue of these levels does not have; reimplemented from the code only), `CEnergyTextInventoryDetailRenderer`'s slot 18 with an old "Format" (checked only without one).
- Runs: all modules with all cases `Test/Nachbau1` `20261026-224730-3962` and `ACT 2/M9/09 Assimilate Cave1` (start point `Respawn2`, `--no-level`) `20261026-224730-1802`: all 739 checks the same, 5818 hooks installed (230 new; the two not installed are `DebugLog_SectionBegin`/`End` as before), `Zip CRC` and `All checks done` in the log; module times on Cave1 `hud_classes` 0.9 s, `hud_data` 3.2 s, `hud_details` 0.9 s (0.6 s on Nachbau1, fewer loaded images), `hud_render` 4.7 s. The detail checks on Cave1: 12 weapons, 4 animation overlays, the counts per class in the log. Shot set `20261026-230106-9760` … `20261026-230107-805a` (126 s, both VMs): all nine scenes identical or different only in their animated areas (`hud_nachbau1`, `hud_cave1`, `automap`, `inventory` with its log and voice pages among them).

### The window toolkit [verified 2026-10-27, VM; the drawing slots through recorded frame calls]

The game's own window toolkit (`0x401000`–`0x414cf0`, section 6, "Subsystem assignment corrections") is reimplemented in eight modules: 256 functions (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`). 200 of them are among the 266 functions `docs/functions.csv` counts as User interface in the range (5 were verified before, 61 remain, below); the other 56 are virtual slots the table does not list (thunks of a few instructions that Ghidra did not make functions). Every call to another function of the toolkit goes through its exe address, so the original's side of a check runs the original all the way down; return values are what the original leaves in eax where it defines it (functions that set al only are compared in al and say so in their comment).

The classes (layouts in the files' head comments) [confirmed: constructors, destructors and the slots below; vtables from the constructors]:

|---|---|---|---|
| `CJWindow`, the base class: child list, focus, mouse and keyboard dispatch, accelerators, rectangles and layout helpers, scroll info, INI position, cursor table, constructors, destructor, init | `0x5eb404`, 0x100 (76 slots) | `ui_window.cpp` (`ui_window.h`) | 72 |
| `CScreenWindow`: tool tip, key repeat, cursor, mouse update | `0x5eb198` | `ui_window.cpp` | 10 |
| `CJTabControl` and the toolkit's bevel `0x40a740` | `0x5eb2d4`, 0x11c | `ui_tabs.cpp` | 10 |

| "Resize Control", the button, the radio button, the toggle button | `0x5eb72c`, 0x104; `0x5eb85c`, 0x138; `0x5ebaec`; `0x5ebc44` | `ui_button.cpp` | 40 |

**The harness** (`reimpl/src/checks_ui_common.h`, namespace `zax::uic`):
- **Fake windows** in one static block (16 windows of 0x400 bytes and an extra area of 0x6000 bytes for the case's rectangles, texts, scroll infos and the objects a call makes), at the same addresses on both sides, so pointers compare raw; every side builds the block from the case seed again.
- **Recording vtables** for 30 classes: the 26 window classes, `CFrame`, `COffsetClippedProxyFrame`, the toolkit's callback objects (`0x5ea350`) and the button look (`0x5f88b4`, also standing in for the look factory). Every slot is a thunk that logs the call (class, slot, ecx, the arguments by a per-slot kind: raw, the 4, 8 or 16 bytes or the C string behind a pointer, the low byte, ignored), pops the stack arguments (counted from the `ret n` of every slot's implementation) and answers from a sequence of values that depends only on the seed and the number of the call (a value, a bool, a small number, a window of the block, a fresh rectangle, a text). Slot 0, and slot 5 when it answers true, take the fake out of its parent's child list as the real ones do.
- **Stand-ins**: exe functions outside the module jump to recording thunks of the same kind for a group of cases (keys, cursor, sounds, the INI file, the screen window's helpers, the font's drawing, the frame's fill, rectangle and blit functions, the allocators). Constructors called by the code under test are stand-ins that return their object and may give it a fake vtable (the buttons, the grip and the label the frame windows make, the image frame of a button). The allocators give blocks of the extra area (objects a call makes lie at the same addresses on both sides); blocks freed through them are wiped. `GetTickCount`'s import answers a case value.
- **Compared**: eax (masked per test), the call log (hash, count, the first calls in the report), the whole block (ZString members canonicalised to their texts, the scroll infos by content), the module's globals (case values set before each side) and the pool's free list (no block memory may reach the real pool).
- Constructors and destructors run on real objects in the extra area (their parents, children and textures fakes); the colours' palette index bytes the constructors leave from the stack (`+0x8a` … `+0xda`) are cleared before the comparison.
- `[Reimpl] UiOnly=` (test names) and `UiTrace=1` (every case and side in the log, to find a crash or a hang).

**Drawing**: the toolkit's drawing slots only call the frame's slots (fill, rectangle, line, blit with a blend mode), the bevel `0x40a740`, the font's text functions and the window texture (slot 72); the checks compare those calls with their arguments (the rectangles by content) on fake frames instead of pixels. The frame and blitter code stays the original's (frame check harness above). The drawing of the children `0x40b620` (proxy frames and the dirty-rect cache) is a stand-in.

**Findings** [confirmed: code, the checks]:
- `clang` keeps x87 temporaries unrounded across a `(float)` conversion when the value stays in a register: the scroll bar's range and the position it hands to its owner must go through a store (`round_float`, a volatile float) to match the original's `fst dword` (the first run differed in 29 of 10,950 cases by one ulp of `+0x158`). The other phase 4 modules with floats should do the same.
- The font's wrap layout (`0x4a7010`/`0x4a7110`, used by a wrapping text label) caches its last text and parameters in the font (`+0x48` …) and hangs when the wrap width is narrower than a word (the original as well); the label checks use a copy of the font per side and widths of at least 150.
- Kept quirks: the check box disabled reads the opacity of `g_BlendTransparentMask` twice and restores `g_BlendBlackBias` with it; a horizontal own scroll bar of a window sets its height to the parent's client width (`0x40f5d0` where the width was meant) and places its top with its width; the scroll bar's rect cut `0x412fb0` tests a horizontal bar's edges for equality only; joining a radio group takes the partner's tab stop (`+0x5d`, `+0x5f` of the partner); the text label's constructor sets its title five times (the inlined setters); the slider's default step is (count + 10) / 20; the "Window Title Tile" texture loads under the name "Window Texture".
- Setups the original crashes on as well (the checks avoid them): Ctrl+Tab in a tab control without tabs, a radio ring without a parent, a resize grip or a frame drag without a parent, a slider drag on a slider exactly as wide as its thumb + 1, Escape with a capture and no screen window.

**Not reimplemented** (`docs/functions.csv` counts them as User interface; section 12): the list box family `CJListBox`, the drop list and the combo boxes `0x4041f0`–`0x408eb0` (44 functions), the edit field and the number field `0x410b50`–`0x412050` (10 open in the table, about 25 with their slots) (both done since 2026-10-27: subsection "List boxes, combo boxes, edit and number fields, the mouse cursor"), the file dialog `0x414910`–`0x414bf0` (done since 2026-10-27: next subsection), the base class's drawing of the children `0x40b620` and its scroll bar update `0x40f110`, the frame window's frame (slot 76 `0x402f80`, not in the table) and the modal loop `0x40f5f0` (it pumps the Windows messages: phase 5). Raw input (the keyboard state `0x6c1050`, the cursor object `0x6cff40`) and DirectDraw stay for phase 5; the toolkit only reads them through stand-ins in the checks.

Check in the VM (`checks_ui_*.cpp`, in the game thread; cases per module with all cases):
- Per module (cases with all cases; time on `Assimilate Cave1`): `ui_window` 12,850 (`checks_ui_window.cpp`, 14.6 s; the counts were halved from 25,450, which took 34 s) and `ui_screen` 3,800 (`checks_ui_screen.cpp`: the screen window, the base class's constructors, destructors and init on real objects; 4.5 s), `ui_tabs` 4,600 (2.5 s), `ui_grid` 6,000 (4.5 s), `ui_frame` 8,800 (7.0 s), `ui_button` 7,350 (6.0 s), `ui_slider` 3,350 (1.7 s), `ui_label` 4,900 (3.0 s), `ui_scrollbar` 10,950 (7.9 s); all the same.
- All modules with all cases: `Test/Nachbau1` `20261027-001354-e9d7` (checks 397 s) and `ACT 2/M9/09 Assimilate Cave1` (start point `Respawn2`, `--no-level`) `20261027-001359-cd16` (checks 421 s): all 734 checks the same, 5844 hooks installed (the two not installed are `DebugLog_SectionBegin`/`End` as before), `Zip CRC` and `All checks done` in the log.
- During the work every module ran alone (`--ini OnlyChecks=`) until it was the same; the differences found on the way were the reimplementation's (the slider's step formula, the frame window's notify returning a value the original leaves undefined, a button's tip returning the parent's eax, the scroll bar's float rounding) or the setup's (listed above).

**The launcher** [confirmed: `zax-launcher/zax_launcher_dll.c`, the check run]: `Zax-Launcher.dll` puts a jump into the game menu's constructor at `0x5bfe14` (its "Load &Map (F9)" button, `/NoLoadMap` leaves it out) and redirects the main menu's constructor at six call sites, one of them `0x5bff30` in the game menu's notify. The reimplemented constructor keeps the original when that jump is there (in every VM job, so in the game the original constructor runs; the check takes the jump out for its cases), and the reimplemented notify calls the main menu through the target of the exe's call `0x5bff30`, so the launcher's redirect still applies. The first runs showed it: without this the original side had one button more (+0x13c) in every case of the game menu's constructor.

**Check in the VM** (`checks_ui_menus.cpp`, 6,620 cases with all cases): the constructors run on real objects in the extra area; the toolkit's constructors they call are stand-ins that give the object the vtable of a fake of its class (button, label, sequence window, plain window, edit field, file dialog, list box), a random rectangle, the real font and a title (a ZString rep of the harness's own, so the stand-in calls nothing); the game's objects behind the globals (the reporter `0x6c02cc` and its screen, the application `0x713f14`, the world `0x6c2080`, the object their slot 1 gives, the game type, the directory list) are fakes of the new harness class "game object" (100 slots with the stack arguments the screens use); the font list's records, the difficulty count, `g_MainMenu`, the demo flag `0x62485c` and the chat flag are case values. The notify functions run on a fake dialog with fake member buttons and every branch (the main menu, the quit menu, "Select Map" and the save/load screen made inside them run with the same stand-ins; "Select Map"'s list of game types `0x5bde70` is a stand-in). `checks_ui_options.cpp`: Create on a pool block filled with a pattern, CreateArray with 0–3 elements, both destructors, the getters, RegisterFields into a fake class info and with the class variable 0, and the registered descriptors of the running game (50 cases).

Harness changes (`checks_ui_common.h`): the class "game object" (`C_OBJECT`), six fixed answers per case (`K_FIXED0`–`K_FIXED5`, `g_case.fixed`), the file dialog's slot 78 counted with its one argument (the derived dialogs' Ok), the recording handler reentrant (an effect that calls recorded functions itself kept the outer call's pop count: before, a title made with `make_text` inside a constructor stand-in corrupted the stack), and the exception report names the handler's address (the DLL is relocated in the game).

Findings [confirmed: code, the checks]:
- `FieldDesc_Name` `0x5007a0` takes no stack argument: the `push 0` before it in the difficulty menu is already the button constructor's third argument (a first version passed one and shifted the stack by 4).
- The difficulty menu reads before its index array when there is no difficulty (`(n - 1) >> 1` and `[count - 1]`); the file dialog's notify reads the list box at +0x134 on Open without testing it. The checks avoid both.
- `0x62485c` is the demo flag (`Game_FullVersionText` adds "Demo" with it): no CD key check in the main menu, and the quit menu leaves out its button `0x714544`.
- The pointer array of the difficulty buttons has `ZPtrArray`'s deleting destructor `0x5bfb20` (phase 1, `ptr_array.h`); the local index array of the constructor (vtable `0x5ee138`, then `0x5ee15c`) grows with `0x5c11c0`.

### List boxes, combo boxes, edit and number fields, the mouse cursor 0x4041f0–0x408f1e, 0x410b50–0x412280, 0x5184e0–0x5187b0, 0x592350–0x592400 [verified 2026-10-27, VM; the drawing slots through recorded frame calls, Windows' cursor and the clipboard through stand-ins]

127 functions in three modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): `reimpl/src/ui_listbox.cpp` (73) with `checks_ui_listbox.cpp`, `reimpl/src/ui_edit.cpp` (39) with `checks_ui_edit.cpp` and `reimpl/src/ui_cursor.cpp` (15) with `checks_ui_cursor.cpp`, all on the toolkit's harness. 70 of them are among the 237 open User interface functions of `docs/functions.csv`; the other 57 are virtual slots and helpers the table does not list (the list box's slots 9–95, the drop list's, the combo boxes', the edit and number fields', the sort's compare `0x406c60`, the header callback `0x406b00`, the slots of `ListBoxListSource`). The previous UI batch had stopped at the screens because their windows are built from these classes: the menus' checks had to use constructor stand-ins for them. Every call to another function of the toolkit goes through its exe address, as in the toolkit's modules.

**The checks**: the list box is a fake (window 0; its own slots recorded, answering a row height, gaps, indents, icon widths, texts) with real rows; the drop list and the combo box's closed list likewise. Their source is a tree of the case (`checks_ui_listmodel.h`): a fake object whose slots log their calls (the root, parents, texts with tabs for columns, child counts, children, a file list, selectable rows), the rows built from the tree with some nodes expanded. The column header is a block with columns, the scroll bar, the frames, the buttons and the callbacks fakes, the icon list a fake with records and a loader. Stand-ins: the base class's functions (constructor and destructor, sizes, mouse, keys, focus, tool tip), the frame's fill, blit and clip, the font's text and widths, the bevel, the scroll bar's position and range, the header's column functions, the opacities, the time (`0x4d2460`), the keyboard state, the sounds, the clipboard (`0x46d700`/`0x46d760`: the checks never touch the real one) and Windows' cursor. The constructors of the list box, the drop list and the button are stand-ins in the combo box's checks that make the new object a copy of the case's fakes. The number field's edit field is a fake of the check file whose slot 48 returns its value in st0 (a recorded slot answers in eax, and the original adds st0). The C runtime's string functions, `qsort`, `atof`, the text helpers and the ZString functions run.

**Setups the original crashes on** [confirmed: VM runs of the first versions of the checks, the crash on the original's side]: `SelectId` `0x404390` expands row -1 when the parent of an id is not shown, which reads before the row array (faults on an empty box without one); `ShowId` `0x406920` calls itself for ever for an id that is not shown when its parents end at a root that is no row (the parent of -1 is -1, the root has children; with `ListBoxListSource` for every id that is not a row) — the checks' source answers a child count of 0 for the root after eight such calls in a side; `UpdateBar` `0x4074f0` writes through a null bar when +0x256 (the bar belongs to someone else) is set without one; the sort's compare `0x406c60` steps to the sort column with `strchr(…, 9) + 1` and faults on a text with fewer tabs, and it cuts the source's texts in place (a 0, then the tab back), so they must be writable; `SetSource` `0x406fc0` with no source selects through it. The checks avoid them, and the combo box's init divides by the font height / 5 (a font lower than 5 pixels: the checks use 5 and more).

**Findings** [confirmed: code, the checks]:
- `SetSource` keeps the old selection only when the old selected *id* is less than the row count (it compares the id with the count as if it were an index), then selects it again with its parents expanded.
- The drop list's height is the number of rows plus 10 for a tree, at most 14; the combo box's closed list draws a caret after the typed text when it is active and the reporter's flag 8 (`0x6c02cc` +0x38) is set.
- The edit field's Draw returns without putting the opacities back when the visible client area is empty (disabled fields then leave the reduced opacities set); its Key compares a character with `al <= 0xff`, so every key from 0x20 is typed; the caret is a block over the next character unless `0x60a648` (key 16) is set.
- The number field and the edit field treat a range bound that compares equal to 0.0 or unordered (NaN) as none (`test ah, 0x40` after `fcomp 0.0`); the number field's step is added to the edit field's value in x87 precision and rounded once (`round_float`); the cursor's animation frame goes back to 0 unless the frame count is greater (so also for NaN).
- `0x408e70` is the compiler's vector destructor iterator (backwards, thiscall destructor), filed as User interface.

Harness changes (`checks_ui_common.h`/`.cpp`, relevant for later UI batches): `Case::object_args` (the "game object" class's stack arguments per case; the class now has 112 slots), the stub answer kind `'p'` (gives its first stack argument after the effect: output objects), the answer kind `K_FLOAT` (a float in st0 as well), `g_effect_ecx` (the object of the call whose effect runs), `NSTUB` 96 → 128 (`.rept 3600`), `g_args` 9 arguments.

Findings [confirmed: code, the checks]:
- A stand-in of a function of the same module is not effective: the module's hooks are put out and in around each side and overwrite it; such functions run (stub them in their own module's tests only through what they call).
- Methods on a caller's local (FileBuf, FieldColor, the stack "Dummy" window of `0x564ce0`): their stand-ins are logged as fastcall with ecx ignored, else the uninitialised local is hashed; output pointers of stand-ins are logged by their 4 bytes (`'a'`) or ignored, not as 8 or 16 bytes.
- The HUD bar's slide (`0x5084a0`–`0x5085f0`): starting from hidden or shown sets the time to the slide's length, turning back mirrors it (length − time).
- `KeyButton::Click` `0x471370` does nothing without a configuration (the button's own click only with one); the inventory screen's Open calls the reporter's slot 28 only when it was closed.
- The voice log panel's Notify and Show ask the list box for its choice twice (the first answer unused); the sort compare counts an unordered time as less.
- Setups the original crashes on (the checks avoid them): the first character, the "Inventory Window" sequence, the dialogue window's frame sequence and the end game credits' font read without a test; the popup menu's Run reads the chosen item without a test; `Dialog_AddLine` reads the font's height without a test; the credits text's 999 lines need 256 KB (the checks give a buffer of their own); a refused display mode in the video dialog's destructor ends the game ("Couldn't set resolution"); the item records' categories must be item types ("FATAL ERROR!" and exit; a missing record faults).

- Not hookable (4 bytes): `0x518690` (the cursor's shown flag), `0x592380` (`ListBoxListSource::NoIndex`).
