### The game side of the sound: envelopes, ambient sounds, music, the sound manager and resources, the readers, the sound list and the streams 0x49d610–0x49f9c9, 0x4ce3e0–0x4ee747, 0x51d4f0–0x51e670, 0x57bdc0–0x57ee90, 0x587060–0x5879f5, 0x595ac0–0x5994fe [verified 2026-10-26, VM; DirectSound, ACM, the multimedia timer and the file system with fakes only]

184 functions are reimplemented in seven modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): 149 of the 163 functions `docs/functions.csv` counted as Sound and open, and 35 it lacks or files elsewhere (vtable-only slots of the sound resource, the readers and the sound list, the first copies of the class getters, the base look's destructor). DirectSound, ACM (msacm32), vorbisfile and the multimedia timer stay calls into them; the checks give them fakes that record their calls and never play a sound.

- `reimpl/src/envelopes.cpp` (45): `CEnvelope` (0x24, class `0x6bdefc`, vtable `0x5f3cbc`) and its six kinds `CTimeEnvelope`, `CConeAngleEnvelope`, `CSpeedEnvelope`, `CTrajectoryEnvelope`, `CFacingAngleEnvelope`, `CLengthEnvelope` (classes `0x6bdf00`–`0x6bdf14`): both getter copies, Create, CreateArray, the deleting destructors, RegisterFields, and CEnvelope's slots 23 Advance, 24 Reset, 25 Assign.
- `reimpl/src/ambient_sound.cpp` (14): `CAmbientSound` (0x2c, class `0x6c1d10`, version 2) with its class functions, message, "Who Started" setter and frame `0x4ee100`; the layer's list of ambient sounds (+0xf0: add `0x4ee4e0`, remove, start, distances `0x4ee6e0`) and `0x4ee730` (the layer's save data).
- `reimpl/src/music.cpp` (30): `CMusicMixerData` (0x18) and `CMusicMixer` (0x34) with the out-of-line constructor `0x51e360`, the song setter, the track switch `0x51e520`, stop and frame `0x51e470`; the application's menu music `0x4ce510`/`0x4ce3e0`; the music stream object `0x4e1fe0`/`0x4e2150`; the sound file list's destructor and Find `0x4e2030`; the voice-over player `0x595ac0`–`0x595be0`; and four functions of the toolkit's looks (below).
- `reimpl/src/sound_reader.cpp` (23): the readers (base, raw PCM, WAVE, the Ogg reader's constructor), the factory `0x57ca10`, the two pools and the ring buffer reads `0x57d330`/`0x57d550`.
- `reimpl/src/sound_resource.cpp` (37): the sound manager's activation and its ten slots, `CSoundResource`'s 16 slots and the 3D update `0x57c4f0`, the buffer format `0x57c7b0`, the listener's getters and setters, the options `0x57ee90`.
- `reimpl/src/sound_list.cpp` (26): the sound list (`0x713708` "Sound List"; also the voice-overs' `0x6c2480`).
- `reimpl/src/sound_stream.cpp` (9): the threaded stream (constructor, destructor, frame, queue, take, play, stop, volume) and its multimedia timer callback `0x587700`.

**CEnvelope** [confirmed: code; checked]: +8 "Start Value", +0xc "Current Value", +0x10 "End Value", +0x14 "Speed", +0x18 "Direction" (±1), +0x1c "Using Start" (it runs towards the end value), +0x20 "Ending Behavior" (name list `0x6bdee0`: 0 stop, 1 start over, 2 reverse; default "Stop at end"). Advance (seconds): at the value it runs towards the ending behaviour applies (0: nothing moves; 1: back to the start value; 2: the direction turns and "Using Start" flips), then the value moves by speed × direction × seconds and stops at that value — with a direction below 0 (or NaN) when it falls below, else when it rises above; a reached value is copied as an integer (a signalling NaN stays signalling). Reset: the start value, towards the end value, the direction 1 when the end value is above the start value, else −1. The kinds only change units and ranges of the inherited descriptors (seconds; degrees 0–180, −90–90 and −360–360 in steps of 0.5; units/s; lengths 0–10,000).

**CAmbientSound** [confirmed: code; checked with fakes]: +8 the sound (a copy of the sound list's resource, `0x57e8e0`, kept, type 0x101), +0xc "Ambient Sound Index", +0x10 "Who Started" (listened to), +0x14 the part's layer (its +0x48), +0x18 "Muted", +0x19 outside the inner radius, +0x1a "ShouldBePlaying", +0x1c/+0x20 the inner radius and its square, +0x24/+0x28 the outer radius and the far distance. The frame (listener position): the sound is fetched on first use; in another layer than the current one (`0x6c1c70`) it is muted (the resource's flag 0x20); with a part: the distance² from the listener to the part's 3D position (x, 0, −y), scaled by the distance factor `0x7136ac`, beyond the resource's far distance² it is muted; inside the inner radius² it plays without a position (slot 3 off), outside with the position (slot 4); an unmuted sound that was dropped starts again (`Resource_ReloadThen` at the position). Only `CAmbientSoundAI` adds them, which three levels use (`01 Main`, `22 End Game Jungle` twice); the check maps have none.

**Music** [confirmed: code; checked with fakes]: `CMusicMixerData` +8 "Num Seconds To Switch" (5), +0xc/+0x10/+0x14 "Full Mix Song", "Med Mix Song", "Ambiant Song" (indices of the music folder list `0x6c0f10`); `CMusicMixer` +8 the seconds since the switch, +0xc the data, +0x24/+0x28 current and queued track (2), +0x2c changed, +0x30 the stream. A switch during a fade only queues the track; otherwise the volume comes from the reporter's +0x64 (Zax.CFG "Music Volume", −800; −3333 off); a stopped stream starts the song, a playing one cross-fades into it (`0x5871f0`, gain 1, looping when the songs changed) unless it is the same song unchanged, and starts it outright when the formats differ. The frame lowers the old song's gain from 1 to 0 over the fade time, then the queued song becomes the current one. The voice-over player (`0x713c28`) plays a voice when "Play Voiceovers" is on and its priority is at least the playing one's, and lowers the other sounds (`ResourceCache_SetLowPriority`) until it ends.

**The sound manager and the sound resources** [confirmed: code, DirectSound slots; checked with fakes; interface names: assumption, after the DirectSound headers; the code has only slot numbers]: the manager `0x7136b8` is the game's resource cache (`g_ResourceCache` `0x713688` after `0x57bdc0`): +4 the master level, +0xc muted, +0x10 the primary buffer's volume, +0x30 stereo. Init: `DirectSoundCreate`, cooperative level 2 with the main window, the primary buffer (flags 0x81, one retry), 22,050 Hz 16-bit mono/stereo — the format's rate is set as rate + 5 = 22,055 samples per second (`0x57c7b0`, as in the exe) —, played looping. `CSoundResource` (0x9c): Load (slot 15) makes a static buffer of the file's whole PCM (flags 0xe8, 4 stereo, 0x40 16-bit; the retry resets the flags to 0xe8), copies the PCM in through Lock/Unlock and sets frequency, volume 0 and pan 0; sounds above 500,000 bytes are counted (`0x713690`). The 3D update: beyond the far distance (+0x3c) the priority −3333 (silent); else the volume (as the resource's priority, `Resource_SetPriority`) from the distance between near (+0x38) and far, linear in hundredths of a decibel (`0x5f7468`), nothing below −3333, and the pan from cos(atan2(dy, dx)) × distance, at most the far distance, over twice the far distance (`0x600b20`). The frequency slot 9 goes through `Resource_ReloadFalse`, which always gives 0, so it never sets a frequency (as in the exe). Zax.CFG (`0x57ee90`): "Master Mute"/"Master Voume" (sic), "SFx Mute" (0.25)/"SFx Voume" (sic, 1.0) as the cache's scale, "Sounds Mixing Chanels" (32), "Stereo Sounds" (1), "Music Mute"/"Music Volume" (−800).

**The readers** [confirmed: code; checked with fakes and the level's files]: the game parses RIFF/WAVE itself (chunks "fmt ", "data", "fact" up to the RIFF size) and converts compressed WAVE data (ADPCM) with ACM (`acmFormatSuggest` with the tag, `acmStreamOpen`, `acmStreamSize`, one header per read; at the end of the file the missing PCM is silence); it does not decode ADPCM itself. The factory takes a file starting with "RIFF"…"WAVE" as WAVE, one whose extension (with its dot) is "ogg" as raw 22,050 Hz mono 16-bit PCM, every other as Ogg Vorbis, so for the game's files .wav is WAVE and .ogg Ogg [the raw reader is unreachable for every name: confirmed: code `0x57ca10`, `Path_Extension` `0x4a3f80` (the extension starts with its dot or is empty, so it never equals "ogg"), reimpl/src/sound_reader.cpp, reimpl/src/path_util.cpp; VM]. Quirks kept: the WAVE reader frees a pool-allocated format with operator delete when it converts (and the converted format, a heap block, with the pool's delete), its destructor gives its stream buffer back twice. The pools: a pointer array of 100,000-byte stream buffers (`0x716080`) and of 0x2c0-byte Ogg states (`0x7160e0`), each with a byte array of free flags; the first use anywhere takes three blocks and gives them back. ReadParts fills the two parts of a locked ring buffer (through the stream buffer when there are two); ReadMix mixes the next bytes into them: out = (in − out) × (1 − gain) + out, truncated, the low 16 bits with −32768 made −32767 (the first part with the factor on the FPU, the second with it stored as a float).

**The sound list** [confirmed: code; checked with fakes and the level's list]: records of 0x108 bytes (name, +0x100 used, +0x101 a second flag, +0x104 the resource). Load (list name, folder, mask, extension): the folder's files (sorted with `_stricmp`), each with a new resource that only keeps its file name (`Resource_Load` mode 1); the callers load "Sounds" and the voice-overs from "Levels" with ".wav" and ".ogg". Find tries a missing .wav as .ogg and a missing .ogg as .wav (the sound file list `0x4e2030` only .wav → .ogg; its second branch never runs, section 6). The ambient sounds get copies (slot 1 of a new resource); playing goes through the resource's slot 2.

**The streams** [confirmed: code; checked with fakes]: the music and the voice-overs play through a 100,000-byte ring buffer that the multimedia timer (`timeSetEvent(50, 5, 0x587700, state, periodic)`, with "Use Threaded Stream"; else the frame) refills when at least 40,000 bytes are free behind the write position; a queued reader is mixed in for the cross-fade; at the end the rest is silence (0x80 for 8-bit, 0 for 16-bit) and the buffer stops once the end has played; a volume at or below −3000 mutes the stream (its buffer stopped). The state: section header of `sound_stream.cpp`. The callback runs in the timer's thread.

**Not sound** (misassigned in `docs/functions.csv`): `0x4e2220`, `0x5994d0`, `0x599510` (and `0x5994e0`) are the window toolkit's looks (the button look `0x5f88b4`, its base `0x602da8`/`0x602dac`); reimplemented here because they are small. `0x4ef000`, `0x4ef170`, `0x4f6ad0`, `0x4f6ae0`, `0x56c250` ("CAmbientSound" slots 23–64) belong to the animated texture list `0x6c1ee8` (vtable `0x5f8e48`) and its sequence loading with frame filters: rendering, left open.

**Not hookable** (relative jumps in the first five bytes): `0x4e2020` (thunk), `0x57d310` (`OggCallback_Tell`), `0x587290`, `0x5875e0`, `0x5876c0`, `0x5876d0`, `0x5876e0`, `0x595af0`, `0x595bd0`.

Checks (`checks_<module>.cpp`, in the game thread) with the shared sound fake world `reimpl/src/checks_sound_common.h`/`.cpp`:
- **Arenas**: operator new/free and the pool's new/delete (`0x417710`/`0x54d130`) give blocks of an arena per side while a side runs (other threads get the real allocators), filled with the case's pattern as far as blocks go; blocks compare by offset.
- **Recorders**: direct stand-ins (patched entries) and fake objects (recording vtables) for DirectSound and its buffers, ACM, the file buffer, the resource cache and resource base, the readers, the layer parts, the file search, Zax.CFG; COM calls logged with their arguments (pointers mapped, stack locals not logged, formats and descriptions by their bytes), answers from the case (HRESULT failures, written outputs). timeSetEvent/timeKillEvent through their import slots.
- **The timer thread**: the live streams' callbacks are paused for the sound checks (their state's +0xe, which the callback tests first, set twice 120 ms apart and put back), and the sites the timer runs through are never put out (their cases call the original through the trampoline). Before that pause the timer thread ran through the recorders and broke both the cases and the music (runs `20261026-212912-d363`, `-213407-de6a`).
- **The pools** are set per case (constructed or not, warm or not, blocks in the arena with room, so no pool array grows from arena data into the game's pool); a case that constructs a pool grows it from the game's pool and gives those blocks back after each side.
- Cases that the game never has were dropped as found: a buffer format without a primary buffer, a successful CreateSoundBuffer without a buffer, file masks without a dot, list lookups beyond the list, RIFF files with a garbage RIFF size (the chunk loop does not end in the exe either).

Runs: `20261026-222104-1b33` (Test/Nachbau1) and `20261026-222109-9394` (Assimilate Cave1, Respawn2), all modules with all cases: all 754 checks the same, 5772 hooks installed (all but the launcher's two debug log sites, section 8). The seven modules take 0.1–6 s each on Cave1 (envelopes 0.2 s, ambient sound 1.0 s, music 1.8 s, sound list 1.7 s, readers 3.8 s, resources 5.9 s, streams 2.4 s). The level's data as copies: the 64 envelopes of Cave1's objects through their slots (384 cases), the world's mixer, the application's music and the voice player as copies (30), the level's sound list (261 records) as a copy through Find, PathOf, Size and Loaded (320), 30 of its resources through the 3D update with the real listener, 23 of its files through the factory, Open and Read (46), the three live stream states through the timer callback (24); Cave1 has no ambient sounds. ### Sprites and entities: the draw items and queues, Entity_Draw, the sequence classes, the fonts [verified 2026-10-27, VM; the drawing through the exe's frame and blitter code]

Three modules, 78 functions (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): `reimpl/src/entity_draw.cpp` (25: the draw items, their pool and queues, `Entity_Draw`, `DrawRotationSequenceLayers`, the entities' draw, dirty rectangle and hit test slots, the line entity's drawing), `sequence_classes.cpp` (38: `CSequence`, `CRotationSequence`, `CVerticalCut`: classes, frame keeping, frame selection, the loaded sequence's finishing, the text lines of the deltas) and `font_text.cpp` (15: `CFont`'s class, measuring and drawing text), each with `checks_<module>.cpp`. The frame, blend and blitter functions they call stay the exe's (R1–R7; R4/R5 in parallel).

**How an entity reaches the screen** [confirmed: code; VM]:
- The world asks every visible part to draw (slot 23: ground queue, queue, clip rectangle, force, position). `Entity_Draw` `0x488d70` (entity; model, sequence, ground queue, queue, clip, force, position int[3], sort extra) adds the entity's offsets (slots 52–54) to the position and calls `DrawRotationSequenceLayers` `0x4886a0` with the visibility (flags 0x20000 and 0x800000; an invisible part only with force, then at half opacity), the ghost and light bits (flags bits 22 and 21), the opacity (slot 92), the facing (slot 46) and the rotation argument (slot 85); then flag 0x200000 (slot 58, not for CEntityAnimated), the children's slot 27 (slots 86/88) and the AIs' drawing (`CLayerPart` slot 23 `0x4fa9a0`). The tail `0x488f18` that `docs/functions.csv` calls `Entity_MarkResting` is not a function.
- `DrawRotationSequenceLayers` walks the model chain (the model, then the one its +0xac names, each from its default sequence) and every layer of the model (`CModel::ResolveSequenceAt`/`ResolveSequence`); for each layer whose frame (`CRotationSequence_FrameIndex`) meets the clip rectangle it makes one draw item per strip ("Sort/Cutting Lines", `0x560260`/`0x560270`; `g_NoCutting` `0x6bdd48` draws the frame whole) from the pool `0x6bdd08`. Shadows ("Render/Is Shadow") are drawn at the position moved by the height (z · `0x5f1e34`, z · `0x5eee2c`, fstp float, fistp), "Render On Ground" layers at y, the others at y − z. The sort key is layer + (strip offset + y + the model's "Sorting Y" + extra) · 8; a strip whose offset is lower than its left neighbour's links back to that one (+8, +0xc 0), one lower than its right neighbour's links ahead to the next pool item (+0xc 1). The blend mode is the sequence's "Render/Blit Type" or, with a hue remap holder on the entity (dynamic field `0x6c0520`), `HueRemapCache_Get`. Ground layers go to the first queue, the others to the second; al says whether a layer was opaque because of "Auto-Animate" (flag 0x80).
- The draw item (0x54 bytes, vtable `0x5f1e00`, base `0x5f1e1c`): +4 the item drawn above it, +8 the strip partner, +0x10 the root entity, +0x14 the item it was merged into, +0x18 the key, +0x1c/+0x20 the position, +0x24 opaque, +0x25 ghost, +0x26 shadow, +0x28 the opacity, +0x2c the entity's attachments draw around it, +0x30 the blend mode, +0x34 a clip frame (target: the frame, rectangle: the strip). Slot 1 blits the strip with the item's mode at its opacity (and puts 1.0 back), slot 3 is the strip rectangle at the position, slot 4 asks the frame's pixel, slot 5 joins another item's rectangle (`DrawQueue_MergeStrips` `0x49ca60`: a strip is merged into its partner when nothing that overlaps it lies between them in the sorted queue, else the first item overlapping the partner is linked above it). The queues are pointer arrays sorted with qsort by key, then x (`0x49c9a0`).
- Slot 82 (`0x489a40`) adds the same frame rectangles to the dirty rectangle list (`0x480fc0`), with the rendering height (+0x6c) instead of the position's z and no "Render On Ground" case. Slot 38 (`0x489cd0`, hit test) draws the entity into two function-local static queues (`0x6bdd30`, `0x6bdce8`; guard `0x6bdd00`) with a 1 × 1 clip rectangle and asks the items from the top; mode 3 asks the model's polygon.

**The sequence classes** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, the slots; VM]: layouts in the head comment of `sequence_classes.cpp`. CSequence +0x08 the frame array, +0x0c..+0x18 the frames' bounding rectangle, +0x1c the load and render flags, +0x20 the blit type (index into the blend mode name list `0x4669a0`, a function-local static), +0x24 the frames per second, +0x28 the count, +0x2c/+0x30 the render offset (its setters `0x56bca0`/`0x56bda0`, not in `docs/functions.csv`, move every frame's origin), +0x34 the file buffer the frames' blocks lie in. CRotationSequence adds the rotations, the frame deltas (+0x44, "Frame Delta <n>=<x>, <y>" lines) and the cutting lines and triggers. `CFont` (0x84) is a CSequence of glyphs with "First ASCII"/"Last ASCII", "Fixed Width", the glyphs' blend mode (+0x38, Transparent Mask) and the line height above the glyphs (+0x80, an unnamed field).

**Text** [confirmed: code; VM]: `0x4a6470` draws a string (justification 0 left, 1 centred, 2 right; a fixed character makes every glyph that character's width, centred in it) through `Frame_BlitAt` with the font's mode; fonts without lower case letters ("Last ASCII" + 1 < 0x60) draw in capitals (the C runtime's `toupper`); `0x4a66c0` draws lines (cut at each '\n' and put back), `0x4a6b90` a number; the measuring functions give glyph widths, the line height, the text height and the lowest glyph bottom.

**Quirks kept** [confirmed: code]:
- The hit test subtracts the item's position before calling slot 4, which subtracts it again.
- The glyph lookup of the measuring code compares the index with last − first + 1 (one past the last glyph), the drawing with the frame count.
- `CRotationSequence`'s slot 27 ends the game with "There are not an equal number of frames per rotation…" when the frames do not divide by the rotations and the sequence is being loaded by name (`0x713130`).
- The draw item pool grows by 300 items and then by one more each time `used` reaches the count below 300.

During an entity case the world's draw item pool is a fake of 400 items built by the original constructor and restored before each side, the queues are recording fakes, the entity's, its children's and the overlay's changed fields are put back after every side, and a run of the original before the case loads and caches what drawing loads on first use (models of the chain, the hue remap cache). ### Effects and text: the hue change effect and its cache, the text overlays, the fonts' word-wrapped text, the sequences' loading, the animated water [verified 2026-10-27, VM; the drawing through the exe's frame, blitter, filter and font code]

**The hue change effect** [confirmed: code; VM]: `CHueChangeEffect` (8 bytes, vtable `0x5f7ba0`, class `0x6c0508`, version 1, parent `CRenderEffect`) has no fields. The hue remap cache is a function-local static pointer array at `0x6c0510` (guard `0x6c0524` bit 0, atexit `0x4d4be0`, vtable `0x5f7c6c`; its slot 0 `0x4d4b20` frees the entries and then the array's block through the pool `0x506470`). An entry is a 0x60-byte heap block: the six floats of a `CHueRemapHolder` (+8..+0x1c) and at +0x18 a `CBlendHueRemap` (constructor `0x43bfe0`, built by `0x43c0e0` with the first three and `0x43c410` with the last three). `HueRemapCache_Get` (fastcall holder) compares each entry's six floats with fcomp + `test ah, 0x40` (NaN counts as equal) and appends a new entry through slot 2 when none matches; `HueRemapCache_Clear` frees the entries (from the last) only from 32 entries on.

**The text overlays** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, code; VM]: `CFrameOverlayTextOverlay` (0x28, vtable `0x5f4c24`, class `0x6bfafc`, version 0): +8 "Text Font" (index into the font list `0x6be1e0`, default "Character Dialog"), +0xc/+0x10 "Text HotSpot Coordinates" (no default: the constructor leaves them as the memory was), +0x14 "Text Wrapping Width" (0x80), +0x18 "Pixels Between Lines" (2), +0x1c "Justification" (the list `0x6be1b8`, "Justify Left"), +0x20 "Text String" (a LocalEntry, "* Some cool message to put in the slideshow!"). `CFrameOverlayOptions` (0x18, vtable `0x5f4c80`, class `0x6bfb00`): +8 "Text Overlays", an embedded array {vtable `0x5f4cdc`, data, count, capacity} whose data is a CreateArray block (freed through the first element's slot 1 with 3); its Add `0x4b5540` grows to max(count + 1, ⌊capacity × 1.2⌋) (the float `0x5ea5f4`), constructs every new element (`0x4b56a0`) and copies +4..+0x1c and the LocalEntry (`0x4b58c0`). The drawing `0x4b52e0` (options; frame) draws every overlay word-wrapped (`0x4a6790`) with its font at its hot spot; the font lookup is inline (none without records or while the record loads, out-of-range indices take 0, a missing font is loaded through the list's slot 37), and eax is the overlay count (undefined without overlays). The options list (0x140, vtable `0x5f4b80`; not hooked, see below) `0x4b5490` deletes the records' objects from the last, the records block, empties the record list, deletes the helper +0x13c through its slot 7 and runs the aliases' destructor. `0x4b59b0` (the image field kind's default; `CImageFieldDesc` in section 6) sizes the object's frame from the descriptor's +0x28/+0x2c/+0x30 (`CFrame_SetSize`) and fills it with slot 26 and the colour +0x34.
- **Quirk kept**: `Add` copies +4 of the elements too (CObject's own dword), so a source with dynamic properties would share them.

**The fonts' word-wrapped text** [confirmed: code; VM]: the layout fields of `CFont` (0x84): +0x48 the text, +0x4c a heap copy, +0x50 the box width, +0x54 the line spacing, +0x58/+0x64 the justification of the first and the following lines, +0x5c/+0x60 and +0x68/+0x6c their left and right margins, +0x70 the height, +0x74 the line count, +0x78 the widest line's right edge, +0x7c the last line's. A line's width is the box's minus its margins; the line breaking is `0x4a7510` (font; text, width, 0, ZString line, the break test `0x506f60`, force), forced (a word cut) when the current width is at least the next one. `0x4a6790` (frame, x, y, text, width, spacing, justification) draws line after line and returns their height; `0x4a68b0` (one paragraph, y by pointer, the margins and the following lines' values) places a line at x + left margin, + half the line width when centred, + the line width when right-justified, and returns the line count; `0x4a6ae0` splits a copy of the text at each '\n' into paragraphs; `0x4a6d10` measures one paragraph like `0x4a68b0` (the right edges into two optional outputs); `0x4a6190` lays out +0x48 into the fields (height = the first glyph's height × lines + spacing × (lines − 1)).
- **Quirks kept** [observed in the code]: the count of characters left, which the space skipping stops at, is the text's length only on the first line and then the previous line's length. When nothing fits on the first line and the following lines are wider, the paragraph functions take the wider width and count an empty line, but the width they test at the end is not updated on that path, so an empty rest never ends (in the original too; the checks keep the first width at least the following one).

**The sequences' loading** [confirmed: code; VM]: the shared frame filter list `0x713360` gets the default set 3, 6, 7, 11, 8 (`0x56b260`); `0x56b440` adapts it to a sequence's load flags (+0x1c: 0x10 takes 12 for 11, 8 takes 9 for 8 and sets filter 3's parameter to 3, 1 adds 2, without 2 filter 7 goes, without 4 filter 6 goes) and blit type ("Blend Black Bias" takes 4, "Blend Amplify Light" 5 for 7). The cache file `0x56b780` (fastcall ZString out, path; name, filter list): `Files_CacheFolder(path)` + path, then `<that>/<name>.seq` or `.seq16` (`ZString_SetPath3`), `-…seq24`/`seq32` (`ZString_SetDashPath`), by the list's target depth or the display's; false only for 32 bits. `0x56b890` frees the frames and reads the cache file with `Object_ReadBinary` (file buffer option 0x18 set; a buffer with Advance calls is detached into +0x34); true when it read and the sequence has frames. Slot 15 (`0x56b9d0`) reads the bounding rectangle and per frame a byte and a frame (`0x4a9340`; a failed one frees all), slot 13 (`0x56ba90`) writes them (a frame with width and height, `0x4a9740`); `CRotationSequence`'s slots 15/13 (`0x55f910`, `0x55f980`) add the frame deltas (count × 8 bytes). `0x56bb70` (frame, filter 6, filter 2) appends a frame (a new pointer array), runs filter 2 and then 6 on it when asked, and rebuilds the bounding rectangle from 99999, 999999, −999999, −999999 with every frame's slot 36.
- **Quirk kept** [confirmed: code; VM]: slot 15 reads the frame's byte into the stack slot of its file argument; when the file ends there, the byte left is the file pointer's low byte, so a short file goes on creating frames (the check with 9 bytes found the reimplementation's first version reading 0 instead).
- **Found in the checks**: the frame writer `0x4a9740` leaves two bytes of its 0x10-byte header (after the height) as the stack had them, so a written cache file differs from run to run in those bytes; the checks compare what is written by reading it back. The game data has no `Properties.txt`, so `0x56b320` (read the sequence's Properties.txt, else write one, else a message box and `exit(-1)`) would write a file in a check; it is not hooked.

**The animated water** [confirmed: constructors, RegisterFields, code; VM]: `CWaterWarpEffect` (0x86c, vtable `0x60292c`, class `0x713dc8`, version 1, no parent): four embedded `CWaterWaveFormData` (0x218, section 6) "V1 Wave" +8, "V2 Wave" +0x220, "H1 Wave" +0x438, "H2 Wave" +0x650 (+8 amplitude, +0xc speed, +0x10 period, +0x14 a table of 128 ints) and +0x868 "Show Grid". The constructor sets V1 (3.07, 19.13, 2), V2 (1.33, −37, 6), H1 (3.05, 15.27, 2), H2 (1.1, −29.33, 6) and fills every table: entry i = fistp(float(fcos(((i · period) << 1) · the float `0x602928`) · amplitude)). A wave's phase is fistp(float(game time (the double at `g_ErrorReporter` +0x40) × speed)) mod 128, non-negative. The warps (thiscall effect; destination, source; 128 × 128 frames of rows of 128 pixels): `0x597690` shifts every row by H1 + H2 (16 bits), `0x597780` every column by V1 + V2, `0x597880` (8 or 16 bits by the destination's depth, nothing else) and `0x597ad0` (16 bits, rows and columns swapped) both in one pass. `CWaterWarpEffectFrame` (0x880, vtable `0x602988`, class `0x713dcc`, parent `CWaterWarpEffect`): +0x86c the bent frame (128 × 128 at the display's depth, made on first use), +0x870 "Static Texture" (the ground textures `0x6c1d50`), +0x874 "Animated Texture" (`0x6c1ee8`), +0x878 "Render Type" (the list `0x713c60`, "Horizontal Then Vertical"), +0x87c the game time of the last update. Its RegisterFields ends with `0x598280` added to the static list `0x62e6a8` (`0x419ea0`, tail jump). The update `0x598420` (fastcall) compares the game time double with the stored float as it is (fcom; NaN counts as equal) and does nothing when equal; render types 0–3 take the static texture (loaded with `DefinitionList_LoadRecord` `0x55e090` when missing), 4 and above the animated texture's frame at ⌊time × its slot 26⌉ mod its frame count; 0, 1, 2 and 4, 3 run `0x597690`, `0x597780`, `0x597880`, `0x597ad0`.

**The hue remap table** `0x5280e0` [confirmed: code; VM] (this the 256-byte table, source palette, the parameters centre, new hue and range in degrees, a clear flag; called by the hue blend builders, section 9 R1): with the flag every entry first maps to itself; every non-black palette entry whose hue (`0x526c40` RGB → hue, lightness, saturation; the hue rounded up to tenths through `ceil`) lies within centre ± range maps to the nearest palette entry (`0x526e40`, 0 … 0x100) of the same lightness and saturation at the new hue (HSL → RGB inline, the blue channel unrounded).

**CWarpEffect and CSimpleWarpEffect** [confirmed: getters, constructors, RegisterFields, code; VM]: `CWarpEffect` (0x10, vtable `0x6027e4`, class `0x713c50`, abstract, parent `CRenderEffect`): +8 the strength, +0xc the rate; slots 23/24 the network block (strength · 255 and slot 31 · 8 as bytes; back · 1/255 and · 0.125), 25/26 begin (slots 28, 29) and end (slot 30) on an entity's frame (its dynamic property +0x34 when it is a CFrame), 27 nothing (six arguments), 31 the rate. `CSimpleWarpEffect` (0x30, vtable `0x60049c`, class `0x713574`): +0x10 … +0x20 the frame's five pixel blocks while on, +0x24 on, +0x28 the copy's bytes, +0x2c "Warp Effect" (the sequence list `0x6c2788`), slot 31 the sequence's rate. Begin gives an uncompressed frame the render buffer (`0x55e2f0`, width · height) as pixels and a compressed one (flags 2: five blocks, 4: two) a copy of its layout in the render buffer (the size dwords); draw bends the saved blocks into the copy (`0x571c50` per block with the block's row table, slots 46–50, and the frame's origin) or copies an uncompressed buffer back through the 8-bit table `0x6767c0` row (byte `0x713570`); end releases the buffer and puts the blocks back. `0x571c50` takes the sequence's frame at game time × rate (rate 0: ⌊(count − 1) · strength + 0.5⌋, wrapped by subtraction) and walks the RLE rows (0x80 skip, 0x40 a run of n values, else one value for n pixels; the copy keeps the layout) with the texture's pixel at (x & width mask, y & height mask) from the origin: in 8 bits by the strength the texture (≥ 0.9, `0x571ff0`), the tables `0x6767d0`/`0x6767c0` with the source as row (≥ 0.7, ≥ 0.5) or column (≥ 0.3, ≥ 0.1), the fade table `0x6767d0` alone (`0x572f40`); in 16 bits the texture (≥ 1, `0x573440`) or the 5-6-5 blend towards it with the weight of the fade table `g_FadeTables` + ⌊strength · 255⌉ · 0x400 (`0x6b67e8`, its last dword; low bit set; `0x5730f0`).
- **Quirks kept** [observed in the code]: the run and row loops are do-while loops (a run of 0 pixels runs 2^32 times; a row whose runs do not add up to the width never ends), a fill writes one source value for n pixels, Draw's block loop calls the row table slot after the data slot, the blend's differences are multiplied and shifted as unsigned 32-bit values.

**CLightningLayerPart** [confirmed: Create, RegisterFields, code; VM]: 0xb4 bytes (vtable `0x5f984c`, class `0x6c2b8c`, parent `CSimpleLayerPart`): +0x54/+0x58/+0x5c/+0x60 Z, X Length (100), Y Length (25), Height (setters `0x500700`–`0x500730` jumping to slots 83–86, which set the field between two relists), +0x64 the draw items (0x58-byte records), +0x74 the points, +0x84/+0x88 the cosine and sine of the bolt's angle + π/2, +0x8c Width (0.25), +0x90 Min Segment Length (5), +0x94 Center Color and +0xa4 Edge Color (defaults white and (103, 35, 166), RegisterFields' statics `0x6c2b78`/`0x6c2b68`, guard `0x6c2b88`). The geometry `0x500080` subdivides the line from the position to the position + (X Length, Y Length − Height) by random midpoint displacement (`0x4fff60`: while a random length below the minimum plus the minimum is not above the length, the midpoint moves by Random_Range(±length · width) along the normal); the draw (slot 23) makes ⌊|Y Length| · 0.05⌉ (1 … segments) draw items over runs of the points, each with its sort row, the part's slots 52/53, the offset, the colours and its bounding box (`0x4feb30`), into the queue (`DrawQueue_Add`), then CLayerPart's slot 23. The network block (slots 25/27) packs the colours: red and green in 4 bits each, blue as centre (0 … 10) · 11 + edge with bit 7 when both are opaque, the alpha nibbles only otherwise. Slot 37 gives for kinds 0, 2 and 5 the box around the bolt widened along its normal, slot 38 hits kinds 0–3; slot 61 (`0x5717d0`, in other parts' vtables too) is the class's short name.

**The effect lists and the image field** [confirmed: code; VM]: the lists "Frame Overlay Options" (vtable `0x5f4b80`, `.FOO`) and "Water Warp Effects" (`0x602a88`, `.txt`) have the definition list slots of `def_list_slots.h` (slot 0 the deleting destructor, 35 the file of an object, 37 the object a file makes, 39 an entry's path; hooked as instances of those templates); `0x598910` keeps the object of "<dir>/<name>.txt" only when it is a `CWaterWarpEffectFrame`. `0x52b5d0` (4 bytes), `0x5965c0` (4 bytes) and `0x596650` (`ret 0x18`) are hooked through the nop padding behind them (as the earlier 5-byte hooks with `c3 90`).

### The world's frame: the frame slots, the layer's draw pass, the dirty tiles, the HUD, the game types' HUD, the status text, the view's helpers and four AIs' drawing [verified 2026-10-27, VM; the orchestration through recording stand-ins, the drawing through the exe's frame, blitter and font code]

Five modules, 38 functions (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): `reimpl/src/world_frame.cpp` (5: the world's slots 3 and 4 and their parts, a layer rendered whole), `layer_draw.cpp` (17: the dirty tile frame, the draw pass, the dirty tiles, the tile helpers, the queue outlines, two COffsetClippedProxyFrame slots), `hud_world.cpp` (6: `CZaxWorld::DrawHud`, the status text, the three game types' HUD), `view_draw.cpp` (6: the oval, arc and arrow helpers, the polygon outline, the light beam's block reader), `ai_draw.cpp` (4: the draw slot of `CLandscapeAI`, `CScanAreaAI` and the two timeout AIs), each with `checks_<module>.cpp`. **How a frame reaches the screen** [confirmed: code; VM]:
- CZaxWorld's slot 3 (its vtable `0x602dcc`; `0x59db30`, section 8) calls `World::DrawFrame` `0x4f2d90` (CWorld's slot 4, vtable `0x5f8fc0`) and, when it gave al 1, the application base's `0x4ce160`. CWorld's slot 3 `World::Frame` `0x4f2620`, which CZaxWorld overrides, is the base world's per-frame update (the timers, the net layer's slot 27, the cursor's and the music's advance, every player's entity to the world's slot 51 while slot 30 is 0 or slot 31 is set, the sound listener at player 0's layer's view (+0x80 + `0x5eff98`, −10, −(+0x84 + `0x5eff9c`)), slot 48 and `App::Frame` `0x4cdfd0`).
- Slot 4 without a game (+0x310 0): the menu music (song 2) and, unless slot 26 says the menu draws itself, the menu background +0x2fc into the HUD frame +0x2a8: directly when the sizes match, else through the function-local static frame `0x6c2548` (guard `0x6c2678`, atexit `0x4f3160`), sized to +0x2a8 and filled by the scaling blit (`0x4a8f40`, mode `0x6b9ca0`) only when **both** its width and its height differ from +0x2a8's (a change of one dimension keeps the old scaled image) [confirmed: code].

**Quirks kept** [confirmed: code]:
- `0x4f2d90` rescales the menu background only when both dimensions changed; `0x4f2620` pushes the slot 61 byte as a whole stack dword (the upper bytes are stack contents).

The module comments hold the layouts and the behaviour. Findings [confirmed: code, the checks]:
- **Corrections of the blitter map**: `FrameDraw_StaticSwitch` `0x4b3530` is not unreferenced: `DrawItem::StaticSwitch` `0x49c860` calls it. `0x432370` is the "at end" test (al: the record's frame equals the Bink handle's frame count; the rest of eax is the frame). `CJWindow_RunModal` calls no Windows function directly (the tick is the game's `0x4d2460`), so it is not phase 5a.
- The font list (`0x6be1e0`, 0x144 bytes: the definition list and the sequence cache flag at +0x140) frees 0x144 bytes in its slot 0 `0x4a7b20`; the copy `0x4a7c30` of its base frees 0x140.
- `BreakLine` calls its callback for every word it takes, the first time with length 0; a '\n' ends the line after its word; with nothing taken and force it takes single characters and calls the callback once with their count. `MaxLineWidth` splits with the C runtime's `strchr`.
- `Font_SliceStrip`: a strip without flag 0x20 marks the cells with opaque pixels (GetPixel's alpha byte) in column 0 (the baseline, searched in the upper half) and along the last row (the cell edges); a font whose last character is first − 1 divides by zero (the original too; the checks leave it out).
- `CJWindow::DrawChildren`'s corner between the two scroll bars is a blit of the window's slot 72 frame with the Tile mode through the frame's slot 23 (4 arguments; the pushes stand before the slot 72 call). `RunModal` blits the frame to the error reporter's screen when it is another one: the blit's ecx is still the screen loaded for the comparison.
- The error diffusion's red error stays on the FPU (80 bits) while green and blue are rounded to float first; the reimplementation rounds through memory (`mem_float`, a volatile float): clang keeps `(float)` casts of long double values on the FPU unrounded, which gave 1-ulp differences in 1 of 3 `Spread` cases and 1 of 800 `Quantize` cases until then. `App_DrawFrame`'s rate samples are stored the same way.
- `Remap8_Row` with n = 0 loops 2^32 times (do/while), eax the last byte written; `CFrame::WriteFrm` leaves header bytes 0xa–0xb as the stack had them (the checks hash the header without them); `CFrame::ReadFrm` exits the game ("Fatal Error loading a frame") on a block above 4 MB.
- `App_DrawFrame` prints "U:" with `0x6c02d0` and D, P, A with the three counters in the order 0x6bfe88, 0x6c00b0, 0x6bffa0, and colours the line from the 0x6c00b0 sample (red below 30, flashing red/yellow below 20).

Harness changes and notes (`checks_ui_common.cpp`, for every batch on this harness): **thread guard** — a stand-in's site now jumps to a guard (`mov eax, fs:[0x24]; cmp eax, <check thread>; jne <the hook's trampoline>; jmp <recording thunk>`), so the game's other threads run the original code instead of the case's stand-ins, and `GetTickCount`'s stand-in gives them the real clock. Found on `Assimilate Cave1`: with the FileBuf stand-ins on, the music stream's thread read files through them (its calls landed in unrelated cases' logs — `Dither::Begin` with 3 calls, `StaticExit_FilterState`'s eax, `ReadFrm`/`WriteFrm` — 1 to 3 cases of 5,300 per run, never on `Test/Nachbau1`, and the thread got the stand-ins' answers instead of its data); earlier modules that stub the file buffer, the frames or the allocators from the check thread were exposed the same way. Functions without a hook (no trampoline) still reach the thunk from any thread. Notes: a stand-in's ecx is logged by the 4 bytes it points to when it lies on the stack, so methods on a caller's uninitialised local are declared fastcall with ecx ignored (`"xx…"`), and a 'e' stand-in declared so returns 0; an effect cannot reach ecx of a fastcall stand-in (patch a stand-in of your own in the test's setup and take it out in `after`, as the `.tga` loader's frame constructor); `Case::object_args` set in `base` applies to every game object of the case (the error reporter's slot 5 takes no argument: a wrong pop count crashed side 0 at address 3).

The frame, blend, blitter, rasterizer, font, line breaking, file buffer and warp effect functions they call stay the exe's (or the earlier batches' reimplementations), always through their exe addresses.

**The palette object** [confirmed: code; VM] (12 bytes: +0 the data, +4 the kind, +8 a source palette): the kind gives the data's size (`Palette_KindBytes` `0x527d50`, inline everywhere else): 1 a palette of 256 entries b, g, r (0x300 bytes), 2 a remap of 256 indices, 3 0x400 bytes, 4 a 256 × 256 remap (the blend tables, entry src · 256 + dst), 5 and 6 an index per 5-5-5 colour (6 filled on demand from the source), 7 an index per 5-6-5 colour; others 0 bytes. Setting a kind frees the data when it changes (`Assign` `0x526700`, `SetKind` `0x5268f0`, `Load` `0x5269e0` and `BuildLookup` `0x527da0` also for kind 0) and allocates it with the identity when missing. `Nearest` `0x526e40` (r, g, b, first, end): kind 1 the entry of the smallest 30 dr² + 59 dg² + 11 db² (the square table `0x61d3e8`; a distance of 0 stops) as (first + offset) & 0xff; kinds 5–7 the lookups. `Differs` `0x526870` is `repe cmpsb` over the size; `Load`/`Save` `0x5269e0`/`0x526b80` read and write the data whole through a `CFileBuf` on the stack (flags 4 and 3).
- The tables (all from `InitBlendTables` `0x433000`, the lightness remap also from `CJWindow::Init`'s bevel colours): `RgbToHsl` `0x526c40` (fastcall h, s out; r, g, b; l out) and `HueValue` `0x526da0` (p, q, h; st0) are HSL with the x87 order of the original; `BuildLightnessRemap` `0x527040` (source, factor, two unused, first, end, lo, hi, target) scales every entry's lightness by factor / 128 (0x80 the identity) and maps it back to the target's nearest index (the red channel's hue ramp inline with the unrounded hue + 120); `BuildGammaTable` `0x527700` with `FillGammaTable` `0x527420` (fastcall table, palette; factor) a 256 × 256 table of s · k + d · (1 − k), with factor 0 k = (max(s)/255)^1.5 (`_CIpow` `0x5d23e0`) and s rescaled to a maximum of 255; `BuildAmplifyTable` `0x5277b0` d · (1 + s/255) (the Amplify Light table), `BuildHueBlendTable` `0x527980` d's hue moved towards s's (the shorter way round, 342.128 for a turn), the larger saturation, l(d) + l(s)/3; `BuildLookup` `0x527da0` (source, kind, lo, hi) the 5-5-5 or 5-6-5 lookups or a cleared on-demand table; `DrawPalette_Build` `0x527fa0` (histogram, first, colours) a cleared palette with a white last entry and the quantisation into the entries from first.
- **The colour quantiser** `0x54ff70`–`0x550660` [confirmed: code; VM] is Wu's variance cut over a 64 × 64 × 64 dword histogram (`0x712258` while it runs): boxes of 0x30 bytes (variance, count, squares, the r, g, b sums, the inclusive bounds) in `0x712260`, a max-heap of box pointers by variance in `0x712264` (size `0x71225c`), the box count `0x712268`. `BoxBottom` `0x5504f0` sums the moments (32-bit), `BoxVolume` `0x5501f0` finds the bounds of the non-empty cells (each bound searched over the whole input box; written only when found), `Cut` `0x550660` rates every split plane of each axis by the two halves' squares − (r² + g² + b²)/count (x87 over the sums as unsigned 64-bit values, truncated, added as an unsigned dword), splits at the best plane of the best axis (r before g before b on ties), shrinks both halves, recomputes the first half's moments (the second gets the rest) and variances, and updates the heap (a half whose extents sum to 0 leaves it). `Quantize` (fastcall histogram, colours; palette, count) cuts until the colours are reached and writes (count/2 + sum · 4)/count per channel.
- **Quirks kept** [confirmed: code]: `Nearest` of an empty range returns first · 2; the lightness remap ignores its third and fourth arguments; `FillGammaTable` rescales by the first unrounded maximum and then by every channel still above 255 times it; the first box's variance is 1, not computed; an empty histogram leaves the quantiser's bounds undefined (the check never passes one; the game builds palettes from a frame's pixels).

**CRenderablePolygon** [confirmed: constructor, RegisterFields, code; VM] (0x9c bytes, vtable `0x5fe900`, class `0x713100`, version 5.0, parent `CFreeRangePoly`): +0x74 "Render/YSort", +0x78 "Render/Render Type" (the list `0x7130e8`, "Black"), +0x7c "Render/Animated Texture" (`0x6c1ee8`), +0x80 "Render/Static Texture" (`0x6c1d50`), +0x84 "Render/Warp Effect" (`0x713c80`), +0x88 bit 0 "Render/On Ground" (bit 1: the sort key is up to date), +0x8c the draw item, +0x90 the texture frame, +0x94 "Render/Cur Frame". The constructor gives the polygon the default triangle (100, 100), (300, 150), (200, 350) and a draw item (0x54 bytes, vtable `0x5fea48`, the rasterizer's points at +0x28; the base fields stay as the heap had them). Slot 78 `0x55dc30` sets the item's key (bottom + YSort) · 8, x and y; slot 23 `0x55dd90` (ground queue, object queue, view, flag) picks the texture frame by render type (6 the animated texture's slot 23, 5 the static texture's record, 7 the warp effect's `Update` `0x598420`), converts the points (`PolyPoints_FromFloat`), sets the bounds and the rasterizer's kind and queues the item when it meets the view. The item's slots: 1 `0x55d210` draws (`PolyRaster_Draw`, at least three points, not into the reporter's frame), 3 `0x55d250` the bounds, 6 `0x55d970` the deleting destructor. **CScreenFrame** (0xe8 bytes, vtable `0x5ff360`, class `0x71332c`, parent CFrame) [confirmed: code; VM]: the CFrame part (+0xc the back buffer's pixels while it is locked), +0x40 the pages (the flipping chain + 2), +0x44 the back buffers, +0x48 the page shown, +0x4c/+0x54 the display modes (0xc each: width, height, depth), +0x50 the primary surface is in video memory, +0xcc "Display is RGB 565" (0 for 5-5-5), +0xd0 the brightness, +0xd4 the fade state (0 in, 1 out, 2 none), +0xd8 the fade level, +0xdc the fade time, +0xe0 its time left, +0xe4 the time since the last fade. The globals: `0x713334` the DirectDraw object, `0x713338` the back buffer, `0x71333c` a third surface, `0x713340` the clipper, `0x713344` the palette, `0x713348` the primary surface, `0x713318` the back buffer is locked, `0x713284` the back buffer is a surface of its own, `0x6210c0` full screen (exclusive; the cooperative level 0x51), the palette holders `0x713278` (black), `0x713288` (the system palette), `0x713298` (the fade's start), `0x713320` (the fade's current), `0x713268`, and `0x713bd0` the screen depth.
- The drawing slots 51, 52, 55, 57, 64, 65 and 66 call CFrame's own with the back buffer locked (`0x567bb0`) and unlocked again (the inlined Unlock, COM slot 32) when it was not locked already. Slot 23 (Blit) gives a normal blit onto a 16-bit screen the screen blend of the brightness times the fade level (`(level · brightness − 1) · 128`, and · 256 when negative; up or down, 5-6-5 or 5-5-5, from 4 resp. 8 on).
- Slots 28 and 24 fill a rectangle (clipped to the frame) through the back buffer's Blt (`DDBLT_COLORFILL | DDBLT_WAIT`, the effects at `0x6210c8` resp. `0x621138`, the colour at +0x50 of them); a locked back buffer is unlocked around the Blt and locked again. The colour in the frame's format: an 8-bit index (the colour's own when its flag 1 is set, else `FieldColor_PaletteIndex`), a 16-bit pixel (converted to 5-5-5 by the masks `0x62112c`/`0x621130`/`0x621134` unless +0xcc), 24 bits from +4/+6 of the colour **with the colour pointer's top byte as the fourth byte** (the argument's stack slot is reused), 32 bits as they are.
- The fades: `0x568630` fades to black (`0x713278`) through `0x568660` (frame, from, to, blend, palette holder, ms, keep the system colours), which in full screen moves the palette from the frame's to the target over the time (`(b − a) · t + a` per byte, t the elapsed share; the image drawn and flipped every step), then sets the target and draws the image on every page. `0x568870` sets a palette: black at 0 and white at 255, every colour brighter by `(brightness − 1) · 128` above 0.01, into `0x713268` and the DirectDraw palette's 256 entries, where the 10 system colours at each end are kept unless the flag says otherwise; the 16-bit tables rebuilt.
- `0x567ab0` (seconds) moves the fade on; after 5 s with the level at most 0.001 a fade in of 1 s starts.
- The modes: `0x567cd0` (&width, &height) finds a listed mode or the smallest bigger one (both 0 when none; al 1 for an exact match, the upper bytes of eax the index or three times it), `0x567e90` drops a mode of the same size as the next.
- The display setup `0x590ce0` (depth or 0, width, height): the mode of the arguments, else of Zax.CFG (`Screen Width`, `Screen Height`, `Screen Bit Depth`, written back) and the command line (`/ScreenWidth`, `/ScreenHeight`, `/ScreenBitDepth`); 24 bits tried as 32 when the mode fails, a second failure ends the game ("Couldn't set resolution"); the depth told to the application without a depth argument, the brightness `Screen Brightness` (default 1). `0x590f00` switches to 640 × 480 in the screen depth.

**The full-screen image** (0x3c bytes, a local of its callers) [confirmed: code; VM]: +0 the time it was shown (the tick count `0x4d2460`), +4 how long it stays (seconds, 3 by default), +8 the image's rectangle, +0x18 where it lies (centred), +0x28 the blend mode, +0x2c the holder of the shown image (8 bytes, operator new: +0 the frame, +4 owned), +0x30 fade in with the game palette. `Show` waits for the previous image, fades it out, takes the new one (a frame that is not owned, or not of the screen depth while there are overlay options to draw on it, is copied into an owned frame of the screen depth first), draws it on four pages (lock, layout, unlock, flip) and fades it in. `ShowFile` takes the overlay options named like the file without its extension from "Frame Overlay Options" (`0x6bf9b8`, loaded inline).

**The sequence list and window** [confirmed: code; VM]: the image sequence list (0x158, vtable `0x5ff64c`; its base 0x140 with vtable `0x5ff6f0`) keeps its sequences' frame filters at +0x140 (set +0x154); its slot 37 `0x56c250` loads a `CSequence` (0x38) from the cache file with them, the game's defaults `0x56b260` the first time (the function was misfiled as `CAmbientSound`'s slot 60). The debug window ("!DEBUG! <name>", 0x10c, vtable `0x5ff794`) shows one sequence of a list (`0x713380` by default) at its frame rate, wrapping once per advance. `0x56b320` (folder, name) reads `<folder>/-<name>/Properties.txt` into the object, else writes the object's defaults (slot 19) there; neither ends the game.

**The TGA files** [confirmed: code; VM]: the reader `0x58c6f0` (fastcall frame, bytes; name, palette (`0x633388` by default), allocation flag) takes only maps without a colour map, of types 2, 9 or 10 and of 24 or 32 bits; the frame is reallocated when its size differs; the rows go through one of eight converters (frame depth 8, 16, 24, 32 × file depth 24, 32; the 24 → 16 one inline), bottom up unless the descriptor's bit 0x20; type 10 rows are decoded first (`0x58cde0`), the others read in place (type 9 too). The source row's bytes stay in the global `0x7139ec`. The writer `0x58cef0` (fastcall frame, file; open mode) writes RLE only: 8 bits as type 9 with the palette (or a grey ramp without one), 24 and 32 bits as type 10, rows bottom up; a compressed frame is drawn into a plain one first.

**The AI debug drawing** [confirmed: code; VM]: as the four AIs of the world draw batch (section 9, "The world's frame"): `CSkeletonAI` (+0xa8 the state; the facing arrow, the sub-AIs of the state through `AI_Draw`, in states 1, 2 and 4 a cross at the target and a line to it and the velocity as a line in the facing, in states 1 and 2 two ovals, the state's name from `0x621c44`), `CTurretAI` (two range ovals, three values of an animated entity as text). Their colours are the exe's function-local statics (guard bits `0x713618`, `0x713a28`; atexit).

**The save/load details page** `0x564090` [confirmed: code; VM]: with nothing chosen in either list, a page per member of the null-terminated list at +0x160 with the label `0x7131ac`; else the chosen save's statistics (+0x19c for the first list, the saves' array +0x18c for the second) in a new tab control: the summary (date, playing time, percentage, the two counts, coloured green, gold or red against the mission's number), the mission details (0x104, vtable `0x5ff098`), the statistics' items left and right (their colour fonts from `StatsColorFont` `0x5aedf0`). The summary and the two statistics pages are built again until their client width settles (a scroll bar appearing narrows them). The row texts are the exe's function-local static ZStrings `0x7131c8`, `0x713204`, `0x713188`, `0x713194` (guard `0x7131b8`).

**Quirks kept** [confirmed: code]:
- `CScreenFrame::FillRect` builds a 24-bit fill colour with the colour pointer's top byte as its fourth byte.
- `ScreenFrame_SetPalette` without the "all" flag reads the system palette's first and last ten entries into the same ten slots, so the DirectDraw palette's entries 245–255 are stack contents (only their flag byte is set); the game passes the flag 1 everywhere except the constructor's path.
- `ImageFile_Read` returns at a frame depth other than 8, 16, 24 and 32 without freeing its RLE row buffer; `ImageFile_Write`'s run search compares the row's last pixel with the bytes behind the row, and its 8-bit raw packets take the whole limit of up to 128 pixels, not the pixels up to the next run.
- The stream holder's `IsMuted`, `IsPlaying` and `SetCrossFadeGain` return al with the state pointer's upper bytes in eax (clang folded the plain C form into a movzx; inline asm keeps them).
- `ScreenImage::Show` and `SequenceWindow_Ctor` dereference a missing frame or sequence (a check case ended the game on both sides).

**Phase 5a** (the DirectDraw surface handling and Windows; recorded in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`):
- `ScreenFrame_SetMode` `0x567f20`: `DirectDrawCreate`, `SetCooperativeLevel` (8 windowed, 0x51 full screen), `EnumDisplayModes` (callback `0x567d60` fills the mode list), `SetDisplayMode`, `CreateSurface` (primary with one or two back buffers, video memory first; windowed: an offscreen back buffer of the mode, a clipper on the window), `GetAttachedSurface`, `CreatePalette`, `SetPalette`, Lock/Unlock to read the pixel format, "Display is RGB 565" in Zax.CFG, the "BAD SCREEN MODE" errors.
- `ScreenFrame_Release` `0x5678c0` (every page cleared and flipped, then palette, clipper, back buffer, primary surface and DirectDraw released), `ScreenFrame_Lock` `0x567bb0` (restore lost surfaces, `Lock` up to 100 tries), `ScreenFrame_Unlock` `0x567c90`, `ScreenFrame_Flip` `0x5693a0` (windowed: `GetClientRect`, `ClientToScreen`, `OffsetRect`, `Blt` to the primary surface; full screen: `Flip`).
- `App_PumpMessages` `0x5998f0`: `PeekMessageA`, `Sleep`, `IsIconic`, `TranslateMessage`, `DispatchMessageA`; the mouse wheel (the registered message `0x713e14`) and the key and button messages into the input state (`Keys::Press`/`Release`/`AddChar`, `0x6cff50`–`0x6cff60`).

**Open**: the save/load screen's constructor `0x562970` (3.3 KB: the dialog, the saves read from `SaveGames/*.sav` with `DirList` and `ObjectStream` into `CZaxSaveGameStats`, "QuickSave.sav" marked, the header, the lists, the name field, the buttons, the tab control and the first details page). It is pure game code and checkable with the same harness (the directory list, the object stream and the statistics as stand-ins); left for a follow-up for its size.

**Checks** (in the game thread, the toolkit's harness `checks_ui_common.h` with the screens' setup `checks_ui_screens.h`; per module `checks_<module>.cpp`):
- `screen_frame`: the screen frame a fake of the CFrame class's recording vtable with the case's members (formats, brightness, fade state, modes); the back buffer and palette behind `0x713338`/`0x713344` fake COM objects of the check (Blt with the rectangle's contents and the fill colour, Unlock, SetEntries with the entries) recorded; the phase 5a functions, the CFrame drawing functions, the screen blend levels, the palette helpers, the tick count, the INI file and the command line stand-ins; the palette holders in the block; the set mode stand-in fails the first 24-bit try in a third of the display cases (the retry succeeds: other failures end the game). 28 tests, 4380 cases.

**The loaders and the tables** [confirmed: code; VM]: see the module comment of `image_lo4.cpp`. `Bmp_Decode` takes the nearest colour of the given palette (or `0x633388` without one) for 24-bit files in an 8-bit frame; with the remap it builds `0x6bceb8` only for 8-bit files. `CFrame::LoadImage` maps 0 and 0xff of an 8-bit frame to the nearest grey of the palette's entries 0 and 255 in mode 1. `CFrame::LoadTga` keeps one load buffer (`0x6be7c0`, at least 64 KB, grown by doubling) and ends the game on a recursive load or an uncompressed TGA that is not on disk. `InitBlendTables` computes the pixel tables with the x87 in the game's precision (control word 0x27f) through `__ftol`, as the reimplementation does with `x87_ftol`.

## 10. Phase 5a: the system layer (mapped 2026-10-28)

### The map [analysed 2026-10-28, no VM run: map only]

*Note (2026-11-01)*: the map and its counts of open code ("Result", "The open game code that is not system layer", "Total open game code") are the state of 2026-10-28; all of it was closed the same day by the batches C1–C5, P5a-1, P5a-2 and the phase 5 leftovers (below; "The milestone audit").

The mapping batch of phase 5a (section 3). It looked for every function of the game code (`0x401000`–`0x5c3bf0`, without the libraries and the copy protection of section 11) that calls Windows, DirectX, Bink or COM directly and is not reimplemented yet, and for any other game code that is still open. `docs/exe_symbols.csv` has a row for each of them (2,506 new rows, 32 rows extended; the source column names the group and batch of this section).

**How it was done** [confirmed: imports, disassembly]:
- The import table: 200 imports from 11 DLLs. Every call site in `.text` was found by its bytes (`call [IAT]`, `jmp [IAT]`, `mov reg, [IAT]` for the register calls, `call` to an import thunk) and mapped to its function through `docs/functions.csv` and `docs/reimpl.csv`. The game code has three wrappers of its own that are only `jmp [IAT]` (`0x4d2460` GetTickCount, `0x4d24b0` timeGetTime, `0x4dd920` joyGetNumDevs); calls to them count as calls of the API.
- The COM objects: the out pointers of `DirectDrawCreate` (`0x713334`; surfaces `0x713338`/`0x71333c`/`0x713348`, clipper `0x713340`, palette `0x713344`), `DirectSoundCreate` (the sound manager, section 9, "The game side of the sound") and `CoCreateInstance` (the DirectPlay net game, section 6, "Net game, …"), and every function that reads them.
- Functions that neither table knows: every address that is called, or that is pushed, moved or stored as a pointer in `.rdata`/`.data`, 16-byte aligned, starts after padding or a `ret` and lies outside every known function. 2,525 candidates; 19 dropped as jump tables (`jmp [reg*4 + table]`), 2,506 kept. They were classified by their code (the registration stub `push getter; mov ecx, class info; call 0x417690`, the class info getter that calls `ClassInfo_Register`, the static initializer that calls `atexit`, the 10-byte `mov ecx, object; jmp destructor` and the pointers pushed to `atexit`), vtable slots by the nearest vtable start (1,032 vtables: every `.rdata` address the code uses whose first dword is code, plus `docs/classes.csv`).
- Limits: a function reached only through a computed address (none seen) is missed; the vtable names (`Class::vfN`) take the class from the vtable's other known slots and can name a parent class or the wrong one of two neighbouring vtables (`Vtable_<address>::vfN` where none is known). Running `tools/ghidra.sh` after the merge creates the functions at the new rows (ZaxNames.java creates a function for every `function` row) and `docs/functions.csv` counts them. The scripts are in the shared notes folder of the batch (`p5a-map-scripts`).

**Result** [confirmed]:
- **The system layer proper is small: 63 functions, 15.6 KB**, in four groups (below). Most of the Windows code was already reimplemented in phases 1–4 with the original calls and checked with recording fakes: 82 functions call Windows directly (the file search, temp files and folders, the INI files, the platform helpers `0x4d2300`–`0x4d2650`, the joystick with its registry reads, the key names and keyboard rates, `QueryPerformanceCounter`, the random seeds, `CScreenFrame`'s constructor and palette with `GetSystemPaletteEntries`, `DirectSoundCreate`, the ACM reader, the multimedia timer of the streams, the DirectPlay core with `CoCreateInstance`, the class registry's `FreeLibrary` and 25 users of `GetTickCount`); the COM calls of the sound manager (every `IDirectSoundBuffer` and the listener), `CScreenFrame`'s drawing slots and the DirectPlay message handler are reimplemented too. Sound needs no batch of its own in 5a.
- **The rest of the open game code is not system layer and is much larger**: 164 functions of `docs/functions.csv` (79.8 KB, 45 of them under 5 bytes) and **2,475 functions in neither table** (131.0 KB, 69 under 5 bytes). The phase 1–4 batches took their work from `docs/functions.csv`, which lacks the startup code (CRT initializer table entries) and the vtables of the classes that are not registered (window toolkit, application, DirectPlay net game, renderers). That contradicts "every function of the game code reimplemented after phase 4": about 2,640 game functions (211 KB) are still open besides the system layer (lists below).

Check: a fake `IDirectDraw` with fake surfaces, clipper and palette (vtables of recording stand-ins that answer like a 16-bit 565 device; `Lock` hands out a buffer of the harness) put into `0x713334`–`0x713348`, `DirectDrawCreate` through a recording IAT stand-in, both versions run with the same answers, the call logs and the frame object compared (as band C's fake COM objects, section 9).
