Total open game code: **2,702 functions, 226 KB** – 63 of the system layer and 2,639 others; 117 of them are too short to hook (45 + 69 + 3) and can only be shown identical by their bytes or replaced with their callers. C1 and C2 are large in count but mechanical (four code shapes), so they need not keep the usual 100–150 size; C3–C5 have the usual size. P5a-1 and P5a-2 can run in parallel (no shared files), C1–C5 too; P5a-1 is the only batch that needs runs of whole game starts.

Risks:
- The startup code (P5a-1's `WinMain` and start, C1, C2) runs before the check thread; a mistake shows as a game that does not start. Mitigation: the hooks switchable one by one, logging before they run, the logged start against `/Original`.
- The real DirectDraw device in the VMs: Windows on ARM emulates DirectDraw; full screen may not behave as on the original hardware (since 2026-11-01 the x86 VMs, with Windows' own DirectDraw, are primary; the ARM VMs run through DDrawCompat, section 5). The port (phase 7) replaces it anyway; 5a needs the call sequence, which the fakes show.
- DirectPlay and Bink call back on their own threads (`DPlay_MessageHandlerCallback`, the Bink IO background callback); the reimplementation must keep the original's locking (`g_DPlayLock`, the stream flag) exactly.
- No LAN game between two machines has been run yet; DirectPlay 8 on current Windows needs the optional "DirectPlay" feature [assumption: about Windows, not tested] (2026-10-28; since phase 6 the LAN games and their replays run on the VMs, section 13, "Batch 6-11", "Batch 6-14").
- The discovery of the 2,475 functions is a byte-pattern heuristic: a few names or kinds may be wrong; `tools/ghidra.sh` and a regenerated `docs/functions.csv` confirm the starts and sizes.
- Comments in `reimpl/src` (`sound_reader.cpp`, `sound_rest4b.cpp`: "section 10"; `ui_save_load.cpp`: "section 11") still use the old numbers of the libraries and the next steps (now sections 11 and 12); fix them with the next batch that touches those files. (2026-11-01: the two sound files say "section 11" now; `ui_save_load.cpp`'s header still names section 11 and calls the constructor `0x562970` not reimplemented, which is done in `ui_save_load_ctor.cpp`, section 9, "Phase 4 leftovers"; `docs/TODO.md`.)

### Batch C1: the startup class registrations and the class info getters [verified 2026-10-28, VM]

The 616 functions of C1 (487 startup class registrations, 129 "class info getters with the registration inlined") are reimplemented in seven modules; nothing of C1 is left. 592 are generated from the exe's bytes by `tools/gen_classreg.py` (section 5), 24 written by hand; each is hooked and checked against the original in the game thread. Names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv` (the map's names corrected), list in `docs/reimpl.csv`.

| Module | Functions | What [confirmed: code, the checks] |
|---|---|---|
| `classreg_a.cpp`–`classreg_d.cpp` (generated) | 487 (122, 122, 122, 121) | the 16-byte stubs of the C runtime's initializer table, `push getter; mov ecx, object; call ClassInfo_StaticRegister 0x417690; ret`: `static_register(object, getter)`, eax 0x417690's (the object). Each stub has an object byte of its own in `.data` (487 different addresses) that only serves as `this`. Split in four: the check harness holds at most 160 hooks per module |
| `classreg_getters.cpp`, `classreg_vars.h` (generated) | 105 | 103 getters whose code is only the inlined registration of their class and `return [variable]` (92 with one block, 12 with the parent's getter inlined, 1 with two parents inlined; 6 of them referenced only from `.rdata`, a vtable's slot), and the two static registrations with the getter inlined (`CObject` `0x416400`, `CClassThatCanNotBeConstructedOrDerivedFrom` `0x4176b0`: then `ClassRegistry_Add(ClassRegistry_Get(), class, 0)`). `classreg_vars.h` has one function per class variable (120): if the variable is 0, a class info from the pool (`operator_new_ecx(0x48)`), then the parent (an exe getter, an inlined parent's function or an immediate: 0, or −1 for `CObject`) and `ClassInfo_Register` |
| `classreg_slots.cpp` (by hand) | 24 | functions the map counted as getters because they begin with a registration: 10 static initializers that register an extra-list entry (`FieldDesc_RegisterExtra` `0x4190e0`), 3 that make an object field descriptor (`"Palette"`, `"Hue Remap"`, `"SubAI"`), 2 that set a descriptor's class (+0x2c) after registering two classes (eax the descriptor or the class, by the exit taken); the action wrappers' slot 1 (Describe: `"OtherMap %s action"` `0x41f880`, `"This Map %s action"` `0x41fa50`, `"Single %s action"` `0x4b8300`, and `0x4c80f0`); `CLevelOfDifficulty`'s list slot 2 `0x4fe160`; the water warp effect's file callback `0x598280`; `CZaxApp`'s slots 99, 100, 102 (`0x59fca0`, `0x59fd80`, `0x59fe70`: values of the custom rules' display object, made on first use) |

How the generator works [confirmed: code]: a stub is matched byte for byte. A getter's code is run symbolically along the path "variable 0, allocation not null" (pushes, global loads, calls); every `ClassInfo_Register` call closes the block of the last open `operator_new_ecx`, giving {variable, name, version, parent, size, abstract, create, create array, register fields}; the branches are checked (each block's `jne` and `je` must go past its `ClassInfo_Register` call), and the rest of the code may only return `[variable]`. Every copy of a class variable's block must have the same parameters (they do: 120 variables, no conflict). What does not fit is listed as manual; the blocks inside those are harvested by a lenient linear run so the hand-written code uses the same per-variable functions. The order of the calls is the exe's: the class info is allocated before the parent's getter runs, and a failed allocation skips the parent (`class_reg`, `classreg_common.h`).

Findings [confirmed: code]:
- The map's names of these getters came from the first block and were wrong for 37 of 129: 13 getters named after an inlined parent (of the nine "CMultipleActionsAction_ClassInfo", `0x4b8880` is `CMultipleDelayedActionsAction`'s getter with `CMultipleActionsAction`'s inlined, `0x4b9520` `CShuffledSeriesAction`'s with `CSeriesAction` and `CMultipleActionsAction`), and the 24 hand-written ones, which are not getters. The stubs are now named after the class their getter registers (`StaticRegister_<class>`; 55 of 487 names changed, three of them were duplicates).
- The 24 hand-written ones are not getters: static initializers reached through the initializer table or `CallMember` `0x55d050`, wrapper and list slots, a static list callback; their roles are in their `docs/exe_symbols.csv` rows (the name of `0x4c80f0`'s wrapper is an assumption: ours).
- `0x4f96f0`/`0x560660` return the descriptor when their third registration ran and the class otherwise; `0x4fe160` and `0x598280` return `al` with the upper bytes of the previous call; `0x59fe70` returns the last dword it copied, `0x59fd80` a float on the FPU stack. `CZaxApp`'s slots dereference the rules (+0x1c) even when the world's rules are not `CZaxCustomRules` (null), and call slot 19 on a failed allocation; the reimplementation does the same.
- No function of C1 is too short to hook or a shared tail: all stubs are 16 bytes, all others at least 77, and the generator found no jump in any first five bytes.

Check in the VM (`checks_classreg_*.cpp`, on the toolkit's harness `checks_ui_common.h`, with `checks_classreg_common.h`): the registrations run before the check thread (and through the hooks: `DllMain` installs them before the C runtime runs the initializer table, so a game start runs every reimplemented stub, getter and static initializer for real), so the checks call them again with every callee a recording stand-in and the class variables and other globals saved, set per case and put back: `ClassInfo_StaticRegister` (object and getter compared), `operator_new_ecx` (0, 1, a random value or a block), `ClassInfo_Register` (writes its object into the case's variable as the real one does and logs all nine arguments), the parents' getters, the class registry, `RegisterExtra`, `ObjectField_Ctor` (all nine arguments), `IsKindOf`, the class names, the ZString functions, the constructors and slot 19 of the display object; the real `Path_Join`/`PathName` on the function's buffer. Fakes: actions, wrappers and lists are "game object" windows with recording vtables, records, descriptors and the application, world, rules and display object blocks of the extra area. The class variables are 0 in two of three cases (the registration path), else a value; the getters' nested variables independently. Cases with all cases: stubs 974 (2 each), getters 1,260 (12 each), the hand-written ones 434. A first run (`20261028-095652-7029`) ran 0 cases of the stub modules: their test tables used an `extern` stub array and so needed a dynamic initialiser, which the DLL (no C runtime) never runs; the stub array is `constexpr` in the header now and every table `constinit`. A deliberately wrong build (a stub's object +1, `CDeactivateAction`'s size 0xd, `0x41f880`'s format string) differed in exactly those three tests (run `20261028-100546-563e`: 2 of 244, 6 of 1,260 and 8 of 434 cases).

Runs (final build, all on VM-02): our six modules with all cases on `Test/Nachbau1` `20261028-100727-1742` and on `ACT 2/M9/09 Assimilate Cave1` (Respawn2, `--no-level`) `20261028-101155-0f5a`: all 2,668 cases the same, 0.8 s and 1.6 s of checks (`classreg_getters` 1.1 s, the slowest); full run with `CheckScale=0.1` on `Test/Nachbau1` `20261028-100730-c488`: all 1,049 checks the same, 9,293 of 9,295 hooks installed (the two `DebugLog_*` as before; no "Too many hooks"), the game started on the reimplemented registrations, 158 s of checks (the cleanup could not remove the DLL: the known helper artefact); `--shot-set` `20261028-100736-84c0` … `-100738-0470`: all 9 scenes identical or different only in animated areas. A first Cave1 job (`20261028-100733-61f6`) did not start (the DLL of the previous job was still locked), and one module run (`20261028-100543-dcd4`) was cancelled from the Mac 4 s after its start, not by this batch.

### Batch C2: the static initializers, the atexit destructors and the function pointers in .data [verified 2026-10-28, VM; every callee through recording stand-ins, the start order through a logged start against /Original]

Batch C2 of the proposal above: the 1,443 rows of `docs/exe_symbols.csv` of the kinds "static initializer", "atexit destructor" and "function pointer in .data". **1,375 are reimplemented** in seven modules, **55 are a single `ret`** (not hookable, identical by their byte) and **13 are no static initializers** (below). All 1,375 hooks are installed at the start, so every reimplemented initializer runs in the C runtime's `_initterm` loop over `0x609000`–`0x60a3ec` instead of the original, and every exit stub runs from `atexit`'s table at the end.

| Module | Functions | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `static_c2a.cpp` | 139 | `0x400000`–`0x42ffff` |
| `static_c2b.cpp` | 234 (2 by hand) | `0x430000`–`0x4affff` |
| `static_c2c.cpp` | 63 (1) | `0x4b0000`–`0x4cffff` |
| `static_c2d.cpp` | 362 (7) | `0x4d0000`–`0x51ffff` |
| `static_c2e.cpp` | 160 (5) | `0x520000`–`0x56ffff` |
| `static_c2f.cpp` | 417 (3) | `0x570000`–`0x5fffff` |
| `static_c2_manual.cpp` | the 18 by hand | (their hooks and checks in the module of their range) |

**How they are made** [confirmed: `tools/static_init_gen.py`, the code]: the tool reads the C2 rows, disassembles each function over the size the map gave it and translates it symbolically: registers hold constants or C++ expressions; `push` builds the arguments of the next call; the convention of each call comes from the call site (ecx set since the last call: thiscall; the callee's own `ret n`: the arguments it pops; a `ret` callee with the caller's `pop ecx`/`add esp` right after the call: cdecl with that many arguments, also when ecx happens to be set — `0x4f8bf0` loads a vtable into ecx before `atexit`; a `ret` callee without cleanup takes none, the pushes before it belong to the next call, as in `0x42b140`); a call through a constant slot of a vtable in `.rdata` (`0x59a370`) stays an indirect call through that slot; every memory operand with a constant address becomes a load or store of that global at the point where the original has it; a conditional forward jump becomes `if`/`else` with both paths translated to their own `ret`; eax is returned where the function's own code defines it (a call's result, a constant, a byte in al). Anything else (a backward jump, string instructions, a virtual call on an object reached through a global) makes the function manual: 18 are written by hand in `static_c2_manual.cpp` (the tool's `MANUAL` table names them and gives their check setups), the tool generates their hook entries and checks. The generated files say so in their first line; run the tool again after changing it (`.venv/bin/python -I tools/static_init_gen.py`, `--list` for one line per function).

What the functions are [confirmed: code]:
- **Initializers** (626 from the initializer table, 65 more pointers of that table the map called "function pointers in .data"): the `LocalString`s of the user interface and the game's texts (`LocalString_Ctor` `0x501030`, 351), `ZString`s with a text (`0x4dee00`, 68), the action wrappers, enum tables, block readers, record lists, palettes, sequence and texture lists, frames and frame filters, the static fields of the classes (`operator new`, then the field's constructor, the pointer stored or 0 when new fails, `0x42b100`–), `FieldDesc_RegisterExtra` with a class getter (`0x42b140`), the class getters stored into tables (`0x551560`, 18 quest statistics), each followed by `atexit` of its exit stub where the object has a destructor; vtables, counters and flags written inline.
- **Exit stubs** (684): 517 are `mov ecx, object; jmp destructor` (10 bytes; `ZString_Dtor` 461 times), 128 put the class's base vtable back (`mov [object], vtable; ret`, the destructor inlined to nothing), the rest free a pointer (`0x46d6e0`, `0x470850`–), release a shared string buffer by its count (`0x4dea80`–`0x4dec00`), free a pointer array through the pool (`0x4e7b20`), or run an inlined destructor (the manual ones).
- **The 18 by hand**: the six texture lists (`0x4b4020`, `0x4d5360`, `0x4d5460`, `0x4ef1f0`, `0x4ef320`, `0x56bfb0`: the inlined destructor of a texture list global, entries of 0x80 bytes deleted through slot 1 from the last, the guard bits 1 and 2 of `0x6c0538` for the two of `0x4d5360`/`0x4d5460`), the pointer arrays `0x487550` (elements deleted through slot 6 and closed up with `memmove`), `0x525650` and `0x57cde0` (two arrays each, the second sized in bytes), the sound resource list `0x57dfa0`, the list of `0x713e20` `0x59a3c0`, the INI path and "Options" copies `0x46eb90`, the joystick object `0x4dd890`, the four frames `0x4ef3f0`/`0x4ef420`, 256 random generators `0x53f470`, ten polygon pairs `0x5470f0`, the 200 clears of `0x547200`. Layouts in the module's comment.
- eax: 131 functions leave the caller's eax on at least one path (stores only, or a path that sets nothing); their checks do not compare eax. 10 leave a byte in al (the guard exits: al is the bit, the rest of eax the caller's); their checks compare the low byte.

**Not hookable (55)**: initializers and exit stubs that are a single `ret` (50 exit stubs of objects without a destructor, 5 empty initializers of the table), e.g. `0x401270`, `0x40a670`, `0x4184b0`, `0x423950`, `0x42f280`; the full list is the `RETS` table of each `checks_static_c2*.cpp`. A `ret` is `void f() {}`; the checks read the byte in the running exe (all `0xc3`).

**Not static initializers (13)**: rows the map took for initializers that the initializer table does not contain: `0x402f80`, `0x4090d0`, `0x409cb0`, `0x41e460`, `0x4e2be0`, `0x517c60`, `0x525820`, `0x55dcd0`, `0x5c0610` are referenced from vtables in `.rdata` and use ecx as `this` (vtable slots, batches C3/C4), `0x42eb10`, `0x42ee30`, `0x42ef30`, `0x42f130` are pushed as callbacks by code (C3/C4). Their rows in `docs/exe_symbols.csv` are renamed (`VtableSlot_…`, `Callback_…`). The map's count of 649 initializers and 744 exit stubs was 626 + 13 and 734; with the 70 table pointers that is the 1,443 rows. Not in C2 but in the table: the class registrations and getters (C1), `StaticInit_DPlayGame` `0x47eb00` and `StaticInit_GdiFont` `0x4d20d0` (P5a), and the earlier batches' 67 reimplemented ones.

**Check** (`checks_static_c2*.cpp` on the harness `checks_static_c2.h`, built on the toolkit's): per function its callees as recording stand-ins of their convention and argument count (so no live object is constructed or destroyed again, and `atexit` never gets a second entry: an exit stub's destructor is recorded with its object, never run); the globals it reads or writes by address saved, set to case values (random, now and then the game's own), compared after each side and put back; a global the function dereferences points into the harness's block or is null; ranges it fills (the INI path copies, the 200 clears) filled with a pattern, hashed, put back; the hand-written ones get fake arrays, entries, list nodes and objects of the harness's recording "game object" class (their slot calls recorded); a function with `operator new` runs once with new giving a block and once with new failing. Only the tested function's own hook is put out for the original side. 3 cases per straight function, 8 per branching one. A deliberately wrong build (a text argument of `0x403870` off by one, `0x4b4020` writing 1 instead of 0 to +0x34) was found: `static_c2a` 3 of 440 and `static_c2c` 8 of 235 differ (run `20261028-100947-5962`).

**The start order** [confirmed: VM]: `log_start_order` (`checks_static_c2.cpp`, called by `check_class_table` in both modes) logs the C runtime's `atexit` table (`__onexitbegin` `0x71755c` … `__onexitend` `0x717558`), every entry in registration order. A start with the hooks (run `20261028-100716-df57`) and one with `/Original` (run `20261028-101623-c132`) on `Test/Nachbau1`: 725 entries each, the same set; the first 712 (every exit stub the initializer table registers, and the earliest lazy ones) in the same order; of the 13 registered later by function-local statics at their first use, `0x57cde0` (the exit of a function-local static of the sound code, registered from `0x57cb82`/`0x57cc70`/`0x57cf82`) stands at 712 with the hooks and at 724 with `/Original` — the hooked run logs the table later (in the game thread after the ESC, the `/Original` run in the check thread), not a different start.

**Runs** [verified: VM]: development `20261028-095725-311a` (the harness's fake objects made a `ZString` through the pool while the pool functions were stand-ins: exception; now the fakes take the recording vtable only), `-100233-ee9a` (`0x4f8bf0`'s `atexit` translated as thiscall because of the vtable in ecx: exception; fixed in the tool), `-100716-df57` (all six modules the same, 4,599 cases, 0.9 s on `Test/Nachbau1`); final build: CheckScale=0.1, all modules, `Test/Nachbau1` `20261028-101953-ba81`: all 1,049 checks the same, 10,052 of 10,054 hooks installed (the two `DebugLog_*` as before), `Zip CRC` and `All checks done` in the log, the start order's hash `8a6dfe10` the same as the `/Original` run's (725 entries; this run logged the table late enough that `0x57cde0` stood in the same place); the job's cleanup could not remove the DLL (the known helper artefact). Our modules with all cases on `ACT 2/M9/09 Assimilate Cave1` (Respawn2) `20261028-103139-677a`: 4,599 cases the same, 0.9 s (`static_c2d` and `static_c2f` 0.28 s each); the first attempt `20261028-101955-556c` failed in the helper's cleanup before the game started (it ran while the previous job's DLL was still locked). `--shot-set` `20261028-101958-96d2` … `-101959-e1c2`: all 9 scenes identical or different only in animated areas.

### Batch P5a-2: the rest of DirectPlay 8 and the Bink wrapper [verified 2026-10-28, VM; DirectPlay and binkw32 with fake COM objects and recording import stand-ins only]

Groups G3 and G4: **34 functions reimplemented** in two modules (list in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`), the two 4-byte getters left as not hookable. Every COM call goes through the same vtable slot and every Win32 or binkw32 call through the same import entry as in the original (the entry read when called), so the checks see the original's call sequence through stand-ins in the import table.

| Module | Functions | What [confirmed: code, the checks] |
|---|---|---|
| `dplay_rest5a.cpp` | 21 | the factory `0x47eb10` (renamed from `DPlayGame_Ctor`: thiscall on the game type with one unused argument, registered by `0x47eaf0` through `NetHandler_Set`, which the static initializer `0x47eb00` calls through `CallMember`), the message callback `0x47ead0`, and slots 1, 2, 3, 6–11, 14–16, 20–22, 24, 26, 27 of the net game's vtable `0x5f15a8`, named after what they do (`ResetPlayers`, `Host`, `Join`, `SetProvider`, `CreateAndSetProvider`, `SetProviderByName`, `EnumHosts`, `Close`, `IsAvailable`, `SendAndReset`, `Send`, `Frame`, `Kick`, `PlayerAddress`, `Ping`, `GameSpyBasic`, `GameSpyRules`, `GameSpyPlayers`) |
| `bink_rest5a.cpp` | 13 | `BinkSystem_Dtor`, `OpenMovie`, `CloseMovie`, `BinkMovie_Wait`, `DecodeToFrame`, `GetSummary`, `SetPause` and the six file callbacks Bink calls itself: `BinkIo_ReadHeader` `0x4323d0`, `ReadFrame` `0x432480`, `GetBufferSize` `0x432770`, `SetInfo` `0x4327e0`, `Close` `0x432870`, `Idle` `0x4328d0` (renamed from the map's provisional names) |

Not hookable (4 bytes, `mov al, [ecx + n]; ret`): slot 13 `0x47ecf0` `IsHosting` (+0x38) and slot 12 `0x4806e0` `IsRunning` (+0x39).

Findings [confirmed: code, the checks]:
- **Corrections of the map's G3 table**: `0x47eb10` is the factory, not a constructor (it allocates the object itself and returns it; `0x47eaf0`, filed as an `atexit` stub, is the registration body `CallMember` runs); slot 1 `0x47efd0` resets the players and slots (no queue); slot 10 releases the objects after the game type's slot 6; `0x47eb00` registers the factory rather than building a global object.
- **COM slots** (method names after the DirectPlay 8 headers [assumption: the code has only slot numbers]; numbers and arguments confirmed): server 8 SetServerInfo, 10 GetClientAddress, 11 GetLocalHostAddresses, 13 Host, 14 SendTo, 23 Close, 24 DestroyClient, 32 GetConnectionInfo; client 5 EnumHosts, 7 Connect, 8 Send, 11 SetClientInfo, 14 Close, 20 GetConnectionInfo; address 0 QueryInterface (IID `0x6061b0`, whose slot 6 is GetSockAddress), 4 BuildFromURLA, 10 GetURLA, 13 SetSP, 18 AddComponent. All calls are synchronous (`0x80000000`); the application GUID is `0x5f1598`, the port the dword `0x611408` (26784), the provider TCP/IP `0x606160`.
- **Host** `0x47f0b0` takes (player settings, settings), not (settings, player settings) as the map's slot table suggested; the application description is client/server with 16 players, the session name the settings' name, and the same name with its terminator as the reserved data. **Join** `0x47f5d0` (host name, host item, player settings) sets "hosting" (+0x38) too and clears "running"; a host name goes through a new address object: `BuildFromURLA` first, and only on `DPNERR_INVALIDURL` (`0x80158450`) TCP/IP, `L"hostname"` and `L"port"`; a failing `SetSP` of the global address leaks the temporary address (as does every error after it before `Connect`). Both convert the player name with `MultiByteToWideChar(…, -1, out, strlen)`, a buffer one character short, and terminate it themselves.
- `SetProviderByName` returns 1 when there is no provider list at all and leaks the list when the name is missing (after the error box "Could not find an "%s" service Provider"). `EnumHosts` passes the address of its own argument slot as the user context, so the message handler's host items go in front of the caller's list (or a local one); its result is the list head.
- `Close` empties the static part array `0x4e7b70` (the running level's) and calls slot 6 of the game type before releasing the three objects; the factory's 0x900-byte object is too short for the slot array's slot 100 (`+0x900`/`+0x904`), so a create-player message that takes slot 100 writes past it (the original's bug, kept; dplay.h).
- **Locking** kept as in the original: `g_DPlayLock` `0x6bdbf0` around every reset of the slots (the factory also clears +0x8fc once before taking it), the terminate lock `0x6bdad0` in `Frame` around the terminated check, the close and the game type's report; the players array is never locked; the callback takes no lock itself (the message handler does). The checks record Enter/LeaveCriticalSection of the three locks in the call log, so the order is compared.
- **Bink**: `DecodeToFrame` maps bits 16/24/32 to `BinkCopyToBuffer` flags 10/1/3 straight into the frame, decodes 8 bits as 24 bits into the scratch block (`+0x1c`, grown to pitch·height·3) and maps each pixel through the three 16-bit tables and the byte table `*0x633388`; other depths do nothing (eax bits − 8); its inner loop is a do/while (a pitch of 0 loops 2³² times). The record's frame counter wraps to 1 behind the handle's frame count (+8). `AddMovie`'s new records leave +0xc, +0x10 and +0x15–+0x17 as the heap had them (the checks compare only the fields it sets).
- **The file callbacks** are RAD's example `binkfile.c` adapted to the game's `FileBuf` (the BINKIO fields after the Bink 1 SDK header, [assumption: the exe has no names for them]; the game's data from +0x48: the FileBuf, file position, Bink's position, the ring buffer's read/write pointers, free space, start/end, the stream's base offset, the file size, the simulated rate and its time debt). The "stream flag" is a pair of counters: the foreground callbacks take +0x5c with `lock inc byte` and wait (`Sleep(1)`, `BinkService`) while the background counter +0x60 is not 0; `Idle` (Bink's background thread) takes both and works only when both dwords are exactly 1, otherwise returns −1 after `Sleep(1)`. Reimplemented with the same atomic byte increments; the rate's `n·1000/rate` uses the 64-bit product with a 32-bit quotient (`mul`/`div`, inline asm: no runtime division).

Check in the VM (in the game thread; `checks_dplay_rest5a.cpp`, `checks_bink_rest5a.cpp` on `checks_net_common.h`; side 0 with the module's hooks out):
- DirectPlay: fake server, client, address and IP-address objects (a recorder per slot used, logging the contents of the player info, the application description with the wide session name, the buffer descriptors, URLs, components and GUIDs; the client's `EnumHosts` calls the callback `0x47ead0` with host answers synchronously, as DirectPlay does); `CoCreateInstance`, `CoInitialize`, `CoUninitialize`, the four critical section functions and `Sleep` through import stand-ins that record only the check thread's calls on the DirectPlay locks (Enter/Leave passed on to the real functions) and pass every other call on, so the game's other threads are not disturbed; the error box, the GameSpy functions, the disconnect, GameRandom and the static part array's `DeleteAll` as recorders. Cases: the factory with messages through the callback and the object deleted by `0x47ef10` (120), random sequences of the session slots with every COM result (400), the frame, send, kick, address and ping (400), the GameSpy answers (90).
- Bink: the binkw32 imports, `RADTimerRead` and `Sleep` (check thread only) as recorders; the Bink system with fake handles and records, every op and depth (8-bit through a fake byte table put into `0x633388`) (400); the file callbacks on a BINKIO block over the real `Movies/JoWooD.bik` through `BinkIo_Open` and the real FileBuf, with the counters set before some calls so the wait loop and the busy path run (300).
- Development runs: `20261028-100107-a8ac` (the first: differences in the checks only — `Host`'s argument order (a real error, fixed), the heap bytes `AddMovie` and the factory leave unset, a host item's heap identity, the GameRandom letters not reset per side), `20261028-100435-d277`, `20261028-100853-d22e`.
- Final build, in the game thread: our two modules with all cases on `ACT 2/M9/09 Assimilate Cave1` (start point `Respawn2`, `--no-level`) `20261028-105258-b019` and `20261028-105301-6245`: all 6 checks the same (DirectPlay 1,010 cases, Bink 700; 1.2 s each module), 8711 of 8713 hooks installed (the two `DebugLog_*` as expected); all modules with `CheckScale=0.1` on `Test/Nachbau1` `20261028-105304-b67f`: all 1049 checks the same, `Zip CRC` and `All checks done` in the log, no "Too many hooks". Three more differences found on the way were again in the checks, all heap identities (a record block `AddMovie` frees and gets back, the provider list in `SetProviderByName`'s upper eax bytes; runs `20261028-101819-b71c`, `-103632-f558`, `-105055-fcc3`): such values are now compared by their offset in the block or by kind. `--shot-set` (`20261028-103143-54c0` … `-103144-118e`, VM-02): all 9 scenes identical or different only in animated areas.
- The movies: a start with `/Movies` and the reimplementation (`20261028-103137-900d`) plays the JoWooD, Reflexive and intro movies through the reimplemented wrapper and file callbacks into the level; the screenshots at 4, 8, 14 and 24 s show the same movies as the `/Original` start `20261028-101834-fd23` (other frames: the movies run on the clock), the level after them differs only in the Korbo region (1301–1497 × 659–873).

- After the merge of round 5a (main `8b84639`) `dplay rest: factory, static initializer, callback` differed in 101 of 120 cases on `Test/Nachbau1` (`20261028-111016-c72d`) and 104 on `Assimilate Cave1` (`-111012-7f5f`), in the factory object's slots. ### P5a-1: DirectDraw, the window, the message loop, the input, the clipboard and the start [verified 2026-10-28, VM; the windowed paths and the error exits with fakes only]

Groups G1 and G2 (26 hookable functions, all reimplemented; `Cursor::Shown` `0x518690`, 4 bytes, not hookable) in three modules: `reimpl/src/display_ddraw.cpp` (G1: `ScreenFrame_SetMode` `0x567f20`, `ScreenFrame_Release` `0x5678c0`, `ScreenFrame_Lock` `0x567bb0`, `ScreenFrame_Unlock` `0x567c90`, `ScreenFrame_Flip` `0x5693a0`, the `EnumDisplayModes` callback `0x567d60`, the comparator `0x568600`), `reimpl/src/app_window.cpp` (`App_WindowProc` `0x599d50`, `App_PumpMessages` `0x5998f0`, `App_SetWindowedSize` `0x477b60`, Windows' cursor `0x518820`/`0x518860`/`0x518880`, the clipboard `0x46d590`/`0x46d620`, the static GDI font `0x4d20d0`/`0x4d2140`, the wrappers `0x4d2460`/`0x4d24b0`/`0x4dd920`) and `reimpl/src/app_start.cpp` (`WinMain` `0x477940`, `Game_Startup` `0x4cd780`, `CZaxApp_Ctor` `0x59a670`, `CZaxApp_Dtor` `0x59aa10`, `CZaxApp_DeletingDtor` `0x59a9f0` (its relative call in the first bytes goes into the trampoline with `call_at`), `App_Start` `0x5a12d0`). Every Windows and DirectX call goes through the exe's import table (the import thunk `0x5caa82` for `DirectDrawCreate`) or the COM object's vtable with the original's arguments in the original's order; every exe function through its exe address. The three wrappers stay six-byte indirect jumps (`jmp [IAT]`, assembler), so no register changes.

Findings [confirmed: disassembly, the logged start]:
- **Full screen only**: `0x6210c0` (full screen) is 1 in `.data` and no instruction writes it (all nine references read it). The windowed branches of `ScreenFrame_SetMode` (desktop depth check, offscreen back buffer, clipper), `ScreenFrame_Flip` (GetClientRect/ClientToScreen/Blt) and `App_SetWindowedSize` never run in the retail game; they are reimplemented and checked with fakes only. The shot set can only run in full screen (the VMs: 800 × 600 × 16, 5-6-5, two back buffers in video memory).
- The DirectDraw palette `SetMode` creates is a grey ramp (entry i = i, i, i, `PC_RESERVED`), not black (the map's text said black; found by the check: the first reimplementation stored zeros).
- `ScreenFrame_Lock` and the full screen `Flip` use the primary surface and the back buffer without testing them; the release flips only when DirectDraw, the back buffer, the reporter and its screen exist.
- `App_WindowProc` also handles `WM_ACTIVATE` (6) like `WM_ACTIVATEAPP`, `WM_SIZE` like `WM_MOVE`, `WM_CLOSE` like `WM_DESTROY`, and `WM_QUIT` without `PostQuitMessage`; `WM_SYSKEYDOWN` of Alt, Space, the Windows and Apps keys and F10 answers 0. `App_PumpMessages`: a single click sets the button bit from `0x51f450`'s answer, the double click also bit 0/1/2 of `0x6cff5c`; the wheel adds `delta × 1/120` (`0x602db8`) to the float `0x6cff60`.
- `Game_Startup` calls `App_UpdateMusic` a second time when "TestSave.dat" could be written: the original reads that flag's stack byte again at `0x4cdb95`. Its "Screen Bit Depth" and `/ScreenBitDepth` answers are unused (`Display_Init` reads them itself). The launcher's `/ShowFPS` patches this function's `setne cl` at `0x4cdbf7` to `mov cl, 1`; the reimplementation reads those bytes and gives the same flag, so the launcher option keeps working with the hook installed.

The logged start (`reimpl/src/api_trace.cpp`, `[Reimpl] TraceApi=1`, also with `/Original`): in `DllMain`, before the hooks, 92 import table entries (all user32, gdi32, ddraw, the dsound create, winmm without `timeGetTime`, ole32, advapi32 and kernel32's files, folders, INI, modules, processes, global memory, mutex and `Sleep`) point to recorders that write the main thread's calls with their arguments (texts and rectangles by content, handles numbered by their first appearance, addresses left out) and answers into `Zax-Reimpl.log` from the C runtime's static initializers to WinMain's first `PeekMessageA`, then a snapshot of what the start built (the screen frame's fields and modes, DirectDraw's display mode, the primary and back buffer descriptions, the window's globals, the font). `zax-testtools/tools/api_trace_compare.py` compares two logs (`--mask-stack` hides pointers into the main thread's stack, whose frames differ). A crash while tracing logs its address and the trace so far (the first run found a bug of the trace itself: a text argument read through a float).

Checks (`checks_display_ddraw.cpp`, `checks_app_window.cpp`, `checks_app_start.cpp`, shared `checks_sys_common.h` on the toolkit harness `checks_ui_common.h`): every Windows import the functions call is a recording stand-in for the side (the game's other threads go to the real function), DirectDraw is a set of fake COM objects (IDirectDraw, three surfaces, clipper, palette: recorded calls, failing HRESULTs at random, `DDERR_SURFACELOST`, `EnumDisplayModes` calling the callback with the case's mode descriptions, `Lock` filling the description), the application, the resource cache and the frame are recording fakes, every other exe function a stand-in, `exit` leaves the side (`run_escapable`); compared are eax, the call log, the block of fakes and the globals. Cases: the mode set in both modes and at every depth with every `CreateSurface` fallback and every failing call, the early return and the desktop depth errors; lost surfaces and 100 failed Locks; the flip and the release; the callback on random descriptions; the comparator; the window procedure with every message it handles and others; the pump with random message queues in its three waiting modes; the window size; the cursor; the clipboard both ways with every failure; the wrappers; the font; WinMain up to the third round of its loop (with failing class, window and test file); the start-up (uninstaller start, CPU and memory, movies, music, the `/ShowFPS` patch); the application object's constructor and both destructors; the application start.

Findings [confirmed: code]:
- No function of the batch is too short to hook: the ones under 5 bytes (`0x401110`, `0x401160`, `0x401170`, `0x401180`, `0x4011d0`, `0x401200`, `0x401260`, `0x4a5970`, `0x592370`, the tail jumps `0x4ce3d0`, `0x5c0780`) and those with a branch in their first bytes (`0x40bba0`) all have alignment padding behind them that no jump reaches: they are hooked without a trampoline (length 0; the check's original side puts the bytes back).
- `0x40e791` ("code reference") is no function: the map read `f9 e9 …` from the middle of `mov edi, ecx` in the INI position slot `0x40e620`, whose real end is `0x40e8e3` (the map had 369 of its 707 bytes). - Kept quirks: the title drawing reads Transparent Mask's opacity twice and restores Black Bias with it (like the check box); the INI position passes the size flag's upper bytes to `SetTransparent`; placement 19 puts the window at the parent's width; the grid's wheel slot takes a second argument it ignores; the save/load layout keeps the old client widths of its pages in a 4-entry local that a fifth page would overrun; the end screen and the difficulty comparator read through null when a record is missing or loading.
- The check harness: a recorded slot answering "true" with random upper bytes (K_BOOL) never ends a loop that tests the full eax (the INI position's "move while another child is on this rectangle"): such slots answer K_VALUE (0 a third of the time); a fastcall stand-in's effect does not see ecx; stand-ins that construct an object on the caller's stack (FieldColor, the warp effect, the clip frame, CFrame) fill it in the effect so its contents compare; the grid's row slots 77/78 take arguments the toolkit's class table does not know, so the grid is a "game object" fake there.

RegisterFields call the getter inlined or through its address exactly as the exe does; `CMaterialsGeneratorDisplayOptions` builds the defaults of "List Select Color" and "Grid Line Color" in two FieldColors on its stack (`0x40, 0x50, 0x50` and `0xaf, 0x92, 0x36`).
- **The tile map** [confirmed: code]: 0x53ff90 draws the region's cells (counters `+0x2d2c`–`+0x2d34`; the countdown `+0x2cf8` empties the tile cache at 0); 0x540000 per cell takes the tile of layer 1 or 2 (by the marks `+8`, slot 54) from the tile cache (`0x540b80`: a new tile draws the ground `0x540840` and the layer's tiles `0x4e8b60`/`0x4e8ce0`), blits it from the static frame `0x711078` and, drawing all, adds the grid lines (`0x541090`, grid mode `+0x2cec`) and the marks' cross and rectangle; the ground of a cell whose four corners share a texture without a blend table is blitted from the texture directly (8 bits), otherwise built as a tile: `0x540d90` writes the four corner elevations into an 8-bit frame, seeds the random generator `0x6d0be8` from the plasma tables `0x6d1030` by the corners' seeds and fills the cell with `Plasma_Line`/`Plasma_Column`/`Plasma_Map`, then `0x541250` maps every band index to texture pixels (8 bits through the band's 64 KB blend table, 16 bits 5-6-5 by the band's weight (red and blue by weight >> 3, green by weight >> 2 halved; the red difference carries the upper half of the destination address into bits above the result, masked out), 24 bits per byte (weight / 256, truncated toward zero)); `0x541710` builds the 256 band entries from "Blending" (`+0x1068`): the position band · count · `0x5fce00`, its fraction, the weight (fraction − (1 − blending)) / blending, in 8 bits five ranges of the weight (`0x5fcdf8` (a double), `0x5eee10`, `0x5eee14`, `0x5eb2d0`, 1) choose the two textures and the blend table (`0x6767c0`/`0x6767d0`), above 1 the entry is left as it is; in 16/24 bits the weight · `0x5eb728` goes to `+0xc64`.
- **The mini map and the loading screen**: the mini map image is `Levels/<folder>/<name>.tga` of the level ("Loading Mini-Map" progress `0x536080`); a failed load or a wrong size rebuilds it (the layer drawn through `World::RenderLayer` with the callback `0x4ed2b0`, scaled into the image rectangle `0x4ec280`, saved as an 8-bit palette frame and a 24-bit TGA); a missing file ends the game ("Fatal Error loading Mini-Map image", `exit(-1)`). The loading tick only advances the animation's frame by one when the frame for the time differs from the current one (the computed frame itself is not shown).
- **`World_OpenMainMenu`** keeps the launcher's redirection: the reimplementation calls the constructor where the call at `0x59bace` points (`Zax-Launcher.dll` redirects it, docs/EXE_FINDINGS.md "Direct start").

Both loops are endless in the original for a NaN angle or a zero frame count with a non-negative frame; the game never has them, the check avoids them.

**The C runtime's exception helpers, `terminate`, the locale string functions and `abort`** (`checks_crt_seh.cpp`, module `crt_seh`):
- The exe is built without C++ exceptions (no `__CxxFrameHandler`, no `throw`): the cases are SEH frames. Side 0 runs the original with the hooks of `crt_seh` and `crt_thunks` out, side 1 the reimplementation. They must not be mixed: the original's `__local_unwind2` registers `0x5d222c` as its unwind handler and the original `_abnormal_termination` compares the top frame's handler with that address, the reimplementation both with its own label (a fake top frame therefore names the side's own handler).
- Real exceptions: two to four nested VC6 frames written in assembly (the try level at `[ebp-4]`, the scope table, the exception pointers at `[ebp-0x14]`, the saved `esp` at `[ebp-0x18]`), each with a random scope table of up to four entries (`__except` with a recording filter answering execute, continue search or, for `RaiseException`, continue execution; `__finally` with a recording block that calls `_abnormal_termination`), the innermost raising (`RaiseException` with four codes, or a read of address 0); the outermost frame's filter takes everything, so no exception leaves the check. Logged and compared: every filter call (frame, entry, code, flags, try level), every `__finally` and what `_abnormal_termination` says, the `__except` block reached with its try level, the normal ends, the debugger block of `__NLG_Notify` (`0x6297b0`), `fs:[0]` afterwards: 1,500 cases.
- Fake frames, called directly: `__local_unwind2` to random stop levels, `_except_handler3`'s search pass (filters answering continue search or continue execution only: "execute" would unwind a frame that is not on the chain) and its unwind pass (flags 2, 4, 6, 3), `__unwind_handler`, `_abnormal_termination` under a fake top frame, `__NLG_Notify`/`__NLG_Notify1` with set registers, `_seh_longjmp_unwind`, `__CallSettingFrame@12` with a recording funclet, and `crt_thunks`' virtual call thunk `0x4020c0` into a recording slot: 4,000 cases.
- `terminate` through its trampoline with a recording terminate handler in the per-thread data (`+0x60`: none, returning, raising — caught by `terminate`'s own `__except` — and faulting) and `abort` replaced by an escape back into the check (a jump at `0x5dd087` to code that restores `esp` and `fs:[0]`); the target `__NLG_Notify` records is the side's own `__except` block and is compared as "inside terminate". `abort` itself (`crt_startup`) the same way with `_exit` `0x5d0e47` replaced, the message box of `_NMSG_WRITE` a recorder (the cached `MessageBoxA` pointer of `__crtMessageBoxA`, as in `checks_crt_impl.cpp`) and the global `SIGABRT` action (`0x715c34`) a recording handler or `SIG_IGN`: so `abort` is checked after all (it is still never called by the game). `__crtLCMapStringA`, `__crtGetStringTypeA`, `__crtCompareStringA` through their trampolines on random texts (high bytes, embedded lengths, `-1`), five locales, five code pages, flags and buffer sizes, each case from the same "which API" state for both sides (`0x715984`, `0x715bac`, `0x715c5c`: unknown, wide, ANSI): 3,006 cases.
- Sanity: deliberate faults in a scratch build were found (two in `p5_leftovers.cpp` and two in `crt_seh.cpp` each: 51–206 of 300–600 cases differing per function; a `__local_unwind2` that does not update the try level loops for ever, so that mutation hung its job `20261028-195257-dcb2`, cancelled).

**The exit observed**: the logged start (`TraceApi=1`, `api_trace.cpp`) now records the exit too: after the start's trace it waits for the main thread's `PostQuitMessage` and records from there until `ExitProcess` ("API trace exit" … "API trace exit end", flushed before `ExitProcess`), with `HeapFree`, `FlushFileBuffers`, `GetCurrentProcess`, `TerminateProcess`, `VirtualFree` and `ExitProcess` recorded in the exit only (the start's trace is unchanged). The game quits through its menu: in game Esc, "End Game" (key N) to the main menu, EXIT (key X; the helper's mouse click on EXIT only took the sign away in two runs, the game kept running for 13 and 60 s, the project owner: in the original a click on EXIT ends the game). `EXIT` posts `WM_CLOSE` (`Platform_CloseWindow` `0x4d2470`), the window procedure calls `PostQuitMessage`, unloads the resource cache, deletes the application and calls `exit(0)`: `doexit`, the atexit table (728 entries), `_fcloseall`, `__endstdio`, `ExitProcess(0)`. Runs `/Original` `20261028-202022-0898` and hooked `20261028-202118-1bb9` (`Test/Nachbau1`): 30,585 lines each, about 15,400 of them the exit (`PostQuitMessage`, 15,387 `HeapFree`, `timeKillEvent`, `CoUninitialize`, `DeleteObject`, the critical sections, `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`, `ExitProcess(0)`); `zax-testtools/tools/api_trace_compare.py --mask-stack`: 11 differing blocks, all the known device context/region handles of `WM_ERASEBKGND` (0x14) and message `0xaf` passed to `DefWindowProcA`. Do not send `Alt+F4` (or other keys) after the game has quit: the foreground window is then the helper's console, and `Alt+F4` closed it (job `20261028-201640-9e90`; the project owner restarted the helper on `VM-01`, `--restore` `20261028-201937-dcf3` put the game folder back).

**A check artefact of batch C4 fixed** (`checks_c4_fields.cpp`, shared file): with this branch's DLL `c4 fields: binary slots of the plain kinds (real data)` differed in 111 of 229 cases (`20261028-202410-4f80`, also with this batch's four hooks disabled `20261028-202903-f58e`, `-202906-f68a`; `main`'s DLL the same `20261028-203024-5e65`): a read slot returns `al = 1` over the upper bytes of a pointer into the side's file buffer, and `rel_file` only recognised that while the buffer's own low byte was at most 1, i.e. depending on where the linker put `g_file`. It now compares such a value relative to the buffer as well; all cases the same afterwards (`20261028-203139-2613`).

**Hooked through the padding: 131 functions** (`reimpl/src/short_hooks.cpp`, generated by `tools/short_hooks_gen.py` with the machinery of `tools/crt_asm_gen.py`). The batches had left every game function shorter than 5 bytes or with a relative branch in its first 5 bytes as "not hookable, identical by bytes" (C2's 55 single `ret`s, C5's 63, C4's 11, P5a's three, the getters of phases 1–4). The audit found alignment padding (`nop`/`int3`) behind all of them up to the next function, and no branch target, pointer or function start in their bytes 1–4 (a scan of every instruction of `docs/functions.csv` for branch targets, immediates and displacements into `.text`, and of every dword of `.rdata`/`.data`), so the hook's jump fits without a trampoline (length 0, as batch C3 did for the toolkit's stubs). Their reimplementation is the same instructions (getters `mov eax, [ecx + n]`, the byte getters that keep the upper bytes of eax, the float getters in st0, `ret n` stubs, the jump thunks with their `ecx` adjustment, `Compass_SetTarget`, the tile cache handle's free, lock and unlock); a jump or call out goes through a pointer to the exe's entry, so a thunk to another of them (`0x4f7ef0` → `0x51f450`, `0x5b4020` → `0x482de0`) enters its hook as in the original. The generator assembles every function and compares each instruction with the original's bytes (231 instructions, all identical apart from the 24 branches made labels or pointers). Left out on purpose: the four open functions, `0x488f18`, the C runtime's funclets and helpers (their callers are reimplemented, they never run) and `_matherr` (no room).

**The gaps** (code between the known functions) [confirmed: `tools/audit.py`; corrected in batch 6-0, below and section 13]: a recursive descent from every start of both tables (branches; jump tables `jmp [reg*4 + table]` and the byte index tables before them; every pointer of `.rdata`/`.data` into `.text`, which reaches the SEH scope tables' filters and handlers), with the declared sizes, the generated assembler modules' ranges and the alignment filler (`nop`, `int3`, `mov edi, edi`, `lea ecx, [ecx]`, `lea esp, [esp]`) as covered. **The game code `0x401000`–`0x5c3bf0` has no gap**: all of it is reached from the tables' functions (the map heuristics missed no function there; what the plain byte scan showed as uncovered, 18 jump tables, 5.3 KB of byte index tables and the tails behind them, belongs to the functions before them). Outside it, ten ranges:

| `0x5ca9e0`–`0x5caa52` | 114 | the import thunks of wsock32 and kernel32 that only the GameSpy SDK calls: GameSpy batch |
| `0x5caa58`–`0x5caa8e` | 56 | the linker's import thunks of msacm32, ddraw and dsound the game code calls (9 × `jmp [IAT]`): identical by bytes (phase 6 gets them from its own linker) |
| `0x5d0748`, `0x5d84c8` | 63 each | the unrolled tails of `memmove` and `memcpy` past the sizes the table gives (reimplemented with them) |
| `0x5d9650`–`0x5d9857` | 519 | `exp` of the x87 library: its code and its dispatch table `0x62c27b` ("exp") refer only to each other: dead |
| `0x5d9c60`–`0x5da466`, `0x5da71e`–`0x5da9eb` | 2,054, 717 | the runtime's Pentium FDIV workaround (`_adj_fdiv_*`, the rest behind `_adj_fprem`; tables `0x62c2a0`–`0x62c400`), reached only from itself and from `exp`: dead |
| `0x5e9c70`–`0x5ea000` | 912 | zero fill at the end of `.text` |

**The check module `not_hookable`** (`checks_not_hookable.cpp`; it replaces C5's `checks_c5_bytes.cpp` and C2's single-`ret` checks, whose functions `short_hooks` covers now): (1) the 38 ranges of `docs/not_reimplemented.csv` that stay the exe's code (identical by bytes, covered by caller, no function, dead code; 9,896 bytes) against the hash of the bytes `tools/audit.py` recorded from Zax.exe, read in the running exe; (2) every hook of the hook tables installed — its site is the jump to its replacement, with or without a trampoline — except the launcher's two `DebugLog_*`; (3) the hook tables against `docs/reimpl.csv`: every row a hook, every hook a row, no address twice. `reimpl/build.sh` makes its tables from the two CSVs at every build, so a merge that adds rows and hooks needs no regeneration; a new function hooked without its `docs/reimpl.csv` row (or the other way round) now fails this check. **The check module `short_hooks`** (`checks_short_hooks.cpp`): each of the 131 functions runs twice from the same registers, eight stack arguments, object memory (a 4 KB arena this points into: random dwords, or pointers into the arena for the tile cache handles, a fake vtable for `Compass_SetTarget`) and globals, once with its site put back to the original bytes and once through the hook; compared are all seven registers after the return, the bytes popped, the arena, the global, the FPU stack (depth and st0) and the call or jump out of it (the target a recording stand-in that pops what the real function pops; calls from other threads go on to the target's hook). 24 cases per function.

## 11. Libraries and copy protection (analysed 2026-10-25)

The 827 functions of `docs/functions.csv` outside the game code (about 193 KB) belong to five statically linked libraries and the copy protection. The port replaces them; this section names them, gives their versions and documents what the game expects from them. Names with evidence are in `docs/exe_symbols.csv` (source column starting with the library); `tools/function_table.py` has the corrected `RANGES`. "confirmed" there means matched against the library's source (strings, constants, tables, the call graph of the source file) or byte-identical to an already named function; "assumption" means placed by its position in the object file and its callers only (mostly small static helpers). Static analysis only (REA/Ghidra, own Python scans in the scratchpad); nothing of the protection was run or unpacked.

| Library | Range (`RANGES`) | Version | Functions named (confirmed / assumption) |
|---|---|---|---|
| vorbisfile | `0x5c3bf0`–`0x5c5280` | 1.0 beta 4 (vorbisfile.c 1.41, 2001-02-26) | 23 / 0 |
| GameSpy SDK | `0x5c5280`–`0x5caa90` (wsock32 thunks `0x5ca9e0`–`0x5caa8e` at the end) | 2001 SDK: CD key, query and reporting, server browsing ("CEngine"), MD5; no version string | 22 / 38 |
| zlib | `0x5caa90`–`0x5d0320` | 1.1.3 | 39 / 17 |
| C runtime | `0x5d0320`–`0x5de2f0`, `0x5e96f0`–`0x5e98b0`, `0x402090`–`0x4020d0` | Microsoft Visual C++ 6.0, static multithreaded (LIBCMT) | 250 / 43 (+16 named before) |
| libogg + libvorbis | `0x5de2f0`–`0x5e96f0`, `0x5e98b0`–`0x5ea000` | libvorbis 1.0 beta 4 (2001-02), libogg of the same release | 86 / 72 |
| Copy protection | `0x718000`–`0x759000` (`.cms_t`, `.cms_d`) | SecuROM (Sony DADC), version 4 era; only the loader is left | 142 / 11 |

In `docs/functions.csv` 698 of the 827 are named now (all of zlib and Ogg Vorbis, the GameSpy SDK except 8 small server-list helpers; 276 of 340 runtime functions: what is left are the x87 math error helpers `0x5d5160`–`0x5d5c9f`, `0x5d9857`–`0x5da66c`, `0x5dc4c5`, the 12-byte long double helpers `0x5db6e7`–`0x5db854`, `0x5dd09e`–`0x5dd45f` and the 9-byte SEH unlock funclets; 141 of 198 protection functions: the rest are runtime functions of the loader that differ from the game's copy by more than addresses). Ghidra missed 22 library functions that only tables or jumps reach (`deflate_fast` and `deflate_slow` from zlib's configuration table, `mapping0_look`/`pack`/`unpack`, `res0_pack`/`unpack`/`look`, `floor0_unpack` from the Vorbis export bundles, `lsp.c`'s qsort comparator, `_purecall`, `_alldiv` …); they are named but are not rows of `docs/functions.csv` until the next `tools/ghidra.sh` (added by the later runs: `deflate_fast`, `_purecall`, `mapping0_look`, `floor0_unpack` are rows now).

**Range corrections** [confirmed]: the runtime runs up to `_fileno` `0x5de2e0`, not `0x5de000` (`0x5de000`–`0x5de2e8` was counted as Ogg Vorbis: `__crtsetenv`, `findenv` …); libogg's `framing.c` starts at `0x5de2f0`; zlib's `inflate_fast` ends at `0x5d0312`, so the runtime starts with `operator delete` `0x5d0320`; and the "runtime" range `0x5e96f0`–`0x5ea000` is the `RtlUnwind` thunk, `_allshr`, `memchr` and `acos` only up to `0x5e98b0`, after that libogg's `bitwise.c` (`oggpack_*`, linked after the runtime objects).

**Compiler options of the libraries** [confirmed: code]: libogg, libvorbis and vorbisfile were compiled with `__fastcall` as the default convention (`/Gr`: first two arguments in ecx/edx; `vorbis_block_init` takes `v` in ecx and `vb` in edx, `oggpack_readinit` ends with `ret 4`), and so were zlib (`compress2` gets dest/destLen in ecx/edx, `zcfree` pushes edx) and the `ov_callbacks` of the game (`0x525380` ends with `ret 8`). The GameSpy SDK is cdecl. The linker folded identical functions across libraries (`/OPT:ICF`): vorbisfile's `host_is_big_endian` is the game's `0x46b760` (`xor eax, eax; ret`), libvorbis' empty `_analysis_output` `0x5e44e0` is also a game vtable slot (`0x5fc1f8`), zlib's empty `tr_static_init` is time0's `0x5e6450`, and time0's `return ""` uses the game's empty text `0x62e558`. Unused functions are not linked (`/OPT:REF`): no `ov_open`, `ov_bitrate`, `ogg_stream_packetin`, `deflateParams` …

### zlib 1.1.3

- **Version** [confirmed]: the copyright strings `deflate 1.1.3 Copyright 1995-1998 Jean-loup Gailly` and `inflate 1.1.3 Copyright 1995-1998 Mark Adler`, the version `"1.1.3"` that `deflateInit2_`/`inflateInit2_` compare, the error texts of 1.1.3's `infblock.c`/`inftrees.c`/`infcodes.c` (the old inflate before 1.2), the configuration table `0x606218` (levels 0–9: stored, fast ×3, slow ×6 with the 1.1.3 good/lazy/nice/chain values).
- **What the game calls** [confirmed: all callers]: only `compress2` and `uncompress`. `Pack` (`0x5c3b40`) allocates `n · 101 / 100 + 12` bytes and calls `compress2(dest, &destLen, src, n, -1)` (level −1 = `Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION` = 6; window bits 15, memory level 8, zlib header with adler32, as `compress2` always does); it accepts the results 0–2 and returns the packed size, else 0. `Unpack` (`0x5c3ba0`) allocates the known unpacked size and calls `uncompress`. Callers: the temp file field kind (`TempFileField_FromText` `0x58b8f0` and `_ReadBinary` `0x58bf20`: the blocks stored as dword `0x3e9`, packed size, size, data) and two `CZaxApp` methods around `0x59acec`/`0x59b0d2` ("QuestMode") and `0x59e45a`/`0x59e64a` that Ghidra did not find as functions: the save game written (`0x59ab00`, slot 111) and read (`0x59add0`, slot 74) and a layer saved to a file (`0x59e520`, slot 75) and read from a stream (`0x59e3e0`, slot 76) [confirmed: code, reimpl/src/c4_app2.cpp; VM] (until 2026-10-29: "[assumption: save game data]" for all four — the second pair packs and unpacks layer files).
- **Not used for the archives** [confirmed]: `inflate` is reached only through `uncompress`; the zip code (`0x5c0000`–`0x5c3b20`) reads stored entries only. `Data.dat` and `GERMAN.RED` are uncompressed zips (FORMATS.md 1). Section 1 said "zlib for Data.dat"; that is corrected there.
- **For the port**: any zlib (or miniz) with `compress2`/`uncompress` semantics. The byte stream of `deflate` changed after 1.1.3 for the same input; the game only inflates what it deflated itself, and inflate accepts every version's output, so byte-identical packing is not needed — except where packed bytes are compared or hashed (none found) [assumption: only the callers above searched; since phase 5b the game packs with the source-built zlib 1.1.3 anyway].

### Ogg Vorbis (vorbisfile, libvorbis 1.0 beta 4, libogg)

- **Version** [confirmed against the sources, git tags `v1.0.0beta3`, `v1.0.0beta4`, `v1.0.0rc1` of xiph/vorbis, read 2026-10-25]: the registries have exactly one floor (floor0, export bundle `0x62e3f8`), one residue (residue0, `0x62e3d8`), one mapping (`0x62e378`) and one time backend (`0x62e430`) — as `registry.c` 1.6 of 1.0 beta 4; 1.0rc1 (June 2001) added floor1 and residues 1/2. `mapping0_forward` passes `"pcm"`, `"windowed"`, `"fft"`, `"mdct"`, `"lfft"`, `"lmdct"`, `"prefloor"`, `"floor"` to `_analysis_output` — the list of `mapping0.c` 1.27 (2001-02-26) of beta 4; beta 3 (1.18, 2000-11) has `"decay"`, `"mdct"`, `"lmdct"`, … instead. The decoder-only build has no vendor string (`vorbis_commentheader_out` is not linked). libogg [the release shipped with beta 4: confirmed later, phase 5b below: all libogg functions of the exe match libogg 1.0beta4's source, `0x5de610` is beta 4's static `_os_checksum`; VM]: the CRC table is built at runtime (`_ogg_crc_entry` with 0x04c11db7, table `0x715c60`), `ogg_sync_pageseek` and `ogg_stream_pagein`/`packetout` only. The encoder parts (psy, envelope, lpc/lsp, residue/floor forward, `vorbis_book_init_encode`) are linked only because the export bundles point to them; they never run.
- **Decoder consequence** [confirmed: source of beta 4 + rc1 change log]: the Vorbis I bitstream was frozen only with 1.0rc1/rc2; beta 4 streams can use the early floor0-only setup. Current libvorbis decodes the game's streams [verified 2026-11-01: all 1,507 `.ogg` of `DATA.dat` and `GERMAN.RED` with libvorbis 1.3.7: no decode error, the same sample counts as beta 4, the PCM within ±1; section 13, "Batch analyses 2026-11-01", 3; stb_vorbis not tested].
- **What the game calls** [confirmed: code `0x525380`–`0x525ba0`, `0x5255a8`]: a stream object (sound subsystem) with the `OggVorbis_File` pointer at +0x18:
  - `OggStream_Open` `0x525aa0` (thiscall, `CFileBuf *`): `ov_open_callbacks(this, vf, NULL, 0, g_OggCallbacks)`; `g_OggCallbacks` `0x6d0150` = {read `0x525380` (`FileBuf_Read`), seek `0x5253a0`, close `0x525400` (slot 1 of the stream), tell `0x57d310` (`FileBuf_Seek`)}, filled on first use. Then `ov_info(vf, -1)` and `ov_pcm_total(vf, -1)`: total bytes = samples · channels · 2; a `WAVEFORMATEX` at +4 (PCM, channels and rate of the stream, 16 bits, block align = channels · 2).
  - `OggStream_Read` `0x5259b0` (buffer, bytes): `ov_read(vf, buf + done, bytes - done, 0 (little endian), 2 (16 bit), 1 (signed), &bitstream)` until the buffer is full or `ov_read` returns 0; `OV_HOLE` (−3) and `OV_EBADLINK` (−137) are skipped and read again; the largest single return is kept in `0x6d0160`; a reentry flag at +0x1d.
  - `OggStream_Tell` `0x525a30`: `__ftol(ov_time_tell(vf) · avg bytes per second)`; `OggStream_Seek` `0x525a60` (byte offset): `ov_time_seek(vf, offset / (double)avg bytes per second)` — positions go through seconds as doubles, not through `ov_pcm_seek`.
  - `OggStream_Close` `0x525ba0`: `ov_clear`.
  The music folders are streamed with "Use Threaded Stream" (Zax.CFG) [confirmed: code `0x587060` (it reads the key; its callers `0x4e1fe0`, the music mixer `0x51dfc4`/`0x51e085`/`0x51e3c3`, the voice-over player `0x595b7d`), `0x587310` opens a file through the reader factory `0x57ca10`, which gives .ogg the Ogg Vorbis reader; reimpl/src/sound_stream.cpp, music.cpp, sound_reader.cpp; VM]; the voice-overs too.
- **For the port**: libvorbis/vorbisfile or stb_vorbis with the same interface (16-bit signed little-endian interleaved PCM, total samples, seeking by time). `ov_read`'s float to int conversion in beta 4 is `vorbis_ftoi` with the FPU rounding (round to nearest) and clamping to ±32767/−32768; current libvorbis does the same, so the PCM should agree to the last bit only if the decoder's float path agrees, which it does not have to (sound only, no game state depends on it) [verified for the source-built beta 4: 177 of 697,696 samples differ by one, phase 5b below; current libvorbis 1.3.7 against a native build of beta 4 with the game's rounding: 0.099 % of the samples differ by one, none by more, the lengths are the same, 2026-11-01, section 13, "Batch analyses 2026-11-01", 3].

### zlib and Ogg Vorbis built from their original sources (phase 5b) [verified 2026-10-28, VM]

All 237 library functions of the exe — zlib 1.1.3 (56) and libogg, libvorbis and vorbisfile 1.0 beta 4 (181) — are hooked with the same functions built from the original releases (`reimpl/third_party/`: sources, archives, checksums and licences in its `README.md`), and checked against the exe's copies in the running game (`reimpl/src/checks_zlib.cpp`, `checks_vorbis.cpp`, module names `zlib` and `vorbis`). The game's packing (`Pack`/`Unpack`) and its music, voice-overs and quips run on the source-built libraries.

- **Sources** [confirmed: checksums]: `zlib-1.1.3.tar.gz` from zlib.net/fossils (SHA-256 `cae5847b…fbb906f4`; every file identical to the tag `v1.1.3` of madler/zlib), `libogg-1.0beta4.tar.gz` (`c8a4157b…6c842b2a9`) and `libvorbis-1.0beta4.tar.gz` (`732c254d…df38202`) from downloads.xiph.org, both as in Xiph's `SHA256SUMS`. 72 files copied unchanged (`cmp` against the archives); no script or build file of the archives was run. Licences: zlib's (in `zlib-1.1.3/README`), Xiph's BSD licence (`COPYING`); a binary distribution of the DLL must carry the BSD notice.
- **Build** (`reimpl/build.sh`, `reimpl/src/libs/`, `reimpl/src/libc/`): one wrapper per source file includes it as it is and exports the addresses of the functions the exe has (static ones too) for the hook tables `zlib_hooks.inc`/`vorbis_hooks.inc` (generated from the exe's bytes). C with `__fastcall` as the default (`/Gr`, above, "Compiler options of the libraries"); clang applies that default only with SSE2 in the target, so the build enables SSE2 and `#pragma clang attribute push(__attribute__((target("no-sse"))), apply_to = function)` in each wrapper turns it off for every function: x87 code only (no `xmm` in any object). The C runtime of the libraries is the exe's own (`malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`free`, `memmove`, `memchr`, `qsort`, `floor`, `ldexp`, `_errno`, …, by address), the x87 sequences MSVC 6 inlined (`fsin`, `fcos`, `fsqrt`, `fldln2/fyl2x`, `fldl2e/f2xm1/fscale`, `fld1/fpatan`; returned as the register's long double, as MSVC leaves them in `st(0)`), `_CIpow` `0x5d23e0` and `_CIacos` `0x5e97e0` called in their register form, and the exe's `_chkstk` `0x5d2080` for `alloca`.
- **The exe's libraries were built with 4-byte structure packing** (`/Zp4`) [confirmed: code, sizes]: `OggVorbis_File` has `os` at +0x74, `vd` at +0x1dc, `vb` at +0x244 and the callbacks at +0x2b0 (`ov_clear` `0x5c3bf0`, `_seek_helper` `0x5c3fb6` `call [esi+0x2b4]`), `vorbis_block_init` clears 0x6c bytes: 8-byte alignment of the `ogg_int64_t` members would give +0x78, +0x1e0, +0x250, +0x2c0 and 0x70. With `-fpack-struct=4` every size and offset agrees (`codec_setup_info` 0xe54, `deflate_state` 0x16b8). The first build without it read the callbacks 16 bytes too far.
- **`comp` `0x5e9430` is `__cdecl`** [confirmed: code] (it reads its arguments at `[esp+4]`/`[esp+8]`), unlike the rest of the `/Gr` build; it is `lsp.c`'s comparator passed to `qsort`. The wrapper `libs/vorbis_lsp.c` gives the hook a cdecl entry into the source's `comp`, and the source-built `qsort` call goes through a cdecl adapter (`libc/stdlib.h`); no source line changed.
- **`pow` and `acos`**: the exe has no public `pow`: `0x5d2402` (named `pow` in `exe_symbols.csv`) is the inner part of `_CIpow`, which also expects the high dword of y in eax; calling it as `pow(x, y)` gave wrong results and every Vorbis header with a codebook of map type 1 failed (`OV_EBADHEADER`, first run `20261028-071019-d31e`). The libraries call `_CIpow`/`_CIacos` now, as the exe's code does (`_book_maptype1_quantvals` `0x5e1ea6`). For the C runtime batch: `0x5d2402` is not callable as `pow`.
- **Name corrections** (`exe_symbols.csv`) [confirmed: stack bytes and code]: `0x5e37d0` is `mdct_butterfly_32` (was `mdct_butterflies`), `0x5e3c50` `mdct_butterfly_8` (was `mdct_butterfly_32`), `0x5e3ce0` `mdct_butterfly_generic` (was `mdct_bitreverse`; it takes 4 arguments, `ret 8`); `mdct_butterflies`, `mdct_butterfly_first`, `mdct_butterfly_16` and `mdct_bitreverse` are inlined. `0x5de610` is libogg beta 4's static `_os_checksum` (was `ogg_page_checksum_set`, the name of later releases). Found by comparing the `ret` bytes of every exe function with the source-built one (all other 235 agree).
- **Hooks**: all 237 installed. 11 have no trampoline (a branch or `ret` in their first 5 bytes: `inflateReset`, `vorbis_synthesis_read`, `_vi_psy_free`, `_ilog`, `lpc_clear`, `_analysis_output`, `mapping0_free_info`, `res0_free_info`, `floor0_free_info`, `time0_pack`, `fdrffti`); the checks call the originals with the hooks put out. Folded by the linker (`/OPT:ICF`): `_analysis_output` `0x5e44e0` is also a game vtable slot (`0x5fc1f8`; both `ret 0x10`), `0x5e6450` is time0's empty functions and zlib's `tr_static_init`, `0x5e6430`/`0x5e6460` serve two time0 functions each; vorbisfile's `host_is_big_endian` is the game's `0x46b760`, not hooked (game code) and checked by calling both.
- **Threads**: the music and voice-overs decode in the multimedia timer's thread (`Stream_TimerCallback`). While the Vorbis checks put the hooks out and in, the streams are paused through their "callback running" flag (`checks_libs_common.h`, as `checks_sound_common.cpp` does).

**Checks** (both modules: every case on both sides from the same inputs, hooks put out for the exe's side, called through the exe's addresses):
- `zlib`, all byte-exact: `compress2`/`uncompress` 600 (generated data of 0–70,000 bytes in 9 kinds, levels −1 and 0–9, small output buffers, three uncompress sizes), damaged streams 400, `deflate` streams 300 (window bits 9–15 and raw, memory levels 1–9, the three strategies, invalid parameters and versions, all flush modes, reset), `inflate` streams 300 (pieces, flushes, smaller windows, raw, damaged, reset, `inflateInit_`), `adler32` 300, game files through `Pack`/`Unpack` and `compress2` at levels 1 and 9 (7 files: `Rules.txt`, a dialogue script, Cave1's `.way` and `.zax`, a texture, a model, a voice-over), and **each hook alone**: every hook out, one in at a time, a workload through all 56 functions compared with the exe's alone (the source-built functions call each other directly, so only this shows that an inner function is the one its address was named after). Compared: returns, stream fields, message texts, every output byte.
- `vorbis`: 13 game `.ogg` files read through the game's file layer (6 voice-overs and quips decoded whole as 16-bit signed, 8-bit, unsigned and big-endian PCM, a damaged one, one that cannot seek, one with `initial` bytes, one through the game's own callbacks `0x525380`/`0x5253a0`/`0x525400`/`0x57d310` on a `CFileBuf`, and three songs of 22,050 and 44,100 Hz stereo with `ov_time_seek`, `ov_pcm_seek`, `ov_pcm_seek_page` and `ov_raw_seek`, also outside the stream, and `ov_time_tell` after each): returns, `ov_info`, `ov_pcm_total`, `ov_time_total`, every callback call and the PCM; then the parts the decoder does not reach (the encoder's, in the exe because the backends' export bundles point to them): smallft 200, MDCT 60, LPC/LSP 150, the bit packer 200, the codebooks' encoder side on a game file's 18 books, the psychoacoustics 24 (`_vp_psy_init` with the release's `_psy_set_A0`, `_vp_compute_mask`, `_vp_apply_floor`, `_vp_psy_clear`, `_vi_psy_free`), `_ve_envelope_clear`/`IIR_clear` 40, the backends' `pack`/`copy_info`/`free_info` on a game file's setup, `comp`, the folded functions; and **each hook alone** (181, a workload through the decoder, the seeks and the encoder's parts).

**Differences found** [confirmed: VM runs, disassembly]:
- zlib: none. zlib 1.1.3 accepts `windowBits` 8 in `deflateInit2_` but then writes outside its window (AddressSanitizer on a native build of the same source; zlib 1.2.9 maps 8 to 9); the first run (`20261028-065954-8a27`) compared heap damage and ended the game. Left out of the checks; the game always uses 15.
- Vorbis, integers: none. Every return, size, total, callback call, seek result, codebook, bit packer state and packed setup is identical.
- Vorbis, floating point: the PCM differs in 177 of 697,696 samples of the 13 files (0.025 %), by one unit each (3 of the 12 cases with PCM are bit-identical), and in the 181 single-hook workloads in 91 of 5,383,302 samples, by one (148 of the 181 bit-identical). Cause: x87 register allocation differs between MSVC 6 and clang. Where one compiler keeps a `float` intermediate in an 80-bit register (53-bit precision control) and the other stores it as a float, the rounding differs in the last bit; the decoder's float path (MDCT, floor0's `vorbis_lsp_to_curve`, the window overlap) carries that to a sample now and then (`vorbis_ftoi`). Example: `drfti1` `0x5e8eb0` stores `argh` and `argld` as floats (`fstp dword [esp+0x28]`, `[esp+0x24]`), the clang build keeps them in registers, so the trigonometric tables differ in the last bit. Each float function compared alone on the same inputs stays within 0.34·10⁻⁶ of its largest value (smallft, MDCT, LPC; the codebooks' values are bit-identical), `vorbis_lsp_to_curve` (exponential) within 1.7·10⁻⁵ relative per unit of the logarithm, the psychoacoustic mask (encoder only) within 2.25 dB except 2 single lines in 24 cases where a seed lands on the neighbouring line. The checks compare these with documented tolerances (`checks_vorbis.cpp`: PCM one unit, `SCALE` 10⁻⁵, `EXPONENT` 10⁻⁴, `DECIBEL` 3 dB and at most 2 lines per call) and log how many cases are bit-identical. No game state depends on the PCM (sound only).
- vorbisfile beta 4's `ov_time_tell` divides by `vf->vi[link].rate` with `link` −1 when the stream cannot seek or `pcm_offset` lies before the first link (−1 after a failed seek): it reads the dword 24 bytes before the `vi` array, outside the block, so the result depends on the heap (the exe's side gave tiny values, the source-built one ±infinity in run `20261028-072300-1fe1`). The game's streams always seek; the checks call it only where it is defined.
- Not checked: the encoder's `floor0_forward`, `_curve_to_lpc`, `_f0_fit`, `res0_forward`, `_testhack`, `_encodepart` and `mapping0_forward` (7 functions; hooked, stack bytes equal): they need an encoder state that only `vorbis_analysis_init` sets up, which the exe does not have. The game never encodes.

Runs (all checks identical): `OnlyChecks=zlib,vorbis` with all cases on `Assimilate Cave1` (Respawn2) `20261028-082245-9834` (`vorbis` 6.2 s, `zlib` 3.5 s) and on `Test/Nachbau1` `20261028-080507-ef97` (7.0 s, 3.9 s); the full run with `CheckScale=0.1` on `Test/Nachbau1` `20261028-081548-f0db` (all 1029 checks the same, 8443 hooks installed, the two known `DebugLog_*` ones not (launcher, `/DebugLog`), `Zip CRC` and `All checks done` in the log; its cleanup found the DLL still locked by the exiting game, put back with `--restore` in job `20261028-082233-be0f`); `--shot-set` `20261028-081552-2349` … `-081553-79d4`: all 9 scenes identical or different only in their animated areas. VM-01's share was not mounted for the end of the batch; all three ran on VM-02.
- **Decision (the project owner, 2026-10-28): the Vorbis float differences stay documented.** 177 of 697,696 PCM samples differ by 1 LSB between the source-built decoder (clang) and the exe's (MSVC 6), from where the compilers keep x87 intermediates in 80-bit registers; inaudible. The faithful-and-complete milestone counts Vorbis as matched with this documented tolerance; no source change to force MSVC's float stores.

### GameSpy SDK (2001)

- **Parts** [confirmed: strings, the SDK's message formats]: the CD key SDK (server side `gcd_*`: `key.gamespy.com`, `"\auth\\pid\%d\ch\%s\resp\%s\ip\%d\skey\%d"`, `"\disc\..."`, `"uok"`/`"unok"`/`"ison"`, `"Bad CD Key"`, `"CD Key in use"`; client side `gcd_compute_response` `0x5c9960` with MD5 `0x5c9ee0`–`0x5ca8b0`), query and reporting (`qr_init` `0x5c82a0`, `qr_process_queries` with heartbeats, `qr_send_statechanged`, `qr_shutdown`), server browsing (`ServerListNew`, `ServerListUpdate` against the master, `ServerListLANUpdate`, the server objects with hash tables), `gs_encrypt`/`gs_encode` and GameSpy's `darray`/`hashtable`. No version string; `"\queryid\1.1"` and `gamever` `"1.6"` sent by the server list (the SDK's engine version) [assumption: the meaning; the code has no version string].
- **Constants of the game** [confirmed: code `0x51f310`, `0x518e00`, `0x519cf0`, `0x5c5280`]: game name `"zax"` (query and reporting) and `"Zax"`/`"zax"` (server list: game name, engine name), secret key `"J3An3s"` (built byte by byte on the stack in three places), CD key game id 409 (`gcd_init(0x199)`), the query port 26794 (`0x68aa`), LAN search on ports 26794–26804, heartbeats to `master.gamespy.com:27900` every 300 s (resent after 30 s up to 10 times while the state changes), the server list from `master.gamespy.com:28900` (TCP, `"\secure\"` challenge answered with `gs_encode(gs_encrypt(challenge, secret key))`, names corrected in "GameSpy SDK (2001), reimplemented" below, `"\list\cmp\gamename\%s\final\"`), the CD key server `key.gamespy.com` on port 29910 in the original — in this exe the crack set `htons(0xffff)` (`0x5c5326`), so the check goes nowhere (EXE_FINDINGS.md, "Exe variants"). Answers to `\basic\`, `\info\`, `\rules\`, `\players\` come from the game's callbacks `0x51ef40`–`0x51f0f0` (section 6, "Net game, …"). No server was contacted.
- **The game's calls** [confirmed]: `GameSpy_Start`/`Stop`/`Think` (`0x51f310`/`0x51f3e0`/`0x51f420`: `qr_init` + `gcd_init`, `qr_send_statechanged` + `qr_shutdown` + `gcd_shutdown`, `qr_process_queries` (dedicated) or `qr_process_queries_no_heartbeat`, then `gcd_think`), `gcd_authenticate_user` from `0x5ac100` (a joining client's key response), `gcd_disconnect_user` from `DPlayGame_ProcessSlots` `0x480800`, `gcd_compute_response` from the client's key answer `0x5bce30`, and the server browser window (`0x518e00`–`0x519cf0`: `ServerListNew`/`Update`/`LANUpdate`/`Think`/`Free`, server ping/address/values). The game's own `rand` use is none: only `gcd_authenticate_user` and `gcd_compute_response` call the runtime's `rand` (challenges).
- **For the port**: GameSpy's master servers are gone (2014). The port needs the LAN part (UDP queries on 26794–26804 with the same `\key\value\` answers, so old clients can see new servers if wanted) and either no internet browsing or a replacement master (e.g. OpenSpy speaks this protocol) [assumption: about OpenSpy, not tested]. The CD key check is dropped (as in the crack).

### GameSpy SDK (2001), reimplemented [verified 2026-10-28, VM; Winsock, the clock and rand through recording stand-ins only, no network]

**94 functions reimplemented and hooked** in four modules (rows in `docs/reimpl.csv`, names in `docs/exe_symbols.csv`): the 68 functions of `docs/functions.csv` in `0x5c5280`–`0x5ca9d7`, six small callbacks that are in no table (`0x5c78e0`, `0x5c81e0`, `0x5c8220`, `0x5c8260`, `0x5c8280`, `0x5c8290`) and the 20 wsock32 import thunks `0x5ca9e0`–`0x5caa52`. Nothing in the range is too short to hook (the shortest, `ArrayLength` `0x5c9cc0`, has 7 bytes; `SocketShutDown` `0x5c9ab0` is a 5-byte `jmp` to the WSACleanup thunk, hooked without a trampoline). The thunks `0x5caa58`–`0x5caa88` behind them belong to msacm32, ddraw and dsound, not to the SDK. No code outside the SDK calls the wsock32 thunks [confirmed: scan of `.text` for `call`/`jmp` to them].

| Module | Functions | What |
|---|---|---|
| `gamespy_gcd.cpp` | 12 | the CD key SDK (server side) `gcd_init`, `gcd_shutdown`, `gcd_authenticate_user`, `gcd_disconnect_user`, `gcd_think`, `gcd_find_client`, `gcd_process_ison`, `gcd_value_for_key`; the client side `gcd_compute_response`; RSA's `MD5Update`, `MD5Transform`, `MD5Digest` |
| `gamespy_qr.cpp` | 30 | `qr_init`, `qr_process_queries`, `qr_process_queries_no_heartbeat`, `qr_send_statechanged`, `qr_shutdown`, `qr_value_for_key`, `add_queryid`, `packet_send`, `send_basic`/`info`/`rules`/`players`/`echo`/`final`; `gs_encode`, `gs_encrypt`; nonport.c's `msleep`, `SocketStartUp`, `SocketShutDown`; darray.c (`ArrayNew`, `ArrayFree`, `ArrayLength`, `ArrayNth`, `ArrayAppend`, `ArrayReplaceAt`, `ArraySearch`) and hashtable.c (`TableNew2`, `TableFree`, `TableEnter`, `TableLookup`) |
| `gamespy_sb.cpp` | 32 | the server list (`ServerListNew`, `Free`, `Update`, `LANUpdate`, `ModeChange`, `AddServer`, `FindServer`, `LANList`, `ParseInfoList`, `ReadList`, `AddServerData`, `QueryLoop`, `Think`, `Halt`, `Clear`, `CountSlashes`), the servers (`ServerFree`, `ServerNewData`, `mytok`, `LookupKey`, `ServerNew`, `ServerParseKeyVals`, `ServerGetPing`, `ServerGetAddress`, `ServerGetQueryPort`, `ServerGetStringValue`, `ServerGetIntValue`) and the hash table callbacks (`StringHash`, `KeyValHash`, `CaseInsensitiveCompare`, `KeyValCompareKey`, `StringFree`) |
